title: t18657: fix(pulse): expose silent --command dispatch/repo-cap outcomes to OpenCode supervisors
body:
## Task


Make the outcome of silent `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch` and `--command repo-cap` calls visible to an OpenCode pulse supervisor, without changing their exit statuses.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Make the outcome of silent `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch` and `--command repo-cap` calls visible to an OpenCode pulse supervisor, without changing their exit statuses.

## Why

Found while reviewing #34323 (follow-up promised in that review comment).

- OpenCode's Bash tool shows a command with no stdout as `(no output)` and does not show its exit status. Probe: `bash -c "exit 3"` and a real below-cap `repo-cap` call both appear only as `(no output)`.
- The pulse command policy (`.agents/workflows/pulse.md`) forbids `$?`, `||` and other shell control, so the supervisor cannot observe the status any other way.
- `--command dispatch` writes nothing to stdout whether it launches or defers; `_dispatch_launch_worker` logs only to `LOGFILE`. A deferred dispatch (exit 1 or 3) therefore looks identical to a launched one.
- `.agents/workflows/pulse.md:303` tells supervisors to read `repo-cap` as "returns 0 (at cap, skip) or 1 (below cap, safe to dispatch)", but that status is invisible in OpenCode.

#34323 (PR #34326) fixed status propagation inside the router; this is the remaining observability gap.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-commands.sh` — after the `dispatch` and `repo-cap` delegates return, print one machine-readable outcome line to stdout, for example `PULSE_COMMAND_RESULT command=dispatch rc=<n> outcome=<launched|deferred|failed>` and `PULSE_COMMAND_RESULT command=repo-cap rc=<n> outcome=<at-cap|below-cap>`. Capturing the status with `if`, `||` or `&&` disables errexit inside the delegate. Either choose a pattern that keeps errexit semantics, or show in the PR that the delegates' failure handling does not depend on errexit. Preserve the router's returned status exactly.
- `EDIT: .agents/workflows/pulse.md` and `.agents/workflows/pulse-sweep.md` — document the outcome line as the way supervisors read dispatch and repo-cap results.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh` — extend `test_policy_compatible_command_router` to assert the outcome lines and unchanged statuses for dispatch 0/1/3 and repo-cap 0/1.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-commands.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/pulse.md`
- `.agents/workflows/pulse-sweep.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh`

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Errexit: `pulse-wrapper.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 72). Wrapping a delegate in `if`/`||` disables errexit inside every function it calls, which can change fail-closed behaviour in `dispatch_with_dedup`. Choose a capture pattern that keeps errexit semantics, or prove the delegate is errexit-independent.
- Stdout consumers: `rg -n -- "--command (dispatch|repo-cap)" .agents` shows only workflow docs as consumers today; re-check before changing stdout.
- Keep usage exit 2 and all dispatch safety gates (dedup, footprint, capacity, ownership, canary) unchanged.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-commands.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--command dispatch` prints exactly one outcome line naming the status, for exits 0, 1 and 3, and still exits with the delegated status.
- [ ] `--command repo-cap` prints an outcome line distinguishing at-cap from below-cap and still exits 0/1 respectively.
- [ ] Usage errors still exit 2 with the usage text on stderr and no outcome line.
- [ ] Errexit behaviour inside `dispatch_with_dedup` on the CLI path is unchanged (explained in the PR).
- [ ] `pulse.md` and `pulse-sweep.md` describe how supervisors read the outcome line.
- [ ] Existing router tests and shellcheck pass.

Ref #34323

title: t18658: test(plugin): make bounded-operation restoration test tolerate host load
body:
## Task


Make the bounded-operation test "restoration runs after success and remains visible when it fails" reliable on a loaded host. It currently fails on unchanged `main` whenever the host is busy.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Make the bounded-operation test "restoration runs after success and remains visible when it fails" reliable on a loaded host. It currently fails on unchanged `main` whenever the host is busy.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-11 while reviewing PR #34325, on a 16-core macOS host with load averages of 60–80:

- At `origin/main`, `node --test --test-name-pattern 'restoration runs after success' .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` failed 8 of 8 runs when three sampling loops ran concurrently. It failed 2 of 8 with lighter contention.
- Failures report `state` `timed_out` or `restoration_failed` where the test expects `succeeded`.
- The test gives a `node -e "process.exit(0)"` command a `budgetMs: 1000` and its restoration a `restorationBudgetMs: 1000` (lines 610–643). Under load, starting node plus the supervisor's synchronous `ps` snapshots (`bounded-operation-process-snapshot.mjs`, `spawnSync` with a 1000 ms timeout each) can exceed one second before the drain completes.
- These plugin tests do not run in CI today, so the failure only shows up in local verification, where it reads as a regression in whatever PR is under test. (It was first suspected as a #34325 regression, and comparing against `main` falsified that.)

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:610-643` — raise the success-path budgets (`budgetMs`, `restorationBudgetMs`) for the two cases that expect success or a clean restoration failure to a load-tolerant value, for example 10000 ms. Keep the deliberately short `restorationBudgetMs: 30` for the timed-out restoration case, because that case asserts a timeout.
- Check the other tests in the same file that pair `budgetMs: 1000` with an expected `succeeded` state, and apply the same treatment where the budget is not what is being tested.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Do not change production budgets or supervisor timing; this is a test-budget fix only.
- Keep assertions that intentionally exercise timeouts (short budgets) unchanged.

### Verification

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-operation-dispatch-launcher.mjs
```

Repeat the single test several times while the host is under load (for example with another `node --test` loop running) and confirm it passes consistently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The restoration test passes repeatedly on a loaded host where it previously failed on `main`.
- [ ] The timed-out restoration case still asserts `restoration_failed` / `timed_out` with its short budget.
- [ ] No production module changes.
- [ ] The full bounded-operation plugin test files pass.

Ref #34324

title: t18659: pulse: recover first-wave dispatch capacity lost to timed-out sentinel stages...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18659` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

pulse: recover first-wave dispatch capacity lost to timed-out sentinel stages and single-repository first waves

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse first wave triage enrichment deferred refill starvation cycle budget` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 open related PRs for the target files; last relevant changes are GH#33647 (65cb9ed1f9), GH#33737 (0da80cfd3b), GH#33560 (fd10ec90bd), GH#33743 (849e2c0af5)
- [x] File refs verified: 4 source files, 2 test files and 1 reference doc checked at origin/main db0e6141c9
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — dispatch-path scheduling with budget/fairness judgement; no security boundary change
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog. The host ran 1-2 of 20 workers for hours while 44 issues were `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`.

## Problem

Pulse dispatch leaves most local worker capacity idle. On one runner over ~15 consecutive cycles (~7.5h, 2026-10-11), the host ran 1-2 of 20 workers while a managed private repo had 44 open `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` issues.

Two compounding causes, both observed in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log`:

1. **Timed-out sentinel-gated stages re-run at full timeout every cycle.**
   - `fix_the_fixer_detector` hits its 60s stage timeout (exit 124) every cycle. `_pulse_run_fix_the_fixer_detector_if_stale` only touches `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-fix-the-fixer-last-run` *after* the helper returns ("Touch sentinel regardless of outcome (fail-open)"), but the stage wrapper kills the function first, so the sentinel never advances. Observed sentinel age: 4 days; 60s lost in every cycle.
   - `cache_prime` hits its 300s timeout (exit 124) every cycle since the last successful prime aged past `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_PRIME_MAX_AGE` (7200s). Only a successful prime (or a successful prefetch batch refresh) refreshes `pulse-cache-prime-last-run`, so a prime that cannot finish within the bound repeats for 300s every cycle (GH#33737 bounded the duration, not the repetition).
   - Together ~360s of a ~1800s cycle. Every cycle in the window then skipped `Post-label dispatch_max` with `remaining=0..599s, required=600s` (six cycles missed by 1-19s) and skipped the end-of-cycle `Dispatch_max`/cycle-final refill drain (`remaining<0`).

2. **The first dispatch wave stops at the first non-empty repository (GH#33647).** `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json` breaks after the first repository with any candidate and rotates `pulse-first-wave-cursor`. Recent first waves entered the loop with `effective_slots=17..20` but `candidates=1..3`. The rotation was even across 17 repositories (~16 first waves each), so the repository with the largest dispatchable backlog got ~7% of first waves. Because normal refills (full census) are budget-skipped every cycle, the first wave is effectively the only dispatch.

## Proposed fix

1. `fix_the_fixer_detector`: claim the cadence slot (touch the sentinel) **before** running the helper, preserving the documented fail-open intent under the stage timeout.
2. `cache_prime`: record a separate attempt marker (`pulse-cache-prime-last-attempt`) before invoking the prime; when the success sentinel exists but is stale, skip priming while the last attempt is younger than the max age. A *missing* success sentinel still primes unconditionally, preserving the incident runbook's "delete sentinel to force a prime" procedure. `prefetch_state` continues to refresh the same caches.
3. First wave: keep polling subsequent repositories (in cursor order) until the accumulated candidate count reaches the free-slot target, or a bounded first-wave enumeration budget (`PULSE_FIRST_WAVE_ENUMERATION_BUDGET_S`, default 180s) elapses, or every repository has been polled. Always include at least the first non-empty repository (current behaviour), keep `product_discovery_complete=false`, and advance the cursor to the last polled repository so rotation continues. Normal (non-first-wave) enumeration is unchanged.

Functions: `_pulse_run_fix_the_fixer_detector_if_stale`, `_pulse_prime_caches_if_stale`, `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json`, and `_dispatch_enumerate_ranked_round` (supplies the free-slot target). The runbook gains a note about the attempt marker.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cache-prime.sh`
- `.agents/reference/incident-recovery-runbook.md`

## Reference pattern

- Sentinel/cadence gates: `_pulse_check_runaway_log` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`.
- First-wave scope and cursor: GH#33647 (`_dispatch_first_wave_advance_cursor`, `_dispatch_repository_rows`).
- Enumeration timing EWMA and admission: `_dispatch_enumeration_expected_seconds`, `_dispatch_record_enumeration_seconds`, `_dispatch_cycle_budget_admits_round` (GH#33560, GH#33737).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh` passes, with assertions that a first wave whose first non-empty repository has fewer candidates than free slots continues to later repositories, stops at the target, honours the time budget, and still rotates/wraps the cursor.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cache-prime.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-fix-the-fixer-observability.sh`, and the sibling pulse dispatch suites pass; ShellCheck is clean on changed scripts.
- Runtime: after deploy, `pulse-stage-timings.log` no longer shows `fix_the_fixer_detector ... 124` or `cache_prime ... 124` in consecutive cycles, and `pulse.log` first waves show `Dispatch_max: entering candidate loop ... candidates=N` with N at or above free slots when backlog exists.

</details>

title: t18660: fix(pulse): explicit For/Ref merge association treats same-line context refer...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18660` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): explicit For/Ref merge association treats same-line context references as extra declarations

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `ambiguous explicit issue identities merge association For Ref worker partial PR` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 open related PRs for the target files; last relevant changes are d403c44b14 (explicit association added) and GH#34312 (8b6b30c5ad, partial continuation consumer)
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (`_extract_pr_work_issue`, explicit mode) and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh` (`test_explicit_merge_association`) checked at origin/main 035691f2f7
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — parser change on the merge-association trust path; fail-closed behaviour for genuine multi-target declarations is preserved
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog: mergeable worker partial-delivery PRs were skipped by every merge pass on one runner.

## Problem

`_extract_pr_work_issue <pr> <repo> explicit` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` (added by d403c44b14) marks a `For #N` / `Ref #N` declaration line ambiguous when **any** `#N` appears later on the same line:

```awk
sub(/^[0-9]+/, "", line)
if (line ~ /#[0-9]+/) print "ambiguous"
```

Worker partial-delivery PRs conventionally open with `For #N.` followed by context prose on the same line, for example `For #101. Continuing the merged checkpoint from PR #99.` or `For #101. Ready partial delivery; do not close the issue or tracker #90.` The same sentence on its own line is ignored, but on the declaration line it is counted as a second declaration, so the PR gets no merge association.

Observed on one runner (2026-10-11, a managed private repo):

- `_check_pr_merge_gates` returns 1 for `origin:worker` PRs without a closing target when explicit association fails, before any other merge gate is evaluated. Five open, non-draft worker PRs with `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN` log `has ambiguous explicit issue identities — no merge association` every merge pass (one of them 100 times since 2026-10-09); two drafts carry the same shape.
- Across the 19 declaration lines of open worker PRs in that repo, 7 are ambiguous under the current rule and 0 under the proposed rule. In the last 150 merged worker PRs, 4 more declaration lines have the same false-ambiguity shape.
- The same resolver gates `_pulse_merge_admin_safety_check` (fails closed) and `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` (`|| return 0`, so the GH#34312 return-to-queue path is skipped for this shape).

Genuine multi-target declarations must stay ambiguous, e.g. `For #34125. For #34147.` (PR #34162 in this repo) and a parenthetical target list such as `For #105 (parent gate #89 / t018).`

## Proposed fix

Bound the declaration's target list at the first sentence/clause terminator (`.`, `;`, `!` or `?` followed by whitespace or end of line):

1. Another `#N` inside that clause stays ambiguous: `For #42 and #43`, `For #42, #43`, `For #42 and Ref #43`, `For #42 (see #41).`
2. After the clause, only another `For`/`Ref` `#N` declaration on the same line stays ambiguous: `For #42. Ref #43.`
3. Incidental references in later sentences (`PR #99`, `tracker #90`) are context, exactly as they already are on their own line.
4. No terminator → the whole remainder is the clause (current behaviour).

No change to closing-target precedence, fence/comment/quote/secondary-section handling, multi-line ambiguity, cross-repository rejection, or repair mode.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh`

## Reference pattern

- Explicit-mode awk parser in `_extract_pr_work_issue` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`) and its fixtures in `test_explicit_merge_association` (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh`).
- Consumers: `_check_pr_merge_gates` (`pulse-merge.sh`), `_pulse_merge_admin_safety_check` (`pulse-merge-gates.sh`), `_pm_restore_partial_continuation` (`pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`).

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-extract-linked-issue.sh` passes, including new cases: context after `For #N.` associates N; `For #42, #43`, `For #42 and #43.`, `For #42. Ref #43.` and `For #42 (see #41).` fail closed.
- Sibling suites that exercise explicit association pass: `test-pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-admin-safety-check.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-worker-briefed.sh`.
- ShellCheck clean on changed scripts.
- Runtime: after deploy, the affected PRs no longer log `has ambiguous explicit issue identities` and proceed to the normal merge gates.

title: t18661: fix(pulse): keep dependants blocked while a consolidated blocker's successor ...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18661` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): keep dependants blocked while a consolidated blocker's successor is open

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `consolidated blocker successor superseded dependency NOT_PLANNED stateReason resolver` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 open related PRs for the target files; last relevant changes are 589016c402 (t18646 blocked-by:GH# labels), 74f9d071c8 (GH#33957 stale sweep), e20544d82e (GH#34056 bounded refresh)
- [x] File refs verified: `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` / `_blocked_by_check_issue_num_live` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`), `_der_native_blockers_closed` / `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`), consolidation close step (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh` `_compose_consolidation_worker_instructions`) checked at origin/main 6ac3f12f71
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — read-side resolver change on the dispatch/unblock safety path; fails closed on unverifiable supersession
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog: dependants of consolidated issues were dispatched before the consolidated work existed.

## What

Dependency readiness treats a native or declared blocker that was **closed as superseded** (`stateReason` `NOT_PLANNED`/`DUPLICATE` plus a trusted `Superseded by #S` comment) as unresolved while its successor chain is still open. Dependants stay blocked (dispatch gate, dep-graph refresh, dependency-event reconciler, stale sweep) until the successor finishes, instead of being dispatched against work that has not happened yet.

## Why

Consolidation (`_compose_consolidation_worker_instructions`, `pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`) comments `Superseded by #NEW`, labels the parent `consolidated` and closes it `not planned`. The parent's native `blocking` edges are not moved to the successor, and every resolver treats any `CLOSED` blocker as done:

- `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` read `blockedBy { nodes { number state } }` and returned "positively clear" for an all-`CLOSED` set; the dispatch gate (`is_blocked_by_unresolved`), final pre-launch attestation and dep-graph refresh rely on it.
- `_der_native_blockers_closed` and `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed` did the same, so close events and the stale sweep flipped dependants to `status:available`.

Read-only scan of one managed private repo (2026-10-11): 482 open issues, **40 dependants with native blockers closed `NOT_PLANNED`**; 39 of those blockers carry a trusted `Superseded by #S` comment whose successor body says `Supersedes #P`; about 14 dependants were `status:available`/`queued` while their successor was still open. Workers dispatched there start before their prerequisite exists, spend tokens and often end in terminal-blocker comments.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-lib.sh` — shared resolver `dep_supersession_outstanding <blocker_repo> <blocker_number> <state_reason> [dependant_ref]` plus the logging wrapper `dep_supersession_blocks`; one response-metered GraphQL read per hop (`issueOrPullRequest { state stateReason comments(last:100) }` + `rateLimit { cost }`), modelled on the exact-cost GraphQL pattern in `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` and the sourced-lib load guard in `task-identity-lib.sh`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` — source the lib; `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` also reads `stateReason repository { nameWithOwner }` and blocks a `CLOSED` node whose supersession is outstanding; `_blocked_by_check_issue_num_live` reads `state,stateReason` and applies the same rule. Net +4 lines (file stays under the 1500-line shell size ratchet).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` — source the lib; `_der_native_blockers_closed` takes an optional `readiness` mode that returns `DER_NOT_READY` for an outstanding superseded node; declared blockers go through the new `_der_live_blocker_resolved`, which applies the rule only when given a dependant ref. `_der_try_unblock` opts in; the closed-event self-check `_der_live_issue_closed` is unchanged.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-supersession-lib.sh` — resolver semantics with a GraphQL fixture mock.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh` and `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh` — wiring cases.

### Resolver rules

1. Only `CLOSED` blockers whose reason is `NOT_PLANNED` or `DUPLICATE` are inspected; `COMPLETED`/legacy empty reasons keep the closed-means-resolved rule with no extra request.
2. aidevops:trust-boundary — the successor comes only from the newest `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` comment whose first non-blank line starts `Superseded by #N` (same repository as the blocker). Other mentions are ignored.
3. Follow the chain at most 3 hops. `OPEN` successor → outstanding. `CLOSED` successor that is itself superseded → next hop. Otherwise (completed, merged PR, closed without a successor) → resolved.
4. A successor equal to the dependant itself resolves (the dependant owns the work; no self-deadlock).
5. Lookup failure, missing cost, unknown state, reopened blocker, cycle or hop limit → outstanding (fail closed), logged with the reason from `DEP_SUPERSESSION_DETAIL`.
6. Readiness only. `_der_completion_blockers_closed` (TODO completion close in `issue-sync-helper-close.sh`) keeps closed-is-done so finished work is never held open by an unrelated successor.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `is_blocked_by_unresolved` (dispatch dedup `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`, final attestation `pulse-dispatch-worker-gates.sh`, stale recovery `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`), `_refresh_dependency_is_resolved` (dep-graph refresh), `_der_try_unblock` (close events, stale sweep). `_der_completion_blockers_closed` is deliberately unchanged.
- **Deliberately unchanged reader:** `_dependency_native_blockers_closed_for` (`issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh`) only exempts an all-closed edge from issue-sync's available→blocked move and never moves blocked→available; the dispatch gate above stays authoritative and refresh corrects the label.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new writes; existing label edits (`_refresh_ensure_unresolved_is_blocked`, `_der_try_unblock`) simply see "unresolved" for these blockers, so refresh moves affected `status:available` dependants back to `status:blocked` (queued/in-progress untouched).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh`, `test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, `test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh`, `test-stale-recovery-blocked-by-recheck.sh`, `test-pulse-dep-graph-todo-drift.sh`, `test-pulse-dispatch-worker-launch-lock.sh`, `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`, `test-pulse-dep-graph-*` siblings, `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`, `test-planning-pr-guard.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A — no config keys; `DEP_SUPERSESSION_MAX_HOPS` env override defaults to 3.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`; the new lib is picked up by the existing deployment.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none — read-side rule applies to existing edges; no relationship edits.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; no persisted state.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** read-only lookups; existing re-read-before-edit guards in the label writers are unchanged. Consolidation posts `Superseded by` before closing the parent, so a closed parent is observed with its marker.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; reverting restores closed-means-resolved.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** runners on older versions keep the old rule; GraphQL nodes without `stateReason` behave as before.
- **Idempotency/retry:** pure function of live GitHub state; retries re-read.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** API failure on a superseded blocker blocks (same as the existing unknown-state rule) and recovers on the next cycle; a dangling marker naming a missing issue stays blocked with a logged `lookup failed` reason until a maintainer corrects it.

```bash

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh

shellcheck .agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Runtime:** read-only probe of `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` on the 40 live dependants: open-successor cases block, completed-successor cases stay clear.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-supersession-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dependant whose native blocker is closed `NOT_PLANNED` with a trusted `Superseded by #S` comment and an open `#S` is reported unresolved by `is_blocked_by_unresolved`, `_refresh_dependency_is_resolved` and `_der_native_blockers_closed ... readiness` (`DER_NOT_READY`).
- [ ] When `#S` is closed `COMPLETED`, the same dependant resolves clear (no regression for finished consolidations).
- [ ] Regression: `COMPLETED` blockers trigger no extra API request; `NOT_PLANNED` blockers without a trusted first-line `Superseded by #N` comment keep resolving clear; untrusted commenters cannot redirect a dependency; completion checks keep closed-is-done.
- [ ] Fail closed: lookup failure, unknown state, cycles and chains longer than 3 hops keep the dependant blocked with a logged reason; a successor that is the dependant itself resolves.

## Context & Decisions

- Read-side guard first: covers historical consolidations without relationship backfills or mass label edits. Moving native edges to the successor at consolidation time, and reconciling a superseded parent's dependants when the successor closes (today the stale sweep and refresh catch them), are separate follow-ups.

title: t18662: fix(pulse): release dependency-ready issues held only by brief terminal-block...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18662` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): release dependency-ready issues held only by brief terminal-blocker text

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `dependency event reconciler terminal blocker vocabulary body hold false positive` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 open related PRs for the target files; last relevant changes are 0e83416a58 (t18661 supersession readiness), 589016c402 (t18646 blocked-by:GH# labels), 74f9d071c8 (GH#33957 resumable stale sweep), 2227f6fcf7 (GH#33881 blocked-by value grammar)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main c30e0ba4fd: `_der_text_has_strong_hold`, `_der_has_hold`, `_der_try_unblock`, `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`); runtime terminal-blocker writers `_apply_terminal_blocker` (`pulse-dispatch-core.sh`) and `_terminal_blocker_recovery` / `terminal_blocker_circuit_comment` (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`) post comments only
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — narrow change on the unblock safety path; every new branch keeps or adds a hold, except the documented body-vocabulary exemption
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog: issues whose dependencies had all closed stayed `status:blocked` indefinitely.

## What

The dependency-event reconciler (close events and the periodic stale sweep) releases `status:blocked` issues whose dependencies are resolved, without treating worker-protocol documentation in the issue body as a hold, and without overriding blocks that no dependency explains:

1. Terminal-blocker vocabulary (`Terminal[_ -]blocker`, which also matches `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=` and `terminal-blocker circuit`) is hold evidence only in trusted comments, not in the issue body. Every other strong marker, operational hold line and hold label keeps its current scope.
2. The reconciler only removes `status:blocked` with positive dependency evidence: at least one native `blockedBy` edge, or a declared blocker ref in the body or a `blocked-by:` label. Without either, the block came from another mechanism and is left alone.
3. A close event keeps reconciling the remaining dependants when one dependant is still waiting on another open blocker (`DER_NOT_READY`), instead of stopping at it. Hard failures still stop the pass.

## Why

`_der_has_hold` runs `_der_text_has_strong_hold` over `body + trusted comments`, and its pattern includes `Terminal[_ -]blocker([_ -]detected)?`. Briefs routinely document the worker protocol in the body, for example: "On exit 1 ... emit `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`. Do not set `status:blocked`: the terminal-blocker circuit keeps this issue `status:available`". The runtime never records terminal-blocker state in bodies — `_apply_terminal_blocker` and the terminal-blocker circuit post comments — so in a body this vocabulary is documentation, not a hold. The dep-graph refresh body gate (`issue_body_has_defer_marker`) already ignores it.

Read-only census of one managed private repo (2026-10-11, 340 open `status:blocked` issues):

- 237 bodies (70%) contain terminal-blocker vocabulary; no other strong hold token appears in any body.
- 11 issues with every dependency closed (10 native, 1 declared) had the body text as their only hold signal, so neither close events nor the stale sweep could release them.
- 3 issues with no dependency at all were blocked by mechanisms the reconciler does not recognise (two cost-circuit-breaker trips, one dispatch infrastructure failure). Only the body text stopped the reconciler from releasing them, because with no native edge and no declared ref `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed` is vacuously true. Change 1 alone would release them, so change 2 is required. It also matches the existing contract in `_hold_dependency_sync_retry` (`issue-sync-relationships-gh.sh`): "Pulse supplies the positive proof required to unblock it".

Change 3 is a code-level defect present since GH#27338: in `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure`, `_der_try_unblock ... || return 1` treats `DER_NOT_READY` (the dependant has another open blocker) as fatal. All later dependants of the closed issue then wait for the stale sweep instead of being released by the close event.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
  - Split the strong-hold pattern into `DER_STRONG_HOLD_RE` (`HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED|Worker Watchdog Kill|ACTION REQUIRED|worker[_ -]blocked|aidevops:brief-hold`) and `DER_TERMINAL_BLOCKER_RE` (`Terminal[_ -]blocker([_ -]detected)?`).
  - `_der_text_has_strong_hold <text> <comments>`: `DER_STRONG_HOLD_RE` over `<text>` (body + comments, unchanged scope), `DER_TERMINAL_BLOCKER_RE` over `<comments>` only, and the existing `**BLOCKED**` + `cannot proceed` pair over `<text>`.
  - `_der_has_hold`: pass `"$text" "$comments"`; the expired-brief-hold rewrite still applies to `comments` first.
  - New `_der_declares_blockers <candidate_json>`: true when `_der_issue_refs` or `_der_task_refs` yields a ref from body + label names (same text construction as `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed`); jq failure is false.
  - `_der_try_unblock`: when `_DER_NATIVE_BLOCKERS_PRESENT` is not `true`, `_der_declares_blockers "$candidate_json" || return 0` before `_der_all_declared_blockers_closed`.
  - `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure`: capture the `_der_try_unblock` status per candidate; continue on `0` or `DER_NOT_READY`, `return 1` otherwise.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh` — classifier cases for body vs comment terminal-blocker vocabulary; stale-sweep cases for body-documented protocol (released) and a no-evidence block (kept); a two-dependant close event where the first is still blocked and the second is released. Add fixture knobs `STALE_DEP_LABEL` (stale-sweep dependency label, default `blocked-by:#10`), `EXTRA_DEPENDANT` (second search candidate #21) and `NATIVE_EXTRA_FOR` (restrict the extra open native blocker to one issue number).

### Complexity Impact

- `_der_text_has_strong_hold` 10 → ~13 lines; `_der_try_unblock` 24 → ~26; `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` 32 → ~35; new helper ~10 lines. All far below the 100-line gate; file ~720 lines.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_der_try_unblock` from `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` (close hooks in `pulse-merge.sh`, `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, `issue-sync-helper-close.sh`, `github-cli-helper.sh`) and `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` (`pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`). `_der_completion_blockers_closed` does not use the hold classifier and is unchanged.
- **Deliberately unchanged:** dep-graph refresh (`pulse-dep-graph.sh`) only visits issues with dependency entries and already ignores body terminal-blocker text; dispatch-time `terminal_blocker_circuit_active` / `terminal_blocker_backoff_active` remain the authority for re-dispatch after a worker BLOCKED exit.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new writes; the only label edit is the existing re-read-guarded `status:blocked` → `status:available` in `_der_try_unblock`.
- **Schemas/config:** none.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none; the next stale sweep applies the rule to existing issues.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; no persisted state.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Safety direction:** change 1 can only release issues whose dependencies are positively resolved and that carry no comment, label or operational hold; changes 2 and 3 never release anything new on their own (2 adds a hold, 3 continues to the same per-candidate checks).
- **Comment-side vocabulary unchanged:** trusted terminal-blocker comments (observations, circuit comments, `Terminal blocker detected`) still hold, including after this change.
- **Evidence removed after blocking:** an issue whose only dependency declaration was deleted stays `status:blocked` until a maintainer or the owning mechanism releases it — the conservative outcome the dependency-sync retry hold already relies on.
- **Mixed versions:** older runners keep the old classifier; both only ever release fully resolved dependants.
- **Partial failure:** API/jq failures keep returning 1 (fail closed); `DER_NOT_READY` is no longer escalated to a failure in the close-event loop.

### Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-supersession-lib.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-closing-reconciliation.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Runtime:** after deployment, the next stale sweep of the census repo releases the dependency-resolved issues whose only hold was body text (stale-sweep log line plus label timeline), while the no-dependency cost-breaker and infrastructure-failure blocks stay `status:blocked`.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18662-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_der_has_hold` returns no hold for a body containing only terminal-blocker worker-protocol text, and still returns a hold for the same vocabulary in a trusted comment, for `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED` / `ACTION REQUIRED` in the body, and for every existing classifier case.
- [ ] The stale sweep releases a `status:blocked` issue whose dependencies are closed and whose body documents the terminal-blocker protocol.
- [ ] The stale sweep leaves a `status:blocked` issue with no native edge, no declared ref and no `blocked-by:` label unchanged, even with no hold markers.
- [ ] A close event with two dependants, where the first still has another open blocker, releases the second.
- [ ] Existing reconciler, supersession and stale-recovery suites pass; ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` are clean.

## Context & Decisions

- Only the terminal-blocker family moves to comment scope: it is the only strong token observed in bodies, and every runtime writer of it posts comments. `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED`, `ACTION REQUIRED`, `aidevops:brief-hold`, watchdog and `worker_blocked` markers keep body scope; the existing "strong machine markers remain authoritative inside examples" decision stands.
- Not in scope: relaxing comment-side terminal-blocker holds (the dispatch-time circuit already decides retries, but trusted comments stay holds here), teaching the reconciler cost-breaker or infrastructure-failure markers (the evidence guard leaves those blocks to their own release paths), and dep-graph refresh budget or starvation.
- A worker BLOCKED release without an observation comment (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` alone) is not a reconciler hold today and stays that way; the dispatch-time backoff and circuit handle repeated blocked releases.

title: t18663: fix(pulse): stop stale-blocked sweep and dep-graph refresh starving repos wit...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18663` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): stop stale-blocked sweep and dep-graph refresh starving repos with real backlogs

## Done when

- [ ] A repo with a clean pass inside the interval is not re-listed, and the remaining due repos share the whole sweep budget.
- [ ] Partial and failed passes never stamp the repo; a partial pass never touches the global sentinel; missing or future-dated stamps keep a repo due.
- [ ] Dep-graph refresh gives each repo with entries `(budget - elapsed) / remaining active repos` seconds (minimum 1), smallest backlog first, so idle repos no longer reduce the share.
- [ ] The new tests fail against the previous implementation and pass with the change; existing stale-sweep, dep-graph, readiness and budget-priority suites pass; ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` are clean.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
  - New `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_stamp <slug>`: `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-complete/<owner>__<repo>`; rejects slugs outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` (same `/` → `__` mapping as `_der_stale_cursor_file`).
  - New `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_fresh <slug> <interval> <now>`: true only for a readable stamp with `0 <= now - mtime < interval`; missing, unreadable or future-dated stamps make the repo due.
  - New `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_mark_complete <slug>`: best-effort `touch`; a write failure only keeps the repo due.
  - `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`: build the due list in rotation order, skip fresh repos, divide the remaining budget by the due count, and stamp a repo only when `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` returns 0. Log `fresh_repos=<n>` in the summary line.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` — `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`: list repos as `<entry_count>\t<slug>` sorted by count then slug; count active repos (entries > 0); for each active repo `share = (budget - elapsed) / active_left`, minimum 1s.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh` — the rotation scenario clears per-repo stamps between sweeps; new cases: a fresh repo is skipped and the due repo gets the whole budget; a partial pass stamps neither the repo nor the sentinel; a clean pass stamps both; a failed pass stays due; a future-dated stamp never suppresses a repo; `fresh_repos` is logged.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh` — new `test_refresh_budget_shared_by_active_repos`: idle repos do not dilute the share (`budget_secs=30` with one active repo among four); a small backlog runs first and the large backlog receives the rolled-forward time and completes.

### Complexity Impact

- `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` 59 → 76 lines; three new helpers of 6–9 lines; `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` 34 → 45 lines. All below the 100-line gate.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` is called once per cycle from `pulse-wrapper.sh` under `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` is called from the in-cycle pipeline after `build_dependency_graph_cache` (`pulse-wrapper.sh`), from `_pulse_run_blocker_refresh_catchup` (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) and from `normalize_repo_dependency_readiness` with a one-repo graph (`pulse-dep-graph.sh`). No other code reads the summary log line (`rg 'partial_repos='`) or `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_BUDGET_SECS`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new GitHub writes. New local state: one empty stamp file per repo under `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-complete/`. Unblock decisions remain `_der_try_unblock` (stale sweep) and `_refresh_try_unblock_issue` (graph refresh), unchanged; `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues`, its cursor, batch limit and deadline contract, `_refresh_graph_repo` and `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_MAX_CANDIDATES` are untouched.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh` (sweep cadence, rotation, fair share, stage wiring) and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh` (bounded traversal, cursor, elapsed budget); runtime evidence is the sweep summary and `dep-graph-cache: refresh` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no schema or config file changes; `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_INTERVAL`, `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_BUDGET_SECS` keep their meaning and defaults.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no backfill is needed: with no stamps after deploy every repo is due on the first sweep, which is the current behaviour; `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-complete/` is created on the first clean pass.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; older code ignores `~/.aidevops/cache/stale-blocked-complete/`, and deleting it only makes every repo due again.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`, add `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_stamp`, `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_fresh` and `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_mark_complete` above `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`.
2. In `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`, build the due list in rotation order (skipping fresh repos), share the remaining budget by the due count, stamp only on return 0, and add `fresh_repos=` to the summary line.
3. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`, sort repos by entry count, count active repos, and recompute each active share from the time left.
4. Extend both existing test scripts with the cases listed above, confirm the new cases fail against the previous implementation, then run the Verification Before Dispatch commands.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the mkdir-based pulse instance lock (`acquire_instance_lock`, `pulse-wrapper.sh`) allows one sweep at a time; stamps are single `touch` calls, and a stamp racing a manual run can only make a repo due early or late by one interval.
- **Migration/rollback:** no ordering requirement; deploy and revert are both safe at any point because a missing stamp means due, and old code never reads stamps.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners ignore stamps and sweep every repo as today; the summary log line only gains a trailing `fresh_repos=` field, which no code parses.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a repo is skipped only after a clean, complete pass inside the configured interval, the cadence the global sentinel already promised; partial and failed passes stay due and retry next cycle as today. `/` → `__` stamp names match the existing stale cursor files, and GitHub owners cannot contain `_`, so names do not collide.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a killed sweep leaves stamps only for repos that finished cleanly and persists the rotation offset before each start, so the next cycle resumes with the remaining due repos; unreadable or future-dated stamps make a repo due; a stamp write failure only keeps the repo due. The dep-graph refresh still checks elapsed time before each new candidate and visits at least one.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-graphql-budget-priority.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** `test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh` proves the per-repo cadence, due-only budget share, partial/failed/future-stamp hazards and stage wiring (acceptance 1–2); `test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh` proves the active-repo share and rollover (acceptance 3) plus the unchanged cursor and elapsed-budget contract; the non-dep-block, readiness-normalization, budget-priority and housekeeping suites cover the other callers of `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`; ShellCheck and `linters-local.sh --changed` cover both edited scripts (acceptance 4).
- **Runtime:** after deployment, sweep summaries report a growing `fresh_repos` count and a shrinking `partial_repos` count over consecutive cycles until the sentinel is touched; dep-graph refresh lines for repos with entries report `budget_secs` above 1.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-blocked-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh`

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `stale blocked sweep fair share starvation dep-graph refresh budget` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found 0 open related PRs for the target files; last relevant changes are 0e83416a58 (t18661 supersession readiness), 035691f2f7 (GH#34331 first-wave capacity), 589016c402 (t18646 blocked-by:GH# labels), e20544d82e (#34056 bounded dep-graph refresh), 74f9d071c8 (GH#33957 resumable stale sweep)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 34247feb1f: `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`, `_pulse_stale_blocked_sweep_deadline` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`); `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`, `_refresh_graph_repo` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`); `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` (`.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, unchanged)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — scheduling-only change in two bounded pulse stages; no unblock decision changes
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while maximising worker throughput for a managed private repo's enrichment backlog: after t18662 the reconciler could release dependency-ready issues, but the two periodic recovery stages reached that repo's backlog at about one issue per cycle.

## What

Both periodic recovery stages spend their time budget on repos that still have work:

1. **Stale-blocked sweep** (`_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due`): each repo records its own completion stamp after a clean, complete pass. A repo whose stamp is younger than `PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_INTERVAL` is not re-listed; the sweep budget is shared only among due repos (partial, failed or never swept). The global sentinel, rotation offset, fair-share deadlines and hard stop keep their current meaning.
2. **Dep-graph refresh** (`refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`): `DEP_GRAPH_REFRESH_BUDGET_SECS` is shared only among repos with dependency entries. They run smallest backlog first, and each share is recomputed from the time actually left, so unused time rolls forward to the largest backlog. Repos without entries keep a 1s share; they do no candidate work.

## Why

Pulse log evidence (2026-10-11):

- **Stale sweep never converges.** The last 8 sweep summaries report `failures=0 partial_repos=31..51 repos=57`. The sweep budget is about 45s (`PULSE_STALE_BLOCKED_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` 60 minus the 15s margin) split across all 57 repos, so the integer share is 0–1s. `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` stops after its first visit once the share deadline passes, so repos with only 2 candidates log `visited=1 ... complete=false`. Because some repo is always partial, the global sentinel is never touched and every cycle re-lists every repo, including repos that already finished. The managed private repo with ~340 blocked candidates advanced one issue per visit.
- **Dep-graph refresh share rounds down to 1s.** The graph cache holds 57 repos, but only 6 have `blocked_by` entries (162 entries, the largest has 152). The 30s budget is divided by all 57 repos (`30 / 57 = 0`, clamped to 1), so recent full-cycle refresh lines all log `budget_secs=1`; the 153-candidate repo logs `visited=1 ... complete=false` on each refresh, as does a 6-candidate repo. Repo-scoped refreshes (`normalize_repo_dependency_readiness`) build a one-repo graph and keep the full budget.

Neither stage changes what is released; both only control how quickly dependency-ready issues are found. Close events (`reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure`) remain the primary release path; these stages recover missed events.

## Context & Decisions

- Per-repo stamps instead of a smaller global sentinel: the global sentinel can only mark a traversal of all repos, which one large backlog prevents indefinitely.
- Failed passes stay due, as today, so transient listing failures retry on the next cycle; once no repo is partial the global sentinel still rests the whole sweep for the interval.
- Smallest-first ordering for the graph refresh is deterministic, and it lets each small backlog finish its batch before the largest one takes the remaining time. Ordering within the stale sweep keeps the persisted rotation.
- Not in scope: raising stage timeouts, batch limits or dispatch capacity; host CPU gate tuning; changing what either stage releases.

**Task ID:** `t18664` | **Status:** open

## Outcome

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `auto-update deployment incomplete runtime bundle rollback agents_stale` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: no open PRs touch `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`; no open or closed issue reports the rollback. The bundle check was added in 48a522d013 (2026-07-11); last helper change 41d9b663f2 (t18626)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main f8bb961c48: `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root`, `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_valid`, `_cmd_check_perform_update` (`.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`); `pin_aidevops_active_runtime_bundle_root` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-runtime.sh`); Pulse pin export (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — one-function fix in update verification; setup, activation and rollback mechanics unchanged
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found while verifying that a released Pulse fix was running: v3.39.8, v3.39.9 and v3.39.10 each deployed, passed setup, then were rolled back by the automatic updater one second after `SETUP_COMPLETE`.

## What

Post-update verification checks the bundle behind the global activation link (`~/.aidevops/agents`), whichever process runs the update. `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root` stops resolving the caller's inherited `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pin, so a Pulse-run update (routine r902) verifies the bundle it just activated instead of the Pulse's own older bundle.

## Why

- `pulse-wrapper.sh` exports `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pinned to its own physical bundle (`pwd -P`). Routine r902 runs `aidevops auto-update check` as a Pulse child, so the pin is inherited; `aidevops.sh` keeps an inherited value.
- `_cmd_check_perform_update` runs setup (which re-binds to the activation link via `pin_aidevops_active_runtime_bundle_root`, and activates the new bundle correctly), then verifies with `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root`, which resolves the stale pin. The old bundle's `VERSION` never matches the new version, so every Pulse-run update logs `Update pulled vX but agents at vX — deployment incomplete` and rolls back to the bundle it just replaced. The launchd-scheduled path has a clean environment and succeeds, which is why some updates stick.
- Runner evidence (`~/.aidevops/logs/auto-update.log`): 84 same-version `deployment incomplete` rollbacks since 2026-07-23 against 30 `Update complete` lines since July; today v3.39.8, v3.39.9 and v3.39.10 all rolled back. Recovery only comes 3–7 minutes later from `_cmd_check_stale_agent_redeploy` (`Deployed agents stale ... re-deploying`).
- Cost per release on every runner: two extra full setup runs, two extra Pulse restarts that discard the in-flight dispatch cycle, and minutes of running the previous release. A manual `aidevops update` started in that window reports "already up to date" because it compares the version before the rollback lands.
- Local reproduction with the real functions in a sandbox HOME (activation link → new bundle): clean env → verification valid; Pulse-style pin → resolves the old bundle → `INVALID(rollback)`; CLI symlink pin → valid.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh` — `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root` resolves `${HOME}/.aidevops/agents` (the activation link) with `pwd -P`, ignoring an inherited `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR`; comment cites the Pulse pin and the matching rule in `pin_aidevops_active_runtime_bundle_root`.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_auto_update_runtime_bundle_root` is called twice, both in `_cmd_check_perform_update`: `prior_bundle_root` (rollback target, now the bundle active before the update instead of the caller's pin) and `active_bundle_root` (verification). Sibling reads in the same flow already use `$HOME/.aidevops/...` (`deployed_version`, `_auto_update_rollback_runtime_bundle` previous link and bundles root).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new writes. Setup, activation, Pulse reconciliation and `runtime-bundle-rollback-helper.sh` are unchanged; a genuinely invalid or missing bundle still rolls back.
- **Existing verification/tests:** no test calls these functions (`rg '_auto_update_runtime_bundle' .agents/scripts/tests` is empty); `test-linux-lifecycle-smoke.sh` sets `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` equal to `$HOME/.aidevops/agents`, so it is unaffected.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because no schema or config changes.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the change only affects future update runs.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR to restore pin-based resolution.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Mixed-version:** the fix runs from the updater's own (old) bundle, so the first update to the release containing it may still roll back on a Pulse-run updater and self-heal through the stale-agent redeploy; updates after that verify correctly.
- **Custom agents directories:** the auto-updater already assumes the default layout (`INSTALL_DIR`, `deployed_version`, rollback links), so ignoring a custom `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` here removes an inconsistency rather than a feature.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-update-health-check.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cmd-update-sha-drift.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the sandbox reproduction (real functions, Pulse-style pin) must report `valid` for all three environments after the change; the existing auto-update suites cover the helper's other subcommands; ShellCheck and the changed-file linters cover the edit.
- **Runtime:** after this release is deployed, the next Pulse-run update logs `Update complete: vX -> vY (agents deployed)` with no `deployment incomplete` or `Rolled back runtime activation` line.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18664-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR` pinned to an older bundle and the activation link on the new bundle, post-update verification checks the new bundle and passes.
- [ ] A missing, unvalidated or version-mismatched active bundle still fails verification and rolls back.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the existing auto-update suites and `linters-local.sh --changed` pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Fix the verifier instead of unsetting the pin in the r902 wrapper: any caller with an inherited pin (Pulse routines, workers, interactive sessions) hits the same false negative, and setup already applies the activation-link rule for global reconciliation.
- Not in scope: rollback-helper behaviour, the stale-agent redeploy debounce, or setup's own pin handling.

title: t18665: fix(pulse): rotate dispatch attempts so repeatedly blocked head candidates st...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18665` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-11
**Tags:** `bug` `framework`

## Outcome

fix(pulse): rotate dispatch attempts so repeatedly blocked head candidates stop starving the never-attempted backlog

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse dispatch candidate ordering starvation repeated blocked head first wave` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open or recently merged PRs on the dispatch candidate files; no open issue covers dispatch starvation or round-robin ordering. Related history: 035691f2f7 (GH#34331 first-wave capacity), 849e2c0af5 (GH#33743 capability cooldown), 65cb9ed1f9 (GH#33647 first wave), d3c07a1b07 (#32580 benign-block skip; its ledger is now reinitialised on every `dispatch_max` run, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:562-570`)
- [x] File refs verified at origin/main 51296462a4: `_dispatch_process_candidate` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:515`; attempt log line 574, launch confirmed 598); `dispatch_max` and its ordering call (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:759`, `:811`); `_dispatch_order_idle_borrowing_candidates` (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:570`); ranking sort (`pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:548`); capability-cooldown per-candidate state (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:972-1120`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — order-only change in one round orchestrator plus a runner-local stamp; every dispatch gate unchanged
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — implemented interactively in the same session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-11
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Enrichment throughput drive on a managed private repo: the runner sat at 0–2 of 20 worker slots for 12 cycles while that repo's available backlog was non-empty.

## What

`dispatch_max` orders each round so candidates attempted within a window without a worker launch go after the candidates of the same priority tier that were not attempted in that window; the recently attempted ones rotate oldest attempt first. A runner-local per-candidate stamp is written at `DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_ATTEMPT` and removed when a worker launch is confirmed.

## Why

- Rounds are bounded by the cycle wall-clock budget: a round stops taking candidates once less than the 600 s per-candidate floor remains. Two recent large rounds covered only a prefix of the ranked list — `processed=26/82` and `processed=28/80`, both `implementation_dispatched=0` and both ending with `Dispatch_max stopping early: cycle wall-clock budget below per-candidate floor` (28 such stops in the current `pulse.log`). Dedup layers alone took up to 144.5 s per attempt for the managed private repo below (p90 30.9 s; `dispatch-stages.tsv`, 9–11 Oct).
- The ranking is deterministic (priority tier, score, `createdAt`), and the benign-block ledger is deliberately cycle-local so stale active claims cannot suppress later cycles. Every round therefore re-attempts the same head candidates.
- Runner evidence (current `pulse.log`; read-only available-issue probe at 11:06Z): the managed private repo's top head candidates were attempted 15–23 times each (`blocked_by_unresolved`, `footprint_overlap`, `dedup_active_claim`, `consolidated`, `terminal_blocker_circuit`). Meanwhile 24 of its 47 `status:available` issues in the enrichment class (20 of them `auto-dispatch`) had never been attempted on this runner. 17 of those 24 are `tier:thinking`, which the score ranks 1200 points below `tier:standard`.
- Last 12 cycles (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`, to 11:02Z): 0–2 of 20 workers active; 9 of the 12 dispatched nothing.
- Order-only rotation lets bounded rounds reach the untried tail without weakening any gate.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` — after `_dispatch_filter_capability_cooled_candidates`, following its per-candidate state pattern:
  - window knob `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_ATTEMPT_RECENCY_SECONDS` (default 86400, `0` disables, capped at 604800);
  - `_dispatch_attempt_recency_path`, `_dispatch_attempt_recency_stamp` (mktemp + mv), `_dispatch_attempt_recency_clear`;
  - `_dispatch_attempt_recency_stamps` (emit in-window stamps; remove expired, future-dated and malformed ones);
  - `_dispatch_order_attempt_recency_candidates`: one jq stable sort by `[-priority_rank, attempted, attempt epoch, original index]`. It fails open and emits one log line plus a stats counter when it demotes anything.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` — `_dispatch_process_candidate`: stamp after `attempt_epoch=$(date +%s)`; clear after `dispatch_worker_spawned`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` — new `_dispatch_order_round_candidates` (recency order when loaded, then `_dispatch_order_idle_borrowing_candidates`); `dispatch_max` calls it in place of the direct idle-borrowing call.

### Complexity Impact

- `_dispatch_process_candidate`: 96 → 98 body lines (+2).
- `dispatch_max`: 99 → 99 (one call replaced).
- New functions each stay under 40 lines.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_dispatch_process_candidate` is the only attempt path for the floor, parallel and priority loops. `dispatch_max` runs every round:
  - via `apply_dispatch_max`: normal passes, event refills, preflight/post-label refills;
  - directly: `_dispatch_min_worker_floor_refill`, `maybe_refill_underfilled_pool_during_active_pulse` and `_run_early_exit_recycle_loop`.
  - The priority phases (`_dispatch_priority_phase_candidates`) and the floor/max loops consume candidates in input order.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** new runner-local soft state `~/.aidevops/cache/dispatch-attempt-recency/<owner>--<repo>--<issue>` (one epoch per file). No GitHub writes, and no label, claim, ledger or reservation changes.
- **Existing verification/tests:** the suites that drive `dispatch_max` or `_dispatch_process_candidate` isolate `HOME`, so they see no stamps and today's order.
- **Schemas/config:** one environment knob; no config file change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/*.sh` into the runtime bundle.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Stamps start empty, so the first round after deploy keeps today's order and stamps what it attempts.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_ATTEMPT_RECENCY_SECONDS=0` disables the rotation; reverting the PR restores today's order; leftover stamps are inert once the code is gone.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Priority:** `priority:critical`/`priority:high` tiers still lead strictly (GH#32703). Only the order inside a tier changes, and score order is kept among candidates not attempted recently.
- **Retry latency:** a recently attempted, still-blocked candidate is retried after its tier's fresher candidates, and at most one window later (default 24 h).
- **Safety:** ordering only. Dedup, claim, footprint, dependency, capability, eligibility and budget gates are unchanged and still run for every attempted candidate.
- **Concurrency:** parallel candidate subshells write distinct files atomically; a prune race can only lose a stamp, which falls back to today's order.
- **Bash 3.2:** no associative arrays or `mapfile`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-idle-debt-borrowing.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** a scratch harness sources the real libraries under a sandbox `HOME` and checks:
  - no stamps → identical order;
  - stamps → fresh first within each tier, oldest attempt first, critical tier still first;
  - expired, future-dated and malformed stamps are removed;
  - window `0` or malformed JSON → unchanged order.
- **Pre-existing failure:** `test-pulse-wrapper-silent-dispatch.sh` fails 4/21 identically on an untouched `git archive` of origin/main 51296462a4. The secret-name gate from #32748 preempts the expected skip lines; tracked by t18666 (GH#34364).
- **Runtime:** after deploy, `pulse.log` shows the rotation line. On a later private-repo wave, the read-only available-issue probe shows previously never-attempted candidates being attempted and some launching.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure change.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t18665-brief.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A candidate attempted without a launch inside the window is ordered after every not-recently-attempted candidate of its priority tier, and recently attempted candidates rotate oldest attempt first.
- [ ] `priority:critical`/`priority:high` candidates still lead lower tiers regardless of stamps. With no stamps, or with the window set to `0`, round order is identical to today's.
- [ ] A confirmed launch removes the stamp. Expired, future-dated and malformed stamps are removed, and any state or jq failure returns the original order.
- [ ] ShellCheck, the listed dispatch suites and `linters-local.sh --changed` pass, apart from the pre-existing silent-dispatch failures noted above, which must match base exactly.

## Context & Decisions

- **Order, don't skip:** a cross-cycle skip ledger was rejected. The benign-block ledger is cycle-local on purpose (active claims clear), and skipping could starve a candidate whose blocker cleared. Demotion keeps every candidate reachable and every gate authoritative.
- **Time window, not `updatedAt`:** Pulse housekeeping updates issues itself, so an `updatedAt` reset could re-promote the same heads every cycle.
- **Applied in `dispatch_max`, after the 120 s ranked snapshot:** stamps written by the previous round's parallel subshells take effect in the next round.
- **Not in scope:** cycle-budget reserve sizing for refill rounds and per-candidate ceremony cost. Each needs its own fresh evidence before a separate task.

</details>
