title: site-crawler: LibreCrawl engine, and docs that match what the helper does
body:
## What

Add LibreCrawl (MIT, self-hosted SEO crawler, <https://github.com/PhialsBasement/LibreCrawl>) as a crawl engine for `site-crawler-helper.sh`, and make `seo/site-crawler.md` describe only what the helper actually does.

- `site-crawler-helper.sh crawl <url> --engine librecrawl` (and `--engine auto|crawl4ai|fallback`; `auto` keeps today's order and tries LibreCrawl first only when it answers at `LIBRECRAWL_URL`). The LibreCrawl engine drives its REST API, waits for the crawl, exports pages, links and issues, and writes the **same output layout** as the other engines (`crawl-data.csv`, `broken-links.csv`, `redirects.csv`, `meta-issues.csv`, `summary.json`, `_latest` symlink) plus the raw exports (`librecrawl-urls.json`, `librecrawl-links.csv`, `librecrawl-issues.csv`) so other tools can import them unchanged.
- Flags that today exist only in the docs map to LibreCrawl settings when `--engine librecrawl`: `--render-js` → `enableJavaScript`, `--user-agent` → `userAgent`, `--ignore-robots` → `respectRobotsTxt=false`, `--include` / `--exclude` → `includePatterns` / `excludePatterns`, `--depth` → `maxDepth`, `--max-urls` → `maxUrls`, `--include-pagespeed` → `enablePageSpeed` (with the PageSpeed key from `aidevops secret`, never on the command line). Other engines reject these flags with a clear message instead of ignoring them.
- `site-crawler-helper.sh status` reports whether LibreCrawl is reachable and in local mode.
- `seo/librecrawl.md`: run it with Docker Compose in local mode bound to `127.0.0.1` (`LOCAL_MODE=true`; the compose file binds `127.0.0.1:5000` by default), never expose local mode on a network (it gives every visitor admin), how to update, and how the helper uses it.

## Why

`seo/site-crawler.md` promises JS rendering, custom user agents, include/exclude patterns, authenticated crawls, PageSpeed, `audit-duplicates` and `audit-schema`, but `site-crawler-helper.sh` (and its `-crawl4ai`, `-fallback`, `-markdown` modules) implements none of those flags or commands: `rg -- "render-js|user-agent|ignore-robots|audit-duplicates|audit-schema|--include|--exclude" .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper*.sh` returns nothing. LibreCrawl already does most of them, is maintained upstream, handles very large crawls (SQLite-backed queue, resume after a crash, memory limits), and exports JSON/CSV. Adding it as an engine is cheaper than building those features, and its exports become a shared input for site tools such as SEO Pro Stats's crawl import (https://github.com/wpallstars/seoprostats/issues/331).

## How

### LibreCrawl API (read from `main` at commit `05a1372de833`; check against the current release)

- Base `${LIBRECRAWL_URL:-http://localhost:5000}`; JSON bodies; session cookie (keep the cookie jar in a `mktemp -d` directory removed on exit).
- Sign in: `POST /api/guest-login`. In local mode guests get the admin tier (JS rendering, no rate limit). Outside local mode a guest is limited to 3 crawls a day and no JS: detect with `GET /api/user/info` (`tier`) and stop with guidance rather than half-working.
- Settings: `POST /api/save_settings` with the camelCase keys (`maxDepth` 1–10, `maxUrls`, `crawlDelay`, `userAgent`, `respectRobotsTxt`, `includePatterns`, `excludePatterns`, `enableJavaScript`, `enablePageSpeed`, `googleApiKey`, `crawlExternalLinks`, `crawlImages`, `concurrency`), then `POST /api/update_crawler_settings`.
- Crawl: `POST /api/start_crawl {"url": ...}` returns `crawl_id`; poll `GET /api/crawl_status` every 2 s until `status` is `completed` (bounded by a `--timeout`, default 60 min; `POST /api/stop_crawl` on timeout or Ctrl-C).
- Export: `POST /api/export_data` with `format: json` and `fields` including `url,status_code,title,meta_description,h1,canonical_url,robots,depth,response_time,size,redirects,word_count,internal_links,external_links,lang,hreflang,json_ld`, plus the special fields `issues_detected` and `links_detailed` (returned as separate files). Links columns: `source_url,target_url,anchor_text,is_internal,target_domain,target_status,placement` (`placement` is navigation, footer, body or image).

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh` — `check_librecrawl`, `crawl_with_librecrawl <url> <output_dir> <max_urls> <depth> [opts]`, export mapping to the shared CSVs; model on `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-crawl4ai.sh` (`check_crawl4ai`, `crawl_with_crawl4ai`, report generation). Use `curl` and `jq` only.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh` — source the new module next to the crawl4ai one (line ~60); `_do_crawl_parse_opts` gains `--engine` and the mapped flags; `do_crawl` (lines 232–261) picks the engine; `check_status` and `show_help` list LibreCrawl.
- `NEW: .agents/seo/librecrawl.md` — subagent doc as above; model on `.agents/seo/screaming-frog.md`.
- `EDIT: .agents/seo/site-crawler.md` — a capability table by engine; remove or mark as not implemented any command or flag no engine provides (`audit-duplicates`, `audit-schema`, `--auth-type` today).
- `EDIT: .agents/seo.md` — `librecrawl` in the subagents list and the Technical line.
- `EDIT: .agents/aidevops/recommendations.md` — LibreCrawl row next to Crawl4AI (free, self-hosted SEO crawler).

### Hazards

- Never start LibreCrawl in local mode on `0.0.0.0`; the helper only connects, it does not launch containers.
- Keep the other engines' behaviour unchanged when `--engine` is not given (`auto` order: Crawl4AI, then fallback, unless LibreCrawl answers).
- Shell rules: `local var="$1"`, explicit `return 0/1`, ShellCheck clean, Bash 3.2 compatible; the main helper is 524 lines, keep new logic in the module.

## Out of scope (separate issues if wanted)

- Pushing a crawl to SEO Pro Stats's crawl import over its REST API (after that import exists).
- Porting LibreCrawl ideas into the fallback crawler (weighted near-duplicate score over title, description, H1 and word count; link placement detection; resumable SQLite queue).

## Verification

```bash
docker compose up -d   # in a LibreCrawl checkout, LOCAL_MODE=true
.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh status
.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl https://example.com --engine librecrawl --max-urls 50 --depth 2
# expect crawl-data.csv, broken-links.csv, redirects.csv, summary.json and the three librecrawl-* files under ~/Downloads/example.com/_latest/
.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl https://example.com --max-urls 20   # unchanged behaviour without --engine
.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl https://example.com --engine fallback --render-js   # clear "needs --engine librecrawl" error
shellcheck .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh`
- `.agents/seo/librecrawl.md`
- `.agents/seo/site-crawler.md`
- `.agents/seo.md`
- `.agents/aidevops/recommendations.md`

title: GH#34615 follow-up: fail closed for the authenticated Playwriter relay on non-POSIX (Windows) platforms
body:
## Problem

Follow-up from GH#34615 / PR #34623 closeout review (P2). On POSIX, the authenticated Playwriter relay launcher runs the relay under a guardian that leads its own process group and stops the whole group (package runner `npx`/`bun x` plus the real `playwriter-serve` listener) on disconnect. On Windows (`process.platform === "win32"`) there are no process groups: the guardian only signals its direct child (the package runner). A relay descendant that outlives its runner can stay listening on `127.0.0.1:19988` after MCP disconnect. This was also the pre-PR behaviour, so it is not a regression, but `playwriter.md` now qualifies the teardown guarantee as macOS/Linux only, and nothing enforces that boundary on Windows.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-guardian.mjs` — `signalRelay()` non-POSIX branch; `spawnGuardian()` (`detached: POSIX_GROUPS`).
- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-lifecycle.mjs` — `POSIX_GROUPS`, `terminateProcessGroup()` (throws on non-POSIX).
- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-reconcile.mjs` — `reconcileOwnedRelays()` returns early on non-POSIX.
- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` — `main()` / `supervise()` entry.
- `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md` — teardown paragraph.
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-guardian.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-lifecycle.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`

## Recommended approach

Fail closed: the authenticated relay mode refuses to start on non-POSIX platforms with a fixed error naming the limitation, so it can never leave a listener running unnoticed. Document this in `playwriter.md`. Only implement Windows process-tree termination (for example, a job object, or `taskkill /T /F /PID <guardian child>` with ownership proof) if a maintainer explicitly asks for Windows support. That needs a Windows runtime to verify.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the POSIX path, the ownership-marker checks, the reviewed `playwriter@0.8.0` pin, loopback binding, or telemetry opt-out.
- Never terminate a process merely because it listens on port 19988.
- Use the existing test file; no new runner.

## Verification

- `node --check` on the four modules.
- `node --test --test-timeout=30000 .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` passes. Add a focused test that the launcher rejects a non-POSIX platform. Inject the platform through an existing seam if one exists; if none does, note that and verify by inspection rather than adding a test-only interface.
- `qlty smells --no-snippets <changed files>` shows no new smells, so the CI Qlty Regression Gate passes.

title: GH#34615 follow-up: exact argv and process-start identity for stale Playwriter relay reconciliation
body:
## Problem

Follow-up from GH#34615 / PR #34623 closeout review (P2 hardening). When a new session starts, `reconcileOwnedRelays()` stops an owned relay left by a dead supervisor. It does so only when four conditions hold: marker-protected state, a dead supervisor PID, a live process group, and a group leader whose `ps` command line contains `playwriter@0.8.0` plus the guardian flag (or `serve --host 127.0.0.1` for legacy v1 state). Two gaps remain:

1. The command check uses substring matching. An unrelated process whose command line merely contains those strings and happens to hold the recorded PID/PGID would match.
2. There is no process-start identity. After PID reuse, the inspect-then-signal sequence cannot prove that the process is the one that was recorded.

The private state, the dead-supervisor check and the PGID match already constrain this heavily. No normal failure path has been observed, so this is hardening, not a bug fix.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-reconcile.mjs` — `inspectProcess()`, `staleRelayGroup()`, `readSessionState()`.
- `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` — `writeState()` (v2 state: `relayGroupId`), `RELAY_CONTRACT`.
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` — follow the `startSyntheticGroup` / `writeSession` pattern in the "reconciles an owned relay" and "never stops a relay without proven stale ownership" tests.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-relay-reconcile.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`

## Recommended approach

- Match exact argv tokens rather than substrings: the guardian leader must be `<node> <launcher path> --aidevops-relay-guardian <reviewed runner command>`. Compare tokens against `RELAY_CONTRACT`, extended with the launcher path where needed.
- Record the guardian's process start time in v2 state when it is written (for example `ps -o lstart= -p <pid>`, normalised). Require an exact match before signalling, and keep v1 legacy handling working.
- On any mismatch, keep the current fail-safe outcome (`undefined`): leave the process and its state alone.

## Constraints

- Never stop a process without proven ownership; never act on a port listener alone.
- Keep the state-schema change backward compatible: v2 state without the new field should be treated as unproven, or handled by the existing rules if a maintainer prefers, but document the choice.
- No new test runner. Keep Qlty smells flat, because the CI Qlty Regression Gate fails on any added smell.

## Verification

- `node --test --test-timeout=30000 .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs` passes, with negative cases for (a) a command that merely contains the package and guardian strings in a non-argv position and (b) a recorded start time that differs from the live process. Both must be left alive with their state preserved.
- `node --check` on the changed modules; CI Qlty Regression Gate green.

- The signed tag object `a1af8e65e381530579d09524808d7dd96bdd5ec2` exists on GitHub (`gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/git/tags/a1af8e65...` returns `tag: v3.39.31`, object `92ff98fab7`), but no ref points to it and it cannot be fetched into another clone.
- The lane executor is a different host (`host_id d50a1498…`, pid 1803146). Its local clone is the only place holding the `v3.39.31` tag ref.
- From another maintainer host, `aidevops release status 34603` and `aidevops release reconcile 34603` both exit 2 with `release-tag-discovery … result=not-found items=0`, because discovery only looks at local tag refs.

## Why it matters

1. Once the protected release PR has merged, nothing completes it automatically. `release.md` says to "run `aidevops release reconcile <source-PR>` once it has merged", but no routine or hook does that, so the lane blocks all publication until someone notices.
2. Only the original host can recover, even though the immutable signed tag object is already on GitHub and is pinned by PR #34609's `aidevops:release-provenance` marker.

## Proposed fix (worker-ready)

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`, tag discovery (around `_full_loop_release_candidate_tags_for_pr` / lines 385-465): when the lane has `phase=remote-publication`, a `tag`, and no local candidate, look for the merged `chore/release-v<semver>-provenance` PR. Read its `aidevops:release-provenance` marker (tag, tag-object, release-commit) and fetch or adopt the tag object from GitHub. A fetchable ref may be needed, e.g. have version-manager push the signed tag object to a staging ref such as `refs/aidevops/release-tags/v<semver>` before opening the protected PR. Then run the existing `_full_loop_release_verify_candidate_tag_provenance` signature, manifest and ancestry checks before pushing `refs/tags/v<semver>`. Fail closed on any mismatch.
- Trigger: have `full-loop-helper.sh merge` (it already special-cases `chore/release-v<semver>-provenance` heads in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`) and/or the pulse run the same-source reconcile once such a PR is observed merged.
- Reference contracts: `.agents/workflows/release.md` (protected-main paragraph), `.agents/reference/release-lane-coordination.md:120-139`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`

## Verification

- Manual: on a host without the local tag, `aidevops release reconcile 34603` pushes `v3.39.31` and reaches a terminal receipt.

## Immediate unblock (operator)

On the original executor host, run `aidevops release reconcile 34603`.

title: fix(dispatch): private-org-member runners blocked by external-author gate (author_association=CONTRIBUTOR skips permission lookup)
body:
## Problem

The pre-dispatch external-author gate (GH#22399) permanently blocks dispatch of issues written by a runner whose organisation membership is **private**. For those users, GitHub REST reports `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR` instead of `MEMBER`, even when they are an org admin with `admin` repository permission. `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` treats every association other than `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` as confirmed untrusted. It returns `untrusted-association:CONTRIBUTOR` **without** checking the per-repository permission endpoint.

Closed #24546 had the same root cause (private org membership shows as CONTRIBUTOR), but that fix only covered the maintainer-gate workflow, not this shell helper.

## Evidence (pulse runner, 2026-10-14, aidevops v3.39.31)

- Issue author is the runner itself. `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/issues/<N> --jq .author_association` returns `CONTRIBUTOR`.
- `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/collaborators/<runner>/permission` returns `{"permission":"admin","role":"admin"}`.
- `gh api orgs/<org>/memberships/<runner>` returns `{"role":"admin","state":"active"}`, and `orgs/<org>/public_members/<runner>` returns HTTP 404 (private membership).
- `pulse.log` has 82 lines like this one, covering 25 distinct `origin:worker` issues in one private managed repo (one issue blocked 13 times):
  `Dispatch blocked for #<N> in <org>/<repo>: author_association=CONTRIBUTOR, author_type=User, external_source=false, authority=untrusted-association:CONTRIBUTOR; applying needs-maintainer-review until cryptographic approval lands (GH#22399)`
- Secondary symptom: after these blocks the `needs-maintainer-review` label is not present on the issues. They stay `status:available`, so every pulse cycle selects them again and spends about 1 minute on the dedup chain before deferring again.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`, function `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` (the `*)` branch near line 100). Route `CONTRIBUTOR` (and possibly `NONE`, which private-membership users can also get) through the same authenticated permission lookup that `COLLABORATOR` already uses. Only `admin|maintain|write` grants trust. `read|triage|none`/404 stays untrusted. Lookup failure stays rc=2 (fail closed, no label mutation).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh:103` currently asserts "contributor is untrusted without spending a permission lookup". Update it so CONTRIBUTOR with write+ permission is trusted, and CONTRIBUTOR with read/none stays untrusted.
- Check the caller `_check_external_issue_author_gate` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh:203` to see why the NMR label add does not persist (it may be a race with write-authorised-author normalisation). Make the gate result and the labels agree.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-commit-gates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`

Scope note (integration recovery): `_lia_author_authority` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` pre-filters associations and only calls `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` for `COLLABORATOR`, so a labelless issue by a private-org admin (`CONTRIBUTOR`/`NONE`) would still be backfilled with `needs-maintainer-review` + `external-contributor`. It must route those associations through the same shared helper.

## Reference pattern

The existing `COLLABORATOR)` branch in the same function: `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup` followed by a case on the permission. Keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` markers and GH#17671 defence-in-depth intact.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-external-author-gate.sh`
- `shellcheck` on modified scripts.
- After deploying, `pulse.log` should show no new `untrusted-association:CONTRIBUTOR` blocks for issues written by an admin/write runner. True outside contributors (permission read/none) must still be blocked.

title: fix: respect Nix ownership when updating managed tools
body:
## Problem

On NixOS, `aidevops update` attempts to upgrade ripgrep using brew/apt-get/dnf/yum and fails with `No supported package manager found (brew/apt-get/dnf/yum)`. Ripgrep is installed and working from the Nix store (15.1.0). The updater should respect installation ownership rather than attempt an unrelated package manager.

## Implementation scope

- Modify `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh`: resolve installed binary symlinks and identify `/nix/store/` ownership before latest-version lookups or automatic update queueing.
- Represent Nix-owned tools as externally managed in console/JSON output, with no executable update command. Explain that users should update through the Nix configuration or profile that owns the tool.
- Never automatically invoke `nixos-rebuild`, Home Manager, or profile upgrades. Do not infer ownership merely from the presence of `nix`.
- Preserve existing update behavior for non-Nix binaries, including on hosts with Nix installed.
- Reference pattern: `check_tool`, `_print_tool_status`, `_output_summary_and_updates`, and existing `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-version-check-*.sh` checks.

## Acceptance and verification

- Nix-owned binaries (direct store paths and profile/system symlinks) receive an explicit externally-managed status, are excluded from automatic updates, and do not cause maintenance failure or false claims that an update was applied.
- Non-Nix tools retain existing classification and update routing.
- Run ShellCheck, bash syntax validation, existing tool-version regression checks, and the real `--category brew --update` and JSON paths on NixOS.

## Execution ownership

Requested by the operator for interactive implementation and assignment to their authenticated GitHub account. The primary interactive session owns implementation; no separate worker is needed while it is active.

title: Playwriter MCP reports disconnected extension while two enabled tabs show green icons
body:
## Description

Playwriter MCP reports that the Chrome extension is disconnected even though the operator confirms that Playwriter is active in two tabs and both extension icons are green. This blocks an explicitly requested read-only homepage review. The operator reports that an aidevops Playwriter MCP fix is already awaited and requests capturing this incident for pickup after a harness update, not another instruction to enable the extension.

## Operator notes

“its fucking active in two tabs both are green icon. its an issue with playwriter mcp that we are waiting on a fix from aidevops. create an issue with my notes and we can pick it up with harness update”

The green-icon state is operator-reported; the agent could not independently inspect browser state. The MCP diagnostic must not be presented as proof that the operator has not enabled the extension.

## Expected Behavior

An explicitly selected Playwriter agent should access consent-enabled tabs through the maintained MCP path. If the browser and MCP disagree about connection state, report the disagreement and investigate the harness/relay path rather than repeatedly directing the operator to activate already-green tabs.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** Explicit Playwriter Task delegation from OpenCode, followed by MCP activation and tab enumeration using `context.pages()`.

**Actual output:** Both the initial attempt and the user-requested retry reported successful MCP server connection followed by:

```text
The Playwriter Chrome extension is not connected.
```

The retry also attempted one bounded connection reset and reported the same diagnostic. These details come from the Playwriter child-agent reports; a raw transport trace was not captured. Do not treat this excerpt as a complete raw tool transcript.

**Expected output:** Accessible consent-enabled browser tabs and a successful read-only inspection.

**Causal status:** unconfirmed investigation. The observed MCP/extension-state mismatch is established by tool reports plus operator notes; the precise harness, relay, profile, version, or lifecycle cause is not established.

**Owning-path proof:** Entry point is explicit Playwriter Task delegation followed by registry-managed MCP activation. The internal relay call chain, installed package/extension versions, and backend state were not captured. No causal code or introducing commit is confirmed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In OpenCode, explicitly request a Playwriter review of a public homepage.
2. Enable Playwriter on the intended Chrome tabs; in this incident the operator confirms two tabs with green extension icons.
3. Activate the maintained Playwriter MCP and enumerate accessible tabs with `context.pages()`.
4. Observe the disconnected-extension diagnostic despite the operator-reported green state.
5. Retry once, including a bounded connection reset; the same diagnostic is returned.

## Workarounds Applied

- Initial attempt: MCP activation/preflight; no accessible browser tab.
- User-requested retry: reconnect and one bounded reset; no improvement.
- The agent twice asked the user to enable the extension, which was already green according to the operator. This did not resolve the issue and should not be repeated as an assumed diagnosis.
- MCP was disconnected after each attempt. No alternative browser engine, site changes, relay replacement, process termination, or auth changes were attempted.

## Environment

- Observed on 2026-10-14.
- aidevops v3.39.31; OpenCode v1.19.0, as provided by the session runtime greeting.
- macOS; explicit legacy Playwriter agent and on-demand MCP path.
- Exact macOS, Chrome, extension, Playwriter package, and installed harness commit versions were not captured.
- No screenshots or live DOM evidence were obtained. Homepage diagnosis remains open; no theme files or remote settings were modified.

## Files and Reference Pattern

Exact edit targets and line numbers are unknown pending investigation. Inspect the maintained Playwriter MCP activation, browser launcher, authenticated relay ownership/lifecycle, and connection-error reporting paths. Use the existing scoped activation/relay checks and fresh-process browser-consent verification pattern from #34549 and #34615. Do not assume either issue establishes this incident's cause.

## Related Work and Deduplication

- Searched Playwriter issues and PRs across all states; no exact open green-tabs/disconnected-MCP report was identified.
- #34549 / #34558: reviewed Playwriter 0.8.0 adoption (merged).
- #34615 / #34623: owned relay disconnect teardown (merged).
- #34630 / #34635: stale relay process identity reconciliation (merged).
- These are relevant harness-update context, not proof that the current incident is fixed. The observing session's installed commit and restart state were not verified against those merges.

## Resume After Harness Update

**Manual hold requested by operator:** Capture now and pick up after the aidevops harness update. Do not auto-dispatch, update the installation, reset browser consent, or change local configuration as part of filing this report.

1. After the operator's harness update and fresh session, record the loaded harness and Playwriter/extension versions without exposing credentials or unrelated tab information.
2. With one explicitly approved tab showing green, verify actual MCP enumeration and read-only page access through the maintained path.
3. If still failing, capture bounded activation/relay connection evidence, process ownership/profile/version state, and the exact tool diagnostic. Keep causal attribution unconfirmed until traced.
4. Verify that connection errors distinguish unavailable transport from unenabled tabs; green UI state plus MCP failure must be described as a mismatch, not user setup failure.
5. Resume the original homepage image-over-button review only after browser access works. Successful MCP registration alone is not acceptance evidence.

## Dispatch Hold

Operator explicitly requests capture now and pickup after the aidevops harness update; no automatic implementation or local configuration changes

title: Playwriter: run the guarded relay by default with an ephemeral per-session token (no launch flag)
body:
## Problem

The guarded Playwriter relay from GH#34615 (guardian process-group teardown on MCP disconnect) only runs when OpenCode starts with `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRITER_AUTHENTICATED_RELAY=1` and with `PLAYWRITER_TOKEN` injected through `aidevops secret PLAYWRITER_TOKEN -- opencode`. Users who start OpenCode normally get the plain `bun x playwriter@0.8.0` command. Upstream then starts its own relay detached from the session (ppid 1, own process group) on `127.0.0.1:19988`, and that relay outlives disconnect. Playwriter is used occasionally by some users. Asking them to change how they start OpenCode is not an acceptable price for correct teardown. It should work like every other on-demand MCP.

Evidence (macOS, 2026-10-14): with the plain command, the relay was still listening after disconnect. When the plugin-resolved guarded command was spawned directly, stdin close and SIGTERM both left no listener, no process and no runtime directory (see #34615 comment).

## Reproducer

1. Start OpenCode normally, without `AIDEVOPS_PLAYWRITER_AUTHENTICATED_RELAY` set, with the framework-generated `mcp.playwriter` entry `bun x playwriter@0.8.0`.
2. Select `@playwriter`: it connects the MCP and runs one `execute` call, then disconnects.
3. `lsof -nP -iTCP:19988 -sTCP:LISTEN` still shows the upstream relay (`playwriter-ws-server`/`playwriter-serve`, ppid 1).

Expected: no listener after disconnect, as with the guarded launcher. Causal status: confirmed. The plugin wraps the command only when the flag is set (`authenticatedPlaywriterRelayEnabled()` in `mcp-registry.mjs`), and the launcher rejects runs without the flag (`main()` in `playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`).

## Key finding

The token does not need to come from the operator. In `playwriter@0.8.0`, `cdp-relay.js` checks the token only on the MCP/CDP client routes (`/cdp`, `/cli/*`, `/recording/*`). The extension's `/extension` WebSocket is gated by loopback address plus a known `chrome-extension://` origin and never reads the token. The launcher starts both the relay and the MCP child, so it can mint a random per-session token in memory and pass it to both through the environment only.

## Change

- Plugin (`mcp-registry.mjs`): wrap framework-generated Playwriter commands with the guarded launcher by default on POSIX platforms; no environment flag. Windows keeps the existing confined plain command (no process groups; see #34629 / PR #34632). Custom user commands remain untouched.
- Launcher: drop the opt-in flag requirement. Use `PLAYWRITER_TOKEN` when the operator injected one of at least 32 characters; otherwise mint an ephemeral token with `crypto.randomBytes`. Never write it to config, argv, state, logs or the marker. A conflicting relay on the port still fails closed with an actionable message.
- Docs: `playwriter.md` describes default behaviour, the optional persistent token, and the single-relay limitation.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/browser/playwriter.md`

## Verification

- `node --test --test-timeout=30000 .agents/scripts/tests/test-playwriter-authenticated-relay.mjs`
- `node --test --test-timeout=60000 --test-reporter=dot .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-mcp-activation.mjs`
- macOS host lifecycle with no flag and no `PLAYWRITER_TOKEN`: MCP initialize, then stdin close and SIGTERM leave no `19988` listener, process or runtime session directory.
- No token value in process arguments or runtime files.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: t18691: site-crawler: verify LibreCrawl --user-agent, --include/--exclude, --timeout and Ctrl-C against a live server
body:
## Task


Verify the LibreCrawl engine paths that PR #34637 shipped but did not exercise, and fix any defect found:

1. `--user-agent UA` reaches the crawled site as the request `User-Agent`.
2. `--include` / `--exclude` regexes limit which URLs LibreCrawl crawls.
3. `--timeout MIN` stops a long crawl through `POST /api/stop_crawl`, exports partial results, writes `"complete": false` in `summary.json` and exits non-zero.
4. Ctrl-C (SIGINT) during a crawl stops the LibreCrawl crawl, removes the private temp directory and exits 130.

Follow-up from #34628 / PR #34637 (merged as `578f1f04bd`). That PR verified status, engine selection, the output layout, broken links, redirects, meta issues and PageSpeed export against a live LibreCrawl server. It did not observe the four behaviours above.

## Done when

- [ ] The fixture server log shows the `--user-agent` value on crawler requests, or the docs are corrected to state exactly when it applies.
- [ ] `--include /blog/` produces `crawl-data.csv` rows only for the start URL and `/blog/` URLs; `--exclude /shop/` produces no `/shop/` rows. If upstream matching differs from "Python regex matched anywhere in the URL", `seo/librecrawl.md` says what it actually does.
- [ ] `--timeout 1` on a crawl longer than one minute exits non-zero, writes `summary.json` with `"complete": false`, and leaves the CSVs with the rows crawled so far; LibreCrawl's crawl is no longer running.
- [ ] Ctrl-C exits 130, LibreCrawl's crawl is no longer running, and no `librecrawl-*` temp directory remains.
- [ ] Regression: a normal crawl still completes with `"complete": true`; `--engine fallback --user-agent x` is still rejected; `shellcheck -x` and `linters-local.sh --changed` pass.
- [ ] The PR body lists the observed evidence for each criterion (command, exit code, relevant log or file lines).

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Setup (local only, never on a network interface)

- Run LibreCrawl in local mode from an upstream checkout (`https://github.com/PhialsBasement/LibreCrawl`): `LOCAL_MODE=true EXTERNAL_PORT=5055 docker compose up -d --build`, then `export LIBRECRAWL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5055` and `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh status` (expect "local mode"). Leave `HOST_BINDING` unset so it stays on `127.0.0.1`.
- Serve a fixture site from a temp directory under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}`. The crawler runs inside the container, so crawl `http://host.docker.internal:<port>/`; on Linux add `extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` or use the bridge IP. Use relative links: absolute `127.0.0.1` links are unreachable from inside the container and show up as external with status 0.
- `--user-agent`: Python's `http.server` does not log headers. Use a small `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` subclass that logs `self.headers['User-Agent']`, or any local server with UA logging.
- `--include` / `--exclude`: the fixture needs at least two sections (for example `/blog/…` and `/shop/…`).
- `--timeout 1`: the crawl must last longer than 1 minute. Use a few hundred generated pages, or a handler that sleeps per request.
- Ctrl-C: run the crawl in a foreground terminal, or send `SIGINT` to the helper PID, while `crawl_status` reports `running`.

### Code to read

- `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh`
  - `_librecrawl_apply_settings`: sends `userAgent`/`jsUserAgent` and `includePatterns`/`excludePatterns` (comma list split into lines).
  - `_librecrawl_wait`: timeout calls `_librecrawl_stop` and sets `_LIBRECRAWL_FINAL_STATUS=timeout`.
  - `_librecrawl_run`: on timeout it still exports, then returns non-zero.
  - `crawl_with_librecrawl`: sets `trap '_librecrawl_on_interrupt' INT TERM`.
  - `_librecrawl_on_interrupt`: stops the crawl, cleans up, `exit 130`.
  - `_librecrawl_write_reports`: writes `summary.json` and its `complete` field.
- `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh`: `_do_crawl_parse_opts` collects the flags; `do_crawl` reports failure when the crawl is incomplete.
- Upstream settings handling (`main` at `05a1372de833`, the commit the helper was written against): confirm how `includePatterns` and `excludePatterns` are matched, and whether `userAgent` applies when JS rendering is off.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh`: only if a behaviour is wrong
- `EDIT: .agents/seo/librecrawl.md`: correct any claim the tests disprove (flag mapping table, timeout/Ctrl-C wording)
- `EDIT: .agents/seo/site-crawler.md`: only if the capability table changes

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh`
- `.agents/seo/librecrawl.md`
- `.agents/seo/site-crawler.md`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `rg -n "site-crawler-helper" .agents` finds `site-crawler-helper.sh` (sources the module); the docs `seo/site-crawler.md`, `seo/librecrawl.md` and `seo.md`; and `eeat-score-helper.sh`, which reads `crawl-data.csv` (columns unchanged by this task).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the helper writes only under `--output` (default `~/Downloads/{domain}/`) and its own `mktemp -d` directory. Remote mutation is limited to the LibreCrawl guest session (settings, start/stop crawl).
- **Existing verification/tests:** no existing tests map to these files (`linters-local.sh --changed` on PR #34637 reported "Targeted tests: no mapped changed files"). Verification is the normal CLI path against a live LibreCrawl plus its output files. The fixture site is a temp artifact; do not commit it unless the maintainer asks for a test.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A because the helper has no config file (`rg -n "CONFIG_FILE" .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper*.sh` shows only an unused `site-crawler.json` constant); LibreCrawl settings are sent per session from `_librecrawl_apply_settings`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `subagent-index.toon` already lists `librecrawl` (no regeneration needed unless a doc is added or removed). Deployed copies under `~/.aidevops/agents/` refresh through `setup.sh` after merge.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the output layout written by `_librecrawl_write_reports` stays the same; earlier crawl folders are never rewritten.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** runtime cleanup is `_librecrawl_cleanup` (removes the `mktemp -d` directory) and `_librecrawl_stop` (`POST /api/stop_crawl`). After testing, stop the fixture server and the LibreCrawl container. Code and doc changes revert with the PR.

### Implementation Steps

1. Start LibreCrawl in local mode and the fixture server (see Setup), then confirm `site-crawler-helper.sh status` reports local mode.
2. Run each command in "Verification Before Dispatch" and record the exit code, the relevant fixture log lines and the `crawl-data.csv` / `summary.json` lines.
3. For each failing criterion, find the cause in the functions listed under "Code to read" or in upstream LibreCrawl's settings handling. Fix the helper when the helper is wrong; when upstream behaves differently from the docs, correct `seo/librecrawl.md` (and `seo/site-crawler.md` if the capability table changes).
4. Re-run the failing command and the regression commands; run `shellcheck -x` and `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.
5. Open the PR with the evidence for every acceptance criterion. If all four behaviours already work, the PR may be docs-only (for example, replacing the "Not observed" caveat) or the issue can be closed with the evidence as a comment.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** one crawl per LibreCrawl session. Do not run two helper crawls against the same server at once while testing, because LibreCrawl's crawl status is per session and the tests read it. Security: never start LibreCrawl with `LOCAL_MODE=true` on `0.0.0.0` or a LAN IP; local mode gives every visitor admin.
- **Migration/rollback:** no data migration. Reverting the PR restores the previous helper and docs; output folders already written stay valid.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** keep the CSV columns, file names, `summary.json` keys, the `auto` engine order and the rejection of LibreCrawl-only flags on other engines unchanged, so `eeat-score-helper.sh` and `generate-sitemap` keep reading the same files.
- **Idempotency/retry:** `_librecrawl_stop` is guarded by `_LIBRECRAWL_CRAWL_ACTIVE` and safe to call twice (timeout path, then the final stop in `crawl_with_librecrawl`). Re-running a crawl creates a new timestamped folder and moves `_latest`.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a timeout must still leave usable partial CSV/JSON and `"complete": false`; a Ctrl-C must not leave the remote crawl running or the `librecrawl-*` temp directory behind. Shell rules: `local var="$1"`, explicit returns, ShellCheck clean, Bash 3.2, no new repeated string literals (`linters-local.sh` string-literal ratchet).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
# helper + module
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
# runtime (LibreCrawl local mode on 127.0.0.1:5055, fixture on host port P)
LIBRECRAWL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5055 .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl http://host.docker.internal:P/ --user-agent "aidevops-ua-check/1.0" --max-urls 10   # fixture log shows that UA
LIBRECRAWL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5055 .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl http://host.docker.internal:P/ --include /blog/ --max-urls 50   # crawl-data.csv: start URL + /blog/ only
LIBRECRAWL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5055 .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl http://host.docker.internal:P/ --exclude /shop/ --max-urls 50   # no /shop/ rows
LIBRECRAWL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5055 .agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper.sh crawl http://host.docker.internal:P/ --timeout 1 --max-urls 1000   # exit != 0, summary.json "complete": false, partial CSVs
# Ctrl-C during a long crawl: exit 130; afterwards LibreCrawl crawl_status is not "running"; no librecrawl-XXXXXX dir left in $TMPDIR
```

- **Surface mapping:** `shellcheck` and `linters-local.sh --changed` cover any edit to `site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh` (shell rules, string-literal ratchet, complexity gates) and markdownlint on the two docs. The `--user-agent` run proves the `userAgent`/`jsUserAgent` settings in `_librecrawl_apply_settings` (criterion 1). The `--include`/`--exclude` runs prove `includePatterns`/`excludePatterns` and the doc's matching claim (criterion 2). The `--timeout 1` run proves `_librecrawl_wait` → `_librecrawl_stop` → export → `summary.json` `complete` (criterion 3, partial-failure hazard). The Ctrl-C run proves `_librecrawl_on_interrupt` and temp cleanup (criterion 4, partial-failure hazard). A normal crawl plus `--engine fallback --user-agent x` proves the regression criterion (backward compatibility).
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required; the change is confined to one engine module and two docs with no shared contracts.

</details>

title: docs: guidance for app-proxied object storage (bounded SDK client, abort forwarding, edge-cache split)
body:
## What

Add short guidance for app-proxied object storage (S3/R2/B2 streamed through a Node route) to `.agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md`, with a pointer from `.agents/services/hosting/backblaze-b2.md` if it fits. The framework currently has nothing on bounding storage SDK clients or diagnosing a wedged socket pool. A search for `requestTimeout|maxSockets|socket pool` under `tools/runtime`, `reference` and `services/hosting` found nothing relevant.

## Why (observed evidence, managed project)

- Every stored-image request stalled for 211–340 s before headers, while every other API route on the same Node process answered in 3–50 ms.
- A fresh S3 client created inside the same container reached the bucket in 180–850 ms. That points to the long-lived shared client's keep-alive pool, not the network or the bucket.
- A container restart cleared it, but only temporarily.
- Root cause: AWS SDK v3 `NodeHttpHandler` has no connection, request or socket timeout by default, so stalled or leaked sockets queue all later requests. The route also did not forward the client's abort signal, so abandoned image loads could keep their sockets.
- Fix that worked: bounded `requestHandler` options (connect 5 s, time-to-headers 20 s with `throwOnRequestTimeout`, socket idle 30 s, a larger `maxSockets`). Forward `request.signal` as `abortSignal` to `GetObjectCommand`. Return 504 on `TimeoutError`.
- Second win: public catalogue objects were served `private`, so Cloudflare returned `BYPASS`. Making them `public` with `s-maxage`, while tenant objects, expiring tokens and range responses stay `private`, gave `cf-cache-status: HIT` (0.60 s down to 0.13 s). Resized variants (`?w=`) cut a hero image from 62 KB to 29 KB.

## How

1. `.agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md`: add a compact "Proxied object storage" subsection covering the diagnosis signature above, the three client bounds, abort-signal forwarding, and a 504-on-timeout rule. Keep it vendor-neutral, naming AWS SDK v3 / `@smithy/node-http-handler` as the common case.
2. Add one line on cache split: shared-cache `public, s-maxage` only for non-tenant, non-expiring, whole-object responses; everything else `private`. Avoid `immutable` when objects can be deleted.
3. Do not include project names, hostnames or private paths.

## Verification

- `rg -n "throwOnRequestTimeout|abortSignal" .agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md` finds the new guidance.
- Markdown lint passes for the edited file.

title: prework-discovery: surface open claimed issues for out-of-scope blockers before investigating
body:
## What

When an interactive session runs into a blocker outside its own task (for example a broken shared deploy pipeline), it should check for an open issue already claimed by another session before investigating. Today `prework-discovery-helper.sh` reports only recent commits and open PRs that touch the target files. A blocker in a different area (deploy and migrations, while the task touches storage and UI files) is invisible to it.

## Why (observed evidence)

- Session A (image-serving task) found that develop deploys had been failing for hours. It spent about 30 minutes on read-only investigation: candidate-container watchers, image diffs, and an isolated `docker run` of the candidate image.
- Session B had claimed a tracking issue for exactly that failure (`status:claimed`, self-assigned) about 10 minutes before Session A's investigation began. Session B posted the root cause shortly after.
- Session A found the claim only when it searched issues by hand (`gh search issues "develop deploy"`). The work was duplicated, and both sessions polled the same remote host.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/prework-discovery-helper.sh`: add an "Open claimed issues" section. It lists open issues labelled `status:claimed` or `origin:interactive` whose titles match the given keywords, or match `deploy|migration|CI` when a `--blocker` flag is passed.
2. `.agents/reference/agent-routing.md` or `workflows/full-loop.md`: one line telling the session, before investigating a non-task blocker, to run the helper with `--blocker "<symptom keywords>"`. If a claimed issue exists, add evidence there and continue the session's own task instead of re-investigating.
3. Keep output bounded, for example 5 results.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/prework-discovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-prework-discovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

title: release: co-maintainer-signed snapshot tag with unregistered SSH key strands the release lane (v3.39.31)
body:
## What

The v3.39.31 release lane (source PR #34603) cannot publish from any route on a host other than the signer's. It has blocked every aidevops release since 2026-10-14T07:30Z.

The signed tag object `a1af8e65e381530579d09524808d7dd96bdd5ec2` was SSH-signed by co-maintainer alex-solovyev (key `SHA256:AB+kyU36wH/XdzUxoNrJggNHneHy1Ko2J5R1bADyCNc`). That key is:

1. **Not registered as a GitHub SSH signing key.** `gh api users/alex-solovyev/ssh_signing_keys` returns `[]`, and `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/git/tags/a1af8e65…` returns `verification: {verified: false, reason: "unknown_key"}`. `_release_provenance_verify_github_tag` (`.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:484-521`) requires `.verification.verified == true`, so the publish workflow and any later release using v3.39.31 as baseline would fail. `aidevops release sources` already fails with `cannot read GitHub tag ref v3.39.31`.
2. **Not in other maintainers' `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.** `git verify-tag v3.39.31` prints `Good "git" signature … No principal matched.` and exits non-zero. `_version_manager_is_signed_snapshot` (`.agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh:533-546`) therefore returns false, so `_version_manager_publish_reachable_tag` (line 596) treats a fully snapshot-bound tag as legacy. It reports `aggregation-required` with the misleading hint "Create a newly reviewed exact-tip aggregation release".
3. That hint then leads into exact-tip aggregation. Since GH#31472 removed the merge fence, aggregation loses the race against ordinary merges. Three successive aggregates (#34653, #34658, #34662) were all superseded during their ~10-14 min CI runs. `recover-aggregate` would also fail, because it requires a locally verifiable signed tag.

## Proposed fix (worker-ready)

- **Preflight before tagging.** In `.agents/scripts/version-manager.sh` (signing step) or `full-loop-release-helper.sh` (before the lane leaves `reserved`/`preparing`), verify that the configured signing key is registered as a GitHub signing key for the authenticated user (`gh api user/ssh_signing_keys` or `user/gpg_keys`). Fail closed with a precise remediation message before any tag, protected PR or lane phase change.
- **Snapshot detection must not depend on personal trust files.** In `_version_manager_is_signed_snapshot`, use the same authority as publication (GitHub tag verification for the exact tag object, already staged by #34636). Alternatively, report a distinct `signer-untrusted` result rather than `aggregation-required`, naming the signer and key fingerprint.
- **Accurate hints.** `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` / `version-manager-protected-main.sh:597-599` should not recommend aggregation when the tag is snapshot-bound but its signature is unverifiable.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/release-lane-coordination.md` "Snapshot contract" point 6 (snapshot tags may publish after main drifts).

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-main-fallback.sh` with a snapshot tag signed by a key absent from `allowed_signers`. Expect `signer-untrusted`, not `aggregation-required`.
- Add a preflight test showing that an unregistered signing key stops before tag creation and before any lane mutation.

## Immediate unblock (operator, out of band)

alex-solovyev adds the signing key above to his GitHub account as an **SSH signing key**. Confirm `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/git/tags/a1af8e65e381530579d09524808d7dd96bdd5ec2 --jq .verification.verified` returns `true`. Then run `aidevops release reconcile 34603` from a host whose `allowed_signers` trusts that key, such as his own.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: docs: hostinger.md shared image library: find the ImageMagick package, policy and Ghostscript build date without rpm/ldd; GD trade-offs
body:
## What

Extend the **Shared image library** bullet in `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` → **Read-only audit notes** (line 96 on `main`) with four checks and one trade-off. They came from answering a second Hostinger support request about ImageMagick and Ghostscript over SSH on shared hosting (2026-10-14). The guide covers the first request (#34649, PR #34654).

## Why

Support then said the libraries are server-managed. They will check the package patch status with their server team, and they offered GD as a stopgap. To answer usefully you need to know which ImageMagick package Imagick loads, whether its security policy restricts anything, roughly how old the Ghostscript build is, and what WordPress loses on GD. Today's guide says none of this. Without `rpm`, `ldd` or `/etc/os-release` in the jailed shell, the commands below are the read-only way to find out.

## How

Add to the **Shared image library** bullet (keep the "observed, recheck per account" framing):

1. **Which ImageMagick:** `/opt/alt/php85/usr/bin/php -r 'print_r(Imagick::getConfigureOptions("CONFIGURE_PATH"));'` gives its configuration folder (observed `/opt/alt/alt-ImageMagick/etc/ImageMagick-7/`, the `alt-ImageMagick` package). Older `imagick` builds lack `getConfigureOptions()`.
2. **Security policy:** read `policy.xml` in that folder. Observed: no active rules, only `<policy domain="Undefined" rights="none"/>` (ImageMagick's open policy). So PDF, PS, EPS, XPS, MVG and MSL are all enabled, and PDFs go to Ghostscript. Ask the host whether a restrictive policy can cover the time before an update.
3. **Package build dates without `rpm`:** `ls -l --time-style=+%Y-%m-%d /usr/bin/gs /usr/lib64/libgs.so*`. rpm keeps each file's build-time date, so this shows roughly when the package was built (observed 2026-10-06 for Ghostscript 9.27). A recent date suggests a rebuild with backported fixes; the host must confirm the release.
4. **Libraries without `ldd`:** in PHP, read `/proc/self/maps` and keep paths that match `libgd|libavif|libwebp|libMagick`. Observed GD libraries were under `/opt/alt/libgd` and `/opt/alt/libwebp`.
5. **GD trade-off:** with `imagick` disabled, WordPress (7.1 observed) still makes JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and AVIF sizes on GD 2.3.3. It stops making PDF thumbnails and converting HEIC uploads, and GD drops embedded colour profiles.

Also note in **Missing commands** that `/etc/os-release` is not readable in the jailed shell.

No host names, account names or site domains.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- The five points are in the **Shared image library** bullet, or a sub-list under it, and the `/etc/os-release` note is in **Missing commands**. Both follow the guide's existing style and contain no host or account identifiers.
- The commands can be copied and are read-only.
- The repository's Markdown checks pass for the file.

## Verification

- Read the rendered section, and confirm each command is read-only and contains no private identifiers.

title: release: recover-aggregate resolves the unpublished tag as snapshot base and requires aggregate mode (protected main)
body:
## What

`aidevops release recover-aggregate` cannot recover an unpublished protected-main release, so the documented recovery for a stranded v3.39.31 lane (source #34603) is unusable.

Observed on 2026-10-14 after reviewed exact-tip aggregation #34673 merged as `0831b87c93a39f6b86454e7b31cc2f3d1eb791da` (still the `origin/main` tip when recovery ran):

```text
aidevops release recover-aggregate 34603 --tag v3.39.31 --expected-sources <33 PRs from the #34673 trailers>
release-provenance: GitHub tag ref v3.39.31 in marcusquinn/aidevops: GitHub read failed (exit 1, attempt 1; not retryable)
release-provenance: cannot read GitHub tag ref v3.39.31
```

Recovery made no changes: the lane stayed in `remote-publication` with no receipt, and the remote tag stayed absent.

## Root cause

1. **The base tag resolves to the unpublished tag itself.** `_full_loop_recovery_prepare_aggregate` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh:664-680`) calls `_full_loop_resolve_requested_release_source` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:200-238`). That always runs `resolve-source --snapshot`. With no `AIDEVOPS_RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_*` env pinned, `_release_provenance_resolve_snapshot` (`.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:238-279`) runs `git describe --tags --abbrev=0 <aggregate>`. On protected main, the signed release commit has already merged (here via #34609), so that returns the unpublished local `v3.39.31`. `_release_provenance_verify_github_tag` then fails because the tag is not on GitHub. Confirmed: `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --abbrev=0 0831b87c` returns `v3.39.31`.
2. **The mode contract doesn't match (found by reading the code).** Even with a correct base, `_release_provenance_resolve_snapshot` returns `mode:"snapshot"` (line 276), but `_full_loop_recovery_prepare_aggregate` line 677 requires `mode == "aggregate"`. So recovery fails closed either way.

## Proposed fix (worker-ready)

- In aggregate recovery, resolve sources from the lane's pinned `snapshot_base` / `snapshot_base_tag` / `snapshot_base_object` (or the existing tag's `_RELEASE_PROVENANCE_SNAPSHOT_BASE` trailer), never via `git describe`. Alternatively, have `describe` exclude tags absent from the remote and the active lane's own tag.
- Align line 677 with the snapshot resolver: either accept `snapshot` mode whose `source_merge` is the reviewed aggregate tip, or resolve via the non-snapshot aggregate path. Keep the existing exact-tip, trailer-manifest and authorization-subset checks.
- Reference: `.agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md` "Preconditions" and "Transaction"; `.agents/workflows/release.md:176-205`. Related: #31971 (repin recovered snapshot), #34664 / #34665 (signer trust).

## Verification

- Extend the existing aggregate-recovery test (`rg -l "recover-aggregate" .agents/scripts/tests/`) with a protected-main fixture: unpublished signed tag whose commit is an ancestor of the aggregate tip. Expect the base to resolve to the previous published tag and recovery to reach `aggregate-publication-committing`.
- Run ShellCheck on the changed scripts.

## Current state for the operator

v3.39.31 remains unpublished and blocks releases. Merged aggregation #34673 is a metadata-only empty commit and is harmless. With this fixed, the next recovery still needs a fresh exact-tip aggregate. Signer registration (#34664) is the alternative unblock.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: site-crawler: LibreCrawl account sign-in for shared servers and push crawls into SEO Pro Stats
body:
## Why

`site-crawler-helper.sh --engine librecrawl` (GH#34628) crawls through a LibreCrawl server and writes the shared report layout plus LibreCrawl's raw exports. Two gaps stop it feeding the SEO Pro Stats WordPress plugin, which now imports crawls (`wpallstars/seoprostats` 1.11.0, its issue #331) and is getting a scheduled server connection (its issue #337):

1. **Guest sign-in only.** `_librecrawl_login()` (`.agents/scripts/site-crawler-helper-librecrawl.sh:143`) calls `POST /api/guest-login`. A shared LibreCrawl server (the new Cloudron package, `marcusquinn/cloudron-librecrawl-app` issue #1) runs with guest and registration off, so the helper cannot use it. Guest tier is also limited to 3 crawls a day without JavaScript rendering.
2. **No push.** GH#34628 left "push results into SEO Pro Stats" out of scope. A LibreCrawl on this computer is not reachable from hosted WordPress sites, so for local crawls the only route into the plugin is aidevops uploading the result.

## What

1. **Account sign-in**: when `LIBRECRAWL_USERNAME` is set (environment or `aidevops secret` `LIBRECRAWL_USERNAME` / `LIBRECRAWL_PASSWORD`), `_librecrawl_login()` calls `POST /api/login` with `{"username","password"}` (JSON body from `jq -n`, password never in argv or logs) and keeps the session cookie in the existing private cookie jar; otherwise it keeps today's guest path. A 401 answer names the sign-in as the cause. `check_librecrawl` reports the tier; warn when it is `guest` against a non-local server.

title: canonical Git guard: allow clone to a destination outside the canonical checkout (documented gh repo clone is blocked from any canonical cwd)
body:
## Why

The canonical Git guard classifies a command by its effective working directory (`classify_git_argv`, `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py:243`). `git clone` (including the one `gh repo clone` runs) is therefore blocked whenever the shell sits in any canonical checkout, even when the clone writes only to a new folder elsewhere:

```text
$ gh repo clone <owner>/<new-repo> <workspace>/<new-repo>   # cwd: another canonical repo
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git clone'.
```

The documented way to get a new canonical repository is exactly that command (`.agents/reference/repo-organization.md:20`), and interactive sessions start in a canonical checkout, so the documented step fails by default. This is the third time it has been met: GH#32791 (keywords hub: fixed by cloning with `cwd=path.parent` in `keywords_hub.py`) and GH#33767 (`wp-plugin-new-helper.sh`: same workaround). Each fix patched one caller; the next caller hits it again. Running the same clone from the parent folder works, which shows the block protects nothing here.

## Reproducer

Observed 2026-10-14 on aidevops 3.39.31 (OpenCode), creating a new public repository:

1. Start an interactive session whose working directory is any canonical checkout.
2. `gh repo create <owner>/<new-repo> --public --add-readme`
3. `gh repo clone <owner>/<new-repo> <workspace>/<new-repo>` → `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git clone'` (exit 42); nothing is written.
4. The same command with the shell's working directory set to `<workspace>` (not a repository) succeeds, and `aidevops repos add --slug <owner>/<new-repo> --confirm REGISTER_CANONICAL_REPOSITORY` then registers it.

Expected: step 3 succeeds, as the destination is outside the canonical checkout.

## What

1. **Policy**: in `classify_git_argv`, classify `clone` by its destination, not the working directory: allow it when the destination is given and resolves (from the effective cwd and any `-C`) to a path outside every canonical worktree root, that is absent or an empty directory. A clone without a destination (lands in `cwd/<name>`), or into a path inside the canonical worktree, stays blocked. Keep the existing `--separate-git-dir`/template options blocked if they point inside a canonical `.git`.
2. **Message**: when a clone is still blocked, say why and what to do: "clone into a path outside this checkout (the workspace layout in `reference/repo-organization.md`), or run it from that path's parent".
3. **Docs**: `.agents/reference/repo-organization.md` notes that cloning a new repository from inside a canonical checkout is allowed when the destination is outside it.
4. Leave GH#32791's and GH#33767's caller-side `cwd=parent` in place (harmless).

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py` — a `_is_clone_outside_canonical()` check called from `classify_git_argv` before the generic block (around line 277).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/canonical_git_invocation.py` — if needed, a helper to read the clone destination from argv (skip options and their values; the destination is the second positional).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` — cases: clone to an outside path from a canonical cwd (allowed); clone without destination (blocked); clone into a subfolder of the canonical checkout (blocked); clone into a non-empty existing folder (blocked).
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/repo-organization.md`.

Reference: `_is_isolated_routines_publisher()` and `_is_linked_worktree_remove_for_canonical()` in the same file (narrow, argv-checked allowances).

## Check

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` passes with the new cases.
- From a canonical checkout: `gh repo clone <any public repo> <new path outside it>` succeeds; `git clone <url>` (no destination) is still blocked.
- ShellCheck and the Python linters configured for `.agents/scripts` pass.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_policy.py`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_git_invocation.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh`
- `.agents/reference/repo-organization.md`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical_shell_parser.py`

### Integration scope recovery

The assigned worker preserves draft PR #34678. Independent review found that `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` can redirect clone object writes into canonical metadata. `canonical_shell_parser.py` currently discards this environment assignment before policy classification, so the new allowance requires this adjacent parser to reject Git write/configuration overrides consistently with inherited-environment checks. The existing guard suite reproduces the assignment bypass; verification remains `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh` plus scoped Python compilation and ShellCheck. Collision discovery found no open related PR or competing claim for this parser. This adds no authority or security exception; it preserves the issue's canonical-write protection.

title: Multi-account providers: credentials become unidentifiable as an operator grows from one account to many
body:
## Situation

A non-developer operator relies on aidevops sessions to choose credential names and walk them through creating tokens. The operator pastes values in when asked. They started with one Cloudflare account and now have several: their main business account, a personal account, and a growing number of client accounts. They expect 10–50. This growth path is normal: nobody plans for many accounts on day one.

## What happened

Over time, sessions gave Cloudflare credentials names that describe purpose or project (`…_MAIN`, `…_DOMAINS`, `…_BROWSER_RENDERING`, project-prefixed names), not the account. Today neither the operator nor a new session can tell, from aidevops alone, which account a credential opens, which account is the default, or which account owns a given domain or resource. Answering these questions took live API calls and a custom script.

## Evidence (v3.39.31)

- Guidance tells sessions to use the plain name for a single account and suffix only when needed (`.agents/tools/credentials/gopass.md:89`, `.agents/tools/credentials/api-key-setup.md:84`). Nothing revisits the first credential when a second account arrives.
- Four different naming patterns are documented (`gopass.md:76`, `gopass.md:97-98`, `api-key-setup.md:84`, `.agents/configs/site-inventory.json.txt:20-21`). The dashboard token label (`.agents/services/hosting/cloudflare.md:66`) uses yet another form.
- `aidevops secret` stores a value and a name only. Nothing records the account, reach, purpose, owner (business, personal or client) or expiry.
- Tools assume one unlabelled `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (`.agents/scripts/onboarding-helper.sh:237`, `.agents/tools/api/cloudflare-cf-cli.md:29`, `.agents/scripts/validate-mcp-integrations.sh:135`). Onboarding reports Cloudflare as unconfigured while five tokens exist. Setting an unlabelled token would silently create a hidden default.
- The site inventory's DNS account link (`.agents/reference/site-operations.md:48-56`) covers websites only. It is filled in by hand and never checked against the provider (`site-operations.md:58-62`). It doesn't cover storage buckets, Workers/Pages projects, browser rendering or form-protection keys.
- Some resulting real-world states: two differently named tokens open exactly the same domains. Every token is set to never expire, contrary to `cloudflare.md:127`. A leftover "moved" domain in one account caused a session to read the wrong account's data. aidevops gave no way to notice any of these.
- Checking what a rename would break needed a manual search across every repo and worktree, and still missed a script that builds secret names from parts.

## Risks as accounts grow

- Changes made in the wrong account, including client accounts.
- Features breaking silently after a rename or rotation.
- Not knowing what to revoke when a client leaves.
- Every session rediscovering the same facts at the operator's expense.
- Cleaning up after the fact is itself risky. In this install, renaming one credential would silently disable a feature, others would cause hard failures, and one consumer can't be found by searching for the name. So operators tend to leave the mess in place, and it grows.

## What "good" would need to guarantee

These are outcomes, not a design; how to achieve them is for the maintainers to decide.

1. When a session adds a credential, it is recorded consistently enough to be identified later. This holds even if it's the operator's first and only account at that provider.
2. Adding a second account doesn't leave earlier credentials ambiguous, and making them clear doesn't break anything that already uses them.
3. Without live API calls, a session can say which account a credential belongs to, what it can reach, and who it's for.
4. A default account per provider is explicit or explicitly absent, never inferred from an unlabelled variable.
5. A session can answer "which account owns this domain or resource?", or state that it doesn't know.
6. Recorded facts can be checked against the provider, and drift shows up: leftover or moved items, overlapping tokens, missing expiry.
7. Before renaming, rotating or revoking a credential, the operator can see what depends on it.
8. The operator never has to invent a naming scheme or keep the record up to date by hand.
9. An existing install whose credentials are already inconsistent can get organised safely, without a risky bulk rename and without breaking working scripts, deployments or scheduled jobs.

Cloudflare is the motivating case, but the same pattern applies to any provider where one operator holds several accounts.

## Related (closed)

#21848, #26819, #34303. These improved naming guidance and added site-level account links, but don't cover these guarantees.

## Dispatch Hold

Problem-only report from a non-maintainer operator; the reporter asked that maintainers decide the solution design before any implementation.
