title: Workers released as blocked with reason=unknown after opening a PR; blocked label kept after merge
body:
## Observed

Two headless workers in one managed repository released their issues as `blocked` with `reason=unknown`, both carrying the same terminal-blocker fingerprint (`blocker=6986da1ae19a0543f4b73332`), and the framework could not classify the cause:

- Worker A (aidevops v3.38.42, OpenCode v1.18.35, openai/gpt-6.1-sol, tier bundle): dispatched 2026-10-09T21:31Z, opened its PR at 21:43Z, released 21:51Z (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`, "Terminal blocker: reason=unknown owner=worker-triage"). A later pulse posted `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION` and held ordinary redispatch while the PR existed.
- Worker B (aidevops v3.38.45, same runtime and model): dispatched 2026-10-10T01:42Z, opened its PR at 02:04Z, released 02:27Z with the same unknown reason and fingerprint. The issue stayed `status:blocked` after the PR merged and the issue closed (2026-10-12) until labelled by hand on 2026-10-14.

Both PRs were good checkpoints: interactive sessions finished and merged them on 2026-10-12 with no blocker found. The released-issue comments say "Raw evidence remains in protected worker telemetry", but `worker-activity-helper.sh summary` only looks back 24 hours, so by the time anyone looked, the cause could not be seen.

## Expected

- A worker that has opened a PR and then stops should be classified (for example as a post-PR handoff or a known blocker class), not `reason=unknown`.
- An identical fingerprint repeating across attempts should be grouped and surfaced for triage, with the dossier kept long enough to read it.
- When a blocked issue's linked PR merges and the issue closes, `status:blocked` should become `status:done` without manual relabelling.

## Where to look

- The worker release path that writes `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` and the `aidevops:terminal-blocker-observation` marker (worker-triage owner).
- The blocked-checkpoint attention routine that posts `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION`.
- The close/merge label reconciliation that sets `status:done`.
- Retention of the protected dossier and `worker-activity-helper.sh` time windows (`reference/worker-diagnostics.md`).

## Verification

- Replaying a recorded worker session that opens a PR and then exits classifies the release with a known reason, not `unknown`.
- A closed issue with a merged linked PR and `status:blocked` is normalised to `status:done` by the next pulse.
- `worker-activity-helper.sh` (or the triage dossier tool) can show the classification evidence for a release older than 24 hours.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-dispatch-label-cleanup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-label-cleanup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-blocker-log.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

## Continuation ledger and integration evidence

PR #34683 merged as fa6cb432baf9f6f4a0de9922d5de623be21ce2e2 and already implements completed closed-issue label healing. Reuse that delivery; do not recreate it. Classification and dossier retention remain unfinished.

The remaining integration requires `headless-runtime-result.sh` (the terminal BLOCKED branch captures only a class and then deletes the output), `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` (final-assistant capture), `worker-blocker-log.mjs` (existing redacted, size-bounded protected log), and `worker-activity-helper.sh` (windowed diagnostics). No new authority or hard boundary is introduced. Preserve explicit blockers, failed-check and exact-head readiness guards. Convert only unclassified exits with independently verified ready PRs to post-PR handoff. Retain redacted terminal evidence in the existing bounded protected log and surface repeated class fingerprints across retained attempts without claiming they prove a common root cause.

Verification: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-activity-helper.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-label-cleanup.sh`, ShellCheck on changed shell files, and `node --check .agents/scripts/worker-blocker-log.mjs`. Current runner: Bash 5.3, Node 24.21, ShellCheck available. Collision discovery found no open related PR; the dispatched issue is assigned to this runner and the original author is OWNER. Historical raw dossiers are not available to this task: use bounded regression replay, not invented historical attribution.

title: OpenCode sidebar: Prompts quick-nav section that opens the native timeline
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# OpenCode sidebar: "Prompts" quick-nav section that opens the native timeline

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `opencode TUI plugin sidebar slot` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch `v1-tui/tui.tsx` or `v2-plugin/tui.mjs` in last 48h (last change: #33994, 2026-10-07)
- [x] File refs verified: 6 refs checked, all present at HEAD `f36b376b1b`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — two runtimes and an unverified V2 dispatch signature leave local implementation choices
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — V2 API details must be confirmed against the live runtime first

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer review of #34625)
- **Conversation context:** External request #34625 asked to make earlier user prompts easier to find in long OpenCode sessions. Message restyling is not exposed by either OpenCode runtime's plugin API; the maintainer chose a sidebar quick-nav section under the session title whose click opens the native `/timeline` dialog.

## What

Add a collapsible **Prompts** section at the top of the OpenCode session sidebar (directly under the session title) in both OpenCode 1.x and OpenCode V2:

- One truncated single-line row per user prompt, newest first, capped at the last 8 prompts.
- Header row: `▼ Prompts` / `▶ Prompts (N)`; starts expanded; toggled by clicking the header (same interaction as the existing collapsed MCP section).
- Clicking any row (or the header count) opens OpenCode's native **Jump to message** dialog (`session.timeline`, the same as `/timeline` / `<leader>g`), where the user picks the prompt and the transcript scrolls to it.
- Only real user text: skip synthetic and ignored parts, and skip messages with no text (e.g. file-only or compaction).
- Hidden when the session has no user prompts.

## Why

Long sessions bury the user's earlier prompts between model output, and the native timeline is not discoverable. Plugins cannot restyle message cells (no message slot in either runtime) and cannot scroll the transcript, so the sidebar list plus the native timeline dialog is the supported way to get there.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The plugin slot boundaries are verified, but the worker must confirm the V2 `keymap.dispatch` signature and message data shape in the live runtime and pick the matching render code for two different plugin contracts.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

```text
V1 (OpenCode 1.x, v1.19.0 plugin API, packages/plugin/src/tui.ts):
  api.slots.register({ order, slots: { sidebar_content(_ctx, props) {...} } })  // props.session_id
  built-in sidebar context section registers sidebar_content at order 100;
  aidevops McpView uses order 200 → use an order below 100 (e.g. 50) so the section renders first.
  data: api.state.session.messages(sessionID) -> Message[] (role === "user")
        api.state.part(messageID) -> Part[] (type === "text" && !synthetic && !ignored)
  open timeline: api.keymap.dispatchCommand("session.timeline")  (deprecation note in tui.ts names
        api.keymap.dispatchCommand; verify it exists at runtime and fall back to a no-op if not)

V2 (opencode2 runtime, minified bundle inspected 2026-10-14):
  api.ui.slot({ prepend: "sidebar.content", render: (props) => ... })  // props.sessionID
  placement keys: prepend | append | before | after | replace (exactly one)
  sidebar layout: title box, then scrollbox with sidebar.content, then sidebar.footer
  data: api.data.session.message.list(sessionID); user messages render from message.text
  open timeline: api.keymap.dispatch(...)   // command id "session.timeline"; confirm argument shape
  .mjs entrypoint has no JSX: build nodes with solid.createElement/insert/setProp as in
  renderVersionText() in v2-plugin/tui.mjs
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v1-tui/tui.tsx:172-197` — add a `PromptsView` component (model on `McpView`, lines 23-92) and register it as `sidebar_content` with an order below 100.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin/tui.mjs:299-307` — add `setupPromptsSlot(api, {...})` (model on `setupVersionSlots`, lines 197-238) and add it to the `cleanups` list in `setup`.
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-tui-title.mjs` — extend with focused cases for the shared pure helpers (prompt extraction and truncation) and the V2 slot registration (`prepend: "sidebar.content"`), following the existing fake-`api` pattern in that file.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/terminal/terminal-title.md:67-69` — document the section, the opt-out, and the revert path for both runtimes.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/opencode/opencode.md` — add a short "Navigating long sessions" note under `## Usage`: `/timeline` / `<leader>g`, the new sidebar section, and the optional `tui.json` keybinds `messages_last_user`, `messages_previous`, `messages_next` (V1) and `session.message.user.previous` / `session.message.user.next` (V2), all unbound by default.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** OpenCode 1.x loads `v1-tui/tui.tsx` via `tui.json` (registered by `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh:868`); OpenCode V2 loads `v2-plugin/tui.mjs` through the V2 plugin entry. `v1-tui/tui.tsx` already imports helpers from `../v2-plugin/tui.mjs` (line 18), so shared pure helpers belong in `tui.mjs` and are imported by V1.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** None. The section is read-only over session data; the only side effect is dispatching the existing `session.timeline` command.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-tui-title.mjs` (V2 TUI entrypoint, fake api); `node --test tests/*.mjs` via `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package.json:14` and `.github/workflows/plugin-import-check.yml`; live capture via `opencode-test-helper.sh tui-capture` (`.agents/tools/terminal/terminal-title.md:86`).
- **Schemas/config:** No `tui.json` or `opencode.json` change. Add one env opt-out, `AIDEVOPS_TUI_PROMPTS=false`, read the same way as `AIDEVOPS_TUI_VERSION_SLOTS`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/plugins/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/plugins/`; no generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A — no persisted state; the collapsed/expanded state may use `api.kv` (V1) / `api.storage` (V2), which are plugin-namespaced.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** V1 slot registrations dispose with the plugin lifecycle; V2 `ui.slot` returns an unregister function that must be pushed to the disposers, as `setupVersionSlots` does.

### Implementation Steps

1. In `v2-plugin/tui.mjs`, export pure helpers:
   - `extractPromptRows(messages, partsFor, { limit = 8, width = 34 })` → `[{ id, text }]`, newest first; collapse whitespace and newlines to single spaces and truncate with `…`.
   - `isPromptsEnabled(env)` → false only for `AIDEVOPS_TUI_PROMPTS=false|0|none`.
2. V2: `setupPromptsSlot(api, { env, loadSolid, loadSolidJs })`: `api.ui.slot({ prepend: "sidebar.content", render: (props) => ... })`, rows reactive to `api.data.session.message.list(props.sessionID)`. Header and rows use `onMouseUp` to call `api.keymap.dispatch` for `session.timeline`. Wrap every API call in `safeCall` so a missing API degrades to "section hidden", never a TUI error. Theme colours: `theme.text.default` for rows and `theme.text.subdued` / `theme.text.muted` for the count, matching `themeColor()`.
3. V1: `PromptsView` JSX component modelled on `McpView`: `createMemo` over `api.state.session.messages(sessionID)` and `api.state.part(id)`, `<text wrapMode="none">` rows, header toggle, `onMouseDown` → `api.keymap.dispatchCommand?.("session.timeline")`. Register with `api.slots.register({ order: 50, slots: { sidebar_content(_ctx, props) { return <PromptsView api={api} sessionID={props.session_id} /> } } })`.
4. Docs per Files to Modify.
5. Live-verify both runtimes (see Verification).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Read-only reactive view; no shared writes.
- **Migration/rollback:** Pure plugin addition; revert the commit or set `AIDEVOPS_TUI_PROMPTS=false`.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** The V1 sidebar order must keep the existing MCP/footer layout. If `api.keymap.dispatchCommand` (V1) or `api.keymap.dispatch` (V2) is absent, rows still render and clicks do nothing; no exception.
- **Idempotency/retry:** Registering twice must not duplicate the section; follow the existing single-registration-per-setup pattern.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** All API calls go through `safeCall`; a throw hides the section and leaves the rest of the sidebar intact (same guarantee as `setupVersionSlots` `.catch`).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
cd .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops && node --test tests/*.mjs
```

title: gh-wrapper-guard pre-push scans the whole repo on task-id-counter pushes, so claim-task-id.sh times out
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# gh-wrapper-guard pre-push scans the whole repo on task-id-counter pushes, so claim-task-id.sh times out

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `claim-task-id pre-push hook timeout counter` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch the guard files in the last 48h (last change: #22006)
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at HEAD `f36b376b1b`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — small fix in a pre-push hook; worker picks the exact skip condition
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — small and well-specified

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-14
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** While filing #34684, `claim-task-id.sh` failed twice in a row with `Pre-push hook pre-push timed out after 300s (limit=300s); remote push was not attempted` and `AIDEVOPS_TASK_COUNTER_STATUS=setup_error detail=pre_push_hook_failed`. The counter was not advanced; the issue was filed through the `gh_create_issue` wrapper without a task ID.

## Reproducer

From a linked worktree of this repo on aidevops v3.39.31 (HEAD `f36b376b1b`, `origin/task-id-counter` at `a65ddd1f98`):

```bash
claim-task-id.sh --repo-path <worktree> --title "<title>" --brief-file <brief> --labels "enhancement,auto-dispatch,tier:standard"
# ...
# [repo-verify][OK] task-id counter-only invariants passed — skipping full repository verification
# [ERROR] Pre-push hook pre-push timed out after 300s (limit=300s); remote push was not attempted
# [INFO] AIDEVOPS_TASK_COUNTER_STATUS=setup_error detail=pre_push_hook_failed

# During the hang, the process tree shows the stuck child:
#   .beads/hooks/pre-push -> .agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh
#   -> .agents/scripts/gh-wrapper-guard.sh check --base a65ddd1f98e762306d0dec9252bebe76314a7d47

git diff --name-only a65ddd1f98e762306d0dec9252bebe76314a7d47...HEAD -- '*.sh' | wc -l
# 1086
```

This happened on two consecutive attempts. The counter stayed at 18692.

## What

Make `gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh` scan only the commits actually being pushed. A `task-id-counter` CAS push must pass the guard in well under a second, and normal branch pushes must still block raw `gh issue/pr create|edit` calls.

## Why

Since #34411 made hook installers honour `core.hooksPath` (`.beads/hooks`), the gh-wrapper guard runs on every push in this repo, including the CAS counter push in `claim-task-id.sh`. That push updates the orphan `task-id-counter` branch. The hook:

1. reads `<local_sha> <remote_sha>` from stdin but only uses `remote_sha` as `--base` (`.agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh:62-82`), never the pushed `local_sha`;
2. calls `gh-wrapper-guard.sh check --base <counter tip>`, which diffs `"$base_ref"...HEAD` (`.agents/scripts/gh-wrapper-guard.sh:170,181`), where HEAD is the checkout's `main`-based commit.

The two histories are unrelated, so the diff covers the whole tree. Observed: `git diff --name-only <counter-tip>...HEAD -- '*.sh'` lists 1086 files. Each one gets its own `git diff` and scan, which exceeds the 300s hook budget. Result: every interactive `claim-task-id.sh` allocation fails.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The cause and owning boundary are verified. The worker chooses between passing an explicit head and skipping unrelated histories (the recommendation is both) and extends the existing test.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh:62-82` — pass the pushed `local_sha` as the head. Skip a ref when `git merge-base "$base_ref" "$local_sha"` fails (unrelated history, such as the orphan counter branch). For new branches, compute the merge base against `local_sha`, not `HEAD`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-wrapper-guard.sh:158-189,281-304` — accept an optional `--head <sha>` (default `HEAD`, which keeps the CI and manual behaviour) and diff `"$base_ref"..."$head_ref"`. `[[ -f "$file" ]]` reads the working tree; when `--head` is given, read file content from `git show "$head_ref:$file"` or keep scanning diff output only (the diff is what is scanned, so the existence check can use `git cat-file -e "$head_ref:$file"`).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh` — next to Test 10 (around line 260), add: (a) `check --base X --head Y` detects a violation introduced in Y; (b) the pre-push hook given stdin for an orphan-branch push exits 0 quickly without scanning.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** The pre-push hook chain installed by `install-hooks-helper.sh` (including `.beads/hooks/pre-push`); `.github/workflows/gh-wrapper-guard.yml` calls `check --base` (must keep working with the `HEAD` default); `claim-task-id.sh` CAS push triggers the hook.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A. Both scripts only run `git diff`, `git merge-base` and grep, and print results. Neither writes files, refs or config (verified by reading `gh-wrapper-guard.sh:158-189` and the hook body).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A — no config; `GH_WRAPPER_GUARD_DISABLE` behaviour unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/scripts/` and `.agents/hooks/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/`; no generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the guard keeps no state between runs (no cache, DB or marker files), so there is nothing to migrate or backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Reverting the PR restores the previous behaviour. Nothing needs cleaning up because the scripts create no temp files or refs. The hook-chain entry installed by `install-hooks-helper.sh` keeps the same path, so no reinstall is needed.

### Implementation Steps

1. `gh-wrapper-guard.sh`: replace `_parse_base_arg` with a parser that returns both `--base` and optional `--head` (default `HEAD`). Make `cmd_check` take `base_ref head_ref`, and replace both `"$base_ref"...HEAD` diffs with `"$base_ref"..."$head_ref"`. When `head_ref` is not `HEAD`, use `git cat-file -e "$head_ref:$file"` instead of `[[ -f "$file" ]]`.
2. `gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh`: for new branches, use `git merge-base "$local_sha" main` (fallback `master`). Before scanning, `git merge-base "$base_ref" "$local_sha" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue` (unrelated history). Call `bash "$GUARD" check --base "$base_ref" --head "$local_sha"`.
3. Tests: add the two cases from Files to Modify to `test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh`, using its existing temporary-repo setup (`TMPGIT`).
4. Run the verification commands, then a real `claim-task-id.sh` allocation.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Read-only.
- **Migration/rollback:** Revert restores the old (slow) behaviour; no state.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** `check --base <ref>` without `--head` must behave exactly as today (the CI workflow relies on it).
- **Idempotency/retry:** Re-running the hook gives the same result.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** If `merge-base` fails, skip only that ref and log it with `GH_WRAPPER_GUARD_DEBUG=1`; never fail open for refs that share history with `main`.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh
shellcheck .agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh .agents/scripts/gh-wrapper-guard.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
claim-task-id.sh --dry-run --title "probe" --no-issue   # sanity; a real claim must finish without the 300s hook timeout
```

- **Surface mapping:** The test file proves detection on `--head` ranges and the orphan-branch skip. ShellCheck and lint cover both scripts. A real `claim-task-id.sh` allocation in a linked worktree proves the CAS push no longer times out.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-wrapper-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Pushing the orphan `task-id-counter` branch (as `claim-task-id.sh` does) passes the gh-wrapper pre-push guard in under 5 seconds, and `claim-task-id.sh` allocates the next task ID and creates its issue.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "merge-base \"\\$base_ref\" \"\\$local_sha\""
    path: ".agents/hooks/gh-wrapper-guard-pre-push.sh"
  ```
- [ ] Regression: a normal feature-branch push that adds a raw `gh issue create` line in `.agents/scripts/*.sh` is still blocked, and `check --base <ref>` with no `--head` behaves as before.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- Don't work around this by setting `GH_WRAPPER_GUARD_DISABLE=1` inside `claim-task-id.sh`. The hook should scan what is actually pushed.
- Related: #34411 (hooks now run under `core.hooksPath`), GH#29417 (separate pre-push budget for the CAS push).

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** interactive `claim-task-id.sh` allocations in this repo

title: release: recover-aggregate GitHub release probe fails silently when gh omits --include headers on 404
body:
## What

`aidevops release recover-aggregate 34603 --tag v3.39.31 ...` exits 1 with no message after #34677. The new aggregate resolution succeeds (verified: `resolve-source` returns `mode:"aggregate"` for exact-tip aggregate #34682 at `eed79e63`). Recovery then stops in `_full_loop_recovery_verify_channels_absent` before taking the lane, so nothing is mutated.

## Root cause

`_full_loop_recovery_http_status` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh:31-42`) runs `gh api --include --silent "$endpoint" 2>/dev/null` and parses the HTTP status from the first stdout line. With gh 2.102.0 (and the governed transport), a 404 prints nothing to stdout, only `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` on stderr. The parser finds no status code, so `_full_loop_recovery_verify_github_release_absent` fails silently even though the release is absent.

Evidence: `gh api --include --silent repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/releases/tags/v3.39.31` prints only `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`. Every other channel probe passes: npm E404, Homebrew formula still pins v3.39.30, and `ls-remote --exit-code` returns 2 on all three remotes.

## Fix

Apply the same parsing as 2fd50fa4 / #34668 (`release-lane-helper.sh:119-128`): capture stderr and fall back to the terminal `gh: ... (HTTP NNN)` status line. Also report an unknown status explicitly instead of returning silently.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- ShellCheck on the changed script
- Live: rerun `recover-aggregate` for #34603 (Ref #34674)

title: docs: image-library advisories: find who outside the team can get files to ImageMagick and Ghostscript (WordPress audit checklist)
body:
## What

When the host's shared ImageMagick or Ghostscript has open advisories, only the host can patch them (see `services/hosting/hostinger.md` → "Shared image library"). Until then, the useful question is: which site features let people outside the team get a file into WordPress's image editor? A read-only fleet audit (WordPress 7.1.3, 28 sites, October 2026) answered it mostly from settings, plus a short code search. Document the method so the next audit does not have to work it out again.

## Where

- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` → `## Security Checklist` (about line 145): add a short subsection, for example "Image-library advisories: who can reach it", with the checklist below.
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` → the "Shared image library" bullet (about line 96): one line pointing to that subsection.

## Checklist to document (observed facts)

1. ImageMagick runs only when something calls the image editor: core's sub-sizes (`wp_generate_attachment_metadata()`, `media_handle_upload()`, `media_handle_sideload()`, REST media uploads) or a plugin's `wp_get_image_editor()` or `Imagick`. Read-only search per active plugin: `grep -rEn --include='*.php' 'wp_get_image_editor|wp_generate_attachment_metadata|wp_create_image_subsizes|media_handle_upload|media_handle_sideload|new \\?Imagick' wp-content/plugins/<slug>`. A file stored outside the Media Library without these calls never reaches ImageMagick.
2. Who can get an account, and what it can do:
   - `users_can_register` and `default_role`; on multisite the network `registration` setting.
   - WooCommerce: `woocommerce_enable_myaccount_registration` and `woocommerce_enable_signup_and_login_from_checkout`. WooCommerce sends users without `edit_posts`, `manage_woocommerce` or `view_admin_dashboard` away from wp-admin, so uploads that live only on the wp-admin profile screen do not reach customers.
   - Ultimate Multisite: network option `wp-ultimo_v2_settings` → `enable_registration`, `enable_email_verification` and `default_role` (the new site owner's role; administrator and editor can upload), plus the network's `upload_filetypes` (`pdf` means Ghostscript) and `fileupload_maxk`. Check that the sign-up page answers publicly, and read `wu_customers` dates and email domains to tell real sign-ups from the team's own tests.
3. Front-end paths observed, with versions:
   - Tutor LMS 4.1.2: profile and cover photos go to the Media Library with sub-sizes (`classes/User.php`), for any logged-in user. Tutor's own registration needs `users_can_register` (`classes/Student.php`), but WooCommerce or other sign-ups still give access.
   - Fluent Forms Pro: the image editor runs only for the "Media Library" upload location (`src/Uploader.php`, `copyToWpMedia()`); the default location does not.
   - AI Engine: chatbot uploads are per bot in `mwai_chatbots` (`fileUpload`, `imageUpload`).
   - Webmention 5.10.1: remote avatars are resized only when `webmention_avatar_store_enable` is 1 (`includes/class-webmention.php`); `webmention_avatars` only shows them.
   - No image-editor calls found in Bookly Files, Ninja Job Board, Kadence form uploads, or Fluent Support and Fluent Booking app code (their vendored WPFluent `Media` helper was unused).
4. Evidence of real use: image and PDF attachments whose author lacks `upload_files`. Images with author 0 are usually imports; their meta (for example a source-URL key) shows where they came from.
5. While waiting for the host, turn off the specific path (a setting) rather than switching every site to GD; see the GD trade-off bullet.

## Verification

- The repository's markdown checks pass for both files.
- The subsection stays short (about 25 lines or fewer) and names no sites, hostnames, accounts or paths from a real fleet.
- `rg -n "Image-library advisories" .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` finds it, and `hostinger.md` links to it.

title: fix(dispatch-claim): private-org-member runners lose their own claim at consensus (author_association=CONTRIBUTOR) — sibling of GH#34644
body:
## Problem

Dispatch claim consensus discards the runner's own `DISPATCH_CLAIM` when GitHub reports the comment's `author_association` as `CONTRIBUTOR`. That is what GitHub reports for an org admin whose membership is **private**. The claim set comes back empty, so `_resolve_claim_race_result` returns `CLAIM_ERROR: no claims found after posting — blocking dispatch (fail-closed)`. Every dispatch from that runner to that repository fails with `PRE_RUNTIME_FAILURE reason=claim_lock_failed`.

This is a sibling of GH#34644 / PR #34645. That fix routed `CONTRIBUTOR`/`NONE` through the per-repo permission lookup in `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority` (`.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh:61`). The claim-consensus trust filters are separate and still trust by association alone. After #34645 was deployed, the same runner/repo stopped failing at the external-author gate and now fails one stage later, at claim consensus.

## Evidence (pulse runner, 2026-10-14, aidevops v3.39.31, #34645 deployed)

- Runner permission: `gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/collaborators/<runner>/permission` returns `admin`. `orgs/<org>/members/<runner>` returns 204. `orgs/<org>/public_members/<runner>` returns 404 (private membership).
- The claim comment is posted successfully (for example `DISPATCH_CLAIM nonce=57a8947e… runner=<runner> ts=2026-10-14T23:06:40Z`). The REST comment listing reports `author_association: CONTRIBUTOR` for it.
- `pulse.log` stage trace for one attempt: `claim_post rc=0`, then `consensus_window rc=0`, then `claim_comments rc=0`, then `CLAIM_ERROR: no claims found after posting`, then `claim_consensus rc=2`, then `Dedup: claim error … blocking dispatch for this cycle (fail-closed)`.
- `pulse.log` contains 37 `claim error` lines across about 20 distinct `origin:worker` issues in one private managed repository, and no successful launch for that repository in the log window. The framework repo (where the runner shows as a collaborator) has zero such errors.
- Impact: this runner gets zero worker throughput for the affected repository while its slots sit idle.

## Root cause

`trusted_association` accepts only `OWNER|MEMBER|COLLABORATOR`:

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-lease-claims.jq:1-2` (definition), used at `:45` (claims), `:60` (`DISPATCH_LEASE` events) and `:77` (`CLAIM_RELEASED` events).
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:703`, `_filter_claims_with_launch_evidence`, which has the same inline association check for "Dispatching worker" launch evidence.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:578-717`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-lease-claims.jq`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh`

`tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh` is over the large-file threshold (2130 lines). Put the new cases in the focused NEW test file rather than extending that one.

## Changes

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:578-717` (`_fetch_claims` through `_filter_claims_with_launch_evidence`). In `_fetch_claims`, before running the jq parser, collect the distinct comment authors whose association is `CONTRIBUTOR` or `NONE`. Resolve each one once per call with `_gh_actor_has_repo_write_authority "$repo_slug" "$login" "$association"`, sourcing `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` if it is not already loaded. Pass the authors that resolve as write-authorized to jq, for example `--argjson permission_trusted_authors '["login",...]'`. Do the same for `_filter_claims_with_launch_evidence` (line 703).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-lease-claims.jq`. Replace the association-only `trusted_association` checks at lines 45, 60 and 77 with a helper like `trusted_author($assoc; $login)`. It should return true for `OWNER|MEMBER|COLLABORATOR`, or when `$login` is in `$permission_trusted_authors`. Keep the existing `#aidevops:trust-boundary` markers.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh`. Feed `dispatch-lease-claims.jq` fixture claims and comments. Assert that a CONTRIBUTOR claim from an author listed in `permission_trusted_authors` is counted, and that a CONTRIBUTOR claim from an unlisted (read-only or 404) author is still dropped. Stub `gh` for the shell-side lookup the same way `tests/test-shared-gh-actor-authority.sh` does.

Reference pattern: the GH#34644 change in `shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` (`COLLABORATOR | CONTRIBUTOR | NONE)` branch, line 61).

## Constraints

- Fail closed. If a permission lookup fails, leave that author untrusted (current behaviour). Never trust by `runner=` body field alone.
- Only `admin|maintain|write` grants trust. `read|triage|none`/404 stays untrusted. `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, `MANNEQUIN` and unknown values stay untrusted without a lookup.
- Add at most one permission lookup per distinct author per `_fetch_claims` call, to bound API cost on high-comment issues.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-atomic-lease.sh` pass.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lease-claims-private-member.sh` is clean.
- After deploy, on a private-member runner: `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch <N> <org>/<repo> …` for an available issue in the affected repository reaches `outcome=launched`, and `pulse.log` has no new `CLAIM_ERROR: no claims found after posting` lines for that repository.

title: subagent-index-helper.sh generate output depends on shell locale sort order
body:
## What

`subagent-index-helper.sh generate` produces locale-dependent ordering. Under a UTF-8 macOS shell it sorts case-insensitively (`summarize|VERIFICATION|video-*`, `models-pro|models-README|models-sonnet`), while the committed `.agents/subagent-index.toon` uses C/byte order (`VERIFICATION|content-calendar…`, `models-README` before `models-composer2`). Contributors regenerating the index therefore produce unrelated churn lines.

## Evidence

Observed in PR #34702 (t18693): plain regeneration produced 5 changed lines, 2 of them pure reordering; `LC_ALL=C` reduced it to the 3 real changes.

## How

- File: `.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh`, e.g. line 89 (`find … | sort | awk …`) and any other `sort` calls.
- Fix: make sorting deterministic inside the helper (`LC_ALL=C sort`, or `export LC_ALL=C` near the top of `generate`), matching the committed order.
- Verification: in a worktree, run `AIDEVOPS_AGENTS_DIR=<worktree>/.agents .agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh generate` under the default UTF-8 locale on main; `git diff .agents/subagent-index.toon` must be empty. Run `shellcheck` on the helper.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh`

title: fix(release): refresh-aggregate exits 1 silently on a merged stale aggregation PR
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# fix(release): refresh-aggregate exits 1 silently on a merged stale aggregation PR

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `abandon stranded release lane unpublished tag fresh release` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 6 recent commits on target file (latest #34688/afda17a870); 0 open claimed issues; open draft #34650 is an old unmerged aggregate, not a code change
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked at `main` `ccf3073d5c`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`. The error-reporting contract is decided; the worker still chooses the message wording and helper placement.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped. The change is small and the brief carries the full context.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (v3.39.31 release recovery, Ref #34603)
- **Conversation context:** While recovering the stranded v3.39.31 lane, `aidevops release refresh-aggregate 34690` exited 1 in about 5 seconds with no output. #34690 had already merged, and `main` had then advanced through #34691 and #34692.

## Reproducer

Observed live on 2026-10-14 with v3.39.31 deployed (`setup.sh` at `b44b336c42`):

```text
$ aidevops release refresh-aggregate 34690   # #34690 merged as b44b336c42; main then at c1db70b11d
(no output)
exit 1 after ~5s
```

Cause: `full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh:1667-1670` requires `.state == "open"` and returns 1 without a message.

## What

`aidevops release refresh-aggregate <PR>` must never fail without a message. Every refusal in `_full_loop_release_refresh_aggregate` should print one `Successor aggregation refused: <reason>` line to stderr. A stale aggregation PR that was **merged**, and whose merge commit is still an ancestor of `origin/main`, must give a specific diagnostic. That diagnostic names the merge SHA and says to open a successor from that merge commit's trailers. Adopting merged stale PRs as successor input is an optional extension. Implement it only if it reuses the existing manifest helpers without new trust decisions.

## Why

Operators and agents get no signal from a bare exit 1. In this session it cost a full investigation cycle, ending in a hand-built successor (#34701), while concurrent merges kept invalidating exact-tip aggregates.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** This is a known diagnostics pattern inside an already decided fail-closed boundary. The worker chooses wording and whether to extract a helper.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh:1642-1732` (`_full_loop_release_refresh_aggregate`). Replace each bare `|| return 1` that is a user-facing refusal with a stderr diagnostic followed by `return 1`. Model the wording on the existing refusals at lines 1677-1679 (`Successor aggregation refused: ...`) and `_full_loop_successor_complete_manifest` at 1546-1554.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md:6-27`. Document the merged-stale case.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `full-loop-release-helper.sh:883-893` (`refresh-aggregate` dispatch). This is the only caller (`rg -n "_full_loop_release_refresh_aggregate" .agents/scripts`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** inside the function, `release_lane_begin_aggregate_successor`, the refs POST, PR creation and lane bind/finish. These are unchanged; only the messages on refusal paths before them change.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh:1660-1690` calls the function with stderr discarded. Existing assertions must still pass.
- **Schemas/config:** none affected. The change adds only `printf ... >&2` lines. The lane JSON written by `release_lane_begin_aggregate_successor` (`release-lane-helper.sh:596-636`) and the PR body format from `_full_loop_successor_body` stay byte-identical, and no config key is read or added.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` via `setup.sh`. No generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none required. The new messages are emitted only on refusal paths, and no persisted lane, receipt or ref format changes, so existing lanes such as `refs/heads/aidevops/release-lane` need no backfill.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting the PR restores the silent exits in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`. The refusals happen before or instead of the existing writes, so a rollback leaves no orphaned branches, PRs or lane records beyond what the current code already leaves.

### Implementation Steps

1. At line 1666-1670, read `.state`/`.merged_at` before the open-state assertion. If the PR is merged, print `Successor aggregation refused: #<PR> already merged as <merge_commit_sha>; open a successor from its trailers at the current main tip`, then return 1. For other mismatches (closed unmerged, wrong base), print the specific reason.
2. Add messages to the remaining silent refusals: fetch failure; stale head equals main; missing manifest in the body; lane read failure; branch/tree fence mismatch; PR lookup ambiguity.
3. Update the reference doc paragraph.
4. Run `shellcheck` and the existing recovery test.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** unchanged. All new output happens before or instead of the existing returns, and no lane write is added.
- **Migration/rollback:** none. Revert restores the old silent behaviour.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** exit codes are unchanged (still 1), so scripts that check only the status are unaffected.
- **Idempotency/retry:** unchanged.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** refusals after `release_lane_begin_aggregate_successor` keep the existing retry-adoption semantics. Only add messages there.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh
AIDEVOPS_FULL_LOOP_REPO=marcusquinn/aidevops bash .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh refresh-aggregate 34690   # merged PR: expect exit 1 plus a "Successor aggregation refused" line naming b44b336c42
```

- **Surface mapping:** the shellcheck run and the test cover the changed function. The live command against merged #34690 proves the new merged-PR diagnostic and confirms no lane write happens; the merged check runs before `release_lane_read`.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. One function, diagnostics only.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `refresh-aggregate` against a merged aggregation PR exits 1 and prints a `Successor aggregation refused` line that names the merge SHA.
- [ ] Every `return 1` in `_full_loop_release_refresh_aggregate` that a user can reach through valid input has a preceding stderr diagnostic.
- [ ] No exit code, lane write or fence check changes. The existing `test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` passes, and `shellcheck` is clean.

## Context & Decisions

- Silent-exit sibling of #34686 (fixed by #34688), in the same recovery subsystem.
- Non-goal: changing the exact-tip requirement. That is tracked in the companion recovery-starvation issue.

title: fix(release): signed-tag aggregate recovery starves under concurrent merges (exact-tip requirement)
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# fix(release): signed-tag aggregate recovery starves under concurrent merges (exact-tip requirement)

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `abandon stranded release lane unpublished tag fresh release` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: 6 recent commits on target files; #34677 and #34688 are the latest recovery fixes; no open claimed issues
- [x] File refs verified at `main` `ccf3073d5c`
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking`. This changes a release-provenance trust fence.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped. Claimed for interactive implementation.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (v3.39.31 release recovery, Ref #34603)
- **Conversation context:** v3.39.31 has been stranded since 2026-10-14. Its signed tag `a1af8e65e3` targets `92ff98fab7`, which is already on `main` (VERSION=3.39.31), but the tag's signer key is not registered on GitHub. `recover-aggregate` re-signs it, but needs `origin/main` to equal a reviewed aggregation merge. Four consecutive exact-tip aggregates were invalidated before recovery could start: #34682→#34690 (merged, then #34691/#34692 landed), #34701 (#34699 landed during CI), and #34704 (#34695 landed two minutes into CI). Pulse merges by other maintainers land every 2–15 minutes, and required CI takes about 7 minutes.

## Reproducer

Observed live on 2026-10-14 (UTC). Merge times come from `gh pr list --state merged`:

```text
22:47:28 #34690 aggregate merged (b44b336c42) -> recovery start blocked by a stale deploy, then main moved
22:53:46 #34692, 22:55:29 #34691 merged (alex-solovyev pulse)
~23:00   #34701 successor opened at c1db70b11d; required checks green after ~7 min
23:08:28 #34699 merged -> #34701 stale before merge
23:10:29 #34695 merged -> #34704 (opened at cf6811ef59) stale 2 min into CI
```

`release-provenance-helper.sh:400-403` refuses with "release checkout is not the exact origin/main tip" whenever any PR merges between the aggregate's CI start and the start of recovery.

## What

Signed-tag aggregate recovery must be able to complete while ordinary PRs keep merging. That means removing the exact-tip starvation without weakening provenance. It also needs a supported way to retire a stranded, never-published lane, so that a fresh release is never blocked forever.

## Why

- `release_lane_merge_guard` (`.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh:1394-1400`) has been a deliberate no-op since #31472 (4904174c8d, "Release immutable snapshots while PR merges continue"). Normal releases use immutable snapshots for that reason.
- Recovery still requires `HEAD == origin/main` (`release-provenance-helper.sh:399-403` via `_release_provenance_resolve_source`). That conflicts with the snapshot model and makes recovery a race the operator usually loses.
- `.agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md:165` still says "Ordinary merges remain blocked during every recovery and committing phase". That is stale since #31472.
- Nothing can retire an unpublished lane. `_full_loop_release_guard_competing_lane` (`full-loop-release-helper.sh:682-712`) returns 75 for any other source unless the lane is an abandoned reservation or already published, and supersession (`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:1789-1807`) requires a newer *published* tag. A stranded lane therefore blocks every new release indefinitely.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** The trust boundary is release provenance. It requires choosing between snapshot-bound recovery and lane retirement, and rollback semantics must be decided.

## How (Approach)

### Decision options (recommended first)

1. **Snapshot-bound recovery.** Accept a reviewed aggregation merge `A` that is an ancestor of `origin/main`, not necessarily its tip, when `A`'s immutable trailers cover every first-parent commit from the previous baseline through `A`. This mirrors the existing snapshot mode (`mode:"snapshot"`, `snapshot_base` in `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:644-647`). The recovery bump commit already takes `A` as parent (reference doc step 4). The recovered-tag validator already checks the direct aggregate parent rather than the current tip (doc line 159). The protected release PR merge then has to preserve the release commit SHA (`_merge_release_provenance_method`). With this, merged #34690 (`b44b336c42`) recovers v3.39.31 without another aggregate.
2. **Unpublished-lane retirement.** Add `aidevops release retire-unpublished <source-pr> --tag <tag> --reason <text>`. It reuses the channel-absence probes (`_full_loop_recovery_verify_*_absent`), requires a dead or unknown executor, and makes a compare-and-swap write moving the lane to inactive with an auditable terminal receipt. The local unpublished tag is left inert. A fresh snapshot release can then proceed; version handling for the skipped number still needs a decision.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:372-470`: the snapshot-tolerant aggregate resolver for the signed-tag recovery path only.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`: the recovery entry (`_full_loop_release_recover_aggregate` at 1734) and the existing-context preparation.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md:6-27,165`: correct the stale merge-blocking claim and document the chosen mode.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`: existing suite; extend only where the new acceptance path needs coverage.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `full-loop-release-helper.sh:894-903` (`recover-aggregate`), `release-provenance-helper.sh` `resolve-*` subcommands, and the reconcile path in `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** lane compare-and-swap writes in `release-lane-helper.sh` (begin/refresh/commit phases), local tag replacement in version-manager protected-main publication, and receipts.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` (12+ PASS cases, including "retains manifest and exact-tip fences") and `test-release-provenance-helper*.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** lane JSON on `refs/heads/aidevops/release-lane`. Option 2 adds a terminal receipt value.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` via `setup.sh`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** option 1 needs no backfill. The persisted recovery transaction gains a pinned `snapshot_base` field only for new transactions; existing lanes on `refs/heads/aidevops/release-lane` remain exact-tip transactions. Option 2 adds a terminal receipt value that readers in `full-loop-release-helper.sh:674-676` must recognise.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh` restores the exact-tip refusal. A lane left mid-transaction by the new mode must fail closed under old code, never be adopted, so the rollback cannot publish an unverified tag.

### Implementation Steps

1. Decide between option 1 and option 2 (option 1 recommended), and record the decision on the issue.
2. Option 1: add a recovery-only resolver mode in `release-provenance-helper.sh`. It takes an explicit aggregate merge SHA `A`, verifies that `A` is an ancestor of `origin/main`, verifies `A`'s aggregator and manifest trailers with the existing `_release_provenance_verify_pr_record` / `_release_provenance_verify_aggregate_base`, and returns `mode:"aggregate"` with `source_merge:A`. Keep the exact-tip check for every non-recovery caller.
3. Pass the pinned `A` through `_full_loop_release_recover_aggregate` and persist it in the recovery transaction, so retries resolve the same base. Build the bump commit with parent `A`, as now.
4. Correct `release-aggregation-recovery.md:165` and document the snapshot-bound mode.
5. Run shellcheck and the recovery and provenance test suites. Then run the live v3.39.31 recovery against `b44b336c42` (#34690) and verify convergence across GitHub, npm and Homebrew.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** keep the compare-and-swap token rotation. The snapshot base must be pinned in the persisted transaction so a retry resolves the same `A`.
- **Migration/rollback:** the existing exact-tip transactions stay valid, so the exact tip remains a special case of the snapshot.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older clients that see a snapshot-mode recovery transaction must fail closed, not adopt it.
- **Idempotency/retry:** rerunning with the same aggregate must resume, not create a second bump commit.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** the existing rule still applies. Once the release PR or remote tag is durable, nothing restores or mutates provisional state.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh .agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh
aidevops release recover-aggregate 34603 --tag v3.39.31 --expected-sources <#34690 manifest PR list>   # live: succeeds with main ahead of b44b336c42
```

- **Surface mapping:** the tests prove the fences remain. The live run proves that the starvation case is resolved and that publication converges across GitHub, npm and Homebrew.
- **Broad verification trigger:** release infrastructure change. Run `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed` plus the release test suites.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recovery succeeds when `origin/main` has advanced past a reviewed aggregation merge whose trailers fully cover the history up to that merge.
- [ ] Recovery still refuses an aggregate whose trailers omit any first-parent commit up to the aggregate, a tag already on a remote or channel, and an aggregate that is not an ancestor of `origin/main`.
- [ ] `release-aggregation-recovery.md` no longer claims that ordinary merges are blocked during recovery.
- [ ] v3.39.31 publishes, and the #34603 lane reaches a terminal `published` receipt.

## Context & Decisions

- Companion diagnostics issue: the silent `refresh-aggregate` exit (filed alongside).
- Superseded aggregates: #34701 (closed), #34704 (stale), #34650 (old draft).
- Non-goal: re-enabling a global merge freeze. That contradicts #31472.

## What

`opencode-test-helper.sh tui-capture --tui-config <overlay>` cannot verify a worktree copy of the aidevops V1 TUI plugin. OpenCode merges `OPENCODE_TUI_CONFIG` with the global `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`. ## Evidence (GH#34684 / PR #34689)

- With an overlay listing only the worktree `v1-tui/tui.tsx`, the capture rendered the deployed footer and MCP section but not the new **Prompts** section: `--expect Prompts` failed.

- Also note there: project data DBs can be very large (one was 84 GB), and the read-only snapshot step then exceeds a 120 s budget. Prefer a small project data dir via `--cwd`/`--data-dir`.

## What

Replace the GenAIPro "Candidates Pending Verification" entry in
`.agents/content/media-generation-providers.md` with a verified
"reviewed, do not route" record, and add a general decision check that rejects
gateways backed by pooled consumer subscriptions.

## Why

The original entry (PR #34702) said GenAIPro had no verifiable API contract.
The user supplied the API docs. Its OpenAPI 3.1 spec (the docs page's download
source) documents a real API: bearer auth at `https://genaipro.io/api`;
ElevenLabs-model TTS (`eleven_multilingual_v2` … `eleven_v4`); four further TTS
providers; Veo text/frames/ingredients-to-video; Nano Banana images; and a
"ChatGPT Image" endpoint. It is credit-billed, async with webhooks/WebSocket,
and keeps files for 7 days.

First-party evidence suggests the capacity comes from pooled consumer accounts
rather than official APIs:

- The public `GET /api/packages` lists "ChatGPT Plus" day/week/month packages
  priced in VND with "Free choice of ChatGPT account".
- The public frontend bundle has admin views for ChatGPT accounts, Veo
  accounts with Ultra/Pro tiers, Hotmail, and proxies. It also shows user
  notices such as "Please do not log out of your ChatGPT account from all
  devices".
- Veo costs a flat 1 credit per request, whatever the number of videos.

This carries upstream terms, account-ban, continuity and data-handling risk, so
aidevops should not route client or production work to it.

  reviewed services, record the verified API facts and the evidence above, and

title: docs: image-library advisories checklist: correct the WooCommerce, Tutor and Fluent Forms notes; add guest-handler and site-owner checks
body:
## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Follow-up to #34687 (merged as PR #34691). A second read-only pass over the same WordPress fleet read the installed plugin code behind the checklist. Three lines in the merged text are incomplete, and four checks that settled real questions are missing.

## What

Correct and extend `### Image-library advisories: who can reach it` in `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` with the seven exact edits below. Each one is backed by code read in the installed plugins (versions named) or by fleet data. No sites, hostnames or accounts are named, and none may be added.

## Why

- The WooCommerce bullet says customers can't reach uploads on the wp-admin profile screen. That is true, but the redirect skips `admin-ajax.php` and `admin-post.php`, so AJAX upload handlers still reach customers. Tutor LMS's photo upload is one: the audit found a customer-created account whose Tutor photos got sub-sizes.
- The Fluent Forms Pro bullet says the editor runs "only" for the Media Library location. Post forms run it too.
- A guest (`wp_ajax_nopriv_`) upload handler can look open when it is closed. The deciding check is whether the nonce it verifies is ever created and printed to visitors.
- Ultimate Multisite settings show what a sign-up could get; only the customers' roles on their own sites show who can upload now.
- Themes, must-use plugins and snippet plugins hold upload code too, and the plugin-only search misses them.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Seven verbatim `oldString` → `newString` replacements (one is an insertion) in one documentation file. No design decision is left, and the change is reversible with `git revert`.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` (the section added by PR #34691, about lines 154–175)

### Implementation Steps

Make each replacement with exact string matching. Each `oldString` appears once in the file. Keep the surrounding list numbering and indentation.

1. Step 1 search scope.

   oldString:

   ```text
   Search each active plugin (including network-active plugins), then trace callers:
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   Search each active plugin (including network-active plugins), the active theme, must-use plugins and code kept by snippet plugins (for example Code Snippets' `{prefix}snippets` table), then trace callers:
   ```

2. WooCommerce bullet.

   oldString:

   ```text
   uploads confined to its profile screen do not reach those customers, but front-end paths may.
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   uploads confined to its profile screen do not reach those customers. The redirect (`includes/admin/class-wc-admin.php` → `prevent_admin_access()`) exempts `admin-ajax.php` and `admin-post.php`, so other plugins' AJAX upload handlers and front-end paths still reach them.
   ```

3. Ultimate Multisite bullet.

   oldString:

   ```text
   inspect `wu_customers` dates/email domains to distinguish real sign-ups from team tests, keeping evidence private.
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   inspect `wu_customers` dates/email domains to distinguish real sign-ups from team tests, keeping evidence private. Then list which customers hold `upload_files` on a site of their own (`get_blogs_of_user()`, then the role on each site): the settings show what a sign-up could get; this shows who can upload now.
   ```

4. Tutor LMS bullet.

   oldString:

   ```text
   profile/cover photos enter the Media Library with sub-sizes for any logged-in user (`classes/User.php`).
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   profile/cover photos enter the Media Library with sub-sizes for any logged-in user (`classes/User.php` → `update_user_photo()` on `wp_ajax_tutor_user_photo_upload`: a nonce check that Tutor's front-end script data satisfies, and no capability check). It accepts only JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP by `getimagesize()`, so those decoders and the profiles embedded in them are what reach ImageMagick. Evidence of use: `_tutor_profile_photo`/`_tutor_cover_photo` user meta holds the attachment ID, and `sizes` in that attachment's metadata shows the editor ran.
   ```

5. Fluent Forms Pro bullet.

   oldString:

   ```text
   - **Fluent Forms Pro**: `src/Uploader.php` → `copyToWpMedia()` invokes the editor only for the "Media Library" upload location, not the default location; record the installed version when rechecking.
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   - **Fluent Forms Pro 6.2.15**: `src/Uploader.php` → `copyToWpMedia()` invokes the editor for the "Media Library" upload location, not the default location. Post forms do too: `src/Components/Post/PostFormHandler.php` → `setFeaturedImage()` → `getAttachmentToImageUrl()` calls `wp_generate_attachment_metadata()`. Find post forms as `{prefix}fluentform_form_meta` rows with `meta_key = 'postFeeds'`. Record the installed version when rechecking.
   ```

6. A new bullet for guest handlers. Insert it on a new line straight after the bullet that starts `   - **No editor calls found**`, with the same three-space indent.

   ```text
      - **Guest (`wp_ajax_nopriv_`) upload handlers**: check that the nonce a handler verifies is ever created and printed to visitors. Simple Feature Requests 2.4.9.6 registers `wp_ajax_nopriv_sfr_set_feature_request_attachments` (`inc/class-ajax.php`: `wp_handle_upload()`, then `wp_generate_attachment_metadata()`) and checks `sfr-attachment-nonce`. Its front-end script sends `sfr_vars.attachment_nonce`, but the free build never creates that nonce (`inc/class-assets.php` localises only `sfr-nonce`) and its attachment features are premium-only, so the handler is closed there. Recheck when the premium version is installed.
   ```

7. Evidence step.

   oldString:

   ```text
   Author 0 images are usually imports;
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   Author 0 images are usually imports or made by code (for example WooCommerce's placeholder image or a site icon);
   ```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The WooCommerce bullet names the `admin-ajax.php` exemption.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "exempts `admin-ajax.php` and `admin-post.php`"
    path: ".agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md"
  ```

- [ ] The Fluent Forms Pro bullet names post forms and `postFeeds`; the guest-handler bullet and the Ultimate Multisite site-owner check are present.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "rg -q 'PostFormHandler' .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md && rg -q \"meta_key = 'postFeeds'\" .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md && rg -q 'Guest \\(`wp_ajax_nopriv_`\\) upload handlers' .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md && rg -q 'get_blogs_of_user' .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md"
  ```

- [ ] The incorrect "only" claim is gone.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "invokes the editor only for the"
    path: ".agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] The section still names no sites, hostnames or accounts, and the repository's markdown checks pass for the file.

title: t18696: Credential aliases and explicit provider defaults resolve at secret injection
body:
## Task


Make credential cleanup safe: declared aliases and explicit provider defaults resolve at injection time, so an old name keeps working while a canonical name is introduced, without any rename. Phase 2 of #34680 (guarantees 2, 4, 9).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make credential cleanup safe: declared aliases and explicit provider defaults resolve at injection time, so an old name keeps working while a canonical name is introduced, without any rename. Phase 2 of #34680 (guarantees 2, 4, 9).

## Why

Renaming a stored secret silently breaks scripts, deployments and scheduled jobs that use the old name. Tools also assume one unlabelled variable (e.g. `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`), which today can only be satisfied by creating a hidden default.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_store.py`: add `resolve-name NAME`, which returns the stored canonical name for an alias. When NAME is a provider's conventional default variable (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, ...) and is not itself stored, it returns the explicitly declared default credential.
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` `build_secret_env`: when a specifically requested name is not stored, resolve it through the registry and emit the resolved value under the requested name. `run` (inject all) also emits declared aliases of injected credentials. `get` and `check` resolve the same way, so the dispatch capability gate agrees with injection.
- Never infer a default: without an explicit `defaults.<provider>` entry, the bare variable stays unavailable.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_store.py`
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory.py`
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With `CLOUDFLARE_ACME_API_TOKEN` stored and the alias `CLOUDFLARE_DOMAINS_API_TOKEN` declared, `aidevops secret CLOUDFLARE_DOMAINS_API_TOKEN -- sh -c 'test -n "$CLOUDFLARE_DOMAINS_API_TOKEN"'` succeeds and output stays redacted.
- [ ] With `defaults.cloudflare` set, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` resolves to it. With no default, or an explicit null, the request fails exactly as it does today.
- [ ] Installs without a registry behave byte-identically (`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh` passes).

## Verification

<details>

## What

Make credential consumers default-aware: onboarding and MCP validation report the registry's declared Cloudflare default (or its explicit absence) instead of assuming one unlabelled `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. Phase 4 of #34680 (guarantee 4).

Replace the setup hint (line ~881) with `aidevops secret set NAME --provider cloudflare --account REF` plus `aidevops secret default cloudflare NAME`.

<details>

## Task Brief

## What

Consolidate the conflicting credential naming guidance into one convention for new names. Every session records account metadata at creation time, even for a provider's first and only account. Phase 7 of #34680 (guarantees 1, 8).

## Why

Five patterns are documented today:

- `gopass.md:76` `<PROVIDER>_<KIND>_<ACCOUNT>`;
- `gopass.md:97-98` `<PROVIDER>_<ORG>_<PURPOSE>_*`;
- `api-key-setup.md:84` lowercase `-<account>`;
- `site-inventory.json.txt:20-21` `CLOUDFLARE_EXAMPLE_API_TOKEN`;
- `cloudflare.md:66` `AI-Assistant-DevOps-[AccountName]`.

The bare-name single-account default (`gopass.md:89`) leaves earlier credentials ambiguous once a second account arrives.

The bare conventional variable is never stored directly; it resolves only through an explicit `aidevops secret default`.
- Existing names stay valid; point to `aidevops secret organise` and aliases instead of renames.
- Dashboard token label: `aidevops-<account>-<purpose>`, recorded as the credential `purpose`.
- Keep the token label/value pair rule (`*_TOKEN_NAME`/`*_ACCESS_TOKEN`) as a kind suffix.

title: t18700: Read-only Cloudflare credential verification, drift report and resource ownership lookup
body:
## Task


Add explicitly invoked, read-only provider verification and drift reporting, starting with Cloudflare, plus offline resource-ownership lookup. Phase 5 of #34680 (guarantees 3, 5, 6).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add explicitly invoked, read-only provider verification and drift reporting, starting with Cloudflare, plus offline resource-ownership lookup. Phase 5 of #34680 (guarantees 3, 5, 6).

## Why

Recorded facts must be checkable against the provider: overlapping tokens, never-expiring tokens and leftover "moved" zones went unnoticed and caused a session to read the wrong account's data. The site inventory's `dns.account_ref` is hand-maintained and never checked.

## How

- New `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_cloudflare.py`. Calls are read-only and stdlib `urllib`:
  - token verify (status, expiry);
  - accounts;
  - paginated zones (name, account, status);
  - best-effort Workers scripts, Pages projects and R2 buckets per account, where 403 is recorded as `unreadable`.
- `secret-helper.sh verify cloudflare [NAME...]` injects each token through the existing `cmd_run_specific` path (value never in argv, output redacted). It caches `last_verified` and the observed resources in the registry: account names plus SHA-256 ID fingerprints, never raw IDs.
- New `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_drift.py`. `secret drift` works offline from the registry and cache. It reports:
  - missing or never expiry;
  - expiry within 30 days;
  - tokens with identical or overlapping reach;
  - zones visible in more than one account;
  - registry account mismatches;
  - stale verification;
  - stored-but-undescribed credentials;
  - an undeclared default.

  `secret owner RESOURCE` answers from the cache, or returns `unknown`.
- `.agents/scripts/site-context-helper.sh`: when `dns.account_ref` is absent from `dns_accounts`, resolve it from the credential registry's `provider_accounts`. Existing inventories are unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_cloudflare.py`
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_drift.py`
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory.py`
- `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_store.py`
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/site-context-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/site-operations.md`
- `.agents/tools/credentials/credential-inventory.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `aidevops secret drift --json` reports never-expiring tokens, overlapping reach and multi-account zones from cached data with no network access.
- [ ] `aidevops secret owner example.com` returns the owning account and credentials from the cache, or `unknown`; it never guesses.
- [ ] The verifier performs only GET requests, never prints or stores token values or raw account IDs, and runs only on explicit invocation.
- [ ] `site-context-helper.sh validate` and `lookup` behave unchanged for inventories that use `dns_accounts`.

## Verification

Run drift and owner against a cached-data fixture. Exercise the verifier against a live read-only token when available; otherwise run it against recorded API-shaped fixtures, marked as such. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-site-context-helper.sh`; shellcheck; py_compile.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Add `aidevops secret organise`: a guided, plan-first path for an install whose credentials are already inconsistent. It drafts registry entries and aliases and shows dependents, but never renames or deletes anything. Phase 6 of #34680 (guarantees 8, 9).

## Why

Cleaning up after the fact is risky: renames silently disable features, and some consumers can't be found by name. Operators therefore leave the mess in place and it grows.

## How

- New `.agents/scripts/credential_inventory_organise.py`. It combines the names-only `secret-helper.sh inventory`, the registry and the verifier cache, and proposes:
  - draft records for undescribed secrets (provider inferred from a known prefix, `confirmed: false`, evidence noted);
  - account refs from the verified account names;
  - aliases rather than renames for duplicate or overlapping tokens;
  - a default decision per provider;
  - a dependents count per credential.
- `--apply-drafts` writes only `confirmed: false` draft metadata. It never changes secret values, never renames and never deletes.
- Output text or `--json`. Delegate from `secret-helper.sh`.

title: docs: hostinger.md audit notes: disabled functions differ per PHP version; add PHP options and linked-library checks
body:
## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-15
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Follow-up to #34594 and PR #34691. A recheck of the same shared hosting account, while answering "are PHP and its extensions current?", found one line in `### Read-only audit notes` that is true only for one PHP version, and two checks the notes lack.

## What

Make three exact edits to `### Read-only audit notes` in `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`: correct the disabled-functions line, add the other PHP options seen in the same files, and add a check for the libraries linked into each PHP build. Name no sites, hostnames or accounts.

## Why

- The notes say `proc_open()` is disabled. It was for PHP 8.5, the shell default. PHP 8.3 on the same account left it enabled, because each PHP version has its own options file (`~/.cl.selector/alt_phpXX.cfg`). An audit that checks only the default PHP will miss this for sites on another version.
- The same files set `expose_php=On`, so every response names the exact PHP version, and set upload limits of 12 GB, which WordPress uses as its upload limit.
- Asked whether PHP is current, an audit checks PHP and its extensions. Every PHP build here links OpenSSL 1.1.1w, which has had no public fixes since September 2023, and libxml2 2.10.2. WPVulnerability does not check either, so the audit needs its own step.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Three verbatim edits (one replacement, two insertions) in one documentation file, with exact text below. No design decision is left.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` (`### Read-only audit notes`, about lines 89–105)

### Implementation Steps

Use exact string matching. Keep the list's indentation.

1. Replace the disabled-functions bullet.

   oldString:

   ```text
   - **Disabled PHP functions**: Both `shell_exec()` and `proc_open()` are disabled. The latter already prevents `wp db query`; calling either in `wp eval` ends in WordPress's “critical error” message.
   ```

   newString:

   ```text
   - **Disabled PHP functions**: The list is set per PHP version (CloudLinux PHP Selector options in `~/.cl.selector/alt_phpXX.cfg`), so check each version a site runs, for example `/opt/alt/php83/usr/bin/php -r 'echo ini_get("disable_functions"), PHP_EOL;'`. Observed: PHP 8.5 (the shell default) disabled both `shell_exec()` and `proc_open()`; PHP 8.3 on the same account disabled `shell_exec()` but not `proc_open()`. Without `proc_open()`, `wp db query` fails; calling a disabled function in `wp eval` ends in WordPress's “critical error” message.
   - **Other PHP options**: the same files held `expose_php=On`, so every PHP response's `X-Powered-By` header names the exact PHP version, and `upload_max_filesize` and `post_max_size` of `12288M`, which WordPress uses as its upload limit unless something lowers it (`upload_size_limit` filter).
   ```

2. Insert this bullet on a new line straight before the bullet that starts `- **Site PHP builds**`, at the same (top-level) indent:

   ```text
   - **Libraries linked into PHP**: `/opt/alt/php85/usr/bin/php -r 'echo OPENSSL_VERSION_TEXT, " | curl ", curl_version()["version"], " | libxml ", LIBXML_DOTTED_VERSION, PHP_EOL;'`, and the same for each PHP version in use. Observed on PHP 8.3 and 8.5: OpenSSL 1.1.1w (the last public 1.1.1 release; upstream support ended in September 2023), curl 8.22.0 linked to it, libxml2 2.10.2, ICU 71.1 and zlib 1.2.11. A version string does not show backported fixes, so ask the host whether these builds carry them. WPVulnerability's server checks cover PHP, the web server, the database, ImageMagick, curl, Memcached, Redis and SQLite, not OpenSSL, libxml2 or Ghostscript.
   ```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The disabled-functions bullet says the list is per PHP version and records the PHP 8.3 difference; the old "Both … are disabled" sentence is gone.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "rg -q 'PHP 8.3 on the same account disabled' .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md && ! rg -q 'Both `shell_exec\\(\\)` and `proc_open\\(\\)` are disabled' .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md"
  ```

- [ ] The other-options and linked-libraries bullets are present.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "rg -q 'expose_php=On' .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md && rg -q 'OPENSSL_VERSION_TEXT' .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md"
  ```

- [ ] The section names no sites, hostnames or accounts, and the repository's markdown checks pass for the file.

title: fix(pulse-merge): bot author app/dependabot permission lookup 404s as transient api-failure, starving green Dependabot PRs
body:
## What

Green Dependabot PRs never merge or enter lifecycle reconciliation. The merge pass looks up collaborator permission for author login `app/dependabot`. GitHub has no such route, so the lookup returns 404. The pulse classifies that failure as a transient `api-failure` (rc=2) and skips the PR on every pass.

## Evidence (pulse.log, repeated on every merge pass for many hours)

```
[pulse-wrapper] check_permission_failure_pr: transient permission failure for PR #34641 in marcusquinn/aidevops (HTTP unknown, reason api-failure) — no comment, merge skipped this pass
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #34641 in marcusquinn/aidevops — permission check failed for author app/dependabot (HTTP unknown, reason api-failure)
```

- `gh pr view 34641 --json author` returns `app/dependabot`. PR #34641 is green, MERGEABLE and not a draft.
- `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/collaborators/app/dependabot/permission` returns `Not Found (HTTP 404)`. The `/` in the login splits the REST path.

## Root cause

In `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`, `_pm_gate_author_trust()` (around lines 479-521) returns early when `_is_collaborator_author` returns rc=2 (lines 493-497). That happens before the trusted-Dependabot branch at line 499 (`_is_trusted_dependabot_update_pr`). The Dependabot branch would normally route to crypto-approval or `_pm_gate_route_ineligible_author` worker intake. Bot authors therefore never reach the Dependabot lifecycle, and the "transient" classification means the skip never escalates.

## How to fix

1. Normalise bot logins before the permission lookup. Map `app/<name>` to `<name>[bot]`, or treat `app/*` / `*[bot]` authors as bot authors that skip the collaborator-permission API. Likely location: `_pulse_author_permission_lookup` / `_is_collaborator_author` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-author-checks.sh` (~line 196).
2. Alternatively, in `_pm_gate_author_trust()`, evaluate `_is_trusted_dependabot_update_pr` before the rc=2 early return when the author is a bot identity. Keep the existing `#aidevops:trust-boundary` semantics: Dependabot remains external and still needs current-head maintainer crypto approval, or it routes to worker intake.
3. Keep fail-closed behaviour for genuine transient failures on human authors.

Reference pattern: the existing Dependabot branch in the same function (lines 499-512), plus `trusted-dependabot-lib.sh`.

## Verification

- Run the existing tests: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-gates-role-guard.sh`.
- Live check: after deploy, the next merge pass should log either the Dependabot crypto-approval path or `routed to worker intake (GH#30351)` for PR #34641. It should no longer log `permission check failed for author app/dependabot`.
- ShellCheck must report zero violations on the changed files.
