title: fix(release): recover-aggregate rebuilds a missing authorization record from the fenced lane
body:
## What

`aidevops release recover-aggregate` fails silently (exit 1, no message) when the per-PR release authorization record is absent, even though the release lane still holds the fenced authorization the original run resolved.

## Evidence

Pinned recovery of unpublished v3.39.31 (lane source #34603, reviewed aggregate #34690 pinned via `--aggregate-commit`, from #34743):

- Every earlier check passes under xtrace: signed-tag validation, pinned resolver (mode `aggregate`, all 39 manifest sources), receipt, tag-source subset, and absence on all channels.
- It then stops in `_full_loop_recovery_begin_state_transaction` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`). `_full_loop_read_release_authorization` returns 2 because `~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-release/<repo>-34603.authorization.json` was never written on this host.
- The lane `executor` identity is foreign to this host (`release-lane-owner.py observe` → `missing-or-foreign-identity`). The lane is `remote-publication` with `snapshot_manifest_bound: true`, and its `expected_sources` holds the original 7-source authorization.
- Nothing was mutated: lane, local tag and remote are unchanged.

## Fix

In `_full_loop_recovery_begin_state_transaction`, when the authorization read returns 2 (absent):

- Rebuild the previous authorization from the lane's `expected_sources`. Do this only when the lane is active, in `remote-publication`, has the same `source_pr` and `tag`, has no terminal receipt, and its set is a `release_authorization_subset` of the reviewed aggregate.
- Persist it with `_full_loop_persist_release_authorization`, print one stderr line naming the reconstruction, then continue the normal CAS transaction.
- Every other read failure still fails closed. Also print a reason on this silent-failure path.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` — `_full_loop_recovery_begin_state_transaction`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` — add a case for an absent authorization record (reconstructs from a matching lane; refuses a mismatched source, tag or phase)
- `.agents/reference/release-aggregation-recovery.md` — note under Preconditions

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts
- Production: rerun the pinned v3.39.31 recovery

title: fix(release): recover-aggregate replaces a foreign-signed provisional tag and retries an unchanged committing transaction
body:
## What

`aidevops release recover-aggregate` cannot replace a provisional aggregate tag signed by another collaborator's host, and a failed attempt then blocks every retry.

## Evidence (v3.39.31 / #34603, pin #34690 `b44b336c`)

1. The first pinned run, after #34747, passed the authorization rebuild, provenance, and version consistency checks. The lane moved to `aggregate-publication-committing`, then the run exited 1 with no diagnostic. The tag stayed at provisional object `a1af8e65`.
2. `git verify-tag v3.39.31` exits 1 with `Good "git" signature with ED25519 key SHA256:AB+ky… No principal matched`. The provisional tag was signed by collaborator `alex-solovyev`, whose key is not in this host's `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile`, and he has no GitHub SSH signing keys. `replace_unpublished_aggregate_tag` (`.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`) runs `git verify-tag "$tag_name" || return 1` on the original object before replacement, so it fails silently.
3. The retry exits 1 within 17s. In `_full_loop_release_recover_aggregate` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`), the `transaction` case calls `_full_loop_recovery_tag_is_bound_to_current_aggregate`. That check compares the tag parent with the tag's own Source-Merge trailer, so it is always true. `_full_loop_recovery_transition_durable_publication` then returns 1 because the tag object still equals the provisional one, and the branch returns 1 instead of retrying. The message "fenced transaction was retained for idempotent retry" is therefore false.

## Fix

- `replace_unpublished_aggregate_tag`: authenticate the *original* object by identity instead of local trust. It must be an annotated tag whose object id equals the caller-supplied fenced `original_object` and that is absent from every remote. Keep `git verify-tag` for the *replacement* tag, which this host signs. The provisional is only deleted and kept for restore, never published or trusted.
- `_full_loop_release_recover_aggregate`, `transaction` case: when the current tag object still equals the lane's `provisional_tag_object`, fall through to the normal prepare → begin (`load_existing_state_transaction` accepts the committing phase) → version-manager path. `_version_manager_claim_aggregate_lane` is already idempotent for the committing phase with the same token.
- Make the silent `return 1` sites name their refusal on stderr.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` — `replace_unpublished_aggregate_tag`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` — `_full_loop_release_recover_aggregate`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-main-fallback.sh` (existing suites)

## Verification

- Existing suites pass; ShellCheck is clean.
- Production: rerun the pinned v3.39.31 recovery. It must replace `a1af8e65` with a locally signed tag on a bump commit over `b44b336c`, then queue/publish.

title: fix(release): stage protected release tag in a commit envelope GitHub accepts
body:
## What

Protected-main release recovery cannot stage the signed tag. `_version_manager_stage_protected_tag` pushes the annotated **tag object** to `refs/aidevops/release-tags/<tag>`. GitHub rejects every annotated tag object at a non-`refs/tags/` ref with `remote: fatal error in commit_refs`. The step therefore always fails on GitHub, and every protected-main release that needs a provenance PR stops before the PR is queued.

## Evidence (v3.39.31 / #34603, pin #34690 `b44b336c`)

1. After #34750 was deployed, `recover-aggregate` produced release commit `d775c265` (parent `b44b336c`) and tag object `391ff2e1`. It pushed recovery head `92b66f2f` to `chore/release-v3.39.31-provenance`. Then `_version_manager_stage_protected_tag` returned 1 (`version-manager-protected-main.sh:663-664`).
2. A probe pushed an existing published tag object (`b1fc09b0`, `v3.39.30`) to `refs/aidevops/probe-34749/tag-object`. GitHub rejected it: `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)` / `remote: fatal error in commit_refs`.
3. A commit (`c3271d3b`) pushed to the same namespace was accepted, then deleted. The namespace is valid; only tag objects are rejected.
4. The tests use a local bare remote, which accepts tag objects at any ref. That is why #34636 passed CI but fails against GitHub.

## Fix

Stage the signed tag inside a **commit envelope**: an unsigned commit whose tree holds one blob, `tag`, containing the exact raw tag bytes (`git cat-file tag <obj>`). The envelope's parent is the signed release commit, so the target stays fetchable. Recovery fetches the staging ref, writes the blob with `git hash-object -t tag -w --stdin`, and accepts it only if the hash equals the pinned `tag-object` from the PR's provenance marker. Content addressing keeps the guarantee that only the exact signed bytes can be restored.

Files:
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh` — `_version_manager_stage_protected_tag`: build and push the envelope with create-only CAS. For an existing ref, decode it and require the exact object. Add a shared decode helper.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:416-419` — decode the fetched envelope instead of using `FETCH_HEAD` as the tag.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-main-fallback.sh:237`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh:87` — assert the envelope contract.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-main-fallback.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-discovery.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- ShellCheck on changed scripts
- Live: resume the v3.39.31 pinned recovery. The envelope push must be accepted, and the provenance PR must be queued.

title: fix(release): replace stale PR-less provenance branch left by a failed protected release retry
body:
## What

A failed protected-main release retry leaves an orphan provenance branch that blocks the next retry. `_version_manager_prepare_protected_release_head` pushes `chore/release-vX.Y.Z-provenance` before the staging and PR steps. If a later step fails, aggregate recovery rolls the tag back to its provisional object, but the pushed branch stays on the remote. The next retry signs a new release commit (new SHA). It then finds the old branch, fails `_version_manager_verify_recovery_head`, and stops with "Existing protected release branch has incompatible provenance".

## Reproducer (observed, v3.39.31 / #34603)

1. A recovery run pushed `chore/release-v3.39.31-provenance` @ `92b66f2f`, which contained release commit `d775c265`. It then failed at tag staging (#34753), and `restore_unpublished_aggregate_tag` restored provisional tag `a1af8e65`.
2. The branch remained with no open PR. A retry would have failed the provenance check. I deleted it by hand before the successful retry, which then queued #34755 and published v3.39.31.

## Fix direction

When the branch exists, has **no open PR**, and its head does not contain the current release commit, treat it as stale. Replace it with a lease on the observed SHA (`--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<observed>`) while the aggregate lane fence is held. An open or merged PR with that head must still fail closed. Alternatively, delete the branch during failed-recovery rollback when the CAS still matches.

Files:
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-protected-main.sh` — `_version_manager_prepare_protected_release_head` (existing-branch branch, ~line 323)
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` — `restore_unpublished_aggregate_tag` rollback

title: fix(pulse): runner_capability_unmet drafts stall at status:blocked instead of continuing on a capable runner
body:
## Description

Recent worker issues stall permanently at `status:blocked` after a worker finishes the implementation, pushes a draft PR and stops with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=runner_capability_unmet`. The affected runner has the aidevops ShellCheck wrapper on PATH but no real ShellCheck binary, and no markdownlint. Every affected issue shares blocker fingerprint `0738181c7fb715c10ad8e589`.

Affected open examples: #34731 (draft #34752), #34727 (draft #34728), #34617 (draft #34618), #34703 (draft #34707).

## Root cause

1. **Over-broad blocker contract.** `_worker_headless_contract_blocker_text` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` tells workers to stop with `runner_capability_unmet` whenever any required verification tool is missing. ShellCheck and markdownlint also run in CI (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`; `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` is a required check). Their absence on one runner is not a reason to hold finished work.
2. **Contradictory projection.** The release comment says `Projected state: status:available` and "do not impose a global issue hold", but `_hrff_project_post_release_state` → `clear_active_status_on_release` in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` projects every open draft as `status:blocked`. `status:blocked` issues leave the dispatch candidate set, so neither the GH#33654 exact-head continuation nor the GH#33132 attention record ever runs. Nothing re-arms the issue.
3. **No continuation path.** `_PCC_STALL_RELEASE_PATTERN` in `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` excludes every `blocked` release. A runner-local capability gap does not need a brief correction or approval, so a capable runner should continue the exact head.

## Fix

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`: a missing static linter whose check CI also runs is a CI handoff (mark ready, name the CI job), not a terminal blocker. `runner_capability_unmet` stays for tools with no CI equivalent.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`: optional draft projection argument for `clear_active_status_on_release` (default unchanged: `blocked`).
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`: runner-capability releases project an open draft as `status:available`, as the release comment already promises.
- `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: a `blocked` release with the runner-capability terminal blocker line qualifies for the existing bounded exact-head continuation (one automatic attempt per head, then the attention record).
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`: document the behaviour.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-pr.sh`
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts

title: fix(release): unsuppressed jq 'Cannot index string with string "key"' noise on the release run path
body:
## Description

`aidevops release patch 34547 incremental` (v3.39.32, 2026-10-15) printed an unsuppressed jq error three times, but the release succeeded and queued protected release PR #34761:

```text
jq: error (at <stdin>:1): Cannot index string with string ("key")
```

Where it appeared in the release output:

1. Before the first `RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-existing-guard` line, in the `aidevops release` / `full-loop-release-helper.sh` startup path.
2. Right after `Creating release with patch version bump...` and before `Verifying release worktree HEAD is exactly origin/main...` (`.agents/scripts/version-manager.sh:609-624`).
3. Right after `Committed version changes` and before `Creating git tag: v3.39.32` (`version-manager-git.sh:634` → `version-manager-release.sh:349`).

`aidevops release status 34547` did **not** print the error, so the source is on the release-run path only.

## Reproducer

Run `aidevops release <type> <merged-pr> incremental` from a linked worktree and capture stderr. To find the call site, run with `bash -x` / `BASH_XTRACEFS` and search for the jq call just before each error line.

## Leads already ruled out

- `assert_release_linked_worktree`, `verify_remote_sync`, `_release_contains_efficiency_change`: no jq.
- `shared-gh-request-state.sh` `.key` reads: stderr is already redirected to `/dev/null`.
- No `ssh_signing_keys`/`gpg_keys` API lookups exist in scripts.

The error shape means a jq filter applies `.key` to string values. Typical causes are `.[] | .key` over an object, such as a GitHub error `{"message": ...}`, or over an array of strings. The likely culprit is a gh or wrapper call shared by the run path and the commit/tag path (pre-commit hook, tag signing, gh call recorder).

## Files to modify

Unknown until traced; start with `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/version-manager.sh`, `.agents/scripts/version-manager-git.sh`, `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`, and any sourced gh wrapper/recorder.

## Acceptance

- The release run path emits no jq errors; the filter guards the input type (e.g. `objects | .key` or `type == "object"`) or the malformed input is fixed at its source.
- `shellcheck` is clean on changed scripts; existing release tests (`test-version-manager-*.sh`, `test-full-loop-release-*.sh`) pass.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/release-signing-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-signing-preflight.sh`

Tracing identifies `_release_signing_registered_keys`: failed private API stdout is retained before the public fallback, so GitHub error JSON reaches the signing-key jq filters. Verify with the existing signing preflight test, ShellCheck on both changed scripts, and the existing version-manager/full-loop-release suites.

title: canonical sync: untracked non-colliding file blocks fast-forward-current; sync-mirror restore rolls HEAD back
body:
## Observed

Interactive post-merge canonical sync, aidevops v3.39.32. The canonical checkout
was on `main`, matched `origin/main`, and had exactly one untracked,
non-conflicting file in the repo root (an image unrelated to the PR).

1. `full-loop-helper.sh merge` printed `CANONICAL_SYNC_NEXT=canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror ...`.
2. `canonical-recovery-helper.sh sync-mirror --repo <canonical> --issue N --confirm SYNCHRONIZE_CANONICAL_MIRROR`
   moved the untracked file into
   `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/dirty-main-backups/<id>/untracked/`.
   The file was no longer in the checkout.
3. The printed `RESTORE_COMMAND` (`dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh restore ... --confirm RESTORE_DIRTY_WORKTREE_BACKUP`)
   restored the file. It also reset canonical `HEAD` to the pre-sync SHA, so
   the checkout was behind `origin/main` by the merge commit and the sync was
   undone.
4. `canonical-recovery-helper.sh fast-forward-current ... --confirm FAST_FORWARD_CANONICAL_BRANCH`
   refused with `BLOCKED: canonical worktree is not clean`, even though the
   only dirt was one untracked file that the fast-forward does not touch.

Workaround used: run `sync-mirror` again, then copy the file back from the
backup directory by hand.

## Expected

- `fast-forward-current` should accept untracked files that don't collide
  with any path in the incoming commits, since a fast-forward cannot overwrite
  them. Git itself refuses a merge when an untracked file would be
  overwritten.
- A restore offered as the follow-up to a sync should not roll back the
  synchronized `HEAD`. Possible approaches: a `restore --files-only` mode,
  or have the restore re-apply the preserved dirt on top of the current
  `HEAD`.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`: the `fast-forward-current`
  cleanliness check and the `sync-mirror` untracked handling.
- `.agents/scripts/dirty-worktree-backup-helper.sh`: the `restore` command's
  HEAD handling.
- `reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`: document the expected
  behaviour.

## Verification

In a temporary repo, add one untracked, non-colliding file, push a commit to
the remote, then:

- `fast-forward-current` should succeed and leave the file in place.
- `sync-mirror` followed by `restore` should leave `HEAD` equal to
  `origin/<branch>` with the file present.

title: fix(worker-lifecycle): runtime-owned verified BLOCKED exits to stop audit alerts and blocked→available redispatch loops
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Outcome

When a headless worker stops with `BLOCKED`, the runtime records that stop as one verified operation. Three things follow: (1) the gh-audit anomaly scanner stops filing alerts for that exit; (2) the dependency unblockers stop moving the issue back to `status:available` until the blocker's wake condition is met; (3) any missing runner secret names it reports become dispatch gates.

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-15
- **Session:** opencode:interactive
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Root-cause analysis of GH Audit Anomaly alerts #34534 and #34764. Both came from the same private-repo issue (redacted), which a worker blocked, a peer runner's pulse unblocked, and a second worker blocked again on the same missing runner configuration. Investigation evidence: #34764 (closing comment) and #34534 (comments).

## Why

The worker `BLOCKED` exit is free-form. The model posts a prose checkpoint comment and hand-edits labels through the generic `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit` (audit caller `main`, empty `flags`). The runtime's `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` record is a separate, conditional step. Two downstream consumers then infer intent from text heuristics:

1. **Audit noise.** Without verified provenance, every progress-to-blocked exit is a `protected_label_removed:status:in-progress` alert, and each one costs a human forensic pass (#34361, #34534, #34764). By design (`reference/gh-audit-log.md` "Worked example: worker exit transitions"), generic removals must not be suppressed by destination label. The fix is provenance, not suppression. This mirrors the review-handoff fix in #34614 / PR #34616.
2. **Redispatch loop.** Observed timeline (UTC):
   - 2026-10-13 04:15: a worker posted a prose "checkpoint: BLOCKED" comment and set `status:blocked` itself. No `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment and no unassign followed, so the runtime release never ran.
   - 2026-10-14 14:11: a peer runner's pulse moved the issue `status:blocked` → `status:available` in one edit, with no comment. That matches `pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_refresh_try_unblock_issue` or `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` `_der_try_unblock`. The body's prose prerequisites had closed, and no recognised non-dependency marker existed.
   - 14:15–14:22: the worker was redispatched, failed on the same missing configuration, and the redundant alert #34764 followed.
   - Separately, `_should_defer_auto_unblock` in `pulse-dep-graph.sh` reads only the **last 10** trusted comments (`.[-10:]`). One dispatch attempt posts about 5 ops comments (DISPATCH_CLAIM, DISPATCH_LEASE ×2–3, "Dispatching worker", CLAIM_RELEASED). So even a correct `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` marker falls out of that window after about two attempts.
3. **Missing gate.** The real blocker was a runner configuration name absent from the issue's declared secret names, so the runner-capability gate could not stop dispatch.

## Reproducer

These are observed production events. Exact private identifiers are omitted; they are summarised in the comments on #34764 and #34534.

1. A headless worker on a managed private repo ends with a prose checkpoint comment containing "BLOCKED" (no `**BLOCKED**…cannot proceed`, no `BLOCKED:` final signal). It runs `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit N --remove-label status:in-progress --add-label status:blocked`.
   - Result: the audit entry has `caller_function: main` and `flags: {}`, and the next scan files an anomaly alert (#34534).
   - No `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment and no unassign follow.
2. The issue body's prose prerequisites later close. A peer runner's pulse edits `status:blocked` → `status:available` in a single label edit with no comment. No trusted comment matches `_PULSE_DEP_GRAPH_NON_DEP_BLOCK_MARKERS` or `_der_has_hold`.
3. The pulse redispatches the issue. The worker fails on the same missing runner configuration within 7 minutes and hand-edits the labels again (anomaly alert #34764). This time the runtime does post `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`.
4. Code-level reproduction of the window defect: `pulse-dep-graph.sh:475-484` applies `.[-10:]` to trusted comments. Seed a fixture in `test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh` with one `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` followed by 10 ops comments (DISPATCH_CLAIM / DISPATCH_LEASE). `_should_defer_auto_unblock` returns 1, meaning it allows the unblock.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** Changes span the headless-runtime release path, two independent unblock paths and a trust-boundary audit exemption (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`). Each step must fail closed, and mixed-version runners keep producing old-shape events.

## How (Approach)

### Implementation Steps

**Phase A: runtime-owned, verified blocked exit (audit provenance)**

1. Make the runtime, not the model, own the `status:in-progress` → `status:blocked` projection on `reason=blocked`. Read `_release_dispatch_claim` and `_hrff_project_post_release_state` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:675-800`) and `clear_active_status_on_release` (`.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:1559`). Route the blocked projection through one named function that calls `gh_issue_edit_safe`. Call it only after `_hrff_post_claim_released_comment` has persisted the release.
2. In `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`, follow the `_issue_review_handoff` / `pr_review_handoff_verified` pattern (lines 303-324). Set `flags.worker_blocked_exit_verified = "v1-release-persisted"` only when all of these hold:
   - the caller function is that named function in `headless-runtime-failure.sh`;
   - live GitHub state shows the issue open, with `status:blocked`, without `status:in-progress`/`status:queued`/`status:claimed`;
   - a trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` comment newer than the latest `DISPATCH_CLAIM` exists.

   Mark the check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
3. Add `expected_worker_blocked_exit_transition` to `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`, modelled on `expected_full_loop_review_transition`, and wire it into the final `select`. It requires:
   - `comparable_state`;
   - `framework_script("headless-runtime-failure.sh")`;
   - the flag above;
   - `suspicious == ["protected_label_removed:status:in-progress"]`;
   - `labels_removed == ["status:in-progress"]` and `labels_added == ["status:blocked"]`;
   - zero title/body deltas.

   Pass any new script-name arg through `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh` if the filter needs one.
4. Stop workers hand-editing lifecycle labels. In `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh` `main`, for `issue:edit` only, refuse with exit 2 and a one-line pointer when all of these hold:
   - a headless worker context is present (`WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER`, see `headless-runtime-failure.sh:391`);
   - the target equals that issue;
   - the args add or remove any `status:*` label.

   The pointer says: "emit `BLOCKED: <reason>`; the runtime projects lifecycle state". Do not affect `issue review-handoff`, `full-loop-helper-commit.sh` `_label_issue_in_review`, or non-`status:*` edits. Add one line to `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` near line 105.

**Phase B: a blocked exit always persists its release**

5. Reproduce the 2026-10-13 shape in the existing release test fixtures:
   - the final model output carries a prose checkpoint heading with "BLOCKED" but no `BLOCKED:` signal;
   - the worker already set `status:blocked`;
   - a merged non-closing (`For #N`) checkpoint PR exists.

   Determine from `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh` classification which path skipped the release. Fix it so that if the live issue ends the session with `status:blocked` and this attempt has posted no `CLAIM_RELEASED`, the runtime posts `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` with the terminal-blocker fragment. If the root cause is not knowable from code, record the evidence in the PR and implement the label-state backstop anyway.

**Phase C: unblockers honour the structured blocker regardless of comment position**

6. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_should_defer_auto_unblock` (lines 451-494), replace the `.[-10:]` window for structured markers. Defer when the newest trusted `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` / `aidevops:terminal-blocker-(observation|circuit)` record is newer than the newest `DISPATCH_CLAIM`, however many comments follow. Reuse the predicate already in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:57` rather than a third regex. Keep the existing free-text markers and the `.[-10:]` window for them.
7. Verify `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` `_der_has_hold` / `DER_TERMINAL_BLOCKER_RE` already treats that structured record as a hold across all trusted comments. Change it only if a fixture proves otherwise. Release remains owned by `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` recovery (brief revision or authorised retry directive), not by prerequisite closure.

**Phase D: missing runner secret names become dispatch gates**

8. When the worker's terminal blocker names missing runner secret/config **names**, the runtime applies one `needs-secret:NAME` label per name, so `runner-capability-helper.sh` yields on runners without them. Never write values.
   - Before applying labels, check precedence. `reference/task-lifecycle.md:160-167` says labels win over the body marker, and `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh` also parses body `requires-secrets:`.
   - If adding labels would drop body-declared names, make the gate use the union of all declared sources.
   - Document the rule beside the existing paragraph.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`: Phases A1, B5, D8
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`: Phase B5 classification
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`: Phase A2 provenance
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`: Phase A3
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`: Phase A3 arg pass-through, if needed
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: Phase A4 guard
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`: Phase C6
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`: Phase C7, only if a fixture proves a gap
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: expose the shared predicate for C6
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`: Phase D8 union
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`: add the exemption to the "Anomaly Scanner" list
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`: lifecycle-label ownership line
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md`: secret-name precedence sentence
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:**
  - `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` reads the filter.
  - `pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_refresh_graph_repo` → `_refresh_try_unblock_issue` → `_should_defer_auto_unblock`.
  - `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure` and the stale sweep → `_der_try_unblock` → `_der_has_hold`.
  - `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `terminal_blocker_circuit_comment` / `_terminal_blocker_recovery` read the `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` records.
  - `approval-snapshot-v2.sh:109-113` and `pr-checkpoint-target-lib.sh:155-199` parse the exact `CLAIM_RELEASED` line format. Do not change that format.
- **Writers/mutation paths:**
  - `_release_dispatch_claim` → `_hrff_post_claim_released_comment` → `_hrff_project_post_release_state` → `clear_active_status_on_release`.
  - Generic `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit` (the worker hand-edit path being guarded).
  - `_refresh_try_unblock_issue` and `_der_try_unblock` (the unblock edits).
  - `runner-capability-helper.sh` claim-time gate.
- **Existing verification/tests:** the five test files under Files to Modify already encode these behaviours. Extend their fixtures rather than adding new harnesses. `test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` and `test-pulse-wrapper-terminal-blockers.sh` must stay green unchanged.
- **Schemas/config:** audit log `flags` gains one key. No config files change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh` deploys `.agents/` to `~/.aidevops/agents/`; nothing is generated.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none. Historical audit entries are never rewritten or backfilled (`reference/gh-audit-log.md`).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** no deletion or cleanup paths change. Rollback is a revert of the PR. The guard in `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`, the filter in `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq` and the defer predicate in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` are independent, so any one can be reverted alone. Issues held by Phase C are released through the existing `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `_terminal_blocker_recovery` path.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the unblockers already re-read labels before mutating. Keep that. The release comment must be persisted before the label projection (existing ordering at `headless-runtime-failure.sh:747-752`).
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored state changes.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners keep hand-editing labels and producing generic `main` audit entries. Those must still be reported, so the exemption requires the new flag. Older runners also post `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` in the existing format, which Phase C must honour.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a replayed release must not double-post (the existing `_hrff_post_claim_released_comment` retry semantics). The Phase B backstop must check for an existing release in this attempt first.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if the release comment fails to persist, keep the current fail-closed behaviour: retain lifecycle state and return 1.
- **Liveness:** Phase C makes holds stickier. Preserve the #34348 behaviour: issues blocked only by dependency prose, with no structured blocker record, still release when their declared blockers close.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh   # A2/A3: new flag exempted; generic main progress->blocked still reported
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh         # A1/B5: release persisted before projection; 2026-10-13 shape releases as blocked
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh           # C6: structured record older than 10 comments still defers
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh             # C7: hold honoured; prose-only dependency block still releases (#34348)
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh                       # D8: label + body names gate as a union
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh                # unchanged CLAIM_RELEASED format consumers
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh .agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh .agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** each command's comment names the phase and acceptance criterion it proves.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. No shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure changes.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:**
- Do not suppress generic `main` / empty-flag progress-to-blocked removals.
- Do not rewrite or backfill audit entries.
- Do not change the `CLAIM_RELEASED` line format.
- Never write secret values.
- Do not remove `no-auto-dispatch` from any issue.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (maintainer).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-safe-edit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-filter.jq`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`
- `.agents/reference/task-lifecycle.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A runtime blocked exit produces an audit entry with `flags.worker_blocked_exit_verified == "v1-release-persisted"`, and `gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan --dry-run` does not report it.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Negative: a generic `gh-write-helper.sh` / `main` edit removing `status:in-progress` and adding `status:blocked`, with empty flags, is still reported. So is a flagged entry with any title/body delta or extra label change.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-audit-anomaly-expected-transitions.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Inside a headless worker context, `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit <own-issue> --remove-label status:in-progress --add-label status:blocked` exits 2 with the pointer. `issue review-handoff`, full-loop `_label_issue_in_review` and non-`status:*` edits are unaffected.
- [ ] A worker session ending with the 2026-10-13 shape (prose BLOCKED checkpoint, worker-set `status:blocked`, merged `For #N` PR, no `BLOCKED:` signal) posts exactly one `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `pulse-dep-graph.sh` defers unblocking when the structured blocker record is newer than the latest `DISPATCH_CLAIM` but older than the 10 most recent comments, with all declared dependencies closed.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Negative / regression: an issue blocked only by declared dependencies with no structured blocker record is still released when they close (#34348 behaviour).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh"
  ```

- [ ] A blocker naming missing secret names results in `needs-secret:NAME` labels. A runner lacking either a label-declared or a body-declared name yields before claiming. No secret value appears in any comment, label or log.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `reference/gh-audit-log.md` lists the new exemption, and `reference/worker-discipline.md` states that the runtime owns lifecycle labels on blocked exits.
- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean: `shellcheck` on every changed `.sh` file reports zero violations.

## Context & Decisions

- Follow the #34614 / PR #34616 pattern: add verified provenance at the producing path plus an exact-shape filter. Do not loosen the filter.
- The runtime, not a new worker-invoked CLI, owns the transition. Workers already signal `BLOCKED:`. A second worker-facing command would recreate the free-form problem.
- Private repository names and issue numbers are deliberately omitted. The evidence is summarised in the comments on #34764 and #34534.

title: fix(pulse): runtime freshness flags non-runtime commit drift as high-severity stale runtime
body:
## What

`pulse-check-helper.sh json` reports the high-severity finding `pulse-runtime-stale` ("Merged Pulse fixes are not active in the local runtime") when the only commit between the deployed runtime and canonical `main` changes a file that Pulse does not use.

## Observed evidence (2026-10-16T00:08Z, daily pulse sweep)

- `runtime_freshness.status=deployed_behind_canonical`, `stale=true`, `auto_update_status=up_to_date`, `canonical_dirty=false`, `canonical_behind_upstream=false`.
- deployed_sha `8d49d33bf` = the v3.39.34 release merge; canonical/upstream `d15370b47`.
- `git rev-list --count 8d49d33..d15370b` = 1. That commit is `chore(deps): bump mcp (#34781)`. It changes only `.agents/configs/prospecting-requirements.txt`, which Pulse, dispatch and workers do not use.
- The recommended operator action is "Run setup.sh --stage ai-session from the canonical checkout". That would redeploy the runtime in the middle of a Pulse session without changing Pulse behaviour.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh` `_runtime_deployment_relation()` treats the deployment as current only when the trees are identical or the only changed path is `TODO.md` (`_runtime_commits_differ_only_by_todo`, precedent GH#31905). Any other drift falls through to `deployed_behind_canonical`, and `_runtime_freshness_json` labels that as stale.

## Proposed fix

Replace the TODO-only exemption with a narrow allowlist of paths that cannot affect runtime behaviour. Classify drift as stale only when changed paths match runtime-relevant prefixes, for example `.agents/scripts/`, `.agents/configs/` files consumed by pulse/dispatch, `.agents/prompts/`, `.agents/*.md` agent docs, `setup.sh`. Alternatively, keep the status as informational (severity low/medium) when the drift touches no `.agents/scripts/**` or pulse-consumed config. Do not weaken detection for script or prompt drift.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh`

Notes: in `pulse-current-state-helper.sh`, change `_runtime_commits_differ_only_by_todo` / `_runtime_deployment_relation` (lines ~75-104). In the test file, extend the existing stale-runtime case near line 512 with a non-runtime-path drift case that must report `current`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-helper.sh` passes. A commit touching only `.agents/configs/prospecting-requirements.txt` reports `runtime_freshness.status=current`, and a commit touching `.agents/scripts/*.sh` still reports `deployed_behind_canonical`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-current-state-helper.sh` is clean.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: fix(pulse): dep-graph reducer jq syntax fails on jq 1.7, freezing dependency cache and causing false blocked-by holds
body:
## What

On jq 1.7 (not 1.7.1+), `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` fails to compile. Every dependency-graph cache rebuild then fails for every repo. `build_dependency_graph_cache()` keeps the previous per-repo data and rewrites the cache file with a fresh mtime and `built_at`. As a result, the dependency graph has been frozen since the filter changed, while the cache still looks fresh. Closed blockers stay "open" in the cache, so `is_blocked_by_unresolved()` reports false `(cache: open)` dependency blocks, and the `available -> blocked` normalization runs on stale evidence.

## Observed evidence (runner alex-solovyev, 2026-10-16T00:10Z daily sweep)

- `jq --version` reports `jq-1.7`.
- Reproduction: `gh issue list --repo <slug> --state all --limit 500 --json number,title,body,labels,state` succeeds (500 issues), then `jq -c -f ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` fails with: `jq: error: syntax error, unexpected FIELD ... line 86: ).out) as $refs`.
- Minimal repro on jq 1.7: `jq -n 'reduce range(3) as $i ({a:0}; .a += $i).a'` gives a compile error. `jq -n '(reduce range(3) as $i ({a:0}; .a += $i)) | .a'` returns `3`. A postfix field directly on `reduce`/`foreach` is only accepted from jq 1.7.1.
- `pulse.log`: every `dep-graph-cache: built in Ns` line in the retained log comes after `preserved previous repo cache for <slug> after fetch/build failure` for all 3 pulse repos. No successful rebuild appears.
- Consequence: a managed-repo issue was repeatedly skipped with `is_blocked_by_unresolved: #N blocked by #M (cache: open)`, although `#M` was closed (NOT_PLANNED) a week earlier. In the same window the log shows 11 `dep-graph-cache: normalized #N ... available -> blocked` events that used the frozen graph.
- Introduced by commit `2227f6fcf` (GH#33881, 2026-10-07), lines 79-86 of the filter: `(reduce range(...) as $i ({...}; ...).out) as $refs`.

## Fix

1. In `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` `blocker_value_line`, wrap the reduce and pipe to the field, for example `((reduce range(0; $toks | length) as $i ({...}; ...)) | .out) as $refs`. Check the rest of the filter and the other `.jq`/inline jq programs for any further postfix-on-`reduce`/`foreach` uses.
2. Defence in depth in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `build_dependency_graph_cache()`: when a repo's data is preserved after a build failure, record per-repo freshness (for example `repos[slug].built_at` or `stale_since`). `_blocked_by_load_cache()` should then treat preserved data older than 2x TTL as `use_cache:false` (live lookup) instead of trusting an mtime that was refreshed by the failed rebuild. Also log the reducer failure reason; today it fails silently because of `2>/dev/null`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh`

## Verification

- On jq 1.7 (`jq-1.7` binary, for example the Ubuntu 24.04 `jq` package or the upstream 1.7 release): `printf '[{"number":3,"title":"x","body":"Blocked by: #2","labels":[],"state":"OPEN"}]' | jq -c -f .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq` succeeds, and `.blocked_by["3"].issue_nums == ["2"]`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-stale-label-cleanup.sh` pass.
- After deploy, `pulse.log` shows `dep-graph-cache: built in` without a preceding `preserved previous repo cache` for healthy repos.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` is clean.

title: bug(opencode-v2): scalar MCP timeout disables aidevops plugin and breaks Claude OAuth
body:
## Summary

On OpenCode V2, a scalar MCP timeout generated by aidevops causes native schema validation to disable the entire aidevops plugin. Claude OAuth requests then fail with misleading API-key errors even though the OAuth token itself is valid.

A small local adapter fix restored the plugin and a real Claude Sonnet request. This is a request to incorporate that compatibility fix upstream, not a claim that it has already shipped.

## Environment

- aidevops: **3.39.34**, source base `d15370b47`.
- OpenCode: symptoms observed on **2.0.28**; plugin failure and successful patched verification on **2.0.30**.
- OS: macOS, Apple Silicon.
- Provider: Anthropic / Claude OAuth; successful smoke check used Claude Sonnet 5.5.
- Date: October 15, 2026, local time.

## Observed failure

The initial symptoms after reconnecting Claude OAuth were `x-api-key header is required` and later `invalid x-api-key`. The aidevops diagnostic's live token test returned HTTP 200 from `/v1/models`, which did not verify the actual chat request pipeline.

After correcting the local V2 plugin registration, `opencode api plugin.list` reported:

```text
id: aidevops
status: failed
error: Plugin disabled after mcp.transform failed. Check server logs for details.
```

The relevant sanitized server-log cause was:

```text
disabled plugin after transform failure
plugin.id=aidevops state=mcp
Cause([Die(SchemaError(Expected object
  at ["timeout"]))])
```

## Root cause and target files

1. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/mcp-registry.mjs` defines a numeric execution timeout, including `timeout: 900_000`, and propagates it through `buildMcpConfigEntry`.
2. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-mcp-adapter.mjs`, `toV2McpConfig`, converts V1 enablement/environment fields but currently passes that timeout through unchanged.
3. The running V2 OpenAPI schema, `Mcp.LocalConfigEncoded`, requires `timeout` to be an object with optional positive-integer `startup`, `catalog`, and `execution` fields, not a number.
4. The native `mcp.transform` schema failure disables the plugin. Its provider OAuth hooks consequently do not remain available.

Keep the shared registry's V1 shape unchanged; normalize it at the existing V2 adapter boundary.

## Verified local fix

In `toV2McpConfig`, extract `timeout` alongside `enabled` and `env`, then add:

```js
...(timeout !== undefined ? {
  timeout: typeof timeout === "number" ? { execution: timeout } : timeout,
} : {}),
```

This preserves milliseconds, leaves absent timeout fields absent, and preserves already-structured V2 timeout settings. It does not turn a long tool-execution allowance into a long startup/catalog allowance.

Focused regression coverage was added locally to the existing `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`:

- `900_000` becomes `{ execution: 900_000 }`.
- An absent timeout remains absent.
- An existing `{ startup, catalog, execution }` object is preserved.
- The existing managed-MCP transform/toggle check rejects scalar timeouts at its simulated native schema boundary.

## Reproducer

1. Load aidevops through its packaged V2 entrypoint, `opencode-aidevops/v2-plugin`, using the V2 `plugins` configuration field. Ensure an old auto-loaded V1 plugin symlink is not also being loaded.
2. Use the managed MCP registry containing a numeric timeout; no external MCP connection is required to expose this schema mismatch.
3. Before the patch, inspect `opencode api plugin.list` at the affected location: aidevops is disabled with the timeout schema failure.
4. Apply the adapter normalization and reload the plugin (restart the service if it does not pick up the change).
5. Confirm exactly one aidevops plugin is **active** and no timeout schema failure is emitted.
6. Make an actual session-scoped Claude OAuth request, not only a token/models probe. It must succeed without adding a static API key.

## Local verification completed

- `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/v2-mcp-adapter.mjs` — passed.
- Adapter + on-demand MCP-agent suites — **26 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, using installed plugin dependencies.
- OAuth-auth-hook + V2 profile/context/subagent/TUI suites — **20 passed, 0 failed**.
- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` — all applicable changed-file checks passed, including secret checks.
- Running OpenCode 2.0.30 service: aidevops plugin **active**.
- Temporary Sonnet 5.5 session, via `session.generate`: returned exactly **`AUTH_OK`**. The temporary session was removed afterwards.

The working fix is local only; it has not been pushed, submitted as a PR, or released. No credentials, account emails, or private project paths are included here.

## Duplicate check / related work

Searched open and closed issues/PRs for `mcp.transform`, `Expected object` + `timeout`, `toV2McpConfig`, and MCP/V2 timeout and execution terms. No matching report or fix was found at filing time.

- Related V2 integration work: #31903; not a duplicate of this timeout schema failure.
- Historical OAuth/plugin-registration fix: #13298; the timeout failure persists even with correct V2 registration and is distinct.

## CI / scope

The proposed change is confined to the V2 adapter and existing focused tests. No workflow changes or release action are needed to reproduce or validate it. Prefer targeted local validation and one cohesive upstream patch; do not use push-triggered CI as a debugging loop. Use owned compute for qualification with no GitHub-hosted fallback; unavailable capacity blocks qualification rather than waiving required checks.

## Thanks

Thank you, Marcus (@marcusquinn), for aidevops and the work supporting the new OpenCode V2. The framework has been valuable, and I hope this verified diagnosis and small fix help make the V2 transition smoother for everyone.

title: fix(pulse-dependabot): intake issue creation fails where tier:standard label is missing; log shows INFO line instead of gh error
body:
## What

`pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` fails to create the worker issue for an ineligible Dependabot PR in any repository that lacks the `tier:standard` label, and the log hides the real error.

## Evidence

- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: 22 repeats for two Dependabot PRs in one managed repo and repeats in a second managed repo, each `worker issue creation failed:  [INFO] auto-dispatch label present     skipping self-assignment per t2157`.
- Both affected repos had `dependencies`, `auto-dispatch` and `origin:worker`, but no `tier:standard` (one had only `tier:thinking`, the other only `tier:simple`). A repo with all three tier labels does not show the failure.
- After `label-sync-helper.sh sync --repo <slug>` created the canonical labels in one of them, the failing precondition is gone.

## Cause

1. `_pulse_dependabot_create_intake_issue` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` ~line 528) provisions only `_MANAGED_DEPENDABOT_INTAKE_LABEL_SPECS` (`dependencies`) from `.agents/scripts/managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh`, then creates the issue with `--label "auto-dispatch,origin:worker,tier:standard,dependencies"`. `gh issue create` rejects a missing label, so a repo without `tier:standard` never gets an intake issue.
2. `create_reason` takes `head -n 1` of the combined output; the first line is the t2157 `[INFO]` notice from `gh_create_issue`, so the real `gh` error is never logged (the t18546 / GH#33003 "log the gh error" goal is not met in this case).

## Fix

- Add `tier:standard` (and `auto-dispatch`, `origin:worker`, reusing the existing origin/approval specs and the canonical colours from `label-sync-helper.sh`) to the intake provisioning set, so every label passed to `gh_create_issue` is ensured first.
- Choose the failure reason from the last non-`[INFO]` line (or strip `[INFO]` lines) instead of the first line.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/managed-label-provisioning-lib.sh` (`_MANAGED_DEPENDABOT_INTAKE_LABEL_SPECS`)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` (`_pulse_dependabot_create_intake_issue`)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` (existing test asserts the one-line reason at ~line 238; extend its fixture so the label inventory lacks `tier:standard` and the reason line is the gh error, not the INFO line)

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dependabot-intake.sh` passes.
- ShellCheck clean on both scripts.
- In a repo without `tier:standard`, the next pulse cycle creates the intake issue (or logs the actual `gh` error).

title: full-loop merge: record qlty out-of-credits skip in PR body automatically; close-out must not ask the user
body:
## What

`reference/ci-gate-policy.md` rule 14 says: on private and organisation-owned repositories, skip a `qlty check` failing with "Qlty did not run because you are out of minutes", merge when other checks pass, and note the skipped check in the PR body. The merge and wait paths already classify it as advisory (GH#33640, GH#34085, GH#34309). The PR-body note is still left to the agent's memory. In an interactive full-loop on an organisation repository, the agent merged correctly but left out the note. Its close-out then asked the user whether to top up or remove Qlty, which the policy already decides.

## Fix

Make the note deterministic. When `full-loop-helper.sh merge` (or its pre-merge gate) classifies a non-required `qlty check` as out-of-credits on a limited repository, it appends one idempotent `## Skipped checks` line to the PR body before merging. Use the existing PR-body edit path that keeps the signature footer (`gh-write-helper.sh pr edit`), and mark the line with an HTML comment so a replay does not duplicate it. Also add one line to the close-out guidance (`reference/session.md` "What next") saying that skips classified by policy are not user asks.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` (merge path; find where the qlty out-of-credits classification result is available, for example the helper used for GH#34085)
- `.agents/reference/session.md` ("What next" block guidance)
- Existing tests for the qlty classification, if present, for the idempotent append

## Verification

- On a PR whose only failing check is the qlty out-of-credits status, `full-loop-helper.sh merge` merges and the PR body has exactly one `Skipped checks` qlty line, even after a second run.
- ShellCheck is clean, and the existing qlty classification tests pass.

title: claim-task-id.sh allocates duplicate IDs when an explicitly configured counter_branch is stale
body:
## Observed

In a managed project repo, the gitignored per-checkout `.aidevops.json` pinned `"counter_branch": "develop"`, while other sessions and workers allocated from the dedicated `task-id-counter` branch. `claim-task-id.sh` honoured the explicit config without any staleness check:

- `develop:.task-counter` = 18592; `task-id-counter:.task-counter` = 18602.
- The claim returned `t18592`, which already existed as a closed issue (and t18596–t18601 existed too). The CAS push also advanced `develop`'s stale counter.
- Rerunning with `--counter-branch task-id-counter` correctly allocated t18602.

So an explicit-but-stale counter branch silently hands out duplicate task IDs.

## Expected

Before allocating from an explicitly configured counter branch, compare it against (a) the dedicated `task-id-counter` branch when it exists and (b) the highest `tNNN` in the default branch's TODO.md. If the configured counter is behind either, fail closed (exit 4, `counter_branch_stale`) with guidance to switch to the leading branch or run `--sync-counter-branch`, instead of allocating a duplicate ID.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — `_load_project_config` / counter-branch resolution (explicit config path skips the `resolve_implicit_counter_branch` staleness check).
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` — CAS allocation; add the pre-allocation staleness comparison here.
- Reference pattern: the existing implicit-branch staleness refusal in `resolve_implicit_counter_branch` (GH#33152).

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/` claim-task-id tests: a sandbox with explicit `counter_branch=develop` behind `task-id-counter` must exit 4 without pushing; an up-to-date explicit branch must still allocate normally.
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.

title: t18704: Guard V2 MCP adapter output against the OpenCode V2 Mcp config schema shape
body:
**Task ID:** `t18704` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~40m`
**Logged:** 2026-10-16
**Tags:** `enhancement` `opencode` `interactive` `auto-dispatch`

## Outcome

Guard V2 MCP adapter output against the OpenCode V2 Mcp config schema shape

## Done when

- [ ] Every server emitted by the production V2 transform in the toggle test is checked against the pinned `Mcp.LocalConfig`/`Mcp.RemoteConfig` field types, and the test passes on current main.
- [ ] The helper exists and names its V2 source.
- [ ] Regression guarantee: a scalar `timeout` (the GH#34785 shape) or a leaked V1 `enabled`/`env` key makes the guard fail with the server name; the V1 registry test `test-seo-utils-mcp-registry.mjs` still passes unchanged.
- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`).

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
# 1. The production path is already exercised here (createV2McpRuntime -> initialize -> transforms[0](editor)):
rg -n "V2 MCP toggles reuse one transform" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs

# 2. Pinned V2 shape, extracted from the installed OpenCode V2 2.0.3 binary (Effect Schema classes).
#    Unknown keys are not the concern; wrong types on known keys are.
#    Mcp.LocalConfig:  type:"local"; command:string[] (required); cwd?:string;
#                      environment?:Record<string,string>; disabled?:boolean;
#                      codemode?:boolean; timeout?:Mcp.TimeoutConfig
#    Mcp.RemoteConfig: type:"remote"; url:string (required); headers?:Record<string,string>;
#                      oauth?:Mcp.OAuthConfig | false; disabled?:boolean; codemode?:boolean;
#                      timeout?:Mcp.TimeoutConfig
#    Mcp.TimeoutConfig: startup?, catalog?, execution? — positive integer milliseconds
#    Mcp.OAuthConfig:  client_id?, client_secret?, scope?, redirect_uri?: string;
#                      callback_port?: integer 1..65535
# Re-extract if the V2 runtime changes:
rg -a -o --max-count 1 'class [a-z0-9]+ extends rt\("Mcp\.(Local|Remote|Timeout)Config"\)\(\{.{0,400}' \
  ~/.aidevops/runtimes/opencode-v2/runtime/node_modules/@opencode/cli-darwin-arm64/bin/opencode
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` — add a module-level `assertV2McpConfigShape(name, server)` helper and call it for every value after the first `transforms[0](editor)` in the "V2 MCP toggles reuse one transform and apply the latest override" test. Replace the timeout-only loop added by PR #34789 (`// Every managed server must match the V2 Mcp.TimeoutConfig object shape.`) with the general helper; keep the explicit `seo-utils` `{ execution: 900_000 }` assertion.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** only the test file above; `toV2McpConfig` (`v2-mcp-adapter.mjs:7`) and `buildMcpConfigEntry` (`mcp-registry.mjs:756`) are read, not changed.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A — no production code changes. If the guard finds a real mismatch, fix it in `toV2McpConfig` (V2 boundary), never in the V1 registry shape, and record that in the PR.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs` ("V1 MCP enablement maps to V2 disabled semantics", "V2 MCP toggles ..."), `tests/test-seo-utils-mcp-registry.mjs` (pins the V1 scalar timeout; must stay green).
- **Schemas/config:** the pinned V2 shape lives in the test helper with a comment naming the source (`Mcp.LocalConfig`/`Mcp.RemoteConfig`, OpenCode V2 2.0.3) and the re-extraction command above.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** N/A — tests are not deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/` as runtime code.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the change is test-only; no stored config or user data is rewritten.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the single commit touching `tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the helper near the top of the test file (after imports):

```js
// Pinned from OpenCode V2 2.0.3 Mcp.LocalConfig / Mcp.RemoteConfig (GH#34785).
// A wrong type on any known field makes V2 disable the whole plugin.
function assertV2McpConfigShape(name, server) {
  const isStringRecord = (value) => value && typeof value === "object" && !Array.isArray(value)
    && Object.values(value).every((entry) => typeof entry === "string");
  const isPositiveInt = (value) => Number.isInteger(value) && value > 0;
  assert.ok(server.type === "local" || server.type === "remote", `${name}.type`);
  if (server.type === "local") {
    assert.ok(Array.isArray(server.command) && server.command.every((part) => typeof part === "string"), `${name}.command`);
    if (server.cwd !== undefined) assert.equal(typeof server.cwd, "string", `${name}.cwd`);
    if (server.environment !== undefined) assert.ok(isStringRecord(server.environment), `${name}.environment`);
  } else {
    assert.equal(typeof server.url, "string", `${name}.url`);
    if (server.headers !== undefined) assert.ok(isStringRecord(server.headers), `${name}.headers`);
    // oauth: object (Mcp.OAuthConfig) or literal false
  }
  for (const key of ["disabled", "codemode"]) {
    if (server[key] !== undefined) assert.equal(typeof server[key], "boolean", `${name}.${key}`);
  }
  if (server.timeout !== undefined) {
    // object with only startup/catalog/execution, each a positive integer
  }
  // Also assert V1-only keys never leak: `enabled`, `env`.
}
```

2. In the toggle test, after the first `transforms[0](editor);`, call `assertV2McpConfigShape(name, server)` for every entry in `values`, replacing the timeout-only loop.
3. Run the verification commands below. If the guard fails on a real server, fix `toV2McpConfig` at the V2 boundary in the same PR and say so in the PR body.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A — synchronous test assertions only.
- **Migration/rollback:** N/A — single test commit, trivial revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** the V1 registry shape is unchanged; `test-seo-utils-mcp-registry.mjs` must stay green to prove it.
- **Idempotency/retry:** N/A — pure assertions.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** N/A.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-opencode-v2-adapter.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-seo-utils-mcp-registry.mjs
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Negative proof (manual, not committed):** temporarily revert the `timeout` mapping in `toV2McpConfig` and confirm the guard fails naming `seo-utils.timeout`, then restore it.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change the V1 registry entry shape in `mcp-registry.mjs`; do not add new test runners, harnesses or fixtures.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (maintainer)

body:
## Task


Correct the "Shared image library" bullet in `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`. It says customers can disable `imagick` per website in hPanel's PHP Configuration. On the observed account, a PHP extension switch applies to every website on the account that uses the same PHP version, so turning `imagick` off for one website also turns it off for the others on that version.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Correct the "Shared image library" bullet in `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`. It says customers can disable `imagick` per website in hPanel's PHP Configuration. On the observed account, a PHP extension switch applies to every website on the account that uses the same PHP version, so turning `imagick` off for one website also turns it off for the others on that version.

## Why

Evidence from one Hostinger Cloud account, 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-16:

- `GET /api/hosting/v1/accounts/{username}/websites/{domain}/php/details` for two PHP 8.3 websites returned the same extension set, and both `php/php-info` outputs read `/opt/alt/php83/etc/php.ini` and `/opt/alt/php83/link/conf`.
- `PATCH .../websites/{domain}/php/extensions` with `{"enable":["memcached"]}` for one PHP 8.5 website enabled memcached for every PHP 8.5 website; the same call for a PHP 8.1 website applied to PHP 8.1 on the account. CloudLinux keeps extension settings per account and PHP version.
- One exception: a website that had just switched PHP version lacked memcached while the others on that version kept it, and enabling it again for that website fixed it. So the scope needs checking per site, not assuming.

Following the current text nearly disabled `imagick` for a second production site that relies on it for PDF previews and HEIC conversion.

## How

Replace the per-website sentence: the switch (hPanel PHP Configuration, or `PATCH .../php/extensions` with `disable`) has applied to every website on the account using that PHP version; before turning `imagick` off, list the websites on that version, decide for all of them, and check each one afterwards (`php/details`, or a temporary web PHP file). To stop one WordPress site using ImageMagick without touching the others, filter `wp_image_editors` to GD editors only; direct `new Imagick()` calls in plugins are not covered.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

## Acceptance

- The bullet no longer says `imagick` can be disabled per website; it gives the account-and-PHP-version scope, the per-site check and the WordPress-level alternative.
- The repository's markdown checks pass for the file.

title: worktree add fails on receipt-lock timeout while another add scans ~3k cleanup receipts under the lock
body:
## Observed

On a host with 2,932 receipt files in `~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup/`, interactive worktree creation in a project repo failed twice in a row while pulse workers were creating worktrees (aidevops v3.39.34 interactive, v3.39.36 workers):

- `pre-edit-check.sh` loop-mode auto-create printed `Cleanup-receipt reconciliation refused: could not acquire the receipt lock for ~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup`, then `WORKTREE_COLLISION=creation_failed`. The worktree was rolled back, but the branch it had just created (`feature/auto-<timestamp>`, pointing at the base commit) was left behind.
- Retrying with `worktree-helper.sh add <that branch>` failed the same way (`AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_LIFECYCLE_DISPOSITION=RECONCILIATION_FAILED … status=1`).
- At that moment `.mutation.lock.d/owner` named a live headless worker's `worktree-helper.sh add feature/auto-…-ghNNN --issue NNN`, and the lock directory had been held for at least 64 seconds. A third attempt, made after the lock was released, succeeded.

## Cause (from reading the deployed scripts)

- `_full_loop_receipt_lock_acquire` (`full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:454-495`) waits at most 200 × 0.05 s = 10 s for a live owner, then fails.
- `full_loop_supersede_cleaned_receipts_for_recreated_worktree` (`:991-1063`) holds that lock across two per-file loops:
  - `_full_loop_valid_receipt_file_count` (`:734-747`) runs `jq -e 'type == "object"'` once per receipt (`:316-321`).
  - `_full_loop_active_recreated_receipts_are_cleaned` (`:767-787`) runs `jq` at least once more per receipt.
- With ~3k receipts that is roughly 6k `jq` processes inside the critical section, so the hold time is several times every waiter's 10 s budget. `_full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree_unlocked` (`:667`) already uses a single `jq` pass, so it is not the bottleneck.
- Hold time grows with the receipt count and contention grows with pulse concurrency, so interactive sessions starve behind workers.

## Suggested fix

- Shrink the critical section: replace both per-file loops with single `jq` invocations over all receipts (the pattern `_full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree_unlocked` already uses, with its per-file fallback for malformed JSON), or validate before taking the lock and revalidate only the selected receipts under it.
- Prune or archive receipts in terminal states (cleaned or superseded) past a retention window, so the scanned set stays bounded.
- Retry the whole reconciliation with jittered backoff, or size the acquire budget to the expected hold time, before failing worktree creation.
- When loop-mode auto-create fails after creating its branch, delete that branch if it still points at the base with no new commits, or print it as the explicit continuation target, so retries do not accumulate orphan `feature/auto-*` branches.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`: lock acquire, receipt count, active-receipt check and supersede path.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`: reconciliation failure handling (`:1322-1341`).
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`: loop-mode auto-create failure output (`:540-560`) and branch cleanup on failure.

## Verification

- With ≥3k receipts and a concurrent `worktree-helper.sh add` in another process, a second `add` succeeds (after waiting if needed) instead of failing with `RECONCILIATION_FAILED`.
- Measure the lock hold time of `full_loop_supersede_cleaned_receipts_for_recreated_worktree` with 3k receipts before and after the change; afterwards it should be well inside the acquire budget.
- After a forced reconciliation failure in loop-mode auto-create, no orphan branch remains, or the output names it as the continuation target.

title: cloudron-package-monitor: follow commit-pinned upstreams that publish no releases or tags
body:
## What

`cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh upstream` can only follow upstreams that publish stable semantic-version releases or tags. Add a commit mode for packages that pin an upstream commit because the upstream publishes neither.

## Why

`PhialsBasement/LibreCrawl` (packaged as `marcusquinn/cloudron-librecrawl-app`) has 0 releases and 0 tags. The package pins a commit: `Dockerfile` `ARG LIBRECRAWL_COMMIT=<40-char sha>`, manifest `upstreamVersion: "05a1372"` (7-char short SHA).

A dry run with `monitor_upstream: true` and `upstream_slug: PhialsBasement/LibreCrawl` (temporary `AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE`, no `--apply`) exits non-zero:

```
ERROR: No stable semantic releases tag for PhialsBasement/LibreCrawl matches cloudron_package.upstream_tag_prefixes ["v",""]; configure the tag streams or publish a matching stable release.
```

`_cloudron_monitor_run` counts that entry as a failure, so the whole daily run returns 1 for as long as the package is enabled. That can mask real failures in other packages. Workaround in use: `monitor_upstream: false`. Upstream changes to such packages then go unnoticed.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-package-monitor-helper.sh`: accept `upstream_source: "commits"` in `_cloudron_monitor_upstream_entry` (currently `releases` or `tags` only, line ~492), with an optional `upstream_branch` (default: the upstream repository's default branch). Read the branch head with `gh api repos/<upstream>/commits/<branch>`. Compare with the package manifest's `upstreamVersion`, treated as a SHA prefix of at least 7 characters. When the head is not a match, apply one deduplicated finding fingerprinted by the head SHA (same `_cloudron_monitor_apply_finding` path), including the head date and first line of the message. Report semver tags/releases unchanged.
- Validate `upstreamVersion` as a hex SHA prefix in commit mode; fail closed with a diagnostic otherwise.
- `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`: document `upstream_source: "commits"` and `upstream_branch` in the `cloudron_package` table.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cloudron-package-monitor.sh`: cover head equal to the pin (no finding), a moved head (one finding, same fingerprint on rerun), and a non-SHA `upstreamVersion` (fail closed).

## Acceptance

- With `upstream_source: "commits"`, a package whose `upstreamVersion` matches the upstream branch head exits 0 with no finding; a moved head produces one deduplicated finding.
- Existing `releases`/`tags` behaviour and tests are unchanged.

## Related observation

The package's `repos.json` entry was registered on 2026-10-14, before `CloudronManifest.json` was added. On 2026-10-16 (framework 3.39.33) it still had no `app_type` or `cloudron_package`, so neither monitor covered it until it was set by hand. The re-registration path that would add these defaults has not been traced.

title: secret set succeeds but check/list miss exports in tenant-loader credentials.sh
body:
## Verified defect

With the plaintext credentials fallback and a tenant-loader `credentials.sh`,
`aidevops secret set EXAMPLE_TOKEN` reports success but subsequent
`aidevops secret check EXAMPLE_TOKEN` exits 1 and `secret list` omits the name.

Names-only inspection established all three conditions simultaneously:

- The top-level credentials file contains a direct `export EXAMPLE_TOKEN=...` entry.
- The same file contains the `AIDEVOPS_ACTIVE_TENANT=` loader marker.
- No tenant credentials file contains that entry.

No secret values were printed. A targeted in-memory read of the one requested
entry allowed the operator's separate application task to complete safely.

## Root cause / files

Target `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`, particularly `resolve_credential_files`,
the plaintext `_store_credential` path, and set/check/list/specific-name injection.
In the inspected deployed version, `resolve_credential_files` returns only tenant
files when the loader marker is present, whereas storing appends to the top-level
credentials file. Writer and reader therefore disagree about custody.

## Requested repair

Make successful storage immediately discoverable through check/list and named
subprocess injection in tenant-loader mode. Preserve explicit tenant custody,
deterministic precedence and authoritative gopass behavior. Choose and document
the intended writer/read resolution policy; do not simply source the loader,
execute shell content, or silently broaden cross-tenant access.

Do not rewrite real user credential stores during development or print secret
values in diagnostics. Preserve file permissions, locking, quoting and atomicity.

## Verification

Extend the existing secret-helper fixtures using a temporary HOME and synthetic
values. Exact existing test filename has not been verified; locate the relevant
secret-helper tests before editing.

- Reproduce set → direct export in a tenant loader → check/list/injection mismatch.
- After repair, set succeeds, check exits 0, list contains only the key name, and
  a named child process can assert the expected value without printing it.
- Cover single-file mode, active/inactive tenants, duplicate names, existing
  loader exports, quoted values and unset names; assert documented precedence.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior for gopass-owned unreadable entries.
- Run the relevant existing fixtures and ShellCheck on modified shell helpers.

Observed in aidevops 3.39.27 on Linux. No customer identifiers, secret bytes or
private project paths are included in this report.
