title: receipt lock: stuck worktree-helper remove held .mutation.lock.d ~14 min; subshell holders are recorded as the parent PID
body:
## What

One `worktree-helper.sh remove` process, started by the profile-readme routine, held the global cleanup-receipt lock (`~/.aidevops/state/full-loop-cleanup/.mutation.lock.d`) for about 14 minutes while it was idle. During that window every `worktree-helper.sh add`/`remove`, `pre-edit-check.sh` worktree auto-create and `full-loop-helper.sh adopt-merged-receipt` on the host failed with `receipt-lock-timeout`. The lock freed by itself at about 05:31Z, and the next `adopt-merged-receipt` succeeded at once.

This is a different failure from #34803. PR #34804 bounds receipt-reconciliation scan time. It does not change how the lock records its owner, how long a holder may keep it, or when waiters may reclaim it.

## Evidence (2026-10-16, macOS, Bash 5.3, runtime bundle 3.39.36)

- From about 05:17Z to 05:31Z, the lock `owner` file named the remove process.
- While it held the lock, the process had no child processes. It used 0.01 s of CPU in 10 s (`ps` TIME 0:00.37 → 0:00.38). `sample` put 807/807 samples in `read_comsub → zread → read`, so it was waiting for EOF from a `$(...)` whose producer was no longer its child.
- The remove then printed `Worktree removal refused … Reason: git-metadata-unreadable` (`worktree-helper-cmds.sh:140`). Before that, the routine log showed repeated `native Git repository probe timed out` (`canonical_git_repository.py:32`) for the same repository.
- Once the lock was released, no orphaned `git` or probe process remained, so the process holding the pipe open could not be identified after the fact.

## Code facts

1. `full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:467` writes `$$` as the lock owner. Inside a command substitution, `$$` is the PID of the top-level shell, not the subshell. `worktree-helper-cmds.sh:444` takes the lock inside `$(full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree …)`. The stale-owner check at `full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:483` (`kill -0 "$owner_pid"`) therefore treats the lock as live while the parent lives, even if the subshell holding it has died without releasing it.
2. `_full_loop_receipt_lock_acquire` (`full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:454-495`) has no maximum hold time or lease, so a holder that is alive but stuck blocks every waiter. Waiters give up after about 10 s (200 × `sleep 0.05`) with a generic `receipt-lock-timeout`. The message names neither the holder nor how long it has held the lock. `adopt-merged-receipt` then reports this as an ownership conflict (already noted in #34803).

## How

- Record the real holder: the holding subshell's own PID plus its process start time. Bash 3.2 has no `$BASHPID`, so a portable form is `sh -c 'echo "$PPID"'`. Make the stale check compare both values, so a dead subshell holder can be reclaimed while its parent lives.
- On the remove path, do not take the global lock inside a command substitution. Return the receipt path through a variable instead of `$(...)`, or release from a trap scoped to the holding subshell.
- Name the holder and hold age in the failure, for example `receipt-lock-timeout (holder <pid>, held <N>s)`. Consider a bounded maximum hold, with reclaim only when the holder is verifiably not making progress.

Functions in scope: `_full_loop_receipt_lock_acquire`, `_full_loop_receipt_lock_release` and `full_loop_cleanup_receipt_for_worktree` in the receipt library, plus the remove path around `worktree-helper-cmds.sh:444`. Unknown: which command substitution blocked; its producer was gone by the time it was inspected.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-cmds.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`

## Verification

- Regression: acquire the lock inside `$(...)`, then SIGKILL that subshell while the parent sleeps. A second process must acquire the lock within the waiter budget. This fails before the fix.
- A waiter blocked by a live holder reports the holder PID and hold age.
- `shellcheck` reports no violations on the edited scripts, and `test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` passes.

title: feat(hetzner-helper): snapshot, action-status, metrics commands and HCLOUD_TOKEN_<PROJECT> credential support
body:
## What

Extend `.agents/scripts/hetzner-helper.sh` with snapshot, action-status and metrics commands, and let it read per-project tokens stored as `HCLOUD_TOKEN_<PROJECT>` in the aidevops credential store.

## Why

During a multi-server OS-upgrade session the agent needed provider snapshots before each upgrade and a way to see whether a host was still working while SSH was down (sshd restarts during `do-release-upgrade`). The `hcloud` CLI was not installed, and `hetzner-helper.sh` only reads `api_token` values from its JSON config, so it could not use the `HCLOUD_TOKEN_*` entries already present in `credentials.sh`. The OpenCode shell policy also blocks `source`, so the agent had to write throwaway Python that parsed the credentials file. That is fragile and should be a supported helper path.

Observed API calls that worked:

- `POST /v1/servers/{id}/actions/create_image` with `{"type":"snapshot","description":...,"labels":{...}}`
- `GET /v1/images?type=snapshot&label_selector=...` (poll until `status=available`)
- `GET /v1/servers/{id}/metrics?type=cpu,disk&start=...&end=...&step=60` (CPU and disk-write bursts showed the upgrade was progressing while SSH refused connections)
- `GET /v1/servers?name=...` for `public_net.ipv6.ip`. The assigned /64 exposed a stale IPv6 address configured on the host.

## How

- In `.agents/scripts/hetzner-helper.sh` add subcommands: `snapshot-create <project> <server> <description> [label=value]`, `snapshot-list <project> [label-selector]`, `snapshot-delete <project> <image-id>` (destructive: require confirmation flag), `action-status <project> <action-id>`, `metrics <project> <server> [minutes]`, `server-net <project> <server>`.
- Token resolution order: existing JSON config, then `HCLOUD_TOKEN_<PROJECT_UPPER>` from the environment or `aidevops secret` / `credentials.sh` without printing the value.
- Follow `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` (explicit returns, `local var="$1"`), ShellCheck clean.
- Document the commands in the Hetzner section of `.agents/aidevops/services.md` (or the existing Hetzner reference).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/hetzner-helper.sh`
- `.agents/services/hosting/hetzner.md`

## Acceptance

- `hetzner-helper.sh snapshot-list <project>` works with only `HCLOUD_TOKEN_<PROJECT>` configured.
- Snapshot delete requires an explicit confirmation flag.
- Tokens are never echoed; ShellCheck reports zero violations.

## Verification

Run `shellcheck .agents/scripts/hetzner-helper.sh`, then `hetzner-helper.sh snapshot-list <project>` and `hetzner-helper.sh metrics <project> <server> 10` against a test project.

title: feat(cloudron-helper): fleet health check detecting failed box/mysql, stale backups, full disk and pending migrations
body:
## What

Add a Cloudron fleet health check (routine-ready) that detects a dead platform on a Cloudron host even when the dashboard looks "up", and alerts the operator.

## Why

A Cloudron server ran for **39 days** with `box.service` failed (systemd start timeout after an interrupted auto-update) and `mysql.service` failed for 20 days. The root filesystem was 100% full and an unattended package run was left half-configured (`mysql-server-8.0` unpacked but not configured). Nobody noticed because the host's mail container kept running and the dashboard returned an nginx error page that external monitoring didn't treat as down. Pending DB migrations (`Unknown column ... in field list`) blocked recovery until `box/setup/start.sh` was re-run. Auto-updates and backups silently stopped for the whole period.

## How

- Add a `health` (or `fleet-health`) subcommand to `.agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh` that, per configured server over SSH alias:
  - `systemctl is-active box mysql docker nginx unbound` and `systemctl --failed`
  - `df` root usage threshold (warn 85%, critical 95%)
  - `dpkg --audit` non-empty -> warn
  - `cloudron-support --check-db-migrations` and `--check-services`
  - age of the newest successful backup (`SELECT max(creationTime) FROM box.backups WHERE state='normal'`) above a threshold -> critical
  - `curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/cloudron/status` returns a version
- Output a TOON/JSON summary with non-zero exit on critical findings, suitable for `/routine` scheduling (see `.agents/reference/routines.md`).
- Reference `docs/MONITORING`-style external monitoring guidance as a complement, not a replacement: an external HTTP check against `/api/v1/cloudron/status` expecting JSON would have caught this.

## Acceptance

- `cloudron-helper.sh health <server>` reports the six checks above and exits non-zero on box/mysql failure, stale backups or a full disk.
- A routine definition example is documented.
- ShellCheck clean; no secrets printed.

## Verification

Run against a healthy host (exit 0). Then simulate a failure by checking a stopped non-critical unit name via a test flag, or document a manual drill (stop `box` in a maintenance window, confirm critical exit, restart).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cloudron-helper.sh`
- `.agents/services/hosting/cloudron.md`

title: docs(cloudron): verified host OS-upgrade runbook (22.04->24.04->26.04) with Hetzner GRUB, network and API traps
body:
## What

Add a verified Cloudron host OS-upgrade runbook (Ubuntu 22.04 -> 24.04 -> 26.04) to the Cloudron server-ops knowledge, capturing the non-obvious failure modes observed while upgrading three production Cloudron servers on Hetzner Cloud.

## Why

The official Cloudron guides (`docs.cloudron.io/guides/upgrade-ubuntu-24` and `.../upgrade-ubuntu-26`) assume an interactive SSH session and a healthy host. In practice an agent hit several traps that are not in those guides and cost significant time or created real boot/network risk:

1. **Stale GRUB debconf device IDs cause an infinite prompt loop.** After a provider disk change, `grub-efi/install_devices` pointed at a by-id disk that no longer existed. `shim-signed` postinst -> `grub-multi-install --target=x86_64-efi` looped forever on the prompt even with `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`, hanging `dpkg --configure -a`. Fix: compare `debconf-show grub-efi-amd64 grub-pc` with `/dev/disk/by-id/` and correct with `debconf-set-selections` *before* any apt run.
2. **Hetzner Cloud x86 boots via BIOS but images ship only `grub-efi-amd64`** (+ `grub-pc-bin`). Package upgrades never refresh the BIOS core image in the `BIOS boot` partition. Run `grub-install --target=i386-pc /dev/sda && update-grub` after each release upgrade, before reboot. Detect with `test -d /sys/firmware/efi` (absent = BIOS).
3. **Legacy ifupdown vs netplan.** Old Hetzner images ship a cloud-init generated ifupdown config (`50-cloud-init.cfg` under the ifupdown `interfaces.d` directory). One host had a stale IPv6 /64 there (old address preferred as source -> all outbound IPv6 broken) duplicating a correct netplan config; another host is configured *only* by ifupdown while netplan targets a non-existent NIC name. ifupdown survived 22.04 -> 26.04 in testing, but the runbook must inventory which system owns eth0 before reboot and compare IPv6 with the provider API.
4. **Non-interactive release upgrade works** with a transient `systemd-run` unit (`--setenv=DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`, `StandardInput=null`, stdout/stderr appended to a root-owned log file) running `do-release-upgrade -f DistUpgradeViewNonInteractive`. It answers conffile prompts with "keep" (matching the guide's advice). Expect SSH on port 22 to refuse connections for 10-20 minutes during the configure phase; monitor via provider metrics and open ports, not by retrying SSH aggressively.
5. `do-release-upgrade` refuses until *all* updates are applied: use `apt-get dist-upgrade` (held-back packages) and explicitly install phased updates, then reboot if `reboot-required`.
6. **26.04 post-steps vary per host:** `sudo-rs` was installed on one host and not another; always check `sudo --version`. MySQL 8.0 is removed -> stop the `box` service, `apt install mysql-server` (installs 8.4), re-run Cloudron's box setup script (`box/setup/start.sh` in the Cloudron install tree), then start `box`, exactly as the official 26.04 guide lists.
7. **Hetzner snapshots exclude attached Volumes and CIFS Storage Boxes.** Cloudron app data on volumes is protected only by the Cloudron backup, so the backup must be fresh even when a snapshot exists.
8. **Agent safety rule:** never issue a reboot in the same parallel tool batch as package operations; an agent did this and interrupted a post-upgrade apt step (recovered, but avoidable).
9. **Cloudron API access gotchas:** Cloudron 10 CLI sessions can be invalidated by DB migrations (old `cloudron login` tokens return 401); Cloudron 10.1 stores `apiTokens.accessToken` as SHA-256; dashboards proxied by Cloudflare return `error code: 1010` to Python's default User-Agent (looks like a 403 auth failure but is not).
10. **TLS observation:** on 26.04 (OpenSSL 3.5.5, nginx 1.28.3) Cloudron's host nginx on 443 negotiates `X25519MLKEM768` by default with no Cloudron config change; on 24.04 (OpenSSL 3.0) it was refused. Classic X25519/P-256 remain accepted.

## How

title: Self-hosted DinD runners: Docker Hub anonymous pull limit (429) fails CI jobs; document a pull-through registry mirror and check it in status
body:
## What happened

On 2026-10-16, a private repository's CI ran on an operator's ephemeral DinD runner pool (`reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`: one runner container per job, each with its own inner `dockerd`). Its jobs failed before any test started:

```
docker: Error response from daemon: unknown: failed to resolve reference "docker.io/library/mariadb:10.6": unexpected status from HEAD request to https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/mariadb/manifests/10.6: 429 Too Many Requests
##[error]Process completed with exit code 125.
```

- Between 03:42 and 05:46 UTC, 6 CI runs failed: 3 pushes to `main` and 3 pull-request runs, one of them re-run.
- I read the logs of 10 failed jobs across all 6 runs, on all three runners in the pool. All 10 stopped at `docker run` with exit code 125. Nine logged Docker Hub `429 Too Many Requests`, for `mariadb:10.6` and `rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12`.
- None was a code failure. The same jobs passed whenever their pulls got through. Re-running the failed job about 20 minutes later failed the same way.
- `main` had no green CI run for over 1.5 hours. A merge had to rely on running the same job locally, where the images were already cached.

## Cause

The inner `dockerd` starts empty for every job, so no image is cached between jobs. Every job pulls its images from Docker Hub anonymously. The pool shares one public address, so a single CI run exceeds Docker Hub's anonymous pull limit: lint, three smoke tests and a release build, each pulling 2 to 4 images. Concurrent runs make it worse.

## Proposed fix

Framework side (worker-ready):

1. `.agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`: add a **Registry mirror** section to the DinD pool runbook:
   - Run one pull-through cache on the runner host: `registry:2` with `REGISTRY_PROXY_REMOTEURL=https://registry-1.docker.io`, optionally with a read-only Docker Hub token from `aidevops secret`.
   - Start each inner `dockerd` with `--registry-mirror=<host cache address>` from the `github-runner-dind-start` launch script.
   - Verify with a pull inside a job.
   - Name the alternative: authenticated pulls (`docker login` with a read-only token) raise the limit, but every job still pulls every image.
2. The runbook's troubleshooting table gets a row for `429 Too Many Requests` from `registry-1.docker.io`: check the mirror, or use authenticated pulls.
3. `.agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh status`: read-only, report whether the pool's runners have a registry mirror configured, and warn when they do not.

Operator side (cannot be done by a worker): run the cache on the host, add the mirror flag to the launch script, then restart runner instances gradually, as the runbook describes for other launch-script changes.

## Verification

- A CI run whose jobs pull 10 or more images in total finishes on the pool with no 429.
- `github-runner-org-helper.sh status` shows the mirror, and warns without one.
- ShellCheck is clean on changed scripts. The runbook keeps placeholders for private names.

## Files

- `.agents/reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md`
- `.agents/scripts/github-runner-org-helper.sh` (status output)
- The `github-runner-dind-start` example in the runbook. The real file is on the operator's host and is not in this repository.

title: Coolify helpers cannot discover an existing stored API token/instance (coolify-cli-helper SCRIPT_DIR unbound)
body:
## Observed

During an interactive Coolify provisioning task, the agent could not locate the Coolify API base URL and stopped to ask the owner, even though the URL already existed in sibling operator repos/runbooks on the same machine. Three framework defects contributed:

1. `.agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh` fails on every invocation, including `help`: line 17 runs `source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-constants.sh"` under `set -u` before line 19 assigns `readonly SCRIPT_DIR="$script_dir"`. Output: `line 17: SCRIPT_DIR: unbound variable`.
2. `.agents/scripts/coolify-helper.sh list` only reads `configs/coolify-config.json` and reports it missing. It has no fallback to an existing `COOLIFY_API_TOKEN` secret plus a recorded base URL, so a working, stored token is invisible to the helper path.
3. `aidevops secret describe COOLIFY_API_TOKEN` reports `not recorded`, and `secret resolve coolify` exits 4 (default undeclared). The credential registry therefore carries no base URL/account metadata for an existing provider token, so agents cannot discover which instance the token belongs to.

## Expected

- `coolify-cli-helper.sh help` works (use `$script_dir` on line 17, or assign `SCRIPT_DIR` first).
- Coolify helpers resolve the instance from the credential registry (`secret record COOLIFY_API_TOKEN --provider coolify --account <base-url>`) when the JSON config is absent.
- Discovery guidance (`tools/deployment/coolify.md`) tells agents to check the credential registry and the project's own/sibling infrastructure repos before asking for a URL.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/coolify-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/deployment/coolify.md`

Change notes: fix `coolify-cli-helper.sh` lines 16-19 ordering; add credential-registry config resolution to `coolify-helper.sh`; add discovery order to `coolify.md`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh help` exits 0.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh .agents/scripts/coolify-helper.sh` passes.
- With no JSON config but a recorded `COOLIFY_API_TOKEN` account URL, `coolify-helper.sh list` reports that instance without printing the token.

title: bug: coordinator restore JSON failures lack phase diagnostics and safe deferral
body:
# Recurring coordinator restore JSON failures need phase diagnostics and safe deferral

## Target and authority

Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops. This is upstream Issue Sync tooling, not a downstream application defect. The operator requested continuation on the remaining synchronization failure after the original local audit tooling was delivered. Keep implementation in a reviewed framework PR; no release, deployment, live replay, artifact deletion, or credential change is authorized here.

## Evidence and limits

Observed in a private downstream consumer on 2026-10-16; repository identity and raw log links are deliberately omitted from this public brief. The maintainer retains the source logs locally.

- Original run 38874777946: Issue Sync, pull_request event, created 08:36:07Z. The Record ordered forge event job failed during Restore durable coordinator state at 08:36:40Z with `unexpected end of JSON input`, exit 1. Attempt 1 remained failed when inspected.
- Later run 38927076864: issues event, created 15:49:44Z. The same restore command failed at 15:50:27Z with the same error and exit 1.
- The latest twelve sampled Issue Sync runs all had failure status. Only the two runs above had their failure logs inspected; do not attribute all twelve failures to the same cause without checking.
- A later read-only exact-name artifact-inventory request under the maintainer's local identity succeeded and returned one live checkpoint. This is NOT proof that the workflow token, download endpoint, permissions, or underlying transport recovered.
- The original workflow checked out framework commit `9ba93810c5486e28ce34becc2b500516170a96a1`. The state helper's current blob is `576933f6431056a4d9eda8647d93e139e366c14e`; its latest path commit at inspection was `70db2a5f2ad721186c58712ddaab56c894266fe0` on 2026-09-20.

Source inspection establishes a handling/diagnostics gap, not the cause of GitHub's malformed response: restore_state has separate exact-name inventory, bounded legacy inventory, and ZIP download calls. Rate-limit errors create .restore-deferred, but other gh failures print unqualified stderr and return 1. Validated structured metadata is not explicitly distinguished from empty/malformed or wrong-shaped successful responses. Current CI output does not establish which endpoint failed. Do not claim a rate limit, token problem, checkpoint corruption, or storage exhaustion from the JSON error alone.

## Deduplication and references

Memory recall for forge coordinator restore/JSON failures returned no relevant lesson. Open issue search for coordinator found no active match. The older #29587 rate-limit issue is closed; current code already contains its deferral path. Closed #32055 concerns artifact retention, a different scope. Search for the exact JSON message found closed release-provenance tasks, not this restore path.

Verified reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-forge-event-workflow.sh` already stubs gh/unzip, covers exact-name and bounded legacy lookup, preserves a pre-existing tasks.db during inventory/download rate limits, checks malformed artifact IDs, and checks deferred workflow publication. Extend this existing test, not a new harness or live CI credential test.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/forge-coordinator-state-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-forge-event-workflow.sh`

## Read-only reference

`.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml:105-157` already converts .restore-deferred into available=false and gates event ingestion/manual reconcile/state persistence. Preserve this contract without widening workflow permissions or modifying it as a convenience. Reverify exact lines on current upstream before editing.

## Implementation contract

1. Add bounded, sanitized phase diagnostics distinguishing exact-name inventory, legacy inventory, metadata validation, ZIP download, and extraction failures. Report fixed operation/error categories only. Do not print tokens, signed URLs, archive contents, response bodies, or consumer identities to public reports. Existing actionable hard failures must remain distinguishable from safely deferred transport/invalid-response cases.
2. Explicitly validate successful inventory output as non-empty JSON with the expected artifacts-array shape before selecting IDs or deciding that no checkpoint exists. Empty/malformed/wrong-shaped data must not be treated as a legitimate empty inventory or enable .restore-empty-init. Preserve valid, genuinely empty inventories and current one-page legacy behavior.
3. Use the existing .restore-deferred mechanism for recognized invalid-JSON/empty-response reads or matching gh `unexpected end of JSON input` failures. Preserve the durable checkpoint, skip ingestion and replacement publication, and remove any partial download. Do not silently initialize fresh coordinator state, weaken fencing, replay events, or claim the response was repaired.
4. Preserve current rate-limit behavior, exact artifact-name and expiry selection, ID validation, bounded legacy inventory, and normal successful restore. Do not introduce unbounded retries, pagination scans, new API calls, a permission increase, or artifact cleanup. A retry is not necessary for this scope; the next normal invocation can attempt restoration again under the existing workflow policy.
5. Do not blanket-convert authorization errors, invalid artifact IDs, unzip failures, and unrelated programming errors into successful restores. Preserve their failure semantics with useful safe phase context. A deferred result must be clearly reported as deferred, not restored.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exact-name inventory, legacy inventory and ZIP-download gh failures matching the observed invalid-JSON symptom produce a safe, phase-specific deferred outcome, leaving the checkpoint byte-identical.
- [ ] Empty/malformed/wrong-shaped successful inventory responses cannot start a fresh state or replace a durable checkpoint.
- [ ] Existing workflow conditions still skip ingestion and persistence/upload when restoration is deferred.
- [ ] Existing normal, genuinely empty, legacy, rate-limit and malformed-ID tests retain their semantics; authorization/extraction failures remain explicit failures.
- [ ] Mocked assertions verify bounded call count, no download after invalid inventory, no retained partial ZIP after failed download, no empty-init marker on deferral, and no private data in diagnostic output.
- [ ] No real artifact mutation, downstream fixture, credential change, workflow permission change, or live coordinator replay is needed to verify this fix.

## Verification

Run the existing focused harness: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-forge-event-workflow.sh`. Add cases there using its existing gh/unzip stubs and temporary-state checks for both CLI failure and successful-but-invalid metadata. This is the lowest-cost way to establish the failure and state-preservation behavior without live API/token dependencies.

Run ShellCheck on the two changed Bash files and the framework's applicable scoped format/quality checks. Preserve Bash compatibility, source shared constants where required, explicit function returns, and existing checkpoint behavior. If a real CI follow-up is later available, record whether restore succeeded or deferred; a green deferred run alone does not prove event projection recovered.

Selected tier: standard. Targets, existing test pattern, and state-preservation policy are decided; implementation is limited to parsing, diagnostics, and the existing deferral contract. Automatic dispatch is authorized for this repair brief. Any unforeseen coordination/trust-boundary change is out of scope and must not be improvised.

Rollback: revert the helper/test change; no data migration or artifact deletion is involved. Do not reopen the completed downstream audit-tooling issue to track this framework failure.

title: xAI X Subscription: OpenCode OAuth support unclear — build a workaround for the new plans
body:
## Summary

Industry trend: frontier labs are closing subscription OAuth to third-party tools. xAI still documents SuperGrok/X Premium OAuth for OpenCode today, but the new **X Subscription** plans do not clearly include third-party OpenCode in the shared weekly pool. Need an aidevops path that keeps Grok usable if subscription OAuth is limited or killed on the new plans.

cc @marcusquinn

## Industry trend: frontier labs are closing subscription OAuth to third-party tools

- Anthropic restricted Claude subscription OAuth to its own apps (Feb 2026), then cut off third-party agents like OpenClaw (Apr 4, 2026). OpenCode removed Claude subscription logins after legal requests.
- Google's Gemini CLI FAQ says using its login from OpenCode violates its terms and may lead to suspension.
- Pattern: first-party subscription pools stay; third-party agent OAuth is the first thing to go.

## xAI status (as of 2026-10-16)

- [x.ai/news/grok-opencode](https://x.ai/news/grok-opencode) still endorses **SuperGrok / X Premium** subscription OAuth in OpenCode (device-code / headless flows).
- OpenCode docs (`opencode.ai/docs/providers` → xAI): Option A = SuperGrok subscription device-code OAuth; Option B = console API key. Quote: any Grok or X Premium plan that includes Grok API access works; no separate `XAI_API_KEY` required for the subscription path.
- The new **X Subscription** (Plus $8 / Premium $30 / Super $100 / Ultra $200) uses a shared weekly pool for **eligible first-party usage only across supported Grok and Cursor surfaces** ([docs.x.ai/x-subscription/usage-limits](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/usage-limits)). OpenCode and other third-party tools are **not named**.
- Existing SuperGrok plans continue; switching to the new plans is **optional and permanent** ([docs.x.ai/x-subscription/do-i-have-to-switch](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/do-i-have-to-switch), [docs.x.ai/x-subscription/overview](https://docs.x.ai/x-subscription/overview)).
- Cursor/X pricing FAQ: “Paid plans include Grok API access. **API usage is billed separately at standard model rates and doesn't draw from your plan's usage pool.**” That is console PAYG, not proof that OpenCode SuperGrok OAuth still draws the included weekly bar after unify.
- xAI support has **not** confirmed OpenCode OAuth works on the new X Subscription plans (operator still waiting). Working guess: it may not long-term, or it may authenticate but meter as PAYG.
- Paying xAI API list prices instead of subscription OAuth would cost several times more for heavy multi-tab agent use (OpenCode fleets).

## Ask

Start developing an **aidevops** path that works under the new X Subscription models:

1. **Investigate** whether OpenCode's xAI OAuth works with X Subscription accounts, and what happens to the token/pool after a switch (included weekly pool vs PAYG API).
2. **Explore** Cursor-based or other first-party routes (Cursor is covered by the shared pool), or multi-auth options, so aidevops can keep using Grok without a surprise bill.
3. **Add provider failover** if xAI OAuth starts returning 401/403 (detect, alert, fall back to configured alternate provider/key path without silent spend).
4. **Reduce token burn** where possible: cap context under 200k, prefer fresh sessions on fat threads, route routine steps to cheaper models/effort — aidevops guidance + helpers, not only prose.

## Constraints / non-goals

- Do **not** require operators to switch off grandfathered SuperGrok until OAuth + pool behavior is proven.
- Do **not** treat console API key PAYG as equivalent to subscription pool without an explicit cost model.
- Private email/accounting routing stays local-only (unchanged).

## Files / surfaces (starting points; exact paths may expand)

- OpenCode provider docs / auth store behavior (reference only): xAI SuperGrok OAuth vs API key
- aidevops model routing / provider config: `~/.aidevops/agents/` routing refs, OpenCode `opencode.json` patterns (document; do not force fleet edits)
- Observability: `llm-requests.db` error_type / finish_reason for grok auth failures (failover signal)
- Optional: pool monitor patterns (`castle-grok-pool` is operator-local; framework should stay generic)

Paths unknown until design: any new failover helper, Cursor bridge, or subscription-tier detector.

## Verification

- Documented matrix: SuperGrok Heavy vs X Subscription Ultra — OpenCode OAuth yes/no, pool vs PAYG, evidence links.
- If implementing failover: simulated 401/403 path alerts and switches without spending PAYG silently; dry-run mode.
- Burn guidance: measurable defaults (context cap / session refresh / effort routing) with before/after request stats from observability DB on a test fleet.

title: coolify-cli-helper add-context exposes the API token via argv
body:
## Observed

Found while reviewing #34817. `coolify-cli-helper.sh add-context NAME URL TOKEN [default]` takes the Coolify API token as a positional argument, then passes it on to `coolify context add NAME URL TOKEN` (`.agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh:375-390`, dispatch at `:618`). The token is therefore exposed in:

- the caller's shell history and the agent transcript, because the documented usage puts the literal token on the command line (`show_help` example `add-context production https://coolify.example.com your-api-token true`; `.agents/tools/deployment/coolify-cli.md`);
- the process table (`ps`) for both the helper and the `coolify` child while they run.

This conflicts with the framework rule that secrets are never typed into conversation, and that they are injected through `aidevops secret` subprocess environments instead.

## Reproducer

Code-path evidence (no live token used): `add_context()` builds `context_args=("$context_name" "$url" "$token")` from positional `$3` and runs `coolify context add "${context_args[@]}"` (`.agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh:375-390`). To observe it, put a stub `coolify` on PATH that writes `"$@"` to a temp file, then run `bash .agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh add-context test https://coolify.example.com SYNTHETIC_TOKEN_VALUE`. The stub records the synthetic token in its argv, and the helper's own argv contains it too.

## Expected

- `add-context` no longer accepts the token as argv. It reads it from a named secret, defaulting to `COOLIFY_API_TOKEN` (for example `add-context NAME URL [--token-secret NAME] [--default]`), through `aidevops secret NAME -- ...` or the existing secret-helper injection path.
- If the upstream `coolify context add` CLI only accepts the token as argv, document that residual `ps` exposure, keep the token out of the helper's own argv and output, and check whether upstream supports stdin or env input (verify against the installed `coolify` version; do not guess flags).
- Help text and `coolify-cli.md` examples stop showing a literal token, and point to `aidevops secret set COOLIFY_API_TOKEN`.
- A legacy positional third argument fails with guidance rather than being used silently.

## Files

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/deployment/coolify-cli.md`

Notes: `coolify-cli-helper.sh` — `add_context()` (~375), `main` dispatch (~618), `show_help` examples. `coolify-cli.md` — context setup examples. Reference pattern: `aidevops secret NAME -- CMD` injection in `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` (`cmd_run_specific`), which is read-only for this task.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/coolify-cli-helper.sh help` exits 0 and shows no literal-token example.
- With a stub `coolify` on PATH that records its argv/env to a temp file and a synthetic secret, `add-context` succeeds without the helper's own argv containing the value. Assert the documented residual exposure, if any, against the stub.

title: fix: escape angle-bracket tokens in auto-generated CHANGELOG entries (MD033 on release PRs)
body:
## Problem

The auto-generated release changelog copies commit subjects verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md`. A subject that contains an angle-bracket placeholder becomes inline HTML in Markdown. That fails the changed-lines markdownlint ratchet (MD033) on the protected-main release PR.

Observed on release PR #34837 (v3.39.37): `Code Quality Analysis / Markdown Lint` failed with

```text
CHANGELOG.md:18:65 error MD033/no-inline-html Inline HTML [Element: PROJECT]
```

from the generated entry `- snapshot, action-status, metrics, server-net and HCLOUD_TOKEN_<PROJECT> support (#34814)`.

The release still published because Markdown Lint is not a required check. But every release PR whose range includes such a subject shows a red check, and the signed release commit cannot be fixed after the fact without breaking provenance.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/jobs/117133244869/logs --allow-escape-sequences | rg -n MD033` (Markdown Lint job on release PR #34837, v3.39.37)

**Actual output:**

```text
CHANGELOG.md:18:65 error MD033/no-inline-html Inline HTML [Element: PROJECT]
```

Local equivalent: in a scratch repo with an existing tag, commit `feat: support TOKEN_<NAME> override`, then source `.agents/scripts/version-manager-changelog.sh` and call `generate_changelog_content`. The `### Added` entry contains a raw `<NAME>`, and `markdownlint-cli2` on that output reports MD033.

## Expected

Generated changelog entries are Markdown-safe. Angle-bracket tokens (and other inline-HTML-like sequences) in commit subjects render literally, for example by wrapping the token in backticks or escaping `<` as `\<`. Plain subjects stay unchanged.

## Files

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/version-manager-changelog.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-changelog-maintenance-spacing.sh`

Notes:

- Sanitise in `generate_changelog_content()` (around line 281, the commit loop) or in `_classify_commit_to_category()`, so that both `generate_changelog_preview` and `update_changelog` get it.
- Keep Bash 3.2 compatible: use parameter expansion or `sed`, no `${var//pattern/...}` features beyond 3.2.
- Extending the existing changelog test with one angle-bracket subject is the cheapest way to verify. Do not add new harnesses.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/version-manager-changelog.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-changelog-maintenance-spacing.sh`
- Generate content for a subject containing `<PROJECT>`, and run `markdownlint-cli2` on the output: no MD033.

title: fix: bind Pulse worktree cleanup to rootless descendant lifetime
body:
## Goal

Restore safe rootless cleanup of newly created Pulse worktrees when host-wide process CWD visibility is degraded. Preserve active descendants, unsaved content and unproven legacy worktrees.

## Evidence and implementation scope

Cleanup can repeatedly defer with `cwd-visibility-degraded`. Owner-row release does not establish descendant quiescence. A separate observed failure leaves an empty cleanup-receipt lock owner after a failed write, preventing later leases.

Implementing interactively in the existing repair worktree; this session owns implementation through PR verification and requested local deployment. Do not dispatch a competing implementation.

- Add explicit creation provenance and systemd invocation lifetime metadata in the existing registry via `.agents/scripts/worktree-managed-lifetime.py`.
- Integrate creation/admission in `worktree-helper-add.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` and `pulse-dispatch-worker-systemd.sh`.
- Integrate exclusive sealing and evidence lookup in `worktree-clean-lib.sh`, `audit-worktree-removal-helper.sh`, `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` and `worktree-recovery-lifecycle-helper.sh`.
- Repair the failed owner-write path in `full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh`.
- Document the cooperative containment contract in `.agents/reference/worktree-registry.md` and the worker protocol.

Reference pattern: existing exact-owner registry transactions, cleanup leases and recovery archive identity/content verification. Use systemd user services with `ExitType=cgroup`; no root, separate daemon or second lease database. Do not treat missing or invalid evidence as quiescence. Do not automatically stop a unit after a non-atomic invocation check.

## Acceptance and verification

- New Pulse worktrees enroll before launch; legacy trees are not retroactively enrolled. Managed generations cannot silently use the detached backend.
- A surviving `setsid` child blocks sealing; a readable matching CWD always blocks removal. Unavailable registry evidence refuses mutation.
- Sealing prevents subsequent worker admission and claims while retaining cleanup retry capability.
- Production launch, archive and native-removal fixture preserves an unsaved file without root. Existing cleanup, owner-claim, receipt and archive tests pass; ShellCheck and Python compilation pass.
- Preserve existing archive retention/publication/content checks. Actual local deployment and automatic cleanup verification remain separate from code-level acceptance.

Known boundary: this is cooperative containment, not proof against arbitrary external same-user processes. Workers must not hand worktree access to an external service/container. Missing evidence before reboot remains protected; retained exited unit objects are not automatically retired.

title: validator_timeout_seconds cannot be set by agents: canonical .aidevops.json is write-blocked
body:
## Problem

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` validators time out at the 300 s default on large workspaces. The error tells the agent to set `validator_timeout_seconds` in `.aidevops.json` as the durable project setting. That file is gitignored and is resolved from the canonical checkout (`full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`, around lines 320-347: linked worktrees fall back to the first worktree's `.aidevops.json`).

The canonical write policy then blocks any agent edit to that file with `BLOCKED by canonical write policy: canonical checkouts are read-only session mirrors. ACTION_REQUIRED=create_or_use_linked_worktree`.

The result is that the durable fix the error message recommends cannot be applied by an agent. Each session must instead set `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT` by hand, or ask the user to edit the file.

## Observed

- Private project repo; the full `apps/web` lint took longer than 300 s. It passed with `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT=1500` (about 12 min including typecheck).
- An Edit on `<canonical>/.aidevops.json` to add `"validator_timeout_seconds": 1500` was blocked by the canonical write policy.

## Implementation

Add `aidevops project-config set validator_timeout_seconds <n>` through the existing config-only repair entry point. Resolve the current repository's canonical checkout structurally, validate the allowlisted key and positive integer, refuse tracked/non-ignored or unsafe config files, preserve other fields, and write atomically with local audit evidence. Do not weaken the canonical write policy or enable arbitrary configuration writes. Existing worktree-local override precedence remains unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/project-config-restore-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/project-config-set-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-project-config-set.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-project-validators-shell-only.sh`
- `aidevops.sh`

## Verification

From a linked worktree session, set the timeout through the new command. A later validator invocation in another worktree of the same repo must use the timeout without `AIDEVOPS_VALIDATOR_TIMEOUT`. Exercise invalid inputs, unrelated-field preservation, missing config creation, tracked/non-ignored/symlink rejection, and unchanged Git refs/index. Run the existing shell-only validator suite, Python setter checks, ShellCheck and bash syntax on affected shell files.

## Discovery evidence

Issue open on 2026-10-17; no matching open/closed PR or pushed issue branch. PR #34503 implemented canonical timeout inheritance, not the setter. The existing `project-config-restore-helper.sh` is the config-only CLI integration point. Direct canonical Edit/Write policy remains unchanged.

title: Brief revision never releases status:blocked after a files_scope_excluded stop
body:
## Observed

The runner used aidevops v3.39.37 and OpenCode 1.19.0. Line references below come from the deployed v3.39.34 scripts, so check them against current `main`.

1. A headless worker on a private managed repository stopped with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=files_scope_excluded`. Its release comment said `Projected state: status:available.`, but the runner applied `status:blocked` to the issue in the same second. This was the first observation, so no `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT` comment exists.
2. The brief owner (an interactive session) revised the brief and refreshed the issue body. That changes the task revision (`terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:337-339`), yet nothing returned the issue to `status:available`:
   - `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `tbr_seed` (`:119-132`) queues only issues that have a `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_CIRCUIT` comment. `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` (`:167-196`) therefore never runs for a first-observation `status:blocked`.
   - `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` `_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope_verdict` (`:1061-1065`) skips every `auto-dispatch` issue with `status:blocked`.
   - `reference/worker-discipline.md` ("Integration scope recovery", "Terminal-blocker recovery") says a relevant brief revision re-arms dispatch with no retry directive. It does not mention the label.
3. The brief owner had to change the label by hand. `set_issue_status` (`shared-gh-wrappers-status.sh:767-793`) is documented as "the ONLY sanctioned way to change an issue's status label". However, the OpenCode command policy blocks `bash -c "source …"`, and no helper CLI exposes the function. The fallback was `gh-write-helper.sh issue edit <N> --repo <slug> --remove-label status:blocked --add-label status:available`.

Without manual action, a corrected brief stays undispatched indefinitely.

## Expected

1. The release comment's `Projected state:` matches the label the runtime applies.
2. A brief revision that changes the task revision of a `files_scope_excluded` or `missing_files_scope` hold returns the issue to `status:available` automatically. The `missing_files_scope` pre-claim hold already does this ("The pulse releases this hold automatically once the edited body passes", `pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1110`). If that is not the intended design, the docs should name the exact command the brief owner runs.
3. Interactive sessions have a policy-compatible CLI for sanctioned status transitions.

## Suggested fix

- Release path: find where a `files_scope_excluded` release applies `status:blocked` (`headless-runtime-lib.sh` or its release helper) and make the observation's projected state the state actually applied.
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: also seed open `status:blocked` issues whose newest trusted `terminal-blocker-observation` comment from this runner has a reason that re-arms on brief revision (`files_scope_excluded`, `missing_files_scope`). `_tbr_release_circuit_hold` can then release them once `terminal_blocker_task_revision` differs from the observed revision. Alternatively, release such holds in the pulse pre-claim gate when the stored body revision differs.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh`: add `issue status <N> --repo <slug> <status>`, delegating to `set_issue_status`.
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`: state how the label returns to `status:available` after a brief-owner revision.

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, or the nearest recovery-helper test, with a first-observation `files_scope_excluded` issue labelled `status:blocked`. An unchanged body stays blocked; a changed body is released to `status:available` exactly once.
- `shellcheck` reports zero violations on changed scripts.

- Update any test that asserts the old reason for braces: search the repo for `shell grouping and subshell syntax`.

## Verification

title: pulse-triage: heading-form worker checkpoints and brief-owner revision notices still trigger issue consolidation
body:
## What

Two comment shapes still count as "substantive" in `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh`). An issue whose body already carries the agreed spec therefore gets a `consolidation-task` child, and the child's instructions close the original issue as not planned:

1. **Heading-form worker checkpoints.** A headless worker (aidevops v3.39.37) posted `## Implementation checkpoint — verification blocked` (about 2,900 characters, `<!-- aidevops:origin:worker -->`). #33940 added `^Implementation checkpoint:` to `$patterns`. Its proposed fix also covered "other worker checkpoint shapes", but the heading form still counts.
2. **Brief-owner revision notices.** After a `files_scope_excluded` stop, the interactive brief owner revised the brief, refreshed the issue body from it and posted `## Brief owner decision: files_scope_excluded resolved`. #32905 excludes `^Brief (repaired|scope normalized):`, but `reference/worker-discipline.md:117` ("The owner reviews and records a corrected brief or a precise human-only decision") does not name that prefix. A natural heading counts as a scope comment, even though the refreshed body already carries the decision.

## Evidence (managed private repo, 2026-10-16)

- 20:44Z heading-form worker checkpoint plus 23:19Z brief-owner decision gave a substantive count of 2, the threshold. title: WordPress: apply a reviewed change plan to posts and terms, with dry run, backup, read-back and restore
body:
## What A framework tool for agents to make reviewed, field-level changes to a live WordPress site and undo them, with no plugin installed: - `.agents/scripts/wp-change-plan.php` (new; the repo's first PHP file): a WP-CLI `eval-file` script with three modes: dry run (default), `apply` and `restore BACKUP.json`. - `.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh`: a `--change-plan PLAN.json [apply | restore BACKUP.json] [--user=]` command in `main()` (the `case` at about line 805). It reuses the site's SSH settings as `run_wp_command` resolves them (about lines 340-400: identity file, password env, port, `wp_path`; LocalWP runs locally). It uploads the script and plan to a private temporary directory, runs `wp eval-file` from `wp_path`, downloads the backup and the run output into the agent workspace, and deletes the uploaded copies. Backups stay on the server. - `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-change-plan.md` (new): plan format, rules, rollback and the traps below. Add a pointer from `wp-cli-reference.md` "Backup & Restore" (about line 239) and from `wp-admin.md`. Plan format. Every change is a pair `[now, new]`: ```json { "posts": [{ "id": 123, "note": "why (printed)", "post": {"post_title": ["Old", "New"], "post_name": ["old", "new"], "post_status": ["draft", "publish"], "post_excerpt": ["", "Short summary"]}, "meta": {"rank_math_focus_keyword": ["", "new phrase"]}, "acf": {"close_date": ["", "20261016"], "regions": [["884"], ["1070", "890"]]}, "terms": {"category": [["news"], ["news", "guides"]]}, "thumbnail": [0, 456], "alt": {"456": ["", "Example logo"]} }], "terms": [{ "taxonomy": "category", "id": 12, "note": "why", "term": {"name": ["How-tos", "Guides"], "description": ["", "

Intro

"]}, "meta": {"rank_math_title": ["", "Guides and how-tos"]} }], "delete_terms": [{"taxonomy": "region", "id": 34, "slug": "old-region"}] } ``` `terms` on a post lists the post's complete term slugs in that taxonomy, before and after. `acf` values are as stored (taxonomy fields as term IDs). Rules (decided): 1. The dry run reads every target and prints one line per change: unchanged, will change, or differs (with the site's value). A post or term with any differing "now", unknown field or disallowed value is skipped as a whole. The dry run exits 1 if anything would be skipped. 2. `apply` needs `--user` with `unfiltered_html` and edit rights on each target, otherwise KSES rewrites markup and the read-back fails. Before the first write it saves one JSON backup (mode 600) outside the web root, `~/backups/wp-change-plan/before--.json`. The backup holds the plan, and for each target its row, all its meta and its terms in every touched taxonomy, plus each image's alt text and each term's row and meta. 3. Writes go through core APIs so save hooks run. Per post: `update_field()` (when ACF or SCF is active), then `wp_set_object_terms()`, `update_post_meta()`, `set_post_thumbnail()` and the attachment's `_wp_attachment_image_alt`; then one `wp_update_post()` for the post fields. Terms use `wp_update_term()` and `wp_delete_term()`. 4. Every changed value is read back after each target. WordPress filters some values on save: term names always, and descriptions with KSES. So the script works out the stored form for its user, prints it in the dry run and compares the read-back with it. The first difference stops the run, leaves later targets untouched and prints the restore command. 5. `restore BACKUP.json` puts back each value that still holds what apply wrote, post status first and ACF fields before terms. It reports values changed since and leaves them. 6. `delete_terms` must be a plan of its own. A deletion is refused while any post of any status, child term, nav menu item or ACF field value uses the term. The backup lets the term be recreated, but with a new ID (WordPress does not reuse term IDs); restore prints that ID. 7. Hidden meta keys (`_…`) are refused; the featured image and alt text have their own entries. 8. At the end the script prints the follow-ups it does not do itself: purge page caches, recount the touched taxonomies where counts are deferred, and check the sitemaps. Traps met on a production site (document them in the tool doc): - `wp db export` exits 0 but writes no file where PHP `proc_open()` is disabled, which is common on shared hosting. That is why backups come from PHP as JSON. - Publishing a draft through `wp_update_post()` gives it the current date unless the plan sets `post_date`. - Saving an ACF or SCF taxonomy field with "Save Terms" replaces all the post's terms in that taxonomy. A plan that changes such a field must also list that taxonomy's complete terms, which are written after the fields. The dry run flags a missing `terms` entry. - Plugins that rewrite slugs on save (slug patterns) can change a slug on rename; the slug read-back catches this. ## Why Agents that make reviewed bulk changes on production WordPress sites have no framework tool with per-field preconditions and a field-level undo. Typical changes are titles, statuses, SEO meta, ACF fields, terms, featured images and alt text. `wp search-replace --dry-run` and `wp db export`/`import` cover neither preconditions nor field-level undo. A recent client job changed 23 posts (156 field changes), renamed 2 terms, deleted 1 term and set 21 featured images. For it, the agent wrote four one-off `eval-file` scripts with this pattern; without a framework tool, each new site would rebuild them. ## Verification - `php -l .agents/scripts/wp-change-plan.php` passes, and ShellCheck reports nothing on `wp-helper.sh`. - On a LocalWP site (`tools/wordpress/localwp.md`), with two posts and a category, run a plan that changes a title, a status (draft to publish), a meta key, terms, a featured image, an alt text and a term name: - The dry run prints each change and exits 0. - After one "now" is edited to differ, that post is skipped and the dry run exits 1. - Apply writes, reads back and leaves a mode-600 backup. - After one changed value is edited by hand, restore reports that value and leaves it; the others return to their old values. - A term deletion is refused while a post uses the term and works once it is unused. - On an SSH site, `wp-helper.sh --change-plan ...` leaves no uploaded copy in the temporary directory and downloads the backup. ## Tier `tier:standard`: the behaviour, format and safety rules are decided above. The worker writes the script, the `wp-helper.sh` command and the doc. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.37 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.2 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 1d 2h and 2,618,619 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

title: fix: secret import-credentials tenant imports are unresolvable and plaintext removal advice is unsafe
body:
## What

`aidevops secret import-credentials` cannot complete a plaintext-to-gopass migration on a tenant-loader install.

1. **Imports land where nothing reads them.** In multi-tenant mode `_import_credential_file` (`.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh:1473-1477`) writes to `aidevops/tenants/<tenant>/NAME`. Every resolver reads only the flat `aidevops/NAME` path: `gopass_owns_secret` (:129-137), `get_secret_value` (:143-163), injection (:433-449), `cmd_check` (:1136-1138). After a tenant import, deleting the plaintext value makes the name unresolvable even though gopass holds it.
2. **Plaintext is still the runtime source.** Shell rc files source `credentials.sh` (via the `mcp-env.sh` guard), and many helpers read only the environment (for example `.agents/scripts/updown-helper.sh:43-58` reads `$UPDOWN_API_KEY` and tells the user to set it in `credentials.sh`). The closing hint "You can now remove plaintext values from credentials.sh" is therefore unsafe advice.
3. **Non-secret config is imported as secrets** (`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_PROVIDER_ALLOWLIST`, `GCP_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_SA_KEY_FILE`), and superseded `credentials.sh.bak-*` files (some mode 644) are never flagged.

Observed on a real install: 26 names imported to `aidevops/tenants/default/*`; 8 of them already existed at the flat path with independent values; the user was told to delete plaintext.

## How

- Make the import target and the resolvers agree: for the active tenant, either import to the flat `aidevops/NAME` path (skip when present; report value-equal vs differing without printing values) or teach the resolvers to try `aidevops/tenants/<active>/NAME` before plaintext. Pick one and apply it consistently.
- Add an explicit, separate `aidevops secret prune-plaintext [--dry-run]` that removes a plaintext `export NAME=` line only when `cmd_check NAME` resolves from gopass with the same value, and keeps non-secret config lines.
- Provide gopass-backed environment loading for shells/helpers (or document that env-only helpers must be run via `aidevops secret NAME -- cmd`) before recommending plaintext removal; change the closing hint accordingly.
- Have `secret status`/`drift` warn about `credentials.sh.bak-*` files, especially group/world-readable ones.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/secret-handling.md`

## Verification

- In a temp HOME with a tenant loader and a gopass test store: import, then `secret check NAME` exits 0 and `secret NAME -- printenv NAME` injects after the plaintext line is removed.
- `prune-plaintext --dry-run` lists only names whose gopass value matches; config names are never removed.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` clean; existing `test-secret-helper.sh` passes.

title: claim-task-id: repair stale explicit counter_branch pin instead of failing every claim (follow-up to GH#34791)
body:
## Observed

Follow-up to GH#34791, which made `claim-task-id.sh` fail closed when an explicitly configured `counter_branch` is stale. That guard works: on 2026-10-17, in a managed project repo with a `develop` default branch, a claim failed cleanly:

```
COUNTER_BRANCH_STALE: explicit origin/develop counter=18593, leading branch=task-id-counter counter=18629, default TODO seed=18626; switch --counter-branch to the leading branch or run --sync-counter-branch before allocating
AIDEVOPS_TASK_COUNTER_STATUS=setup_error detail=counter_branch_stale
```

Rerunning with `--counter-branch task-id-counter` allocated correctly. Two gaps remain:

1. **The stale pin is never repaired.** The gitignored per-checkout `.aidevops.json` still contains `"counter_branch": "develop"`, the same pin that caused the duplicate IDs in GH#34791 the day before. Every interactive claim from that checkout keeps failing until someone passes `--counter-branch` by hand or edits the file. Nothing in `aidevops update`, init or the claim path migrates the pin once the repo has moved to the dedicated branch.
2. **The remediation can make things worse.** `--sync-counter-branch` targets `--counter-branch`/config first. With the stale pin, it fast-forwards `develop:.task-counter`, which is a direct counter commit on the integration branch. That keeps the obsolete counter location alive instead of moving to the leading `task-id-counter` branch.

## Expected

- When the explicit `counter_branch` equals the default branch, and the dedicated counter branch exists and leads both it and the TODO seed, guide toward switching rather than catching up. Either:
  - (a) offer an audited, idempotent repair that rewrites only the `counter_branch` key in `.aidevops.json` to the leading dedicated branch, preserving all other keys, file mode and ownership, or
  - (b) have `aidevops update` perform that migration for each registered repo.
- Reorder the `COUNTER_BRANCH_STALE` guidance so that "switch to the leading dedicated branch / repair the config" comes first. Warn that `--sync-counter-branch` against a default-branch pin pushes directly to that branch.
- Keep the GH#34791 fail-closed behaviour; never allocate from the stale branch.

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh
- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-protected-counter-branch.sh

## Implementation notes

- `claim-task-id-counter.sh`: `_cas_validate_explicit_counter_branch` (the `COUNTER_BRANCH_STALE` message) and `sync_counter_branch` (target selection when the config pins the default branch).
- `claim-task-id.sh`: `_load_project_config` sets `_COUNTER_BRANCH_SET`; any repair flag or migration belongs next to it.
- If option (b) is chosen, the `aidevops update` path that revisits registered repos also needs a change; that file is unknown and must be located (start with `rg -n 'aidevops.json' .agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/`).
- Reference pattern: the GH#34791 sandbox cases in `test-claim-task-id-protected-counter-branch.sh`.

## Verification

- Sandbox: explicit `counter_branch=develop` behind `task-id-counter`. The repair or migration rewrites only `counter_branch`, preserves other keys and mode `0600`/`0644`, and a subsequent claim allocates from `task-id-counter` without pushing to `develop`.
- Sandbox: an up-to-date explicit pin is left unchanged.
- The stale-pin error text lists the switch/repair action before `--sync-counter-branch`.
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts; existing counter desync/CAS tests still pass.

title: docs: shell-style-guide note on dynamic-scope shadowing of test fixture variables
body:
## Origin

Found while fixing GH#34846 (PR #34849, merged as `06929545`). A new regression test failed even though the product code was correct.

## What

Add a short section to `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` on **dynamic-scope shadowing**. In bash, a variable read by a stub or helper resolves to the innermost `local` of that name in the active call stack, not the scope where the stub was defined. A test fixture variable with a common name (`comments`, `issue_json`, `body`, `labels`) is therefore silently hidden when the code under test declares a `local` of the same name and then calls the stub.

## Why

ShellCheck can't detect it, and the symptom is a stub that returns empty or stale data, which looks like a product bug. In GH#34846, `test_first_observation_scope_hold_releases_on_revision` stubbed `terminal_blocker_fetch_trusted_comments() { printf '%s\n' "$comments"; }`. `_tbr_check_entry` in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` declares `local comments=""` and then calls that stub, so the stub printed an empty string. Diagnosing it took a full `set -x` trace.

## Tier

`tier:simple`: one documentation section with no code change. The pattern and the incident are given below.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md`: insert a new `## Dynamic-scope shadowing in stubs and fixtures (GH#34846)` section directly after the `## Caller IFS in sourced libraries (GH#34558)` section and its subsections (currently ending around line 552), before `## Watchdog self-write anti-pattern`.

### Reference pattern

Copy the structure of the GH#34558 section: a one-paragraph rule, a short `# Banned:` / `# Allowed:` bash block, a `### Why the failure is silent` subsection, and a `### Originating incident` subsection.

### Implementation Steps

1. Rule: stub and fixture state that code under test may also name locally must use a test-unique prefix (for example `tb_fixture_comments`). Alternatively, pass the data through an exported env var with a unique prefix. Never use bare names that common helper locals use.
2. Banned/allowed example, based on the real case:
   - Banned: `local comments='[]'` plus `fetch() { printf '%s\n' "$comments"; }`, called from a function that declares `local comments=""`.
   - Allowed: `local tb_fixture_comments='[]'` plus `fetch() { printf '%s\n' "$tb_fixture_comments"; }`.
3. Why silent: bash uses dynamic scoping, so ShellCheck passes and the stub returns the callee's empty value. The test then fails on an assertion far from the cause. Diagnose with `set -x` and look for the stub printing an unexpected empty value right after a callee's `local <name>=` line.
4. Originating incident: GH#34846 / PR #34849, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh` `test_first_observation_scope_hold_releases_on_revision` and `_tbr_check_entry` in `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`. The fix renamed the fixture to `tb_fixture_comments`.

### Scope Boundaries

- Documentation only. Do not rename variables in other existing tests or add a lint rule here. If a deterministic detector seems worthwhile, record it in `.agents/configs/prompt-hook-candidates.conf` or file it separately.
- Do not edit always-loaded `AGENTS.md` files.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The new section exists between the GH#34558 section and the watchdog section, with a rule, a banned/allowed block, a "Why the failure is silent" subsection and an "Originating incident" subsection naming GH#34846 and the two files above.
- [ ] `rg -n "Dynamic-scope shadowing" .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` returns exactly one heading.
- [ ] `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` (or the repo's Markdown Lint CI check) passes.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md:523-552`: reference section structure (GH#34558).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`: `test_first_observation_scope_hold_releases_on_revision` (fixed example).
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: `_tbr_check_entry` (callee with `local comments`).
