title: browser-qa-helper: colour-scheme, scroll-to-element, measurement and label options for screenshot evidence
body:
## What Extend `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot` so a single run produces complete evidence for theme-sensitive visual changes: one capture per colour scheme, a below-the-fold element scrolled into a viewport-sized capture, computed-style measurements, the HTTP status and console errors behind each capture, and labelled filenames so before and after runs can share a directory. ## Why Verifying a theme-sensitive change on a deployed page (a thin border that only shows against a light background) needed a temp-only browser script, because `screenshot` cannot produce this evidence: 1. **No colour-scheme emulation.** Each context gets a viewport only (`.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh:395-397`), so `prefers-color-scheme` stays at the browser default and a light/dark pair is impossible. 2. **No way to bring a below-the-fold element into view.** The only route is `--full-page`, which `.agents/workflows/ui-verification.md:38` and `.agents/reference/screenshot-limits.md` rule out for AI review. 3. **No measurements with the capture.** `transition` already loads and validates a `--measure-file` function expression (`.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-transition.sh:30-32`); `screenshot` has nothing equivalent, so computed-style evidence (border width, style and colour, radius, element size) needed separate code. 4. **No HTTP status or console errors per capture.** `smoke` records them in a separate pass (`.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:206-229`), so a visual check loads each page twice and the errors are not tied to the image. 5. **No labels.** Filenames are `--.png` (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:402-403`), so a second run into the same directory overwrites the baseline. `.agents/workflows/ui-verification.md` asks for light/dark checks (`:54`, `:75`) and says not to commit one-off browser scripts (`:50`). This change closes the gap between those two rules. **Workaround used:** a temp-only script (never committed) looped over light and dark, desktop and mobile, and two pages; scrolled a selector into view; read computed border and radius values; recorded HTTP status and console errors; and wrote labelled before, after and recheck captures (24 PNGs over three runs) for a pull-request verification comment. ## How New `screenshot` options. Without them, filenames, existing result fields and the stdout shape stay as they are today. | Option | Behaviour | |---|---| | `--color-schemes LIST` | Comma-separated `light`, `dark`, `no-preference`. One context per viewport and scheme, created with the context `colorScheme` option. Adds the scheme to the filename and a `colorScheme` result field. | | `--scroll-to SELECTOR` | After load, scroll the first match to the viewport centre, let the page settle, then capture. Adds `found` and `scrollY`; a missing match still captures, with `found: false`. | | `--measure-file FILE` | Same function-expression contract as `transition`. Validated before the browser launches; run in the page after the capture. Adds `measurement` (the JSON-able return value) or `measureError`. | | `--label NAME` | Must match `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`. Prefixes filenames and adds a `label` field, so labelled runs can share an output directory. | Every result also gains `httpStatus` (the navigation response status, `null` when there is no response) and `consoleErrors` (console `error` messages in the `{ text, location }` shape `smoke` uses at `browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:210-214`, plus uncaught page errors). The existing `status: ok|error` field keeps its meaning. `--full-page` and the size guardrails (`enforce_screenshot_size_guardrails`, `browser-qa-helper-core.sh:156-218`) stay as they are. Filename order with every option: label, page, viewport, scheme, size — for example `after-index-desktop-dark-1440x900.png`. ### Files to Modify - `EDIT: .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh:363-522` — new options, validation and emitted-script changes; extract helpers first (see Complexity Impact). - `EDIT: .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh:381-413` — add a "Screenshot-specific Options" block after "Common Options", modelled on "Transition-specific Options" (`:395-403`), and one example after `:407`. - `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh:422-429` — add one generator case that passes every new parameter, so the existing `node --check` and prefix evaluation cover the new emitted code. - `EDIT: .agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md:148-181` — document the options in "Step 3: Screenshot Capture", and add a labelled light/dark before/after example to "Advanced: Visual Regression" (`:233-248`). - `EDIT: .agents/workflows/ui-verification.md:44-50` — in the step 2 example, show `--color-schemes light,dark` and `--scroll-to` for theme-sensitive changes. ### Complete Write Surface - **Callers/readers:** `browser-qa-helper.sh:443` dispatches `screenshot`; `run` calls `cmd_screenshot` without the new options (`browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:392`) and embeds its stdout array verbatim (`:411`); `format_as_markdown` (`browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:546-587`) never reads `.screenshots`; `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md:245` compares default filenames such as `index-desktop-1440x900.png`; the test calls `_generate_screenshot_script` with eight positional arguments (`test-browser-qa-helper.sh:425`). Docs that only describe the command and need no change: `.agents/workflows/milestone-validation.md:102`, `.agents/reference/screenshot-limits.md:22-23`, `.agents/AGENTS.md:139`. Search used: `rg -n "browser-qa-helper\.sh (screenshot|run)|cmd_screenshot|_generate_screenshot_script" .agents`. - **Writers/mutation paths:** the emitted script writes PNGs into `--output-dir` (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:404`, `:409`) and prints the results array to stdout (`:420`); `enforce_screenshot_size_guardrails` resizes every `*.png` in that directory in place (`:169`); `cmd_screenshot` creates the output directory (`:488`) and a `mktemp -d` script directory (`:494`). Nothing else is written. - **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` — `test_generated_page_urls` (`:412-450`) runs `node --check` on each emitted script (`:430`) and evaluates everything before `async function run()` in a bare `vm` context that only provides `URL` (`:436-439`); guardrail tests run from `:462-466`. Nothing exercises a real browser capture, so the local fixture runs below are the runtime check. - **Schemas/config:** the only schema is the per-capture result object (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:410`, `:412`); new fields are additive, and option-specific fields appear only with their options. Viewport presets (`get_viewport_dimensions`, `:40-49`) and size defaults are unchanged. - **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys `.agents/` to the runtime agents directory; no generated index lists screenshot options (searched `rg -n "full-page" .agents`: only help, docs and the separate `design-preview-helper.sh` option). - **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the helper keeps no persisted state; earlier screenshots and reports are never read back (the only report write is `browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:490`). - **Cleanup/rollback paths:** the temp script directory is removed on success and failure (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:510`); run shell-side validation before `mkdir -p` (`:488`) and `mktemp` (`:494`) so a rejected option leaves nothing behind. Rollback is a revert: every new behaviour is opt-in and no stored data changes. ### Implementation Steps 1. **Extract before adding.** Move the option loop of `cmd_screenshot` (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:444-480`) into `_parse_screenshot_args`, setting caller-scope `_ss_*` variables as `_screenshot_parse_args` does in `design-preview-helper.sh:188-190`. Add `_validate_screenshot_args`: each scheme must be `light`, `dark` or `no-preference`; `--label` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`; `--measure-file` must be a readable regular file. Escape the selector, label and measure-file path with `js_escape_string` (`:55-64`), as `:502-503` does for the URL; emit validated schemes as literals. 2. **Split the generator.** Turn `_generate_screenshot_script` into a setup emitter (shell-supplied constants and `resolvePageUrl`) and a capture emitter (`async function run()`) that append to one file, as `_generate_transition_script` does (`browser-qa-helper-transition.sh:6-16`). Emit the capture part from a quoted heredoc (`<<'SCRIPT'`, as `browser-qa-helper-transition.sh:16`) so JS template literals need no `\${...}` escaping (compare `browser-qa-helper-core.sh:403`). Append new parameters after the existing eight (`:364-373`) with defaults that emit today's behaviour, so the test call (`test-browser-qa-helper.sh:425`) and the call at `browser-qa-helper-core.sh:505` keep working. 3. **Emit the capture loop.** Add nothing above `async function run()` that uses `import` or top-level `await`: the test evaluates that prefix in a bare `vm` context (`test-browser-qa-helper.sh:436-439`). Read and validate the measure file inside `run()` before the browser launch (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:391`), reusing the check at `browser-qa-helper-transition.sh:30-32`. Skeleton: ```js async function run() { let measureSource = null; if (measureFile) { const { readFile } = await import('node:fs/promises'); measureSource = await readFile(measureFile, 'utf8'); if (typeof (0, eval)(`(${measureSource}\n)`) !== 'function') throw new Error('--measure-file must contain a function expression'); } // ...launch the browser exactly as today... for (const vp of viewports) { for (const scheme of schemes) { // [null] when --color-schemes is absent const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: vp.width, height: vp.height }, ...(scheme ? { colorScheme: scheme } : {}), }); const page = await context.newPage(); let consoleErrors = []; page.on('console', msg => { if (msg.type() === 'error') consoleErrors.push({ text: msg.text(), location: msg.location() }); }); page.on('pageerror', err => consoleErrors.push({ text: err.message })); for (const pagePath of pages) { consoleErrors = []; // filename: [label-]page-viewport[-scheme]-WxH.png // goto + capped networkidle wait as today (:407-408); httpStatus = response ? response.status() : null // --scroll-to: first match; none -> found = false; else scrollIntoView({ block: 'center', behavior: 'instant' }), // repeat the capped networkidle wait so lazy images load, then record window.scrollY // capture as today (:409), then run the measure function in the page -> measurement or measureError // push { page, viewport, file, status, httpStatus, consoleErrors, ...option-specific fields } } await context.close(); } } } ``` 4. **Help and docs.** Add the help block and example in `browser-qa-helper.sh`, the option table and a labelled light/dark before/after example in `browser-qa.md`, and the theme-sensitive example in `ui-verification.md` step 2. Use the placeholder URLs the docs already use; name no real sites, products or hosting platforms. 5. **Test.** In the generator loop of `test_generated_page_urls` (`test-browser-qa-helper.sh:422-429`), add a case that passes every new parameter: schemes `light` and `dark`, a selector containing a single quote, a label and a measure-file path. ### Hazards and Compatibility - **Concurrency/atomicity:** one browser per invocation, with contexts opened and closed in sequence as today (`browser-qa-helper-core.sh:394-417`). Two unlabelled runs into one `--output-dir` still overwrite each other, as today; `--label` is the opt-in fix. The guardrail pass rewrites PNGs in place (`:169`) and leaves images already within `--max-dim` untouched, so earlier labelled files in a shared directory are safe. - **Migration/rollback:** no data migration; all new behaviour is opt-in, so a revert restores today's output exactly. - **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** without the new options, filenames stay `--.png` (relied on by `browser-qa.md:245`); existing result fields keep their names and meanings (`status` stays `ok|error`, and HTTP status goes in the new `httpStatus`); stdout stays one JSON array (`run` embeds it at `browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:411`); and the generator's first eight positional parameters keep their order (`test-browser-qa-helper.sh:425`, `browser-qa-helper-core.sh:505`). - **Idempotency/retry:** repeating a command overwrites the same files with the same result shape; labelled runs cannot collide with unlabelled ones. - **Partial failure/recovery:** a navigation, scroll or measurement failure affects only that result (`status: error`, `found: false` or `measureError`) and the loop continues, matching the per-page `try/catch` at `browser-qa-helper-core.sh:406-413`. Invalid options fail before the browser launches. Measure code is trusted operator code, as for `transition` (`browser-qa-helper-transition.sh:31`); if in-page evaluation fails for any reason, including a strict Content-Security-Policy, record `measureError` and keep the capture. ### Complexity Impact - **Target function:** `cmd_screenshot` in `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh` (`:434-522`) - **Current line count:** 88 lines by the gate's count (closing-brace line minus start line, `complexity-regression-helper.sh:274-287`); threshold 100 - **Estimated growth:** +25 to +30 lines (four options, value checks, new generator arguments) - **Projected post-change:** about 115 lines (115% of threshold) - **Action required:** Extract helpers first — `_parse_screenshot_args` (about 45 lines) and `_validate_screenshot_args` (about 20 lines), then add the new options there. - **Target function:** `_generate_screenshot_script` in the same file (`:365-429`) - **Current line count:** 56 lines by the gate's count, because its awk closes the function at the first column-0 `}`, which is the end of the emitted `run()` at `:421` - **Estimated growth:** +40 to +50 lines of emitted JS - **Projected post-change:** about 100 lines (100% of threshold) - **Action required:** Extract helpers first — split into setup and capture emitters (step 2). The core file grows from 522 to about 600 lines; `browser-qa.md` from 259 to under 300. ### Verification Before Dispatch ```bash shellcheck .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh .agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main --working-tree .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed ``` Runtime check against a local fixture. Set `FIXTURE_DIR` to a new directory under `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp}` and write `index.html` there: ```html

Top

Target
``` and `measure.js`: ```js () => ({ background: getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor, borderTopWidth: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('#target')).borderTopWidth, }) ``` Start the server as a background process (a bounded background operation in restricted runtimes), then run the three captures: ```bash python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory "$FIXTURE_DIR" .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url http://127.0.0.1:8765/ --pages / --viewports desktop,mobile --color-schemes light,dark --scroll-to '#target' --measure-file "$FIXTURE_DIR/measure.js" --label after --output-dir "$FIXTURE_DIR/shots" --max-dim 1568 .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url http://127.0.0.1:8765/ --pages / --viewports desktop --output-dir "$FIXTURE_DIR/plain" .agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url http://127.0.0.1:8765/ --color-schemes sepia --output-dir "$FIXTURE_DIR/bad" ``` Expected: the first run writes four PNGs such as `after-index-desktop-dark-1440x900.png`, and each result has `httpStatus: 200`, the fixture console error, `found: true`, `scrollY` above 0, `measurement.borderTopWidth` of `1px`, and `measurement.background` of `rgb(255, 255, 255)` for light and `rgb(17, 17, 17)` for dark. The second writes only `index-desktop-1440x900.png`, with today's fields plus `httpStatus` and `consoleErrors`. The third exits non-zero and writes no PNG; repeat it with a missing `--measure-file` and with a measure file containing `42`. - **Surface mapping:** `shellcheck` covers the three edited scripts; the test file proves the emitted script still parses, the pre-`run()` prefix still evaluates (the `vm` hazard and mixed-version positional parameters) and the guardrails still pass; `complexity-regression-helper.sh` proves the Complexity Impact extraction; the first fixture run proves the colour-scheme, scroll, measurement, label, `httpStatus` and `consoleErrors` criteria; the second proves the default-output regression criterion; the third and its two variants prove the validation criterion; `linters-local.sh --changed` covers the Markdown edits. - **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — the change is limited to one helper family, its test and two docs; no shared config, root tooling or release infrastructure changes. ### Recoverability Checkpoint - [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` and the three fixture runs - [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: browser-qa screenshot evidence options` - [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification then run: not required — see Broad verification trigger ### Safety-Stop Recovery - **Original objective:** one `screenshot` run yields per-scheme captures, a scrolled element, measurements, HTTP status, console errors and labelled filenames, with default behaviour unchanged. - **Preserved user directions:** a generic framework capability; docs and examples name no real sites, products or hosting platforms. - **Trigger and evidence:** `not triggered` - **Completed and verified:** none yet - **Remaining acceptance criteria:** all - **Unsafe route not to repeat:** `none` - **Next safe route:** if a browser run times out, rerun the fixture with one viewport and one scheme, then widen. - **Resume condition:** the focused test passes and the fixture server answers on `127.0.0.1:8765`. - **Owner and status:** dispatched worker; not-triggered ### Scope Boundaries Initial implementation map. Directly necessary adjacent integration follows `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery": document and verify the minimal corrected scope before editing. Explicit exclusions/hard boundaries remain binding and require a separate authorized brief-owner decision. **Hard boundaries:** do not change `transition`, `smoke`, `run`, `journey` or the size guardrails; add no new dependencies, committed fixtures, test servers or CI gates. **AI brief owner:** the maintainer interactive session that filed this issue. **Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe. ### Files Scope - `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh` - `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh` - `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` - `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md` - `.agents/workflows/ui-verification.md` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] With `--color-schemes light,dark`, each viewport yields one capture per scheme; the scheme appears in the filename and the `colorScheme` field, and a scheme-dependent `--measure-file` value differs between the two. - [ ] `--scroll-to` brings a below-the-fold element into a viewport-sized capture (`found: true`, `scrollY` above 0) without `--full-page`. - [ ] Every result carries `httpStatus` and `consoleErrors`, and the fixture's console error appears in each capture's `consoleErrors`. - [ ] `--label` prefixes filenames, so a labelled run does not overwrite an unlabelled or differently labelled run in the same directory. - [ ] Regression: without the new options, filenames stay `--.png`, existing result fields keep their meaning, stdout stays one JSON array, and `run` (which calls `cmd_screenshot` at `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:392`) behaves as before. - [ ] Negative: an unknown scheme, an invalid label, or a `--measure-file` that is missing or not a function expression exits non-zero before the browser launches and writes no PNG; a missing `--scroll-to` match or a throwing measure function marks only that result. - [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-helper.sh` passes, including the new generator case. ## Context & Decisions - Scroll uses `scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' })` instead of an offset option: one option fewer, and centring clears most sticky headers. - Measurements reuse the `transition` function-expression contract instead of a fixed list of CSS properties: one trusted function covers borders, radii, overflow and sizes. - HTTP status and console errors are recorded per capture instead of relying on a separate `smoke` pass, so each image carries its own error evidence and each page loads once. - Capture happens before measurement, so measure code cannot change the image. --- [aidevops.sh](https://aidevops.sh) v3.39.37 plugin for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v1.19.2 with claude-opus-5-5 spent 1d 3h and 3,579,362 tokens on this with the user in an interactive session.

title: test-consolidation-dispatch: call-budget assertion fails on macOS because BSD wc -l pads its count
body:
## What

`test_non_consolidating_comment_call_budget` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` (around line 1649) fails on macOS:

```
FAIL ordinary empty thread uses one live comment read, no child/ownership/PR ceremony
       rc=1 calls=       1
```

`calls=$(wc -l <"$GH_LOG")` keeps the leading spaces BSD `wc` prints, so the string comparison `"$calls" == 1` fails even though exactly one call was made. GNU `wc` on the Ubuntu CI runner does not pad, so CI passes and only local macOS runs fail.

## Evidence

Reproduced on clean `origin/main` (`e96e425254`) on macOS: 70 run, 1 failed, and the output shows the padded value above.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` — in `test_non_consolidating_comment_call_budget`, compare numerically (`[[ "$rc" == 1 && "$calls" -eq 1 ]]`) or strip the whitespace (`calls=$(wc -l <"$GH_LOG" | tr -d '[:space:]')`). Check the same file for other `wc -l` string comparisons and fix them the same way.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` reports 0 failed on macOS.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` is clean.

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh`

title: routines: Prettier-escaped cron schedules in TODO.md fail the t2423 guard and never run
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

A routine whose `TODO.md` line was rewritten by a Markdown formatter keeps running on its schedule. `routine-schedule-helper.sh` turns the formatter's `\*` and `_` back into `*` inside `cron(...)` before parsing, and the pulse logs the routine ID and expression whenever a schedule cannot be evaluated, instead of treating the error as "not due".

## Why

Prettier is the usual Markdown formatter in JavaScript and TypeScript repositories, often run on every commit through lint-staged (`"*.{json,md}": ["prettier --write"]`). Prettier 3.6.2 rewrites routine lines written in the documented format (`.agents/reference/routines.md:30`, `:61`):

| Written in `TODO.md` | After `prettier --write` |
|---|---|
| `repeat:cron(15 2 * * *)` | `repeat:cron(15 2 \* \* \*)` |
| `repeat:cron(30 9 * * 1-5)` | `repeat:cron(30 9 \* \* 1-5)` |
| `repeat:cron(0 9 1 * *)` | `repeat:cron(0 9 1 \* \*)` |
| `repeat:cron(*/15 * * * *)` | `repeat:cron(_/15 _ \* \* \*)` |
| `repeat:cron(0 */6 * * *)` | `repeat:cron(0 _/6 _ \* \*)` |

`daily(@06:00)`, `weekly(mon@09:00)`, `monthly(1@09:00)` and `cron(0 7,12,17 1-31 1-12 0-6)` come through unchanged. Prettier escapes a lone `*` as `\*`; where two asterisks can pair as emphasis (`*/15 *`), it rewrites both delimiters as `_`.

What the scheduler then does:

1. `_routine_parse_line` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:710-712`) extracts the rewritten expression as is.
2. `_parse_expression` (`.agents/scripts/routine-schedule-helper.sh:249-259`) rejects any `\` through the t2423 regex-metacharacter guard and returns 2. `routine-schedule-helper.sh parse 'cron(0 7 \* \* \*)'` prints `contains regex metacharacters — caller likely passed a pattern instead of a match (t2423 guard)`.
3. The escaped-asterisk warning at `routine-schedule-helper.sh:298-307` can never run: the guard fires first on the `\`. Both arrived in the same commit (f37c5c5c39, #20127).
4. `evaluate_routines` (`pulse-routines.sh:928`) treats exit 2 as "not due" and writes nothing to `$LOGFILE`. The routine never runs, and nothing records why.
5. Removing the backslashes alone is not enough: `_/15` and `_` still fail, because the bash matcher (`routine-schedule-helper.sh:477-523`) and the Python matcher (`:599-622`) accept only `*`, `*/N`, `N`, `N-M` and comma lists.

Seen in a managed project repository: Prettier rewrote a new three-times-daily cron routine before merge, and its `*` fields had to be replaced with full ranges (`1-31 1-12 0-6`) to keep it running. Step schedules such as `*/15` have no equivalent workaround, because neither matcher supports `N-M/S`.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/routine-schedule-helper.sh:229-320` — add `_unescape_markdown_cron` above `_parse_expression` and call it before the guard at `:249`; delete the unreachable warning at `:298-307`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:766-781` — `_routine_schedule_is_due` takes the routine ID as a fourth argument and logs exit 2. Pass `"$_RPL_ID"` at `:928` and `"$routine_id"` at `:813` and `:842` (set at `:806` and `:832`).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh:179-197`, `:499` — add `_test_markdown_escaped_cron` after `_test_metachar_guard` and call it from `main`.
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/routines.md:54-62` — one note under the `repeat:` syntax table.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the normaliser above the doc comment of `_parse_expression` (`routine-schedule-helper.sh:229`):

```bash
#######################################
# Undo Markdown-formatter rewrites inside cron(...) expressions.
# Prettier escapes a lone '*' as '\*' and rewrites '*' pairs that can form
# emphasis ('*/15 *') as '_'. Neither '\' nor '_' is valid in any schedule.
#######################################
_unescape_markdown_cron() {
	local expr="$1"
	if [[ "$expr" =~ ^cron\(.*\)$ ]]; then
		expr="${expr//\\\*/*}"
		expr="${expr//_/*}"
	fi
	printf '%s' "$expr"
	return 0
}
```

   At the top of `_parse_expression`, before the guard, add `expr=$(_unescape_markdown_cron "$expr")`. Keep the guard as it is, so a `\` that is not part of `\*` (for example `cron(0 7 \d \* \*)`) still fails with the t2423 message. A temporary check of this function against the five Prettier outputs above, plus unchanged and guard cases, passed under bash 3.2.57 and bash 5.

2. Delete the comment and `for _field` loop at `routine-schedule-helper.sh:298-307`; after step 1 no `\*` reaches them.

3. In `_routine_schedule_is_due` (`pulse-routines.sh:771-781`), keep the timezone handling, capture the helper's exit status, and on status 2 append one line to `$LOGFILE`, for example `[pulse-wrapper] routine <id>: schedule '<expression>' could not be evaluated (exit 2) — not dispatched`. Return the original status. Like the malformed-registry message at `:898`, this logs once per pulse cycle per affected routine.

4. Extend the existing test file (no new harness) with `_test_markdown_escaped_cron`, asserting with single-quoted literals that:
   - `parse 'cron(15 2 \* \* \*)'` prints `type=cron fields=15 2 * * *`
   - `parse 'cron(_/15 _ \* \* \*)'` prints `type=cron fields=*/15 * * * *`
   - `parse 'cron(0 _/6 _ \* \*)'` prints `type=cron fields=0 */6 * * *`
   - `is-due 'cron(_/15 _ \* \* \*)' 0` exits 0
   - `parse 'cron(0 7 \d \* \*)'` exits 2 and prints `regex metacharacters`
   - `parse 'cron(15 2 * * *)'` prints `type=cron fields=15 2 * * *`, and `parse 'daily(@06:00)'` prints `type=daily hour=6 minute=0`

5. Under the `repeat:` table in `.agents/reference/routines.md`, add: "Markdown formatters can rewrite `*` in `TODO.md`. Prettier writes `\*`, or `_` where two asterisks could form emphasis. The scheduler reads both as `*`; check a routine's effective schedule with `routine-schedule-helper.sh parse '<expression>'`." Name no projects or repositories.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `_parse_expression` serves `is-due` (`routine-schedule-helper.sh:735`), `next-run` (`:791`), `parse` (`:837`) and `systemd-calendar` (`:429`). Runtime callers: `pulse-routines.sh` through `_routine_schedule_is_due` (`:776`, `:779`; called at `:813`, `:842`, `:928`), `routine-helper.sh:228` (`systemd-calendar` with the CLI `--schedule` value) and `repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh:753` (fixed schedule). `routine-helper.sh:177-223` builds launchd XML from the raw CLI value without the helper and already rejects anything other than `*` or digits (`:190-192`), so it stays unchanged. Search used: `rg -n "routine-schedule-helper|ROUTINE_SCHEDULE_HELPER|_routine_schedule_is_due" .agents/scripts`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the helper writes only stdout, stderr and its exit status. The pulse change appends to `$LOGFILE`. No `TODO.md` file is rewritten.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh` (cron `is-due` at `:152-163`, guard at `:179-197`, end-to-end discovery from `:199`), `test-pulse-routines-cron-extraction.sh`, `test-routine-calendar-scheduling.sh`, `test-routine-systemd-calendar.sh` and `test-aidevops-schedule-command.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** none. The `repeat:` syntax is unchanged; input that is rejected today becomes accepted.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys `.agents/scripts/` to the runtime agents directory, where the running pulse picks the change up.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because the helper keeps no state and routine state files keep their format.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** the change creates no files, state or scheduler entries, so there is nothing to clean up. Rollback is a revert of the PR: escaped lines then fail the guard at `routine-schedule-helper.sh:249-259` again and are skipped, as today.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** none; string handling inside one helper call.
- **Migration/rollback:** no data migration; a revert restores today's behaviour exactly.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** every expression that parses today parses identically, because the normaliser only changes `\*` and `_`, which always fail today. Escaped routines that were silently skipped become due at the next pulse, and a routine that has never run is due immediately (`cmd_is_due` returns 0 for `last_run_epoch` 0, `routine-schedule-helper.sh:749-751`). That is the intended fix, but a long-dormant routine will start running without further action.
- **Idempotency/retry:** normalising an already clean expression is a no-op.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if normalised input is still invalid, behaviour matches today (exit 2), now with a pulse log line.

### Complexity Impact

title: fix(pulse): agent routines are killed with the launchd process group when the dispatching cycle exits
body:
## What

Agent routines dispatched by `_routine_dispatch_agent` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`) are killed whenever they outlive the pulse cycle that started them. The killed run never records a terminal state, so the routine stays `running` and is blocked for up to six hours.

## Why

`_routine_dispatch_agent` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:241-278` on current `main`) starts the runner as a plain background subshell, `( ... ) &`. In a non-interactive Bash script that child stays in the pulse wrapper's process group. The launchd job `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse` has no `AbandonProcessGroup` key, so launchd tears down the job's process group when `pulse-wrapper.sh` exits. This is the failure mode already fixed for async housekeeping (GH#33256) and async worktree cleanup (GH#32528).

Script routines were moved to a `setsid` runner in GH#32637 / PR #32668. That brief assumed "Agent routines are already detached (`_routine_dispatch_agent`) and need no change". A background subshell is not detached from the process group.

## Evidence

Maintainer runner, macOS launchd, aidevops v3.39.34. One project's `agent:Build+` routine (`~45m` budget), from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-watchdog.log`:

| Dispatching cycle started | Last routine session event | Watchdog finds wrapper gone | Terminal record |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-16 03:28:05Z | 03:59:23Z | 03:59:40Z | none; next attempt only at 10:28Z |
| 2026-10-16 10:25:42Z | finished inside the cycle | - | `agent completed successfully` |
| 2026-10-17 01:57:35Z | 02:33:06Z, while waiting on a bounded repository preflight | 02:35:13Z | none |

- In both killed runs, `pulse.log` has no `routine <id>: agent exited with code` or `agent completed successfully` line, the lifecycle history ends at `running`, and no routine worker process survives.
- The 2026-10-17 run had already committed its output in a linked worktree but was killed before pushing or opening its PR. The work had to be recovered by hand.
- `_routine_retry_blocked` treats `last_status: running` as active for `AIDEVOPS_ROUTINE_RUNNING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 21600). After the 2026-10-16 kill, the routine's 07:00 Europe/London slot did not run until 10:28Z.

## How

1. In `_routine_dispatch_agent`, launch the runner outside the pulse process group. Mirror `_routine_dispatch_script` and `_routine_run_detached_script` in the same file: `setsid nohup bash -c 'source "$1" && shift && <runner> "$@"'` with the perl `POSIX::setsid` fallback, `</dev/null`, FDs 3-9 closed, a per-routine runner log and the per-routine runner lock (`_routine_acquire_runner_lock`, PID marker). `set -m` around the launch (the GH#33256 approach) is acceptable if the runner still records its terminal state.
2. Record the terminal state from the detached runner with `_routine_finalize_terminal`, keeping the session key.
3. In `_routine_retry_blocked`, when `last_status` is `running` and the runner lock exists with a dead PID (past the existing 60-second grace), finalize the stale run as `failure` so the normal retry backoff applies instead of the six-hour running timeout.

Keep the code Bash 3.2 compatible (`reference/bash-compat.md`). Linux systemd kills by cgroup rather than process group; that path is out of scope unless the chosen approach also covers it.

Change `_routine_dispatch_agent` and `_routine_retry_blocked`, reusing `_routine_acquire_runner_lock`. For coverage, `test-pulse-routines-selector.sh` already overrides `HEADLESS_RUNTIME_HELPER` and has `_wait_for_detached_routine_success` for script routines.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- An agent routine started by a pulse cycle keeps running after `pulse-wrapper.sh` exits, then records `success` or `failure` in routine state and lifecycle history.
- The agent runner's process group differs from the pulse wrapper's.
- A `running` state whose runner is dead no longer blocks the routine for `AIDEVOPS_ROUTINE_RUNNING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`; it becomes `failure` and follows the retry backoff.
- A second dispatch while a live runner holds the lock does not start another agent.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-calendar-scheduling.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- With a stub `HEADLESS_RUNTIME_HELPER` that sleeps, dispatch from a parent shell that exits first. Confirm `ps -o pgid= -p <stub pid>` differs from the parent's PGID and that the terminal state is recorded when the stub finishes.

title: gh shim: pr-linked-issue block gives no remedy when a legacy issue-first CONTRIBUTING block lacks its scope marker
body:
## What

When a repository's `CONTRIBUTING.md` still has the issue-first block from the original rollout (GH#28844) without the later `<!-- aidevops:issue-first-pr:scope=external -->` line, `_shim_local_issue_first_scope` (`.agents/scripts/gh-write-policy-lib.sh`) correctly fails closed to `universal`. The block then stops owner, member and collaborator PRs that have no issue reference, such as routine PRs whose title carries a routine ID, even though the block's own text and the reusable `linked-issue-check` both exempt those authors.

The block message names no remedy. The operator or agent must add an unrelated issue reference, create a throwaway issue, or read the shim code to find that `sync-workflows` refreshes the block.

## Evidence (2026-10-17)

- 38 local managed checkouts have `aidevops:issue-first-pr:start`; only 4 of them also have `issue-first-pr:scope=`. The one legacy block compared matched `.agents/templates/issue-first-pr-contributing.md` except for the missing scope line, and `managed-markdown-block-helper.py check` reported it out of date.
- A routine PR in a managed private repository failed with:

```text
[aidevops][pr-linked-issue][BLOCK] PR creation for <owner/repo> is missing a linked issue reference.
  Target policy scope is universal; create or find the issue first, then include one of: Closes #NNN, Fixes #NNN, Resolves #NNN, For #NNN, or Ref #NNN.
  Task-prefixed titles such as GH#NNN: or tNNN: are also accepted when they map to the project task system.
```

- What fixed it: `sync-workflows-helper.sh --repo <owner/repo> --workflow linked-issue-check --apply --issue <N>`. With an unrelated runner change reverted (see the companion runner issue), the PR added only the scope line.

## How

1. In `_shim_block_pr_create_without_linked_issue_if_needed` (`.agents/scripts/gh-write-policy-lib.sh`), when the scope is `universal` only because a managed `aidevops:issue-first-pr:start` block has no scope declaration, print one more line: the block predates the scope marker, and if the repository's policy is external-only it can be refreshed with `aidevops sync-workflows --workflow linked-issue-check --apply --repo <slug> --issue <N>`. Do not change the fail-closed decision; this is guidance only. The marker-less case is detected in the legacy branch of `_shim_file_issue_first_scope`; expose that reason instead of parsing the file again.
2. In the `sync-workflows` dry run (`_sync_dryrun_emit`, `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh`), say when the planned change includes the `CONTRIBUTING.md` refresh (`_contributing_policy_needs_sync`). The affected repositories then show without anyone reading each file. Today every row prints the same `install policy → workflow + CONTRIBUTING.md` detail.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/gh-write-policy-lib.sh
- .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim-core-cases.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] With a marker-less managed block, a blocked `gh pr create` prints the `sync-workflows` remedy line. With an explicit scope marker, or with no managed block, the message is unchanged.
- [ ] Allow and block decisions are unchanged for every existing case in `test-gh-shim-core-cases.sh`.
- [ ] The dry run distinguishes repositories that need the `CONTRIBUTING.md` refresh from those with workflow-only drift.
- [ ] ShellCheck reports no violations in the changed scripts.

title: sync-workflows --apply strips a caller's runner input when repos.json has no runner for the repository
body:
## What

`_render_sync_target` (`.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh`) injects `with: runner:` only from the registry (`_read_runner_field`, `.initialized_repos[].runner` in `repos.json`). When the registry has no `runner` but the repository's caller workflow already sets one, `--apply` rewrites the caller without it, and `_needs_runner_sync` counts the difference as drift.

A sync for an unrelated reason (the issue-first `CONTRIBUTING.md` scope refresh) produced this diff in a managed private repository whose callers had deliberately moved to a self-hosted runner:

```diff
 jobs:
   check:
     uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/linked-issue-check-reusable.yml@main
-    with:
-      runner: 1cpu-2gb
```

Merged unnoticed, this silently moves the job to the reusable workflow's default, `ubuntu-latest`, which uses GitHub-hosted minutes the repository had opted out of.

## Evidence (2026-10-17)

- 6 registry entries set `runner`. The affected repository set its runner only in its two managed caller files, so its registry entry had none.
- `aidevops update` advises `aidevops sync-workflows --apply [--repo OWNER/REPO]` after template changes. Following that advice across all repositories would strip such runners wherever the registry has none.
- Workaround used: restored the lines in a second commit on the sync PR, and added `"runner"` to that repository's registry entry.

## How

1. In `_render_sync_target`, when `_read_runner_field` is empty, inject the existing caller's value from `_read_runner_from_file`. A registry with no opinion then keeps the repository's choice.
2. In `_needs_runner_sync`, treat an empty registry value as no opinion (no drift), not as "no runner".
3. Optional: print a one-line hint when a caller sets a runner the registry lacks, naming the `runner` registry field.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] No registry runner and caller `runner: X`: `--apply` keeps `runner: X`, and the runner check reports no drift.
- [ ] Registry runner `Y` and caller `runner: X`: the registry still wins (`Y`), as today.
- [ ] No registry runner and no caller runner: output unchanged.
- [ ] `test-sync-workflows-helper.sh` covers all three cases; ShellCheck reports no violations.

title: linked-issue-check: private org members fail the trusted-author exemption (payload author_association=CONTRIBUTOR, no permission fallback)
body:
## What

`.github/workflows/linked-issue-check-reusable.yml` exempts trusted authors by testing `pr.author_association` from the `pull_request_target` payload against `['OWNER', 'MEMBER', 'COLLABORATOR']`. For a person whose organisation membership is private, the payload reports `CONTRIBUTOR`, even when an authenticated REST read shows `MEMBER` and the person has `admin` permission on the repository. The script then falls through to the issue-reference path and posts a `failure` `linked-issue-check` status (`No linked issue — add Closes/Fixes/Resolves/For #NNN to PR body`) on maintainer PRs without an issue reference, such as routine PRs.

This is the root cause already fixed in `maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` (GH#24546/GH#24958, `pr_author_has_maintainer_authority`) and in the shell authority helper (GH#34644, sibling GH#34703). The linked-issue workflow never got the same permission fallback. It also means the statement in GH#34872 that the reusable check exempts owner, member and collaborator authors does not hold for private members.

## Evidence (2026-10-17, reusable workflow at `main` 32b4f5afbd)

- A routine PR in a managed private repository, opened by an organisation admin with private membership. The run log shows `No valid local issue reference found in PR body` and never the trusted-author line (`Trusted ... author — exempt from external linked-issue policy`). The commit status is `failure: No linked issue — add Closes/Fixes/Resolves/For #NNN to PR body`.
- Same account: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<N> --jq .author_association` returns `MEMBER` when authenticated as that user, and `gh api orgs/<org>/public_members/<user>` returns HTTP 404, so the membership is private.
- Earlier the same day, a task-prefixed PR (`tNNN: chore: ...`) by the same account first got the same failure, then `Linked issue found — #NNN` after `Resolves #NNN` was in its body. A trusted payload association would have posted `Trusted task-ID prefix — issue linkage via task system`, so the payload association was outside the trusted list.
- Effect: every issue-less maintainer PR from a private member shows a red `linked-issue-check` status. A routine SOP that merges only after every check has passed stops there, and agents are pushed to add unrelated issue references or create throwaway issues.

## How

In the `actions/github-script` step of `.github/workflows/linked-issue-check-reusable.yml`:

1. Keep the bot, fork-bot, `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR` paths as they are.
2. When `pr.author_association` is `CONTRIBUTOR` or `NONE`, call `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission` for `pr.user.login` before the issue-reference path. Treat only `admin`, `maintain` or `write` as trusted and publish the same success reasons as the trusted path (task-prefix reason when the title has a task ID, otherwise the trusted-author reason). Reference pattern: `pr_author_has_maintainer_authority` in `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` and the `COLLABORATOR` lookup in `.github/workflows/pr-triage-gate.yml`.
3. Fail closed: if the lookup errors, log a warning and continue to the issue-reference path. Never publish `success` because of a lookup error.
4. Keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` marker and add `GH#24546` to it.
5. Downstream callers pin `@main` and grant `issues: read`, `pull-requests: read` and `statuses: write`. The permission endpoint needs only metadata read, which the workflow token always has, as the maintainer gate already shows. Confirm that no caller template change is needed.

### Files Scope

- .github/workflows/linked-issue-check-reusable.yml
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-linked-issue-guidance.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] A PR by a user with `admin`, `maintain` or `write` permission whose payload association is `CONTRIBUTOR` or `NONE` gets a `success` `linked-issue-check` status without an issue reference.
- [ ] A PR by a user with `read`, `triage` or no permission, or whose lookup fails, still needs a valid local issue reference, with the existing failure descriptions.
- [ ] Bot, fork-bot, `OWNER`, `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR` behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] `test-linked-issue-guidance.sh` asserts the permission fallback and its write-level threshold, and all existing assertions still pass.
- [ ] Downstream caller workflows need no change.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-linked-issue-guidance.sh`
- After merge: edit the body of an open issue-less PR by a private org member with write access in a managed repository, so `pull_request_target` reruns, and confirm the `linked-issue-check` status is `success` with the trusted reason.

title: fix(pulse): a dead agent routine runner without a lock still blocks the routine for six hours
body:
## What

`_routine_retry_blocked` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:191` on `main`) recovers a stale `running` routine only when its runner lock directory, `${ROUTINE_STATE_FILE}.<id>.runner`, still exists. When the runner is gone and left no lock, the routine stays blocked for `AIDEVOPS_ROUTINE_RUNNING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 21600). Its lifecycle history also never gets a terminal record for that run. GH#34867 acceptance criterion 3 was meant to remove this block, but PR #34869 recovers only a lock that exists with a dead PID.

## Why

Two paths leave `last_status: running` with no runner lock:

1. **Signal termination.** `_routine_run_detached_agent` and `_routine_run_detached_script` set an EXIT trap that removes the PID marker and the lock directory. Bash runs that trap when SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP terminates the runner while it waits on its child, so the lock is removed and the state stays `running`. This was reproduced with bash 3.2.57 and 5.3.20 using a runner-shaped script (lock directory, the same trap, a foreground `sleep`). After SIGTERM it exits 143 with `state=running exit_trap=ran lock=removed`. Shutdown, logout and manual kills all take this path.
2. **Upgrade with a run in flight.** Agent routines started before PR #34869 never created a lock. A pre-upgrade run killed by the GH#34867 bug therefore stays `running` with no lock.

## Evidence

The evidence comes from a maintainer runner on macOS. Its deployed `pulse-routines.sh` has the same condition at line 191 as `main`.

- GH#34867 killed one project's agent routine at about 02:35Z on 2026-10-17. At 03:58Z, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/routine-state.json` still had `"last_status": "running"` and `"last_attempt": "2026-10-17T02:05:13Z"` for it, and no `.runner` directory existed.
- The routine is blocked until 08:05:13Z, so its next calendar slot (06:00Z) runs about two hours late.
- Its `lifecycle.jsonl` ends at `running` for this run and for the earlier GH#34867 kill on 2026-10-16. Neither run has a terminal record.

## How

1. **Recover a `running` state that has no lock.** In `_routine_retry_blocked`, treat `last_status == running` with no runner lock as a dead runner once `last_attempt` is older than the existing 60-second launch grace.
   - This is safe because a live runner always holds the lock. `_routine_run_detached_agent` claims it before `_routine_update_state "running"` and releases it only after `_routine_finalize_terminal`.
   - Reuse the existing stale-lock path: claim with `_routine_claim_runner_lock` to serialize against another scheduler or a starting runner, re-check state with the same `jq -e` guard, then call `_routine_finalize_terminal "$routine_id" "$_ROUTINE_STATUS_FAILURE" "$attempt_epoch" "routine-${routine_id}"` and release the lock.
2. **Preferred: record the real end time on signals.** In both detached runners, record a terminal `failure` from the trap when the run has not finalized, so the lifecycle shows when the run actually ended. For example, use a `finalized` flag checked in the EXIT trap, or a TERM/INT/HUP trap that finalizes before cleanup. Keep it Bash 3.2 compatible (`reference/bash-compat.md`).
3. **Coverage.** In `pulse-routines.sh`, change `_routine_retry_blocked` and, for step 2, the traps in `_routine_run_detached_agent` and `_routine_run_detached_script`. `test-pulse-routines-selector.sh` already has stale-lock and live-lock cases; add `running` with no lock, and SIGTERM during the agent wait.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- On the next `_routine_retry_blocked` call, `last_status: running` with no runner lock and `last_attempt` older than 60 seconds becomes `failure` in both state and lifecycle, keeping the session key, and follows the failure backoff.
- A `running` state with a live runner lock still blocks, and a lock with a dead PID still recovers as it does now.
- A runner terminated by SIGTERM while it waits on its agent leaves no routine blocked for `AIDEVOPS_ROUTINE_RUNNING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.
- No second agent starts while a live runner holds the lock.

## Verification

title: fix(planning): planning-commit-helper.sh complete from a linked worktree pushes the worktree branch and reports success
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh complete <task> --pr N|--verified` can report success without publishing the completion to the default branch.

`complete_task` (`.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh:243` on `main`) publishes through `todo_commit_push` (line 316). When the default branch has no classic branch protection, `_todo_commit_push_inner` (`.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`) commits on the current branch and runs `git push origin "$current_branch"`. Since GH#32651, `complete` refuses canonical checkouts (line 298), so it runs from a linked worktree, whose branch is never the default branch. The completion commit is pushed to the worktree's branch, `TODO_COMMIT_PUSH_RESULT` is `direct`, and the helper logs "Task completion committed and pushed". The default branch's `TODO.md` still shows the task as open.

The general path, `commit_planning_files` (line 567), already gets this right. For an unprotected default branch it uses `planning_publish` against `origin/<default>` from a temporary index. For a protected one it applies the GH#33707 guard: never report `direct` unless the commit is on `origin/<default>`. `complete_task` uses neither, so it is a sibling of GH#33707 (detached HEAD) for named worktree branches.

A second, smaller defect is in the same function. With `--verified`, `_complete_task_confirm_verified` reads stdin. A caller without a TTY (any agent) reads EOF, which cancels, and line 286 (`|| return 0`) exits 0 with nothing changed.

## Why

- Completion bookkeeping silently goes missing. The task stays `[ ]` on the default branch, so issue sync and dispatch still see it as open, while the operator was told it was pushed.
- The completion commit lands on an unrelated branch. If that branch has an open PR, the PR gains a planning commit. If it has already merged, the commit is orphaned.
- An agent that runs `complete --verified` without a TTY sees exit 0 and believes the task was completed.

## Evidence

Found by code reading on 2026-10-17, not by running `complete`. While completing a verification-only task (no PR) from a linked `plan/` worktree in a managed repo, I checked the publication path first:

- The default branch has no classic protection (`GET repos/<slug>/branches/<default>/protection` returns 404). A ruleset with admin bypass allows direct planning pushes, so `_todo_branch_requires_planning_pr` returns 1 and `complete` would take the `git push origin "$current_branch"` path.
- Workaround used: edit the task line by hand (`[x]`, `verified:`, `completed:`), then run `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: complete tNNN (verified:YYYY-MM-DD)"`. This printed `AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_COMMIT_RESULT=direct` with a publication receipt, and `git log origin/<default>` showed the commit.
- On `main`: `complete_task` is at line 243, its `todo_commit_push` call at line 316, the canonical refusal at line 298, the `--verified` cancel `|| return 0` at line 286, and the GH#33707 guard only in `commit_planning_files` at line 597.

## How

1. In `complete_task`, after `_complete_task_update_todo`, publish through the same logic as `commit_planning_files` instead of calling `todo_commit_push` directly. Either call `commit_planning_files "$commit_msg"`, or extract its publication block into a shared function used by both. Keep the `--pr` merge validation, and keep the success messages: direct publication versus a planning PR URL.
2. Report success only when the completion is on `origin/<default>` (direct) or a planning PR was created. Otherwise return 1 with an error like the GH#33707 message.
3. Make `--verified` cancellation exit non-zero. For non-interactive callers, either fail fast when stdin is not a TTY, or accept an explicit `--yes` (the confirmation still happens before `TODO.md` is edited). Update the usage text (around line 670) to match.
4. Coverage. `test-planning-commit-helper-protected-default-pr.sh` already builds a bare remote and a linked worktree. Add a case with an unprotected default branch and a worktree on a non-default branch: `complete --pr` (merge check stubbed as the file already does) or `--verified --yes` must put the completed line on the remote default branch and must not push the worktree branch. Add a case where `--verified` without a TTY or `--yes` exits non-zero and leaves `TODO.md` unchanged.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-commit-helper-protected-default-pr.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- From a linked worktree on a non-default branch with an unprotected default branch, `planning-commit-helper.sh complete tNNN --pr N` publishes the completed task line to `origin/<default>`, and the worktree's branch is not pushed.
- With a protected default branch, `complete` still creates a planning PR as it does now.
- `complete` never prints "committed and pushed" or exits 0 unless the commit is on `origin/<default>` or a planning PR exists.
- `complete tNNN --verified` with no TTY and no explicit confirmation exits non-zero and does not edit `TODO.md`.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-commit-helper-protected-default-pr.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-lifecycle.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-commit-helper-next-id.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`

title: fix: verify compact worktree archive retention and restore safety
body:
## Goal

Verify the complete compact worktree archive lifecycle and fix unsafe retention and restore behavior. User-authorized interactive implementation; claim before further work. Do not dispatch a duplicate worker while claimed.

## Observed defects

- `worktree-archive-helper.sh prune` selects archives by schema/date without artifact verification; corrupted, incomplete and unknown-content archives can be deleted.
- Symlinked repository buckets can redirect deletion outside the requested archive store.
- Invalid manifest types/timezones stop the entire retention pass.
- There is no compact-retention call in the asynchronous worktree cleanup runner.
- Restore must not overwrite existing tracked files or follow tracked symlinks when unpacking untracked payloads.

## Implementation scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.sh`: complete inventory/hash verification, private archive creation, safe exclusive untracked extraction.
- `.agents/scripts/worktree_archive_prune.py`: verified retention, pin protection, no-follow directory identity checks and private claimed removal.
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`: bounded retention once after successful cleanup; default dry-run, explicit operator apply opt-in.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-archive-lifecycle.py`, existing archive and async-cleanup tests, and `.agents/scripts/worktree-archive-helper.md`.

Use the existing archive schema, async cleanup lock, `timeout_sec`, config loader and Git ignore rules. Do not broadly copy ignored files or secrets into archives. Keep `.env.example` tracked; real environment values belong to a persistent protected source. Full legacy recovery copies require a separate per-copy preservation check before removal.

## Acceptance and verification

- Restore 33 local commits including a merge into a base-only repository; compare HEAD, parent topology, index, staged/unstaged binary patches, status and untracked files/modes/links.
- Exercise age/size retention, preview/apply/idempotency, pins, corrupt/malformed inventories, symlink paths and namespace replacement.
- Preserve external targets on malicious extraction and report restoration failure.
- Run existing archive, async cleanup, removal-audit, managed-lifetime and cleanup-proof-state tests; use native Git for isolated race fixtures, and the explicit rootless systemd integration opt-in where available.
- ShellCheck changed shell files; compile Python; independent deletion-safety review; exact-head repository PR checks before merge.

## Delivery

Merge verified fixes without publishing a release. Operational cleanup must report actual bytes reclaimed and remaining protected/unknown state, never claim an empty disk from passing tests alone.

title: Bug: issue_body_has_defer_marker matches mid-sentence 'hold for' prose, permanently deferring dep-graph auto-unblock of serial issue chains
body:
## Observed

In a managed product repo, a serial chain of 94 factory-generated continuation issues (part N is natively `blocked by` part N-1) stayed `status:blocked`. The chain head's only blocker closed about 4 hours ago and its follow-on consolidated issue closed `status:done` / `solved:worker`. Nothing re-armed the head, so the pulse ran at 0/6 workers with `eligible_available_unassigned=0` (`pulse-check-helper.sh json`: `blocked_explicit_hold=101`).

Evidence from `pulse.log` and `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/supervisor/dep-graph-cache.json`:

- The dep-graph cache entry for the chain head is `{"task_ids":[],"issue_nums":["<closed blocker>"],"has_defer_marker":true}`, and the blocker is in `closed_issues`.
- `dep-graph-cache: refresh repo=<repo> candidates=134 ... visited=10 blocked=0 unblocked=0` repeats every cycle. Every part is skipped through the `body-defer` short-circuit.
- The issue has no comments at all, so there are no worker, watchdog, terminal-blocker or brief-hold markers.
- `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` would classify the issue correctly, but its fair share visits only 0–7 issues per cycle (`resumed_after=13082 pending=178`). It is about 1000 issue numbers behind the head, so it gives no practical recovery.

## Root cause

`issue_body_has_defer_marker()` in `.agents/scripts/issue-hold-marker-lib.sh:14` uses an unanchored, substring-level regex:

```
defer until|do[-[:space:]]not[-[:space:]]dispatch|on[-[:space:]]hold|HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED|hold for |paused[[:space:]:]
```

The factory-generated brief contains explanatory prose such as "Other rows of this phase belong to other parts ...; neither is a hold for this part." The `hold for ` alternative matches mid-sentence, so `_dep_graph_process_issue_json()` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh:162`) caches `has_defer_marker=true`. After that, `_should_defer_auto_unblock()` (`pulse-dep-graph.sh:477-479`) returns `body-defer` for every part, forever.

`dependency-event-reconciler.sh` already solved this: `_der_text_has_operational_hold()` (lines 199-236) with `_der_line_is_operational_hold()` (lines 161-174) only matches a hold phrase at the start of a normalized line (after list/quote/heading/emphasis prefixes). It skips fenced blocks and HTML comments and rejects table rows. `tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh:331` asserts that explanatory prose such as "may be on hold for review" is not a hold.

## Fix

1. Make `issue_body_has_defer_marker()` share the reconciler's line-anchored classifier. Preferred: move `_der_normalize_hold_line`, `_der_line_is_operational_hold`, `_der_fence_marker`, `_der_fence_closes` and `_der_text_has_operational_hold` into `issue-hold-marker-lib.sh`, and have both callers use it. Keep `HUMAN_UNBLOCK_REQUIRED` as an anywhere-in-body strong marker.
2. Callers to keep consistent: `pulse-dep-graph.sh:162` and `interactive-session-helper-postmerge.sh:96`.
3. Cached `has_defer_marker` values recompute on the next dep-graph rebuild, so no migration is needed.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/issue-hold-marker-lib.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh` (consume the shared helper instead of private copies)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh` (add a mid-sentence `... is a hold for this part.` → `false` case; existing line-start cases at lines 62-71 must stay `true`)

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-non-dep-block.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-hold-marker-lib.sh .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh
```

After deployment, the next `dep-graph-cache: refresh` for an affected repo should log `unblocked=N` (N>0) for chain issues whose blockers are closed. Then `pulse-check-helper.sh json` `eligible_available_unassigned` rises above 0.

## Interim mitigation already applied

The supervisor manually released the chain head (`status:blocked` → `status:available`, with an audit comment) and dispatched it. The rest of the chain will stall again at each hand-off until this fix ships.

title: r908 profile README routine is double-scheduled: pulse copy exits 1 every run and last_run_epoch frozen since 2026-08-08
body:
## What

Core routine r908 (Profile README update) runs from two schedulers on the same host:

1. The platform scheduler installed by setup: launchd agent `sh.aidevops.profile-readme-update` (`StartInterval` 3600), wrapped so it reports status with `routine-log-helper.sh update r908`.
2. The pulse `evaluate_routines` stage, from the `core-routines.sh` definition `repeat:cron(0 * * * *)`.

Every pulse-dispatched run fails. The evaluator's `last_run_epoch` for r908 has not changed since 1786225186 (2026-08-08), about 70 days. The README is still published hourly by the launchd copy, so the only problems are false failures, overlapping runs and stderr noise in `pulse.log`.

## Evidence (one macOS install, 2026-10-17)

- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`: all 8 `routine r908: dispatching script .../profile-readme-helper.sh update` dispatches end in `routine r908: script exited with code 1`. Every `routine r908 is due` line shows `last_run_epoch=1786225186`.
- 3 of the 8 print `Profile README update already running; skipping overlapping refresh` just before exiting 1. The overlap guard returns non-zero while the launchd copy holds the lock.
- The other dispatches are followed by `awk: newline in string opencode` / `claude` / `shel... at source line 1` on stderr: 111 such lines in the current `pulse.log`, always directly after an r908 dispatch. A manual `profile-readme-helper.sh generate` exits 0 with no awk error. The failing `awk -v` is therefore in the update/publication path or depends on the pulse-dispatched environment. The exact source has not been identified.
- `launchctl list` shows `sh.aidevops.profile-readme-update` with last exit 0. The profile repository receives `chore: update profile stats` commits about hourly (12:59, 14:08 and 15:17 UTC that day).
- Other core routines show the same stale-epoch pattern and are also scheduled by both launchd and the evaluator. Check whether they share this root cause, and file separately if not:
  - r906 repo sync: `last_run_epoch=1790445828`; launchd `sh.aidevops.repo-sync` last exit 1.
  - r914 repo aidevops health: `last_run_epoch=1790049270`; `sh.aidevops.repo-aidevops-health` last exit 1.
  - r919 mirror sync: `last_run_epoch=0`; `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` last exit 127.

  Core routines that succeed under both schedulers (r902–r905, r907, r909–r911) advance normally.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh:26`: r908 definition.
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` (about lines 560–680): r908 launchd/cron/systemd install through `_core_routine_logged_command`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`: `evaluate_routines` due check and dispatch. Find where `last_run_epoch` is read and written.
- `.agents/scripts/routine-log-helper.sh`: status written by the platform-scheduler wrapper. Check whether it updates the state the evaluator reads.
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`: exit status of the "already running" overlap guard; `_cmd_update_in_repo` (about line 1524).
- Source of the multi-line `awk -v` value: unknown. Reproduce under the pulse-dispatched environment.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Each core routine has one active scheduler per host, or the evaluator skips routines owned by an installed platform scheduler. Choose per the routines design and document the rule.
2. A skipped overlapping profile refresh is not recorded as a failure: it either exits 0 with a skip message or records a distinct non-failure status.
3. r908's `last_run_epoch` advances after a successful run, whichever scheduler ran it.
4. r908 runs produce no `awk: newline in string` lines.

## Verification

- After deploy, across two hourly slots: `rg "routine r908" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows no new `exited with code 1`, and the `last_run_epoch` on `is due` lines advances (or r908 is no longer dispatched by the evaluator, if that is the chosen design).
- `launchctl list | rg profile-readme` (or the cron/systemd equivalent) matches the chosen single-scheduler design.
- The profile repository still receives the hourly stats commit.
- Existing tests pass: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-routine-tracking-updates.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-launchd-install-if-changed.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh`.

title: docs(routines): document pulse routine start latency (up to one pulse cycle) and the missed-run check
body:
## What

Document routine start latency in `.agents/reference/routines.md`, in the "Scheduler ownership" section next to the sentence about diagnosing missed runs.

Pulse-owned routines are evaluated only in the pulse `evaluate_routines` stage, once per pulse cycle. A routine starts at the first evaluation after its scheduled slot. That is usually a few minutes late, but can be up to one full pulse cycle late on a busy host.

## Why

On one host on 2026-10-17, consecutive `evaluate_routines` passes were 28 to 82 minutes apart. The times come from timestamped `[canonical-recovery-routine]` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`; that routine runs on every pass. A `cron(0 7,12,17 ...)` slot that fell just after a pass had not started 25 minutes later. That looks like a missed run but is expected. Without this note, sessions spend time diagnosing normal latency as a scheduler fault.

## How

Add two or three sentences. Suggested content:

- Pulse-owned routines start at the first `evaluate_routines` pass after the slot, so expect lateness of up to one pulse cycle.
- Treat a run as missed only when a pass after the slot did not mark it due. Check with `rg "Stage start: evaluate_routines|routine <id> is due" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.
- Platform-unit routines (launchd/systemd) are not affected.

Reference pattern: the existing prose style in the same section (lines ~99–108).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/reference/routines.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- "Scheduler ownership" states the latency bound and the missed-run check.
- No other sections change.

## Verification

- Run the repository's markdown lint on the changed file, as configured for `.agents/` docs.
- `rg -n "evaluate_routines" .agents/reference/routines.md` shows the new guidance.

## What

Give env-only credential consumers a gopass fallback so `aidevops secret prune-plaintext` can remove plaintext from `credentials.sh` without breaking them. Deliverable: one shared resolver (env → credential files → `gopass show -o aidevops/NAME`) and the helpers below switched to it, for shell and Node callers.

## Why

Follow-up to #34854 / PR #34855. On a real install, `import-credentials` placed 11 secrets in gopass and `prune-plaintext --dry-run` reported 10 removable (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ahrefs ×2, Outscraper, NeuronWriter, Updown, Higgsfield pass, HF key/secret). Pruning was held back because these helpers read only the shell environment or regex-parse `credentials.sh`, with no gopass path, so they would fail unless every invocation used `aidevops secret NAME -- cmd`. The helper's own hint ("Keep plaintext until callers use injection") makes this the blocker to finishing plaintext → gopass migration.

## How

Reference patterns (already in repo, verified):

- `.agents/scripts/serp-probe-helper.sh:66-80` `resolve_secret()` — env → source credentials.sh → `gopass show -o "aidevops/${name}"`. Promote this to one shared function (suggest `aidevops_resolve_secret` in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` or a small sourced lib) and make serp-probe-helper use it.
- `.agents/scripts/dataforseo-credentials.sh:6-30` — loader with gopass fallback used by an MCP launcher.
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh:143-163` `get_secret_value()` — flat `aidevops/NAME` path is canonical for gopass (tenant-aligned in PR #34855).

Callers to switch (file:line verified at current `main`):

| File | Lines | Name(s) | Current behaviour |
|------|-------|---------|-------------------|
| `.agents/scripts/updown-helper.sh` | 43-58 | `UPDOWN_API_KEY` | env, then config file; error says set in credentials.sh |
| `.agents/scripts/seo-export-ahrefs.sh` | 45-56 | `AHREFS_API_KEY` | sources credentials.sh only |
| `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper.sh` | 180-182 | `AHREFS_API_KEY` | env only |
| `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh` | ~386 | `AHREFS_API_KEY` | env only |
| `.agents/scripts/higgsfield-helper.sh` | 83-93 | `HIGGSFIELD_USER/PASS` | greps credentials.sh for presence |
| `.agents/scripts/higgsfield/higgsfield-discovery.mjs` | ~33 | `HIGGSFIELD_PASS` | regex-parses credentials.sh |
| `.agents/scripts/higgsfield/higgsfield-api-client.mjs` | 27-28 | `HF_API_KEY/SECRET` | regex-parses credentials.sh |
| `.agents/scripts/fallback-chain-helper.sh` | ~106 | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | env var name lookup |
| `.agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh` | ~102 | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | env var name lookup |
| `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/mcp-setup.sh` | 933-936 | `AHREFS_API_KEY` | env presence check |
| `.agents/scripts/validate-mcp-integrations.sh` | 119-120 | `AHREFS_API_KEY` | env presence check |
| `.agents/scripts/onboarding-helper.sh` | ~360 (`is_configured`) | `OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY` etc. | status report |

For `.mjs` callers: env first, then `execFileSync('gopass', ['show', '-o', 'aidevops/' + name])` with stderr ignored and a short timeout; never log values. Status/presence checks may use `secret-helper.sh check NAME` instead of fetching values.

Update user-facing hints in touched files from "set in credentials.sh" to `aidevops secret set NAME`.

### Non-goals

- Do not change `headless-runtime-provider.sh` / `headless-runtime-lib.sh` OpenAI key detection: env presence there drives provider/auth routing, and resolving from gopass could silently change OAuth-pool vs API-key selection. Document as out of scope; file separately if wanted.
- Do not change `prune-plaintext` classification or run it.
- Outscraper MCP config literal is a separate issue.

### Complexity Impact

Small per-function edits (≤10 lines each); no function should approach the 80-line threshold. Shared resolver ~20 lines.

## Acceptance

1. With a name absent from env and credential files but present at `aidevops/NAME` in gopass, `updown-helper.sh`, `seo-export-ahrefs.sh`, `keyword-research-helper.sh` (Ahrefs provider) and the Higgsfield clients resolve the key (verify in an isolated `HOME` + throwaway gopass store, reusing the isolation approach from PR #34855's `test-secret-helper.sh` coverage).
2. Env and plaintext values still take precedence over gopass (no behaviour change for current installs).
3. No secret value is printed in errors, logs, or `set -x`-free output paths; gopass stderr is suppressed.
4. Presence checks (`mcp-setup.sh`, `validate-mcp-integrations.sh`, `onboarding-helper.sh`) report gopass-held names as configured.
5. ShellCheck zero violations on changed shell files; `node --check` on changed `.mjs`; existing `tests/test-secret-helper.sh` passes.

## Context

- Observed on an install after PR #34855: dry-run output listed the 10 names above as prunable; plaintext retained pending this fix.
- Paths of personal installs intentionally omitted.

title: fix: outscraper MCP setup copies OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY literal into OpenCode config
body:
## What

Stop persisting the Outscraper API key as a literal in the OpenCode config. The `outscraper` MCP entry should resolve `OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY` at launch (env → credentials → gopass), and setup should migrate existing literal values to that launcher form.

## Why

On a real install the OpenCode config contained `mcp.outscraper.env.OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY` as a 58-character literal value. That is a second plaintext copy outside `credentials.sh`, so `aidevops secret prune-plaintext` cannot remove it, and the config file is not covered by the credentials file's 600-permission contract. Rotating the key in gopass also leaves the config stale.

## How

- Write path: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh:1538-1552` sources `credentials.sh` and writes the key with `jq ... .mcp.outscraper.environment = {"OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY": $key}`. The live config held it under `.env`, not `.environment`; confirm whether another writer (or OpenCode normalisation) produces `.env` — search with `rg -n "outscraper" .agents/scripts setup.sh`. Exact second write path not yet confirmed.
- Registration: `.agents/scripts/lib/mcp_config.py:133-149` `_register_outscraper` builds a `bash -c` command; keep the `mcp<2` pin (`OUTSCRAPER_UV_RUN`, GH#34620).
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/lib/mcp_config.py:152-160` dataforseo uses `bash -c 'source "$HOME/.aidevops/agents/scripts/dataforseo-credentials.sh" && dataforseo_load_credentials && exec ...'` with gopass fallback in `.agents/scripts/dataforseo-credentials.sh:6-30`. Mirror this for Outscraper (small loader or the shared resolver from the companion gopass-fallback issue if merged first).
- Migration: on setup, if `mcp.outscraper.env`/`environment` holds a literal `OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY`, replace the entry with the launcher form and drop the literal. Never print the value.
- Also scan other `mcp.*.env`/`environment` blocks the setup writes for secret-shaped names (`*_KEY|*_TOKEN|*_SECRET|*_PASS(WORD)?`) and report names only; fix any setup-written ones in the same way or file follow-ups.

## Acceptance

1. Fresh setup writes no literal secret value into the OpenCode config for outscraper.
2. Re-running setup on a config with a literal `OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY` removes it and installs the launcher form; the MCP starts with the key from gopass when it is absent from env and `credentials.sh`.
3. `mcp<2` pin preserved; existing `mcp_config.py` tests (if present) pass; ShellCheck clean on changed shell.
4. No value appears in setup output or logs.

## Context

- Related: #34854 / PR #34855 (plaintext → gopass migration) and the companion env-only helper gopass-fallback issue #34892.
- Interim manual fix for affected users: none applied; the literal stays until this lands.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/lib/mcp_config.py`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/outscraper-credentials.sh`
- `tests/test-migrate-mcp-npx-to-binary.sh`

Verification: ShellCheck on changed shell files; existing migration regression script; isolated synthetic-home runtime checks for registration, migration, credential precedence, gopass fallback, and no credential output. The setup writer scan found OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY as the only inline secret-valued MCP environment assignment; other setup MCP environment fields reference credential file paths or project identifiers.
