title: setup_mirror_sync never replaces a dead legacy bash -lc mirror-sync LaunchAgent (exit 127)
body:
## What

`setup_mirror_sync` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` (about lines 1100-1133) never replaces a dead legacy `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` LaunchAgent that runs its script through `bash -lc`.

For an unmarked plist, the collision check reads `ProgramArguments.1` as the script path. For `/bin/bash -lc "<script> check"` that value is `-lc`. It is not absolute, so the check treats the job as an ambiguous live program and fails closed with `Mirror sync label collision: existing program is live; leaving it unchanged`. The function comment says only a *healthy* foreign job should be left alone. This job is dead, so mirror sync never runs from launchd and setup cannot repair it.

## Evidence (one macOS install, 2026-10-17)

- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.mirror-sync.plist` has no `<!-- aidevops:mirror-sync -->` marker. Its `ProgramArguments` are `/bin/bash`, `-lc`, `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh check`. That custom script no longer exists; the canonical helper is `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`.
- `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` shows `LastExitStatus = 32512` (exit 127).
- `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.launchd.log` contains only `No such file or directory` lines. The canonical `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.log` was last written in April 2026.
- The existing setup test (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:136-150`) only covers `ProgramArguments = (/bin/bash, <absolute script>)`. It does not cover the `-c` / `-lc` command-string form.
- Related: PR #34891 (for #34888) makes Pulse skip core routines whose canonical label is loaded. A review there asks Pulse to fall back to its own run when the platform job cannot start. This issue is the setup half: replace the dead job, not just bypass it.

## Reproducer

Verified on 2026-10-17 against the deployed `schedulers-platform.sh`. The setup follows the existing harness in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:117-150`:

- isolated `HOME`, with `mirror-sync-helper.sh` copied in;
- `setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` sourced;
- `_launchd_install_if_changed`, `uname` (returns `Darwin`) and `plutil` stubbed.

1. Stub `plutil` to return `/bin/bash` for `ProgramArguments.0`, `-lc` for `ProgramArguments.1`, and `$ROOT/legacy-missing.sh check` for `ProgramArguments.2`. Do not create `$ROOT/legacy-missing.sh`.
2. Write `repos.json` with `{"initialized_repos":[{"slug":"private/mirror","mirror_upstream":"vendor/source"}]}`, and an unmarked `$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.mirror-sync.plist`.
3. Run `setup_mirror_sync`, then print `INSTALLS`.

**Symptom command:** `setup_mirror_sync; printf 'INSTALLS=%s\n' "$INSTALLS"` (inside the harness above)

**Actual output:**

```text
warning: Mirror sync label collision: existing program is live; leaving it unchanged
INSTALLS=0
```

**Expected output:** `INSTALLS=1`, with the dead plist replaced by the canonical marked plist.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`: the collision check in `setup_mirror_sync` (about lines 1109-1123). The canonical plist comes from `_mirror_sync_plist_content` (about lines 1081-1096).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`: extend the `plutil` stub cases at lines 136-150.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

1. For an unmarked existing plist whose `ProgramArguments.1` is exactly `-c` or `-lc`, take the first whitespace-delimited token of `ProgramArguments.2` as the script path:
   - absolute path that does not exist: the job is dead. Install the canonical plist through `_launchd_install_if_changed`, as already happens when `ProgramArguments.1` is a missing absolute script.
   - absolute path that exists: the job is live. Leave it unchanged with the existing warning.
   - any other shape (relative token, other flags, unparseable): fail closed as today.
2. Existing behaviour is unchanged for a missing or non-absolute program (`ProgramArguments.0`), for marked plists, and for the current absolute-script cases.
3. Replacing a dead legacy plist logs one line naming the label and the missing script path.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` passes with new cases:
  - `-lc` with a missing absolute script → installed;
  - `-lc` with an existing script → kept;
  - `-lc` with a non-absolute command → kept.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` reports no new findings.
- On an affected host after deploy, `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) installs the marked canonical plist. `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` then shows the canonical helper with `sync`, and the next 20:00 run writes to `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.log`.

title: mirror-sync-helper.sh discards git stderr, so scheduled FAIL states are undiagnosable
body:
## What

`git_remote` in `.agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh` (lines 25-46) runs every git network command with `2>/dev/null`. When a command fails, `sync_one` records a fixed detail: `upstream authentication or discovery failed` (line 59), `remote fetch failed` (line 69), or one of the push messages. A scheduled run therefore leaves no failure reason anywhere: not in the state file, the Pulse log, or routine tracking. That makes an environment-specific failure impossible to diagnose after the fact.

## Evidence (one macOS install, 2026-10-17)

- Routine r919 (`run:scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh sync`) has 38 consecutive failed Pulse runs. `pulse.log` records only `routine r919: script exited with code 1`.
- `mirror-sync-helper.sh status` shows `FAIL <mirror> upstream authentication or discovery failed` for both configured mirrors.
- On the same host, in an interactive shell, these succeed:
  - `mirror-sync-helper.sh check --repo <mirror>` authenticates and reports `DIVERGED <mirror> local commits require merge`;
  - `git ls-remote --symref <upstream-url> HEAD` through the `gh auth git-credential` helper.

  The failure is therefore specific to the scheduled environment, but nothing records why.

## Reproducer

Observed on the affected host after scheduled r919 runs. The failure can be reproduced generically by registering a mirror whose upstream is unreachable, as the existing `expected auth/fetch failure` test case does (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`, around line 112), then running `mirror-sync-helper.sh sync`.

**Symptom command:** `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh status`

**Actual output:**

```text
FAIL <mirror-a> upstream authentication or discovery failed
FAIL <mirror-b> upstream authentication or discovery failed
```

**Expected output:** the same FAIL lines, each followed by the sanitized git error that caused it.

Cause: `2>/dev/null` on lines 29, 38 and 42, combined with the fixed detail strings at lines 59, 64 and 69.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`: `git_remote` (lines 25-46) and the `report` call sites in `sync_one` (lines 48-121).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`: the existing failure case around line 112.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

1. When a git network command in `git_remote` fails, keep a bounded, sanitized reason and append it to the FAIL detail. Example: `upstream authentication or discovery failed: fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`.
   - Use the last non-empty stderr line, at most 200 characters.
   - Strip any `user:secret@` userinfo from URLs.
   - Redact token-like strings (`gh[pousr]_...`, `github_pat_...`).
2. Use the reason from the last attempt. Also record when the `gh` fallback was skipped, for example because `gh` was not on `PATH` or `gh auth status` failed.
3. No credential material appears in stdout, the state file or logs. Successful runs behave exactly as before.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` passes. The extended failure case asserts that the FAIL detail contains a reason and does not contain the injected `user:secret@` material.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` reports no new findings.
- After deploy, the next scheduled r919 run on the affected host leaves a `mirror-sync-helper.sh status` line that names the underlying git error.

title: Manual dispatch workers lack lease heartbeat, so remote stale-recovery redispatches live work
body:
## What

A live worker launched with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> <slug>` was flagged stale by another runner's pulse. The issue was unassigned and redispatched while the original worker was still running and making progress.

## Evidence

- The manual dispatch worker (PID alive for 1h16m) had committed and pushed specs, merged a partial data PR, and kept working on local uncommitted specs.
- Another runner's stale-recovery fired with `dispatch claim 3897s old, last activity 1026s old (threshold=600s, interactive=false)` and the reason "The assigned runner had no active worker process", which it cannot observe across hosts.
- The second runner claimed the issue, failed beta admin sign-in (HTTP 401), and the issue ended at `status:blocked`. That contradicts the work contract's `runner_capability_unmet` path, which says to stay `status:available`.

## Likely cause

Manual dispatch seems to write a ledger entry and an initial `DISPATCH_CLAIM` without the ongoing `DISPATCH_LEASE` renewals that pulse-dispatched workers publish. Remote stale-recovery therefore sees only the age of the last push or comment. The paths are not verified: start with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, the lease-renewal code in the headless runtime, and the stale-recovery logic (GH#15060) in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh` or the pulse.

## Fix direction

- Manual dispatches renew the same `DISPATCH_LEASE` heartbeat as pulse dispatches.
- Stale-recovery honours an unexpired lease before treating "last activity" as a dead runner.
- A rejected beta sign-in on a second runner maps to `runner_capability_unmet` (keep `status:available`) rather than `status:blocked`.

## Verification

Manually dispatch a long-running issue. Confirm that lease renewals appear and that no remote stale-recovery comment is posted while the worker PID is alive.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`

Scope evidence (worker discovery, GH#33243): manual dispatch never passed the claim's lease token to its worker, so the worker skipped the `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready` transition (`headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`) that `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` `_stale_recovery_final_evidence_recheck` already honours. The worker's lease transitions must use the claim's `issue-N` lease session while the manual runtime session stays `manual-cli-N-<epoch>`. `headless-runtime-lib.sh` holds the worker contract text for the `runner_capability_unmet` classification.

title: full-loop merge closes parent-task issue referenced only by For #N
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>` closed a `parent-task` issue that the merged PR referenced only with `For #N`. Closing it released a dependency-blocked sibling issue too early.

## Evidence

- The PR body ended with `For #<parent>`, with no `Resolves`, `Closes` or `Fixes` keyword.
- Merge output: `CLOSING_ISSUE_RECONCILIATION=converged pr=<PR> attempts=1 references=1`. The parent issue's timeline shows `closed` by the maintainer's token at the merge timestamp, with no closing comment.
- Two earlier merges, also with `For #<same parent>` in the body, logged `references=0` and left the issue open. The difference: shortly before the third merge the parent gained the `parent-task` label and two sub-issues.
- Side effect: the next-phase issue, which was blocked by the parent, was relabelled from `status:blocked` to `status:available` within seconds.

## Likely cause (unverified)

The closing-issue reconciliation probably counts `For #N` as a closing reference for `parent-task` issues, or closes a parent once a linked PR merges, without checking for open sub-issues. Start with the `CLOSING_ISSUE_RECONCILIATION` logic that `full-loop-helper.sh merge` calls.

## Fix direction

- Never close an issue from a `For #`/`Ref #` reference; only GitHub closing keywords count.
- Never auto-close a `parent-task` issue that has open sub-issues.

## Verification

Merge a PR whose body has only `For #<parent-task with open sub-issues>`. Confirm `references=0` and that the parent stays open.

body:
## Problem

Temporary detached worktrees and stale registrations accumulate after regression
checks. In `file-size-regression-helper.sh`, `scan_violations_ref` installs a

correctly preserves resources when ownership/process evidence is unavailable, but
creation, idle classification, archival and reconciliation need one contract.

## Requested outcome

Implement and verify a rootless lifecycle using the existing ownership registry
and managed lifetime fences, not a parallel supervisor. Ordinary worktrees become
archive candidates after 24 hours of confirmed idle, only without active owners,
open PR protection or preservation markers. Confirm recovery and source stability
before removal. Eliminate unnecessary temporary checkout creation. Preserve unknown
legacy data; do not activate archive expiry or weaken process guards.

## Implementation context

Plan: `todo/tasks/worktree-lifecycle-refactor.md` (prepared in the interactive
implementation branch). Start with `.agents/scripts/file-size-regression-helper.sh`

timeout/SIGTERM/SIGKILL, interrupted creation and removal, live descendants,
concurrent cleaners and late owners, reboot/unknown evidence, source mutation,
corrupt archives, missing Git prerequisites, unsupported recovery states and
capacity exhaustion. Compare recovered contents/state, not just process exit.
Verify rootless execution and Linux/NixOS plus Bash 3.2 portability. Obtain an
independent safety review and passing exact-head CI before merge.

The current interactive session owns implementation through merge. No remote
worker delegation, release, blanket legacy deletion, or irreversible archive
expiry is authorized by this issue.

body:
## Consolidation target: #34896

**Parent issue:** #34896 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** setup_mirror_sync never replaces a dead legacy bash -lc mirror-sync LaunchAgent (exit 127)
**Parent labels:** `bug,status:available,auto-dispatch,origin:interactive,tier:standard,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #34896. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #34896 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the inlined parent body verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #34896:**

```bash
gh issue comment 34896 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 34896 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 34896 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #34896 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #34896** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

`setup_mirror_sync` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` (about lines 1100-1133) never replaces a dead legacy `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` LaunchAgent that runs its script through `bash -lc`.

For an unmarked plist, the collision check reads `ProgramArguments.1` as the script path. For `/bin/bash -lc "<script> check"` that value is `-lc`. It is not absolute, so the check treats the job as an ambiguous live program and fails closed with `Mirror sync label collision: existing program is live; leaving it unchanged`. The function comment says only a *healthy* foreign job should be left alone. This job is dead, so mirror sync never runs from launchd and setup cannot repair it.

## Evidence (one macOS install, 2026-10-17)

- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.mirror-sync.plist` has no `<!-- aidevops:mirror-sync -->` marker. Its `ProgramArguments` are `/bin/bash`, `-lc`, `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh check`. That custom script no longer exists; the canonical helper is `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`.
- `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` shows `LastExitStatus = 32512` (exit 127).
- `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.launchd.log` contains only `No such file or directory` lines. The canonical `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.log` was last written in April 2026.
- The existing setup test (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:136-150`) only covers `ProgramArguments = (/bin/bash, <absolute script>)`. It does not cover the `-c` / `-lc` command-string form.
- Related: PR #34891 (for #34888) makes Pulse skip core routines whose canonical label is loaded. A review there asks Pulse to fall back to its own run when the platform job cannot start. This issue is the setup half: replace the dead job, not just bypass it.

## Reproducer

Verified on 2026-10-17 against the deployed `schedulers-platform.sh`. The setup follows the existing harness in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:117-150`:

- isolated `HOME`, with `mirror-sync-helper.sh` copied in;
- `setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` sourced;
- `_launchd_install_if_changed`, `uname` (returns `Darwin`) and `plutil` stubbed.

1. Stub `plutil` to return `/bin/bash` for `ProgramArguments.0`, `-lc` for `ProgramArguments.1`, and `$ROOT/legacy-missing.sh check` for `ProgramArguments.2`. Do not create `$ROOT/legacy-missing.sh`.
2. Write `repos.json` with `{"initialized_repos":[{"slug":"private/mirror","mirror_upstream":"vendor/source"}]}`, and an unmarked `$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.mirror-sync.plist`.
3. Run `setup_mirror_sync`, then print `INSTALLS`.

**Symptom command:** `setup_mirror_sync; printf 'INSTALLS=%s\n' "$INSTALLS"` (inside the harness above)

**Actual output:**

```text
warning: Mirror sync label collision: existing program is live; leaving it unchanged
INSTALLS=0
```

**Expected output:** `INSTALLS=1`, with the dead plist replaced by the canonical marked plist.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`: the collision check in `setup_mirror_sync` (about lines 1109-1123). The canonical plist comes from `_mirror_sync_plist_content` (about lines 1081-1096).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`: extend the `plutil` stub cases at lines 136-150.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

1. For an unmarked existing plist whose `ProgramArguments.1` is exactly `-c` or `-lc`, take the first whitespace-delimited token of `ProgramArguments.2` as the script path:
   - absolute path that does not exist: the job is dead. Install the canonical plist through `_launchd_install_if_changed`, as already happens when `ProgramArguments.1` is a missing absolute script.
   - absolute path that exists: the job is live. Leave it unchanged with the existing warning.
   - any other shape (relative token, other flags, unparseable): fail closed as today.
2. Existing behaviour is unchanged for a missing or non-absolute program (`ProgramArguments.0`), for marked plists, and for the current absolute-script cases.
3. Replacing a dead legacy plist logs one line naming the label and the missing script path.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` passes with new cases:
  - `-lc` with a missing absolute script → installed;
  - `-lc` with an existing script → kept;
  - `-lc` with a non-absolute command → kept.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` reports no new findings.
- On an affected host after deploy, `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) installs the marked canonical plist. `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` then shows the canonical helper with `sync`, and the next 20:00 run writes to `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.log`.

title: pulse-routines: launchd liveness check misreads command prefixes as missing scripts
body:
## What

`_routine_launchd_cannot_start` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh` (lines 132-177 on `main` at `bee7a0d70`, added by #34900 for #34888) inspects `-c`/`-lc` command strings. At lines 157-159 it treats the first absolute-path token found anywhere in the command as the script path. A healthy job whose command starts with an environment assignment is therefore reported as dead. For example, `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH /bin/echo ok` yields the token `/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH`. That token does not exist, so the function returns `script … missing`. `_routine_platform_owned` then releases ownership, and Pulse also runs the routine. This is the same duplicate dispatch that #34888 fixed.

The candidate loop at line 219 also probes `sh.aidevops.<name>` twice when no explicit label is set. A dead or unloaded job is checked twice, and a dead job writes two identical "cannot start" lines on each evaluation pass (line 226).

## Evidence (2026-10-17)

- The function from #34900's head `44af5d1` was sourced and called with synthetic `launchctl list` output. `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH /bin/echo ok` returned `script /opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH missing`. `cd /tmp && /bin/echo ok` returned no reason.
- On one macOS host, all 23 healthy loaded aidevops jobs were classified as owned. None of them uses this form, so the defect is latent. The generated r908 command contains `$(` before its script path, so the `ProgramArguments` capture ends at the first `)` and the script check never runs for that form.
- Review note: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/34900#issuecomment-6238166867

## Reproducer

1. Source `_routine_launchd_cannot_start` from `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`.
2. Run the symptom command.

**Symptom command:** `_routine_launchd_cannot_start '{ "LastExitStatus" = 0; "Program" = "/bin/bash"; "ProgramArguments" = ( "/bin/bash"; "-lc"; "PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH /bin/echo ok"; ); };'`

**Actual output:** `script /opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH missing`

**Expected output:** no output, because the job can start and stays platform-owned.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`: the `expect_cmd` branch of `_routine_launchd_cannot_start` (lines 157-166) and the candidate loop in `_routine_platform_owned` (lines 219-227).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh`: extend the `job_info` cases in `_test_platform_scheduler_ownership`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

1. In the `-c`/`-lc` branch, only the command's first word counts as a script path. Remove surrounding single or double quotes from it first, and skip one leading `exec`. If the command starts with an assignment (`NAME=value`), a builtin such as `cd`, or a command substitution, the job keeps platform ownership.
2. Existing detection is unchanged. These cases still return a reason: `LastExitStatus` 126, 127, 32256 or 32512; a missing `Program`; a missing first `ProgramArguments` path; and a missing absolute script as the command's first word, such as `/nonexistent/mirror-sync-helper.sh check`.
3. Each distinct label is probed once, so a dead job writes one "cannot start" line per pass.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh` passes. Add these cases:
  - an environment-assignment prefix: the job stays owned;
  - a quoted missing first word such as `'/nonexistent/x.sh' check`: the job is not owned.

  All existing cases must still pass.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-routines-selector.sh` reports no new findings.

title: consolidated: replace dead legacy bash -c/-lc mirror-sync LaunchAgent in setup_mirror_sync
body:
_Supersedes #34896 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make `setup_mirror_sync` in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh` (about lines 1100-1133) replace a dead legacy `sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` LaunchAgent that runs its script through `bash -c` / `bash -lc`, and extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` to cover it.

## Why

For an unmarked plist (no `<!-- aidevops:mirror-sync -->` marker), the collision check reads `ProgramArguments.1` as the script path. For `/bin/bash -lc "<script> check"` that value is `-lc`, which is not absolute, so the check treats the job as an ambiguous live program and fails closed: `Mirror sync label collision: existing program is live; leaving it unchanged`. The function comment says only a *healthy* foreign job should be left alone. This job is dead, so mirror sync never runs from launchd and setup cannot repair it.

Evidence (one macOS install, 2026-10-17):

- `~/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.mirror-sync.plist` is unmarked. `ProgramArguments` are `/bin/bash`, `-lc`, `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh check`. That custom script no longer exists; the canonical helper is `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/mirror-sync-helper.sh`.
- `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` shows `LastExitStatus = 32512` (exit 127).
- `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.launchd.log` contains only `No such file or directory` lines; `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.log` was last written in April 2026.
- The existing test (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:136-150`) only covers `ProgramArguments = (/bin/bash, <absolute script>)`.
- Related: PR #34891 (for #34888) makes Pulse skip core routines whose canonical label is loaded; #34900 lets Pulse fall back when this dead LaunchAgent cannot start. This issue is the setup half: replace the dead job.

## Reproducer

Harness per `test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:117-150`: isolated `HOME` with `mirror-sync-helper.sh` copied in, `schedulers-platform.sh` sourced, `_launchd_install_if_changed`, `uname` (returns `Darwin`) and `plutil` stubbed):

1. Stub `plutil`: `ProgramArguments.0` = `/bin/bash`, `.1` = `-lc`, `.2` = `$ROOT/legacy-missing.sh check`. Do not create `$ROOT/legacy-missing.sh`.
2. `repos.json` = `{"initialized_repos":[{"slug":"private/mirror","mirror_upstream":"vendor/source"}]}`, plus an unmarked `$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/sh.aidevops.mirror-sync.plist`.
3. Run `setup_mirror_sync; printf 'INSTALLS=%s\n' "$INSTALLS"`.

Actual: `warning: Mirror sync label collision: existing program is live; leaving it unchanged` and `INSTALLS=0`. Expected: `INSTALLS=1`, dead plist replaced by the canonical marked plist.

## How

- Edit the collision check in `setup_mirror_sync` (about lines 1109-1123) of `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh`. The canonical plist comes from `_mirror_sync_plist_content` (about lines 1081-1096); install via the existing `_launchd_install_if_changed` path, as already happens when `ProgramArguments.1` is a missing absolute script.
- For an unmarked plist whose `ProgramArguments.1` is exactly `-c` or `-lc`, take the first whitespace-delimited token of `ProgramArguments.2` as the script path (absolute and missing: dead, replace; absolute and existing: live, keep with existing warning; anything else: fail closed as today).
- Log one line when replacing, naming the label and the missing script path.
- Extend the `plutil` stub cases at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh:136-150`. Per the prior attempt: resolve the available Bash in the harness rather than assuming `/bin/bash` exists.
- Prior attempt (commits `ae4511a4a`, `73bc0deaf` on a runner-local branch) exists only on the producing runner; re-implement from this brief within the same Files Scope.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-platform.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unmarked plist, `ProgramArguments.1` exactly `-c` or `-lc`, first token of `ProgramArguments.2` is an absolute path that does not exist: canonical plist installed through `_launchd_install_if_changed` (`INSTALLS=1`).
- [ ] Same shape with an absolute path that exists: left unchanged with the existing warning.
- [ ] Any other shape (relative token, other flags, unparseable): fails closed as today.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged for missing or non-absolute `ProgramArguments.0`, marked plists, and current absolute-script cases.
- [ ] Replacing a dead legacy plist logs one line naming the label and the missing script path.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-mirror-sync-helper.sh` passes with new cases: `-lc` + missing absolute script → installed; `-lc` + existing script → kept; `-lc` + non-absolute command → kept.
- [ ] `shellcheck` on both files reports no new findings.
- [ ] On an affected host after deploy, `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) installs the marked canonical plist; `launchctl list sh.aidevops.mirror-sync` shows the canonical helper with `sync`, and the next 20:00 run writes to `~/.aidevops/logs/mirror-sync.log`.

- @marcusquinn (parent author): problem, evidence, reproducer, acceptance criteria and Files Scope.
- @vladimirdulov (comment 1): a prior worker implemented the change locally (`-c`/`-lc` recovery, fail-closed retained, logging, harness extension, Bash resolution in harness) but could not push: the pre-push `bun run typecheck` failed with `tsc` unavailable (exit 127) on that runner. Verified locally: the test script, `bash -n`, `git diff --check`; direct ShellCheck unavailable (CI matrix in `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` covers it). Native macOS deployment unverified.

title: interactive claim --implementing relabels a live same-login worker to status:claimed, tripping the 3.39.39 ownership fence (worker_ownership_lost) and stranding unpushed work
body:
## Observed

A manual worker was dispatched with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> <slug>`, which applied `status:queued` and a sole assignee. The interactive session then ran `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug> --implementing`, the workaround recorded on #34901 against stale recovery. `claim` changes the label to `status:claimed`.

In v3.39.39 the worker runtime fence (`dispatch-claim-helper.sh verify-worker-ownership`, `cmd_verify_worker_ownership`) accepts only `status:queued` or `status:in-progress`. It reported `WORKER_OWNERSHIP_LOST`, `headless-runtime-run.sh` received exit 85, and the worker stopped after about 20 minutes with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ownership_lost`. The same runner and login owned the issue throughout.

Impact: the worker had already published three artifacts to an external service. Its ledger, specs and work log were committed or uncommitted locally but never pushed. A later worker could have republished them. The data was recovered by hand from the worktree.

## Problem

Two framework paths conflict:

1. `interactive-session-helper.sh claim ... --implementing` sets `status:claimed` with no warning, even when the issue has a live worker dispatched from this runner (`status:queued`/`in-progress`, same assignee).
2. The ownership fence treats `status:claimed` held by the same login as lost ownership, then terminates the worker without first saving its work.

## Proposed fix (choose one or both)

- In `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`: if the issue is `status:queued`/`status:in-progress` with the runner as sole assignee and a live local worker session, refuse or warn, and print the worker PID/session. Never relabel silently.
- In the fence, or on the `worker_ownership_lost` exit path: before termination, ask the worker to push its branch/checkpoint (or have the runtime push a WIP branch), so external side effects recorded only in local files survive.

Files: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` (claim), `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh:1373-1412`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-run.sh:297-304`, `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:2635-2642`.

## Verification

Dispatch a manual worker against a test issue, run `claim --implementing` from the same login, and confirm one of two outcomes: the claim is refused or warned about, or the worker's branch is pushed before termination.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh`

_gsc_load_token() {
	aidevops_load_secret GSC_ACCESS_TOKEN && return 0
	if [[ -n "${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-}" && -f "$GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS" ]]; then
		GSC_ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token 2>/dev/null || true)

	fi

}

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a helper next to `run_test` that never builds a command string containing a secret:

```bash
# Bearer-token connectivity check. The token is read from the named variable and
# piped to curl on stdin (-H @-) so it never appears in any process argv.
run_bearer_test() {
	local test_name="$1"
	local token_var="$2"
	local url="$3"
	((++total_tests))
	print_info "Testing: $test_name"
	if printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "${!token_var}" | curl -fsS -o /dev/null -H @- "$url" 2>/dev/null; then
		print_success "$test_name: PASSED"
		((++passed_tests))
		return 0
	fi
	print_error "$test_name: FAILED"
	((++failed_tests))
	return 1
}
```

2. Replace the call sites, guarding with `|| true` so a failed check is counted, not fatal:

```bash
if aidevops_load_secret AHREFS_API_KEY; then
	run_bearer_test "Ahrefs API connectivity" AHREFS_API_KEY "https://apiv2.ahrefs.com/v2/subscription_info" || true
...
if aidevops_load_secret PERPLEXITY_API_KEY; then
	run_bearer_test "Perplexity API connectivity" PERPLEXITY_API_KEY "<existing perplexity URL>" || true
...
	run_bearer_test "Cloudflare API connectivity" CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" || true
```

   Perplexity's current URL is `https://api.perplexity.ai/chat/completions`, which needs POST; a GET with `-f` will fail. Pick a GET-able authenticated endpoint from Perplexity's docs (Context7) or keep a POST with a minimal body via `-d`. Record the choice in the PR. Keep the Cloudflare `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`/`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` env check as the explicit path; the registry-default path (lines 144-170) is already correct.

title: feat: aidevops security detects credential hygiene drift and offers interactive fixes
body:
## What

Extend `aidevops security` so it detects the credential-hygiene failures found during a real plaintext → gopass migration, and add an interactive `aidevops security fix` that offers the safe remediations by delegating to existing `secret-helper.sh` commands. Detection never prints values.

## Why

During the migration that produced #34854, #34892 and #34893, `aidevops security` reported nothing actionable even though the install had:

- a corrupted tenant credentials line (two `export` statements glued together, so one token silently ended in the text `export` and the second name was never set);
- `$`-expansions that block `secret import-credentials` with only a generic "failed safely" error;
- plaintext values that drifted from gopass (two tokens: plaintext returned 401/400, gopass 200);
- ten plaintext secrets already safely held in gopass (prunable);
- stale `credentials.sh.bak-*` copies (some mode 644);
- a literal secret in an MCP server `env` block in the OpenCode config.

Root causes in the current scanner:

- `.agents/scripts/secret-hygiene-helper.sh:120-135` `_scan_aidevops_creds` inspects only `~/.config/aidevops/credentials.sh`. In tenant-loader mode that is the loader; the tenant files holding the secrets are never examined.
- `.agents/scripts/secret-hygiene-helper.sh:450-499` `scan_mcp_configs` checks only for `uvx`/`npx` launchers, not secret values in `env`/`environment` blocks.

## How

### Detection (default `aidevops security`, `security scan`, names/line numbers only)

Add a names-only, machine-readable audit in `secret-helper.sh` (suggest `secret-helper.sh audit-credentials`), consumed by `secret-hygiene-helper.sh` via `report_finding` (`:84`). Reuse, do not duplicate:

- File set: `resolve_credential_files` (`secret-helper.sh:98`), `is_tenant_loader` (`:60`), `active_tenant_name` (`:67`), `stranded_loader_names` (`:119`).
- Parsing/eligibility rules: the Python validator inside `credential_migration` (`secret-helper.sh:1453-1590`, `literal()` and the `export NAME=` full-line match). Refactor so the same rules yield per-line findings (line number, name, category: `glued-exports`, `shell-expansion`, `inner-quote`, `unsupported-structure`, `crlf`) instead of a single generic failure; `import-credentials` should print those findings too.
- gopass comparison: the prune path already classifies names as prunable / differing / not owned. Expose it as findings: `prunable` (equal, `check` passes), `drift` (gopass differs), `not-in-gopass` for secret-shaped names (same name regex as `credential_migration`).
- Leftovers: `credentials.sh.bak*`, `.credentials-prune-*`, `.credentials-repair-*` style temp files beside any credentials file, with perms.
- Perms/ownership on every credentials file (not just the loader).

Extend `scan_mcp_configs` (`secret-hygiene-helper.sh:450`) to parse each runtime config (registry list already built at `:458-470`) as JSON and report `server` + `name` for secret-shaped names (`*_KEY|*_TOKEN|*_SECRET|*_PASS(WORD)?|*_CREDENTIALS?`) whose value is a non-empty literal (not `{env:…}`/`{file:…}`). Handle both `env` and `environment` keys.

Update `cmd_startup_check` (`:585`) to include a one-line count of these findings.

### Remediation (`aidevops security fix`, interactive only)

Route in `aidevops.sh` `_cmd_security` (`:1763-1812`) and help text (`:1277-1286`). Refuse when non-interactive (no TTY or headless session) with a message pointing at the individual commands. Per category, show names and ask before acting:

| Category | Action | Confirmation |
|----------|--------|--------------|
| Insecure perms | `chmod 600` | none needed (non-destructive) — still listed |
| Not in gopass | `secret-helper.sh import-credentials` | none needed (additive) — still listed |
| Prunable | `secret-helper.sh prune-plaintext --dry-run`, then real prune | yes |
| Leftover backups/temp files | move to trash (use the framework's trash-backed removal, not `rm`) | yes |
| MCP literal secrets | outscraper: reuse the #34893 setup migration; others: report the launcher pattern (`dataforseo-credentials.sh` / `outscraper-credential…` loaders) | yes |
| Drift | report only; tell the user to choose with `aidevops secret set NAME` | — |
| Unparseable lines | report only (line + category) | — |

Log each applied fix with `audit-log-helper.sh` (names only).

### Non-goals

- No live provider API probes in default scans (network, rate limits, per-provider endpoints). Leave a note for a possible opt-in `--probe` later.
- No automatic repair of unparseable lines or drift resolution.
- No change to `prune-plaintext` safety rules.

### Complexity Impact

`credential_migration` is already ~140 lines with embedded Python; extract the parser into a reusable function/module rather than growing it. `scan_mcp_configs` grows ~30 lines — extract a `_scan_mcp_env_literals` helper. `_cmd_security` gains one case arm.

## Acceptance

1. In an isolated `HOME` with a tenant loader and a tenant file containing a glued double-export line, a `$HOME` expansion, a value equal to gopass, a value differing from gopass and a secret not in gopass, `aidevops security scan` reports each with file, line number, name and category, and prints no values (assert the fixture values are absent from output).
2. Tenant files are scanned in loader mode; a `credentials.sh.bak-*` file at mode 644 is reported.
3. An OpenCode/Claude config fixture with a literal `*_API_KEY` in `env` and another in `environment` is reported; `{env:X}` references are not.
4. `aidevops security fix` refuses without a TTY; interactively it applies only confirmed categories, delegates to `import-credentials`/`prune-plaintext`, trashes backups, and leaves drift/unparseable lines untouched.
5. `import-credentials` failure output names the offending line numbers and categories instead of only the generic message.
6. ShellCheck zero violations on changed shell files; existing `tests/test-secret-helper.sh` passes. Extend it (or add a focused hygiene test) for criteria 1–5, reusing the isolated-gopass approach from PR #34855.

## Context

- Related: #34854 / PR #34855, #34892 / PR #34912, #34893.
- The real-install findings above were remediated manually; this issue makes them detectable and fixable for every user.

title: fix: dispatch-single-issue reports false 'consensus claim lost' on freshly created issues
body:
## What

`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch` reports `Consensus claim lost for #N; another runner won` on the first attempt against a freshly created issue, when no other runner holds a claim. An immediate retry wins. Make the first attempt succeed (or report the true reason), and stop discarding the claim helper's reason text.

## Why

Observed twice in one interactive session, 2026-10-17, both on issues created via `framework-issue-helper.sh log` moments earlier (#34892, #34921):

- First `dispatch` → `Consensus claim lost … another runner won`, exit 0, no worker.
- 20–75 s later: issue had no comments, no assignee, labels still `status:available`; `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status` → `No active dispatch`.
- Second `dispatch` → `Consensus claim won`, worker launched normally.

Users asking to "dispatch a worker" get a misleading success-shaped exit and no worker; the message blames a nonexistent runner.

## How

Not yet root-caused. Evidence-led starting points (verify against current `main`):

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh:917-930` — `claim_output` from `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh claim` is captured but only `claim_rc` is used; rc 1 is always worded "another runner won". First fix: print the claim helper's stderr reason (names/ids only) so the cause is visible.
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh` exit 1 paths: `_post_claim` (`:326`, including `CLAIM_SKIPPED: repo_state_not_managed` at `:337`), `_guard_no_active_assignment_before_claim` (`:1144`), `_fetch_claims` (`:605`) / `_fetch_claim_marker_comments` (`:536`) after the consensus window (`DISPATCH_CLAIM_WINDOW`, `:50`), `_delete_losing_claim_comment` (`:1126`). Candidate causes: read-after-write lag on the comments endpoint so our own claim is not visible yet (treated as lost), a just-created issue failing the repo-state/managed check, or a creation-time pulse/claim race whose comment was cleaned up.
- Reproduce: create an issue with `framework-issue-helper.sh log … --auto-dispatch`, then immediately `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> marcusquinn/aidevops`; capture `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh claim` stderr. Set `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_CLAIM_CALL_LOG` (`dispatch-claim-helper.sh:198`) to log stage timings.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-policy.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-claim-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-claim-helper.sh`

Worker scope note: root cause traced to the issue-age hydration window (`dispatch-dedup-assignment.sh` `_is_assigned_check_hydration_window`, 30 s). The pre-claim dedup check uses prefetched metadata without `createdAt` (`dispatch-single-issue-policy.sh` `_dsi_load_issue_meta`), so it fails open; the claim-time `is_assigned` refetches with `createdAt` and blocks with `HYDRATION_WINDOW`, which surfaces as rc 1 = "another runner won".

## Acceptance

1. A lost claim prints the concrete reason from the claim helper (e.g. competing runner login + claim time, `repo_state_not_managed`, own-claim-not-visible) instead of always "another runner won".
2. When our own claim is the only claim but is not yet visible, the helper retries the read within the window rather than reporting loss; dispatching immediately after issue creation succeeds on the first attempt in the reproduction above.
3. A genuine competing claim still yields "lost" and no worker (no regression of consensus dedup).
4. ShellCheck zero violations on changed files; existing dispatch-claim tests pass.

## Context

- Discovered while dispatching #34892 and #34921; both succeeded on retry.

title: docs: conflict-resolution.md omits that --ours/--theirs swap during rebase
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# docs: conflict-resolution.md omits that --ours/--theirs swap during rebase

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `rebase ours theirs swapped conflict resolution` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch target files in last 48h (last commit on the file: `ad99d27b`, 2026-09-30; `prework-discovery-helper.sh` found no open related PRs or claimed issues)
- [x] File refs verified: 14 repo paths checked with `git ls-files`, all present; doc line numbers verified at upstream HEAD (raw file SHA-256 matches the copy the edits below were read from)
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — disqualifier check clean (docs-only verbatim edits; file not listed in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`)
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — every edit is supplied verbatim below

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-17
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (session ID not recorded)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Found during an interactive-session review of the framework's git conflict guidance. The doc's quick reference and per-file resolution blocks describe merge semantics only, while its decision tree and quick commands are explicitly offered for rebase too.

## What

`.agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md` states, without qualification, that `git checkout --ours <file>` keeps "your version" and that `-Xours` means "your branch is authoritative". That holds for `git merge` and `git cherry-pick`, but is reversed during `git rebase` (including `git pull --rebase`): `ours` is the upstream plus commits already replayed, and `theirs` is your commit being replayed.

Add the rebase caveat wherever the doc assigns meaning to `ours`/`theirs`, so an agent resolving a rebase conflict keeps the side it intends.

## Why

Following the current text mid-rebase discards the branch's own change: `git checkout --ours <file>  # keep your version` actually keeps upstream. That silently violates the doc's own rule 5 ("Custom values win over upstream defaults (rebase)"). Workers routinely rebase PR branches, so the trap sits on a hot path.

Primary source, git-rebase(1) (`--merge` and `-X` options): "the side reported as ours is the so-far rebased series, starting with <upstream>, and theirs is the working branch. In other words, the sides are swapped." and "Note the reversal of ours and theirs as noted above for the -m option."

The framework already documents this correctly in one place, `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf:52` (`ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE`): "during rebase, `--ours` refers to the rebased-onto branch (`origin/{default_branch}`), `--theirs` refers to the commit being applied (your branch). This is REVERSED from a normal merge." The tool doc should match it.

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [x] **Exact execution contract supplied?** Eight exact `oldString`/`newString` pairs below.
- [x] **Targets and reference pattern verified?** One file; reference wording from `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf:52`.
- [x] **No semantic or design decision remains?** Wording is fixed below.
- [x] **Bounded, reversible, low-consequence impact?** Docs-only; single-commit revert.
- [x] **No stateful coordination to invent?** None.
- [x] **Focused verification and rollback are explicit?** See Verification Before Dispatch and Acceptance Criteria.
- [x] **No dispatch-path risk override?** Not listed in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`.

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** verbatim docs-only replacements in one file with codebase-pattern verification and single-commit rollback -> tier:simple.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task: the PR uses a normal closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md:26,38,45,58-59,86,91-92,117,165` — add the rebase side-swap caveat (eight edits below).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** agents load the doc on demand via pointers in `.agents/AGENTS.md`, `.agents/workflows/branch.md`, `.agents/workflows/pr.md`, `.agents/tools/git/github-cli.md`, `.agents/tools/git/lumen.md`, `.agents/tools/git/jujutsu.md`, and `.agents/reports/development.md`. None restate `--ours`/`--theirs` semantics: `rg` over the deployed `.agents/` tree for `checkout --(ours|theirs)`, `restore --(ours|theirs)`, and `-X ?(ours|theirs)` matched only this doc and `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** this doc only.
- **Existing verification/tests:** none encode this doc's text; `.agents/scripts/tests/test-conflict-pattern-detection.sh` covers `conflict-patterns.conf`, which is unchanged.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A — `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf` already carries the correct note (line 52), and its `LOCKFILE` entries (lines 34-40) are side-agnostic because the lockfile is regenerated.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/` copy refreshes via `setup.sh` / `aidevops update`; its `tools/git/conflict-resolution/SKILL.md` is generated at deploy time (not tracked) as an 8-line pointer, so nothing to sync. `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json` tracks this file for the simplification routine; do not hand-edit it.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A — docs-only.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the single commit.

### Implementation Steps

Apply each pair as an exact-match edit, preserving leading spaces.

1. Line 26 (AI-context quick reference).

oldString:

```text
- **Strategy options**: `-Xours` (our side wins conflicts), `-Xtheirs` (their side wins), `-Xignore-space-change`
```

newString:

```text
- **Strategy options**: `-Xours` (our side wins conflicts), `-Xtheirs` (their side wins), `-Xignore-space-change`
- **Rebase swaps sides**: during `git rebase` (including `git pull --rebase`), `ours` (`--ours`, `-Xours`) is the upstream plus commits already replayed, and `theirs` (`--theirs`, `-Xtheirs`) is your commit being replayed. Merge and cherry-pick keep the usual meaning (`ours` = current `HEAD`).
```

2. Line 38 (decision tree; the new line aligns `(` under `git`).

oldString:

```text
  |     YES --> git checkout --ours/--theirs <file> && git add <file>
```

newString:

```text
  |     YES --> git checkout --ours/--theirs <file> && git add <file>
  |             (rebase: --ours = upstream, --theirs = your commit)
```

3. Line 45 (decision tree).

oldString:

```text
(regenerate lock file if needed)
```

newString:

```text
(regenerate lock file if needed; rebase swaps --ours/--theirs)
```

4. Lines 58-59 (quick commands).

oldString:

```text
git checkout --ours <file>          # take our version
git checkout --theirs <file>        # take their version
```

newString:

```text
git checkout --ours <file>          # take our version (rebase: upstream)
git checkout --theirs <file>        # take their version (rebase: your commit)
```

5. Line 86 (after the strategy-option table).

oldString:

```text
**Important**: `-Xours` (strategy option) differs from `-s ours` (strategy). The strategy discards the other branch entirely; the option only resolves conflicts in your favor while still merging non-conflicting changes.
```

newString:

```text
**Important**: `-Xours` (strategy option) differs from `-s ours` (strategy). The strategy discards the other branch entirely; the option only resolves conflicts in your favor while still merging non-conflicting changes.

**Rebase reverses the table**: `git rebase -Xours` lets the upstream side win; `git rebase -Xtheirs` lets your replayed commits win. The "When to use" column describes merges.
```

6. Lines 91-92 (per-file resolution).

oldString:

```text
git checkout --ours <file>          # keep your version
git checkout --theirs <file>        # keep their version
```

newString:

```text
git checkout --ours <file>          # merge: keep your version; rebase: keep upstream
git checkout --theirs <file>        # merge: keep their version; rebase: keep your commit
```

7. Line 117 (Rebase scenario).

oldString:

```text
Rebase replays commits one at a time — you may resolve multiple conflicts.
```

newString:

```text
Rebase replays commits one at a time — you may resolve multiple conflicts. Sides are swapped while rebasing: `--ours` is the upstream plus commits already replayed, and `--theirs` is the commit being replayed. Keep your change with `git checkout --theirs <file>`; keep upstream with `git checkout --ours <file>`.
```

8. Line 165 (`ADD_ADD_NEW_FILE` row; compact table, no re-alignment needed).

oldString:

```text
During rebase, `git checkout --ours <path> && git add <path> && git rebase --continue`; append unique additions later.
```

newString:

```text
During rebase, `git checkout --ours <path> && git add <path> && git rebase --continue` keeps the default branch's copy (`--ours` is the upstream while rebasing); append your unique additions in a follow-up commit.
```

9. Run the verification below, then commit.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A — single docs file; no open PRs touch it (discovery above).
- **Migration/rollback:** none; revert the commit.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** docs-only; older deployed copies keep the old text until `aidevops update`.
- **Idempotency/retry:** each oldString disappears after its edit, so a retried edit fails to match instead of duplicating text.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if an oldString no longer matches, re-read the file at HEAD and apply the same wording to the current line.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
# Behaviour check for the documented claim (any machine with git user.name/email set)
tmp=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$tmp" && git init -q -b main \
  && echo base > f && git add f && git commit -qm base \
  && git checkout -qb topic && echo mine > f && git commit -qam mine \
  && git checkout -q main && echo upstream > f && git commit -qam upstream \
  && git checkout -q topic; git rebase main >/dev/null 2>&1
git checkout --ours f && cat f     # prints: upstream
git checkout --theirs f && cat f   # prints: mine
git rebase --abort

# From the aidevops worktree
rg -n 'Rebase swaps sides|Rebase reverses the table|Sides are swapped while rebasing' .agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the temp-repo run proves the rebase semantics the new text states; `rg` proves the three explanatory additions landed; changed-file lint covers markdown formatting of the one changed file.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required — docs-only, one file.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** edit only the file listed in Files Scope; do not change `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf`, `.agents/configs/simplification-state.json`, or any script.

**AI brief owner:** @marcusquinn (maintainer); filed by an interactive AI session.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The quick reference states that rebase swaps `ours`/`theirs`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Rebase swaps sides"
    path: ".agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md"
  ```

- [ ] The Rebase scenario tells agents which flag keeps their own change.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Keep your change with `git checkout --theirs <file>`"
    path: ".agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md"
  ```

- [ ] No `--ours` comment still claims "keep your version" without a rebase qualifier.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "# keep your version$"
    path: ".agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`).

## Context & Decisions

- Docs-only fix: a scan of the framework shell scripts found no `git rebase -X ours|theirs`, `checkout --ours|--theirs`, or `restore --ours|--theirs`, so no script depends on the wrong reading.
- The padded strategy-table rows (lines 81-82) stay unchanged to avoid re-aligning the table; the paragraph added after line 86 qualifies them instead.
- Non-goals: rewriting the doc, or changing conflict-pattern guidance in `conflict-patterns.conf`.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md:26` — quick-reference strategy options (edit 1)
- `.agents/tools/git/conflict-resolution.md:115-125` — Rebase scenario (edit 7)
- `.agents/configs/conflict-patterns.conf:52` — reference wording for the rebase swap (unchanged)

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** none
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 5m | the 257-line target doc |
| Implementation | 10m | eight exact edits |
| Verification | 5m | temp-repo check, `rg`, changed-file lint |
| **Total** | **20m** | |

title: feat: security scan covers mcp-env.sh, plist env overrides and project .env files
body:
## What

Extend the credential-hygiene scan to the env-style files that still carry secrets: `mcp-env.sh`, `plist-env-overrides.json`, and project `.env` files. Names, paths and line numbers only; never values.

## Why

Follow-up to #34921 (credential audit + `aidevops security fix`), whose scope covers `credentials.sh` loader/tenant files and MCP runtime configs but not these:

- Shell rc files gate on `mcp-env.sh` and then source `credentials.sh` (observed: `[[ -f ~/.config/aidevops/mcp-env.sh ]] && source "$HOME/.config/aidevops/credentials.sh"` in `.zshrc`, `.bashrc`, `.bash_profile`). On current installs `mcp-env.sh` is a symlink to `credentials.sh` at both `~/.config/aidevops/` and `~/.config/aidevops/tenants/<tenant>/`. Older installs with a regular-file `mcp-env.sh` would hold secrets that no scan sees, and removing the symlink silently stops shells loading credentials.
- `~/.config/aidevops/plist-env-overrides.json` (launchd environment overrides) can hold literal values and is unscanned.
- Project `.env` handling (`.agents/scripts/secret-hygiene-helper.sh:271-280` in `_scan_ssh_and_env`) only counts `.env` files under `~/Git` (depth 3) and advises "ensure .gitignore"; it does not check tracking or contents.

## How

Implement in `.agents/scripts/secret-hygiene-helper.sh`, reporting through `report_finding` (`:84`). If #34921 has merged, reuse its names-only parser/audit (`secret-helper.sh audit-credentials` or equivalent) and secret-name classifier rather than adding another; otherwise share the name regex from `credential_migration` in `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh:1453-1590` (`(?:^|_)(?:KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASS|CREDENTIALS?)$`).

1. `mcp-env.sh` (each of `~/.config/aidevops/` and `tenants/*/`):
   - symlink to sibling `credentials.sh` → OK;
   - regular file → medium finding; scan it with the same rules as credentials files (perms, unparseable lines, prunable/drift);
   - missing while rc files reference it → low finding ("shells will not load credentials").
2. `plist-env-overrides.json`: parse JSON; report key paths whose final name is secret-shaped and whose value is a non-empty literal; check perms 600.
3. Project `.env` files: enumerate repos from `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` (as `scan_remote_urls` at `:512` does) plus the existing `~/Git` sweep; match `.env` and `.env.*` (exclude `.env.example`, `.env.sample`, `.env.template`). Per file:
   - tracked by Git (`git -C <repo> ls-files --error-unmatch <file>`) → high;
   - untracked and not ignored (`git check-ignore -q` fails) → medium;
   - secret-shaped names with non-empty literal values → list names; note when gopass already holds the same name (`secret-helper.sh check NAME`).
   - Bound the sweep (depth/timeout) as the current `fd` call does.
4. If #34921's `aidevops security fix` exists: offer only `chmod 600` and "recreate `mcp-env.sh` symlink" (with confirmation). `.env` contents and plist overrides are report-only.

### Non-goals

- No editing or deleting of `.env` files or plist overrides.
- No value printing, hashing to output, or provider probes.

### Complexity Impact

`_scan_ssh_and_env` is ~40 lines; move the `.env` logic into a new `_scan_env_files` function rather than growing it. Add `_scan_mcp_env_link` and `_scan_plist_env_overrides` as separate functions called from `scan_plaintext_secrets` (`:292`).

## Acceptance

1. Isolated-`HOME` fixture: regular-file `mcp-env.sh` with a secret export is reported (path, line, name) and scanned like `credentials.sh`; a correct symlink produces no finding.
2. `plist-env-overrides.json` fixture with a literal `*_TOKEN` is reported by key path; non-secret keys are not.
3. Fixture repo: tracked `.env` → high; untracked unignored `.env.local` → medium; ignored `.env` → names only; `.env.example` skipped.
4. Fixture secret values never appear in output (assert absence).
5. ShellCheck zero violations; existing hygiene/secret tests pass.

## Context

- Related: #34921, #34892 / PR #34912, #34893.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: fix(worker): POST_PR_HANDOFF after the worker's own PR merged and closed the issue is routed as failure and escalates tier
body:
## What

A headless worker can merge its own PR, which closes the issue, and then exit with `POST_PR_HANDOFF`. That is a full success, but it is routed as `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`:

- the claim is released as a failure;
- `_report_failure_to_fast_fail` runs with crash type `overwhelmed`, which escalates the tier at threshold 1. It posts "Cascade Tier Escalation: tier:standard → tier:thinking … Previous attempts at `tier:standard` failed to produce a PR" and adds `tier:thinking` to the closed issue;
- the run ends in the failed terminal state.

Route a verified exact-head merged PR whose issue is closed as worker completion.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-17 on a private managed repository. Its name is left out because it is private.

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 17:54 | Worker dispatched (`tier:standard`) |
| 18:16 | Draft PR created, body contains `Resolves #N` |
| 18:33 | PR marked ready |
| 18:34 | `<!-- MERGE_SUMMARY -->` comment posted |
| 18:39 | PR merged; the issue closed as `COMPLETED` |
| 18:47 | `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`: `result=post_pr_handoff`, `exit_code=0`, `next_action=inspect_failure_excerpt` |
| 18:47 | `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified` |
| 18:48 | False "Cascade Tier Escalation" comment; `tier:thinking` label added to the closed issue |
| 19:22 | Full-loop cleanup receipt for the PR: `executor_completion_state=COMPLETE`, `resource_cleanup_state=CLEANED` |

The issue was closed, so no redispatch followed. The failure metric, the false escalation comment and the label are noise, and they count against the standard tier for this kind of task.

## Root cause

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`, `_worker_post_pr_handoff_confirmed` (around lines 596–619), accepts only `ready`. For a merged PR that has its closing reference and merge summary, `_pr_handoff_state_for_branch_or_issue` (`.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`, around line 240) returns `merged|N`.
2. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`, `_hrw_finish_success_run` (around line 2457), therefore sends the run to `_hrw_handle_unverified_post_pr_handoff` (around line 2424).
3. There, `_worker_produced_output` → `_hrw_pr_output_class` (around line 650) → `_hrw_merged_pr_output_class` (around line 638) maps `closed:merged` to `pr_exists`.
4. `_hrw_handle_unverified_post_pr_handoff` handles only `draft_checkpoint`, `merged_checkpoint`, `ready_missing_summary` and `ready_missing_linkage`. `pr_exists` falls to `*)`: unverified release, fast-fail as `overwhelmed`, failed terminal state.

The fail-open `pr_exists` and a verified merged PR with a closed issue are the same string at this point, so the handler cannot tell them apart.

## How

1. Make a verified merged PR with a closed issue confirm the handoff. Either:
   - in `_worker_post_pr_handoff_confirmed`, also accept `merged` when the issue is closed (the `require_merge_summary=1` probe already enforces exact head, closing linkage and `MERGE_SUMMARY`); or
   - add an explicit arm before `*)` in `_hrw_handle_unverified_post_pr_handoff` for that verified state. It releases with `_HRW_REASON_WORKER_COMPLETE` and skips fast-fail and escalation.
2. Keep the fail-open `pr_exists` path (signals that cannot be evaluated) and the open-issue `merged_checkpoint` path unchanged.
3. Reference pattern: the existing-PR recovery block in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` around line 1262 already treats `merged` as `worker_failure_recovered_existing_pr` and releases with `_HRW_REASON_WORKER_COMPLETE`.
4. Tests: add a case beside the GH#33115 cases in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`. Use `post_pr_handoff` with handoff state `merged|N` and a closed issue, and assert: no fast-fail, no escalation, claim released as `worker_complete`. Keep the existing "unverified POST_PR_HANDOFF cannot suppress failure routing" case pinned to fail-open `pr_exists`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A `post_pr_handoff` run with an exact-head merged PR, closing linkage, `MERGE_SUMMARY` and a closed issue releases its claim as `worker_complete`. It produces no fast-fail report, tier escalation comment or tier label, and does not end in the failed terminal state.
- [ ] Fail-open `pr_exists`, `merged_checkpoint` (issue open) and the `ready_missing_*` routes behave as before.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean, and the existing headless-runtime checkpoint and completion tests pass.

Related: GH#33115 (unverified handoff with a durable ready PR), GH#33374 (merged checkpoint or reopened issue is not completion; see the comment above `_hrw_merged_pr_output_class`).

Out of scope, noted for context: the same PR was merged while its body still held the worker's draft text ("Runtime testing … in progress … not a completion claim"). The merge summary said the full evidence was in the PR body. No merge gate checks that a draft-checkpoint body was finalised. That needs its own issue if wanted.

## Task Brief

## What

Give large blocked backlogs enough of the stale-blocked sweep budget to make progress. Today every due repo gets an equal share, so the largest backlog advances by about one issue per sweep.

## Why (observed evidence, 2026-10-17, v3.39.40 with t18707/#34895 deployed)

- Per-repo stamps now converge: 57 of 63 repos have a `stale-blocked-complete` stamp from the last few hours, so #34895 works for small repos.

## How (suggested; verify against current code first)

- In `_pulse_reconcile_stale_blocked_if_due` / `_pulse_stale_blocked_repo_deadline`, either:
